    optim::ACORAnt Colony Optimization for continuous domains (ACOR), Socha & Dorigo (2008). A solution archive of size k is maintained; each iteration, new ants are sampled from a Gaussian kernel mixture built from the archive (ranked by quality, so better solutions attract denser sampling), then the archive is truncated back to its k best members merged with the new ants. Derivative-free, box-constrained.

    optim::AdaDeltaAdaDelta on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Uses squared-gradient and squared-update exponential averages. The update multiplies the gradient by sqrt(previous_update_average+epsilon)/sqrt(current_gradient_average+epsilon). No separate learning-rate option. Tests the gradient used after applying its update; O(p) reset local state. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::AdaDeltaOptionsConfiguration for AdaDelta; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    optim::AdaGradAdaGrad on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Accumulates squared full gradients; divides each update by sqrt(sum+epsilon). Tests the pre-update gradient norm after applying the update. Every optimize call resets the accumulator. O(p) local storage. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::AdaGradOptionsConfiguration for AdaGrad; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    optim::AdamAdam on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Bias-corrected full-batch first and second moments, denominator sqrt(vhat)+epsilon. Tests the pre-update gradient norm after applying its update. No line search or general nonconvex convergence guarantee; O(p) reset local state. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::AdamOptionsConfiguration for Adam; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

    fda::AdaptiveSplineCellOne cell of a complete binary refinement tree, in creation order.
    fda::AdaptiveSplineFitOwned continuous fitted spline, selected tree, and complete refinement audit. Predictions use an equivalent finest-grid B-spline representation, avoiding evaluation-order dependence at cell boundaries. Const evaluation is thread-safe. Path and candidates describe the entire searched path, including prefixes beyond the validation-selected tree. The cells/splits fields describe only the selected model. Fields are snapshots; editing them can invalidate the fit.
    fda::AdaptiveSplineOptionsSearch controls for continuous HB/THB regression and hierarchical P-splines. The domain is fixed before fitting. A common finest dyadic coefficient grid defines the penalty, independent of the chosen hierarchical basis. Lambda zero gives least squares. This API fits genuine hierarchical spaces, unlike the independent residual patches of HierarchicalBSpline. No global risk optimum is asserted. The fixed-lambda API uses a training-driven greedy path; the joint API alternates validation tuning and recursive growth.
    fda::AdaptiveSplineStepA fitted path prefix and its honest held-out validation score.
    fda::AdaptiveSplineTuningOne smoothing-parameter evaluation on an accepted tree. Entries include rejected numerical solves and all interpolation probes.

    algorithms::AdjacentSortInputsFour owned controlled inputs for integer adjacent-exchange sort experiments. All arrays contain 0 through n-1. ascending has no inversions; descending has n(n-1)/2; adjacent_inversion exchanges the middle adjacent pair when n>=2; last_minimum moves zero from first to last, giving n-1 inversions for n>=1. Empty/singleton arrays coincide. The whole generator retains exactly 4n integer entries, with no input aliases or shared state; copies own their vectors.

    filter::AlphaBetaFilterThe constant-gain alpha-beta ("g-h") filter: a constant-velocity tracker that uses the SAME predict/correct structure as KalmanFilter, but with fixed gains alpha (position correction) and beta (velocity correction) instead of a covariance-driven Kalman gain – it is exactly the steady-state behavior a 1D constant-velocity KalmanFilter converges to once its covariance stops changing, with the covariance bookkeeping stripped out entirely. Far cheaper per step (no matrices at all) at the cost of not adapting its gain to changing noise conditions the way a real Kalman filter does.
    filter::AlphaBetaGammaFilterThe constant-gain alpha-beta-gamma filter: AlphaBetaFilter's constant-ACCELERATION generalization (a 3-state g-h-k filter), adding a third fixed gain gamma for the acceleration correction. Same fixed-gain-vs-adaptive-Kalman-gain tradeoff as AlphaBetaFilter, one derivative order higher.

    algorithms::AssignmentDiagnosticsNumerical final-state diagnostics, not an exact optimality certificate. Long-double accumulation is converted to finite doubles. Negative minimum slack or nonzero tightness/gap can reflect rounding or an invalid candidate. No acceptance tolerance is imposed; the caller chooses a scale-aware policy.
    algorithms::AssignmentEventOwned actual state at one reprice or completed augmentation boundary. All vectors have n entries and omit the private virtual column. Reprice's matching precedes path flips, while Augment's matching includes them. Reached flags mark columns already expanded, so next_column is not marked at Reprice. Unmatched columns use kAssignmentUnmatched; no reference to the input is kept.
    algorithms::AssignmentOptionsOptional complete-input and online history admission policies. Zero disables the respective optional cap. Each event costs 1+4*n logical entries (one event plus n entries in each of four owned vectors). The cap excludes input copy, final result/potentials/work, vector capacity, scalar metadata and ordinary/transient solver arrays; it is not peak bytes/RAM. Untraced solves ignore the history cap. No partial history is returned on error.
    algorithms::AssignmentResultMinimum-cost row-to-column permutation and computed total. Owns its values, with the legacy field order and types preserved. Default is an empty, unsolved value; successful solvers require a nonempty square input.
    algorithms::AssignmentRunFinal permutation, computed potentials and selected producing work. Potentials provide numerical diagnostics: exact arithmetic theory certifies optimality, while floating feasibility/tightness must be checked at a suitable scale. Negative inputs need not be feasible against unintroduced rows during execution; completed rows are handled by the active-prefix invariant.
    algorithms::AssignmentTraceOwned original costs and actual state history from one solve. History is generated inside the ordinary kernel, never by replaying a solved assignment. Capture costs O(events*n) time/storage in addition to the solver.
    algorithms::AssignmentWorkSelected actual operation counts from the shared producing kernel. Counts omit input validation, allocations, copies, comparisons, result sum and trace observation. They describe operations, not elapsed time or proof of exact floating-point optimality. Overflow in counters throws rather than wraps.

    optim::AugmentedLagrangianAugmentedLagrangian on the EqualityConstrainedFunction callback interface. Uses fixed inner gradient steps on f+lambda*c+rho*||c||^2/2, capped so each displacement norm is at most one. Updates multipliers after each inner budget and doubles rho until feasibility tolerance or outer budget. No dual-stationarity test is exposed. Objective return alone is not a KKT certificate.     B

    algorithms::BackoffScheduleOwned actual steps and cumulative idle waits, excluding request durations. steps and retry_times have equal length N; retry_times[i] is the ordinary floating sum of delays through i, starting at zero. They are idle-wait offsets, not wall-clock deadlines or a simulation of request success/latency. Zero waits can give equal offsets. Addition rejects delay>DBL_MAX-current before summing; thus no cumulative infinity escapes, though ordinary rounding still applies. total_delay is the final offset, or zero when empty. Intrinsic output owns O(N) records/values; no optional replay/history quota is imposed. Caller data is copied as scalars and independent results share no mutable RNG state.
    algorithms::BackoffStepOne actual checked retry window, applied unit variate and finite delay. Attempt k is the zero-based wait before retry k+1. Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. u is finite in [0,1], including the legacy endpoint one. delay=u*window is finite in [0,window]; underflow/rounding can erase tiny waits or round them to a window endpoint. capped/scaled describe the actual scalar branch, not instruction counts. No sleeping, networking, random draws or optional history is involved.
    algorithms::BakeryCheckResult of exhaustively exploring the bakery protocol's interleavings.
    algorithms::BakeryLockLamport's bakery lock for a fixed number of threads, built from sequentially consistent atomic loads and stores only (no read-modify-write instructions).

    nn::BarImageBatchOwned balanced alternating bar images, true masks, metadata and reproducible row order. Shapes use NHWC. Row 2i is horizontal/class zero and row 2i+1 is vertical/class one. Masks identify the noiseless object, not a threshold on the noisy image. shuffled_rows is a permutation drawn after generation from the same local engine; splitting this order does not alter the original image identities. All values own storage; changing an image does not change its independent mask.
    nn::BarImageOptionsFinite square-image bar geometry and independent clipped pixel noise. Horizontal bars span every column; vertical bars span every row. Position is the first occupied row/column. Both classes share the inclusive position range; max_position=-1 selects side-thickness. Noise is added before clipping to [0,1]. Float32/Float64 output is supported. This is a controlled synthetic task, not a natural-image dataset or a claim about translation-invariant predictions.
    nn::BarlowTwinsResultDifferentiable Barlow Twins loss and cross-view diagnostics.

    BasicMatOwned floating-point matrix backed by canonical DenseMatrix or SparseCSR storage. Initialisers are rows and must be rectangular. Empty rows and zero dimensions are valid. Dense reads are constant time; sparse reads use a row binary search. set() is constant time for dense storage and linear in rows plus stored entries for sparse storage. Expressions borrow lvalue matrices, so those matrices must outlive evaluation. They own temporary matrices and copy expression nodes (including any matrices those nodes own). Mutations before eval()/printing are visible; construction/assignment to Mat or SpMat takes a snapshot, safely handling aliased operands. Nonfinite entries are stored; dense products follow IEEE arithmetic, while sparse products skip structural zeros. Solving rejects nonfinite coefficient/right-hand-side entries. Concurrent reads/evaluations are safe only while all borrowed operands remain unmodified.
    algorithms::BasicPathResultOwned selected vertex path, historical visit counter and success flag. Field order/types preserve the original search_more.hpp layout. Interpret expanded by producer: brute_force_search counts entered simple-path prefixes, including goal and bound-pruned visits; depth_first_search counts first vertex entries; iterative_deepening_dfs accumulates path-prefix entries across depth limits, including goals and cutoffs. Thus expanded is not generally a count of unique vertices or scanned adjacency lists. No input storage is borrowed.

    algorithms::BezierSubdivisionOwned degree-preserving left/right Bezier control nets from one triangle. At split s in [0,1], left(u)=original(s*u) and right(u)=original(s+(1-s)*u) in exact arithmetic. Both nets have the original control count and share a copied meeting point; no views remain. At s=0 the left net is constant; at s=1 the right is constant. Degree-zero input gives one identical point in each net. No tessellation or tolerance- based adaptive stopping is performed. Floating identities hold approximately.

    nn::models::BigGanMomentsOwn six captured channel moment vectors from the selected BigGAN batch-statistics generator.
    nn::models::BigGanOutputOwn both generator paths, source diagnostics, explicit losses and batch moment captures.
    nn::models::BilinearResultOwn both stream maps,outer-product matrix,unit descriptor and class logits.
    vector_expr::BinaryDeferred binary operation retaining recycling at each expression node.
    causal::BinaryATEPoint estimates and overlap diagnostics for a binary-treatment analysis.
    nn::models::BinaryBarDataOwn the reproducible noisy single-bar fixture on a2x4 grid.
    algorithms::BinaryGcdStepOne binary-GCD subtraction after removing twos and ordering the odd operands. Values are exact unsigned integers. The next state is (smaller_odd,difference).
    algorithms::BinaryGcdTraceOwned result and chronological subtraction states from the canonical binary-GCD loop. Zero-input cases return no steps, zero common_twos and zero initial_odd_a. Otherwise gcd equals the final smaller_odd shifted left by common_twos.
    dstruct::BinaryHeap
    nn::models::BinaryPixelDataOwn resized gray values and their thresholded binary image batch.
    algorithms::BinarySearchProbeOne midpoint inspection of a closed binary-search interval. Values are snapshots before either bound is updated. No input pointer is retained.
    algorithms::BinarySearchTraceOwned search answer and the chronological snapshots from the same binary-search loop. Empty inputs have an empty probe list. result.probes equals probes.size().
    dstruct::BinarySearchTree
    algorithms::BinSplitNodeOne owned node of the balanced exponential-series product tree. For q(0)=1 and q(k)=k otherwise, den is the product of q(k) over [begin,end). num/den equals the sum over k in that interval of 1/product(q(j),j=begin..k). This is a normalised subtree, not generally the original sum of 1/k! there. Children are indices into the owning trace's postorder node vector; leaves use -1.
    algorithms::BinSplitResultExact, possibly unreduced exponential-series fraction and its double conversion. num and den are owned unsigned integers; value rounds the ratio after converting both integers to double. Equality to a rounded exp(1) is not exact equality to e.
    algorithms::BinSplitTraceExact result and owned postorder tree from the canonical binary-splitting routine. The last node is the root. N effective terms give N leaves and 2N-1 nodes. No pointers into inputs or shared mutable state survive the call.
    algorithms::BipartiteMatchingResultOwned maximum-cardinality matching in both orientations, with preserved field order. Unmatched entries use kBipartiteUnmatched. A matching is not generally unique; left roots and supplied adjacency order determine deterministic choices.
    algorithms::BirkhoffConstraintOne condition p^(order)(node)=value for ascending polynomial coefficients. Derivative orders at a node may have gaps. Orders above the proposed degree produce zero matrix rows and cannot establish uniqueness.
    algorithms::BisectionOptionsIndependent stopping controls for a recorded bisection search. Position tolerance has x's units; residual tolerance has f(x)'s units. A zero residual tolerance disables that test, while callback zeros still stop.
    algorithms::BisectionStepPre-update bracket, callback values and midpoint from one bisection iteration. Records numerical values without retaining the callback. Endpoint signs are opposite when this record is created. Radius is rounded max(midpoint-lower, upper-midpoint), accounting for midpoint rounding to a noncentral double.
    algorithms::BisectionTraceOwned bisection result, stopping reason and chronological bracket snapshots. Terminal endpoints describe the bracket before the returned estimate's test; a zero endpoint collapses it. Radius is meaningful for evaluated estimates, and remains infinity for a same-sign rejected bracket. It is a rounded interval distance, not an independently certified floating-point interval bound.
    algorithms::BitapMatchOne fixed-length matching window with its actual Hamming distance. Indices are byte offsets in a half-open interval [begin,end). Empty-pattern matches have begin=end. Records own their numbers and retain no input pointers.
    algorithms::BitapStepCanonical post-update Shift-And state after one consumed text byte. In states[d], bit j represents a pattern prefix of length j+1 matching the suffix ending at position with at most d substitutions. One means active; all recorded levels use the same convention. Only pattern-length bits are kept.
    algorithms::BitapTraceOwned overlapping matches, chronological prefix states and exact scan-work counts. Empty patterns match every boundary but consume no bytes and record no steps. State storage is O(n*(k+1)); match storage is O(number of reported windows).
    dstruct::BitArray
    dstruct::Bitboard
    dstruct::BitField
    dstruct::Bitmap
    algorithms::BitonicComparatorA fixed compare/exchange connection between two network wires. first<second. Ascending sends the smaller value to first; descending sends it to second. Stages are zero-based dependency layers with disjoint wire pairs.
    algorithms::BitonicNetworkOwned, value-independent topology generated by the canonical bitonic visitor. Comparators are grouped in nondecreasing stage order. Empty/singleton inputs need no comparators or stages. Construction stores O(n log^2(n+1)) entries.
    algorithms::BitonicStepActual values and swap decision at one canonical integer comparator. The trace follows sequential recursive execution; stage numbers can decrease between independent subproblems. Topology is fixed even when swaps differ.
    algorithms::BitonicTraceOwned input/output and chronological integer compare/exchange events. The unrecorded sorter does not allocate these records. Recording uses O(n log^2(n+1)) storage plus the owned input/output vectors.
    algorithms::BkmDomainSupported unreduced input intervals for the 53-term real greedy variant. Logarithms accept [1,max_argument]; exponentials accept [0,max_exponent]. Limits are the actual double product/sum of all available factors, not rounded decimal estimates. Values are owned, immutable with respect to library state.
    algorithms::BkmStepOne attempted real greedy factor and the resulting accepted state. Both candidate fields are computed from the preceding state. A rejected step keeps product/log_sum unchanged; a true accepted flag includes equality.
    algorithms::BkmTraceOwned result and attempted factors from the same loop as the scalar API. Initial state is product=1, log_sum=0. There is one event per requested term, even after reaching a floating-point plateau. No shared state is modified.
    algorithms::BlastExtensionStepOne actually inspected byte pair outside an exact seed. Each direction starts running/best scores at zero. Best is updated strictly; equality keeps the shorter extension. A drop stops only when best-running>xdrop.
    algorithms::BlastExtensionTraceOwned seed, best anchored segment and actual extension events. The HSP contains the seed even if a caller's search threshold would suppress it. Events include discarded negative tails; HSP endpoints use the best prefix in each direction. No input is modified or retained by reference.
    algorithms::BlastSeedA pair of equal fixed-length byte words, described by their starting positions. Word length belongs to the enclosing operation. Positions are nonnegative; the seed API orders them by query start, then database start.
    cad::BlendOptions
    nn::models::BlockArgsDecoded mobile block architecture metadata.
    rl::environments::BlockingMazeMutable source blocking maze for Dyna-Q adaptation experiments.
    algorithms::BloomFilterOwned approximate set of uint64 keys, using packed bits and deterministic double hashing. Insert/query use exactly the same probes, so inserted keys cannot test negative while the filter remains unmodified except by insertions. Positive queries require an exact backing-set check. There is no erase, resizing or insertion count: duplicates are idempotent and the object retains no original keys. Storage is 64*ceil(m/64) payload bits plus object/allocation bookkeeping. Copies own independent state; moved-from objects support destruction/assignment only. Mutation requires external synchronisation, while concurrent const reads are safe when no thread mutates the object. Probes retain the existing uint64 mapping: (h1+i*h2) wraps modulo 2^64 before reduction modulo m. Odd h2 need not give distinct probes for arbitrary m.
    dstruct::BloomFilter
    algorithms::BlossomContractionOne actual odd-cycle contraction, expanded to original vertex identities. members includes the base's existing group and every merged group, sorted by vertex index. It is an odd set, not a cyclic vertex ordering. Nested blossoms therefore appear as larger sets; contractions reset at the next root search.
    random::BlumBlumShubEducational uint64 Blum-Blum-Shub engine with explicit modular state and bit output. Initialise x0=(seed mod N)^2 mod N, then square modulo N before emitting each low bit. The caller must supply distinct primes p,q congruent to 3 modulo 4; the constructor checks congruence, product range and seed coprimality, not primality. Known small default factors and a modulus of at most 64 bits do not provide cryptographic security. Seed 1 is allowed and gives a constant stream. Instances own their state; copies also preserve the inherited normal cache. Separate objects share no state; concurrent mutation needs external locking.
    random::BlumBlumShubOrbitOwned bounded state path, optionally closed by an actual repeated modular state. states begins at the inspected engine state. On closure it includes the closing duplicate, so states.size()=transient+period+1. Unknown closure has period and transient zero; this is a budget result, not evidence of an infinite orbit.
    random::BlumBlumShubStepOwned before/after modular state and low bit for one actual engine transition. The bit belongs to after, not before. No engine or input is borrowed by a record.
    nn::models::BoardPolicyValuePathLive source AlphaZero board-policy and bounded-value outputs.
    rl::BoardValuePolicyPredict board action values and fit outcomes from the moving player's perspective.
    cad::Body
    sim::BodyOwned rigid-body creation and edit parameters; no dependency on a renderer. Coordinates use SI units. Validation matches the implemented VSim component ranges. Quaternion input must already be unit length within 1e-6.
    cad::BodyMassTrim-aware boundary mass properties per unit density, including imported B-reps. Values come from oriented tetrahedra under the tessellated boundary, rather than full untrimmed surface domains. Curved-face accuracy depends on chord tolerance. Inspect closed status before trusting a manufacturing solid.
    cad::BooleanOptions
    cad::BooleanReport
    algorithms::BoothResultExact widened signed product and radix-2 recoding operation counts. Counts depend on multiplier bit transitions, even when the multiplicand is zero. An addition means signed digit +1, not necessarily a positive numeric contribution when the multiplicand is negative. No inputs or shared state are modified.
    algorithms::BoothStepOne actual multiplier-bit decision and its widened accumulator state. previous is zero below bit zero, then the preceding lower bit. digit equals previous-current. All 32 decisions are recorded, including zero contributions.
    algorithms::BoothTraceOwned operands, exact result/counts and the 32 canonical recoding decisions. Recording allocates O(32) entries. The ordinary function uses the same loop without allocating a trace. Data are owned; independent calls share no state.
    stats::BootstrapNonparametric resampling with replacement, as in R's boot with ordinary resampling.
    stats::BootstrapOptionsBootstrap replication count, confidence level and default-engine seed.
    stats::BootstrapResultOwned bootstrap replicates, estimated bias/standard error and confidence intervals.
    algorithms::BoruvkaChoiceOne component's cheapest outgoing edge at the start of a phase. Choices are recorded before any unions, so multiple components may choose the same edge. Acceptance is recorded separately in BoruvkaPhase.
    algorithms::BoruvkaPhaseOne actual full edge scan followed by cycle-checked unions. Labels refer to components before this phase; choices use ascending internal root order, the same order used for acceptance. A disconnected forest can end with a phase with no choices or merges. Empty and singleton graphs have no phases.
    algorithms::BoruvkaTraceOwned forest, component snapshots and logical edge-scan counters from the canonical kernel. Recording costs O(n*P) storage for P scans in addition to O(n) forest/work storage. No input or shared state is modified; edge indices refer to input order.
    algorithms::BorweinStepOne actual completed quartic update, before any early-stop decision. Iteration is one-based. All values are owned doubles from the canonical loop; unchanged refers to the stored inverse-pi value, not exact convergence to pi.
    algorithms::BorweinTraceOwned actual Borwein states and stopping information, without fabricated plateau records. The seed is separate from the update vector. Negative requested iteration counts are clamped to zero, matching the historical scalar/sequence API. A recorded unchanged update is included, then the kernel stops. Scalar calls use the same kernel without allocating records; sequences pad repeated final estimates to retain their historical requested length.
    fem::BoundaryCondition1DOwned endpoint data for Dirichlet, outward-conormal Neumann or Robin conditions. Dirichlet uses value as u; Neumann uses it as p*du/dn; Robin uses it as the reference value in p*du/dn+alpha*(u-value)=0. Alpha zero gives zero conormal. For coercive diffusion/heat models use nonnegative Robin alpha and sufficient constraints/reaction to remove the constant nullspace. Unsupported enum values and nonfinite data are outside the solver's preconditions, not fully validated.
    geometry::BoundingBox
    gis::BoundingBox
    geometry::BoundingRectangleCandidateActual projected extents and area of one tested hull orientation. Projections are relative to hull[edge]; direction is its unit outgoing edge.
    cad::Box3d
    nn::models::BoxQualityOwn IoU, distance-IoU, complete-IoU and detached aspect coefficient tensors.
    algorithms::BoyerMooreAlignmentOne actual right-to-left scan and the shift that follows it. Full matches use mismatch_index=pattern length, text_byte=0 and bad_character_shift=0; inspect matched to distinguish that sentinel from an actual NUL mismatch byte.
    algorithms::BoyerMooreTablesOwned rightmost-byte and strong good-suffix tables for one pattern. Obtain populated values from boyer_moore_tables(); default field values are placeholders. Tables borrow no pattern storage and can be inspected concurrently.
    algorithms::BoyerMooreTraceOwned tables, all matches, actual alignments and search-comparison count. No text or pattern bytes are copied into the trace. Sizes and positions are byte counts; preprocessing comparisons are excluded. Empty/oversized patterns produce no alignments, but the trace still contains their preprocessed tables.
    nn::data::text::BpeSmall-corpus frequency-weighted byte-pair encoder over Unicode scalar strings.
    algorithms::BranchingArcOwned actual working arc with wide reduced weight and stable original identity. All input arcs remain in input order through every contraction, even when mapped to irrelevant self loops. weight is an actual long-double working cost, not necessarily representable as double or equal to the original cost.
    algorithms::BranchingOptionsWhole-call phase and named edge-visit limits for the iterative construction. Zero means unlimited. Every input edge validates before either cap applies. Edge visits count incoming-choice scans and contraction reweighting, including ignored self loops and root-entering arcs. Recovery/map copies are not edge visits. Failure throws with no partial tree/trace. These are work limits, not complete memory limits; a phase cap also limits retained expansion levels.
    algorithms::BranchingPhaseOwned actual incoming choices, cycle partition and costs of one round. Root choice uses the sentinel and weight zero; missing choices use the sentinel and positive infinity. missing_vertices is nonempty only on failure, before any baseline addition or cycle search. cycles lists vertices in predecessor-following order, opposite to the directed edge traversal order. On contraction, cycle components come first in discovery order, then singleton components in vertex order. component is empty on acyclic/failed rounds. original_to_vertex maps every original vertex into this round's graph.
    algorithms::BranchingTraceOwned actual contraction rounds, recovered original tree and operation counts. One executing kernel serves legacy, tree and trace calls without replay. reduced_total retains the actual sum of round baselines, including a prefix on failure. The returned cost instead sums the recovered original edges in original destination order; floating roundoff can distinguish those totals. A missing incoming choice proves nonexistence, including after a closed cycle is contracted. Failure returns no partial tree, but retains the actual rounds. All storage is independent of caller inputs and other calls.
    algorithms::BranchingWorkActual named validation, scan, cycle and expansion counts. Counters describe executed work, not seconds or a bit-complexity model. Saved vertex entries count compact incoming-choice and original-map copies for contraction recovery; full trace snapshots and final output are excluded.
    algorithms::BreadthFirstStepOne actual dequeue and the discoveries made while expanding it. The goal dequeue is included but its adjacency is not scanned. Discovered vertices are recorded in input adjacency order and are marked before enqueueing.
    algorithms::BreadthFirstTraceOwned BFS result, discovered distances/predecessors and chronological queue events. Distance sentinel n means undiscovered at stopping time, not necessarily unreachable when the goal ended the search early. Predecessor sentinel n is used for start and undiscovered vertices. Discovered vertices may still be queued after the goal is removed, including vertices one layer deeper. A full breadth_first_traversal() has goal_requested=false, empty result.path and result.found=false; result.order then exhausts all reachable vertices.
    algorithms::BrentCycleStepOne actual Brent state after movement, phase entry or checkpoint reset. A checkpoint copies runner to reference without calling f; their equality at that row is not a detected collision, since movement precedes the next test. Indices identify positions in the original orbit, independent of equal state labels.
    algorithms::BrentCycleTraceOwned actual Brent states and summary from the same kernel as ordinary detection. Records add O(mu+lambda) storage; they do not cache the function's state space or trigger extra transition calls. Callback storage is borrowed only during the call.
    algorithms::BresenhamStepOne actual current point/error and the coordinate moves selected after it. Both tests use the saved doubled_error, even when the x move changes error. The final endpoint has terminal=true and no outgoing move flags. All fields are owned values; the point is the centre selected by the canonical loop.
    algorithms::BresenhamTraceOwned raster points and actual integer decisions from the ordinary loop. dx/dy are nonnegative coordinate extents. Move counters exclude the terminal record; a diagonal move increments both axis counters and diagonal_moves. Recording uses O(max(dx,dy)+1) storage beyond the returned points.
    algorithms::BronKerboschNodeOne owned actual recursion-entry frame of pivoted Bron-Kerbosch. r is the current clique in search insertion order. Disjoint p/x contain vertices adjacent to every member of r: p may still branch, x was processed earlier at this frame's ancestors/siblings. They are not lists of already reported vertices. Each frame is captured before its own branch loop mutates p/x. Returned clique members are sorted separately, without changing records.
    algorithms::BronKerboschTraceOwned maximal cliques, actual frames, histogram and logical search counters. Clique members are sorted; outer order is deterministic depth-first discovery order, preserving the historical implementation. The empty zero-vertex graph emits one empty clique. Counts describe this library's vector/matrix search, not wall time or a general optimal-time guarantee. Nodes add O((n+1)*C) retained vertex storage for C calls; ordinary enumeration allocates no diagnostic records.
    algorithms::BruteForceStepOne actual entered simple-path prefix and its local decision/probe counts. Entry fields describe the incumbent before and after this visit's own goal decision; descendant improvements do not rewrite those historical values. Local edge/cycle counts accumulate while the visit remains active. Records are in DFS preorder, and parent ids identify the actual prefix search tree.
    algorithms::BruteForceTraceOwned shortest-path result and actual DFS incumbent-bound diagnostics. Only vertices on the current path are marked, so the search can revisit a vertex along another prefix. Duplicate input arcs can repeat subtrees. Ordinary and traced calls share one explicit-stack kernel and preserve legacy tie order. Retaining full prefixes costs their total length; omitting copies retains O(V) records for V visits, in addition to the graph, live stack and final result.
    algorithms::BruteForceTraceOptionsOptional complete-search visit budget and retained-path choice for diagnostics. Zero max_visits is unlimited. A positive budget throws before entering an excess prefix; no partial optimum is returned. It does not avoid adjacency allocation. record_paths=false omits per-visit path copies while retaining visit ids, parents, vertices, depths, decisions and counters.
    algorithms::BrzozowskiOptionsSeparate optional output-state caps for the two determinisation stages. Zero is unlimited. Each positive cap is enforced before creating an excess subset; exceeding either throws without returning a partial minimisation. Caps count states, not bytes; source validation and large union temporaries can still cost substantial time/storage.
    algorithms::BrzozowskiTraceOwned actual double-reversal stages, with final minimal DFA in second.dfa. first.subsets contains original input-state ids; second.subsets contains first.dfa state ids. Reversed NFAs are the actual sources passed to each construction. Reachable input labels exclude the implicit sink. The first DFA is reachable but need not be minimal if the original has unreachable explicit states. The second DFA is reachable, complete and language-minimal. All snapshots own their storage and can be exponentially large.
    algorithms::BSGSOwned base and strong-generating-chain transversals for a finite permutation group.
    algorithms::BsgsTraceA baby-step giant-step run with its operation counts and, optionally, the visited values.
    BsplineB-spline design factory, analogous to R's splines::bs(). Owns a clamped basis on fixed boundaries, reused for training and prediction. By default the first basis column is omitted, so a formula's intercept does not duplicate the partition of unity. No fitting or smoothing is performed. Const evaluations are independent and safe to run concurrently.
    fda::BSplineTensor-product B-spline basis. A one-dimensional BSpline is a convenient wrapper around BSplineBasis; with two or more bases it evaluates smooth surfaces and higher-dimensional functions. Design matrices are sparse: each row has at most product(degree_i + 1) non-zero entries.
    fda::BSplineBasis
    fda::BSplineRefinementA refined B-spline basis together with the operator that maps coarse coefficients onto it.
    BSplineRegressionA least-squares B-spline regression curve y ≈ Σ_j β_j B_j(x). dm::BSR for short.
    algorithms::BucketSortBucketOwned scatter order, sorted contents and actual work for one bucket. Equal integers retain insertion order; no satellite payload API is exposed. Comparisons count evaluations of predecessor>key, shifts count successful predecessor moves, and placements count final key stores (one per insertion after the first item). Loop-bound tests, scattering and gathering are excluded.
    algorithms::BucketSortTraceOwned snapshots and checked counters from one canonical bucket-sort run. Empty, singleton and all-equal inputs take the historical early exit, with shortcut=true, no allocated buckets/assignments and zero insertion counters. Otherwise bucket_count=input.size(), buckets includes empty buckets, and bucket_of_input records actual scatter destinations. Snapshots use O(n) extra storage; counters throw on size_t overflow rather than wrap. All values are owned; calls share no mutable state. Occupancy alone is an upper-bound predictor: actual shifts also depend on order within each bucket.
    algorithms::BucketSortWorkloadsPaired synthetic samples for comparing bucket occupancy and actual work. Both vectors contain count integers in [0,999]. Uniform values use an integer uniform draw; clustered values use a normal draw with mean 500 and deviation 4, truncated toward zero and clamped. For count>=2 the first two clustered values are replaced by 0 and 999 to stretch the observed range. A local mt19937 engine consumes alternating uniform/normal draws. A seed repeats on a given standard library; distribution mappings are not promised identical across toolchains.
    algorithms::BuddyAllocationTraceActual order search, splits and returned offset from one allocation call. offset=-1 means failure with unchanged state; a positive oversized request has no eligible order and examines zero free lists. Other failures examine every order from desired_order through the arena's maximum. Successful calls record only actual splits, in decreasing parent order. O(H) trace storage, no snapshots.
    algorithms::BuddyAllocatorModel a binary buddy arena using offsets, ordered free sets and live maps. Does not allocate arena payload bytes or return pointers. Both dimensions must be positive powers of two, with minimum<=total. Allocation chooses the smallest adequate nonempty order, then its lowest offset, retaining the left child when splitting. Free coalesces only true same-order buddies. Unknown frees are no-ops. Positive oversize/exhausted requests return -1; nonpositive requests throw. Ordinary and traced calls share kernels. Metadata allocation failure leaves state unchanged; snapshots own their data. Copies are independent offset models. Concurrent mutations need external synchronization. For H orders and B current blocks, operations have conservative O(H log(B+1)) ordered-container cost, not a constant-cost-per-order guarantee. Metadata storage is O(H+B).
    algorithms::BuddyBlockOne current free or allocated interval in an owned arena snapshot. Offsets and sizes are bytes relative to arena zero. Free blocks have requested=0; live blocks have positive requested<=size. No memory pointer or backing bytes are owned by this record.
    algorithms::BuddyFreeTraceActual release, buddy probes and resulting coalesced block from one free call. Unknown, interior, negative and already-free offsets are no-ops: released=false, final_offset=final_order=-1, no probes. A valid offset releases the current live allocation at that offset; stale offsets cannot distinguish later offset reuse. O(H) trace storage, with no arena snapshots or operation replay.
    algorithms::BuddyProbeOne actual same-order buddy membership test during a free operation. buddy_offset=offset XOR block_size(order), using arena-relative offsets. A successful test triggers one merge; a false test stops the cascade. No test occurs once the arena's maximum order has been reached.
    algorithms::BuddySnapshotOwned, address-sorted partition and free lists from one allocator state. blocks covers [0,total_bytes) exactly once. Free blocks are maximally coalesced; adjacent blocks need not be buddies. free_offsets is indexed by order and sorted within each order. Copies remain valid after subsequent allocator changes. Construction takes O((A+F) log(A+F+1)+H) time and O(A+F+H) storage for live allocation count A, free block count F and number of orders H.
    algorithms::BuddySplitOne actual allocation split of a parent into equal-sized children. Parent interval starts at offset and has order parent_order. The retained left child starts at offset; the free right buddy starts at offset+half_size.
    compute::BufferShared allocation or bounded byte view retaining its creating context. Copies alias bytes. A view survives destruction of the original handle. Host pointers are exposed only for CPU allocations. Concurrent writes to overlapping bytes need caller synchronization. A default handle is undefined.
    nn::BuildInfoA snapshot of build and run-time facts, as returned by build_info().
    algorithms::BullyMessageOne actual logical send in deterministic kernel order. ELECTION sends visit higher ids in ascending order; a live recipient's ANSWER follows immediately. Candidate phases use FIFO activation order. Announcements are sent in ascending lower-id order after all candidate phases. phase indexes candidate processing, not physical time; announcements use the number of phases.
    algorithms::BullyResultLeader and attempted-message counts for one explicitly chosen election model. Field order/types retain the original aggregate layout. Attempts to failed destinations count as ELECTION/COORDINATOR messages; only live responders send ANSWER. These are logical sends, not bytes, timings or network rounds.
    algorithms::BullyRoundActual work and highest responder for one processed candidate. A phase sends to all higher ids and gathers their immediate logical answers. Fanout activates every previously inactive live responder once; the shortcut instead activates only the highest responder after completing this phase.
    algorithms::BullyTraceOwned actual candidate phases, logical sends and final learned leaders. fanout distinguishes the full responder model from the legacy shortcut. result and counters come from the same kernel as the corresponding ordinary function; no election is replayed. learned_leader has one entry per process: live nodes learn the winner, down nodes remain -1. An all-down/empty system has no phases or messages and no leader. Records own their storage and inputs are unchanged; calls share no mutable state. See BullyTraceOptions for storage.
    algorithms::BullyTraceOptionsMessage-recording and complete-call budget options for either trace model. max_messages=0 means unlimited; a positive cap counts every attempted logical send, including undelivered ones, and throws before the next send would exceed the cap. No partial trace or leader is returned. record_messages=false omits the O(M) message vector while retaining actual O(n) phase/learned-state records and all counters. Input flags are borrowed only during the call.
    algorithms::BurstSortBurstOne actual overflow and redistribution into a newly created child. At creation, strings=bucket_capacity+1; later subtree sizes may be larger. trigger_input_index is the item being processed, including during redistribution from an earlier burst. No string values or full prefixes are copied into events.
    algorithms::BurstSortNodeOne actual trie node, identified by its index in BurstSortTrace::nodes. Root zero has parent=depth=0 and no incoming byte. Every other parent precedes its child in creation order. Strings ending here precede all byte slots; their original input indices retain encounter order. Compact parent links avoid storing every full prefix, which could otherwise take quadratic space.
    algorithms::BurstSortOptionsPositive leaf capacity and optional whole-call trie-node limit. A bucket bursts only when its size becomes greater than bucket_capacity. max_nodes=0 means unlimited; a positive cap includes the root and throws before an additional node would exceed it. Empty/singleton inputs build no trie.
    algorithms::BurstSortSlotOne occupied byte slot observed during actual ordered collection. child=0 means a leaf bucket; a positive child names a real trie node (root is never a child). Child slots own no bucket records. Leaf snapshots preserve actual encounter order and actual sorted order; full string comparisons use unsigned byte ordering, with original input id as the equality tie break. Slots appear in collection preorder, with ascending byte slots within a node.
    algorithms::BurstSortTraceOwned sorted strings, stable original ids, actual bursts and final trie metadata. Equal strings keep original-id order. Empty/singleton inputs take the historical shortcut: nodes/slots/bursts are empty and all work counters are zero. Otherwise snapshots come from the shared insertion/collection kernel, never a replay or a first-byte reconstruction. Parent links represent deep prefixes without quadratic prefix copies. Actual counters throw on size_t overflow. Calls share no mutable state.
    algorithms::BWTForwardOptionsOptional complete-call byte-comparison limit for forward tracing. Zero means unlimited. A positive budget counts actual byte-pair tests inside rotation comparisons and throws before exceeding it; no partial transform is returned. This bounds the deliberately naive sort's inspected-byte work.
    algorithms::BWTForwardTraceOwned input, actual sorted rotation starts and actual comparison counters. No rotation matrix or comparator history is materialized. start offsets break full-rotation ties. Counters reflect this toolchain's std::sort calls and are not portable fixed formulas; overflow throws rather than wrapping. O(n) storage in addition to the input/result, with worst-case O(n^2 log(n+1)) forward work.
    algorithms::BWTInverseStepOne actual LF inversion step and its right-to-left output write. Repeated rows are allowed: a periodic input can revisit a row before n steps have been taken. Exactly n bytes are written, independent of LF cycle length.
    algorithms::BWTInverseTraceOwned encoded input, LF provenance, decoded bytes and actual inversion steps. Ordinary inversion shares the kernel but does not allocate step/rank/first-column records or copy the encoded input. Tracing uses O(n+256) storage and time, and never replays the inversion to fabricate a path. Calls share no mutable state.
    algorithms::BWTLFMappingOwned stable last-to-first correspondence for any byte last column. counts[c] is the frequency of byte c; starts[c] counts bytes strictly below c. occurrence_rank[i] counts earlier equal bytes in L, so lf[i]=starts[L[i]]+rank[i] and first_column[lf[i]]=L[i]. lf is always a permutation, but that alone does not certify that an arbitrary last-column/primary-index pair is a valid cyclic BWT. O(n+256) construction time/storage; arrays use size_t, not narrowing int counts.
    algorithms::BWTResultLast column and primary row of the sorted cyclic-rotation matrix. No sentinel is appended; every byte, including zero and 128..255, is data. Unsigned-byte lexicographic order is used. Equal rotations are ordered by start offset, so the primary row is the first row equal to the input. Field order and types retain the original aggregate layout; default construction is safely empty.
    nn::BYOLResultOwn normalized BYOL representations and squared alignment losses.
    algorithms::ByteEditOne checked edit at a position in the current evolving byte string. before/after own literal payloads: insert 0/1 bytes, erase 1/0, substitute 1/1 different bytes, transpose 2/2 reversed bytes, match 1/1 equal bytes. Native shortest scripts omit matches, so their vector length equals cost. No references into the trace or source survive. Positions are current-state offsets, not original source offsets.

    C

    nn::models::C3dConfigConfigure all eight C3D convolutions,five pools and two dense layers.
    nn::models::C3dOutputOwn every C3D endpoint and its differentiation graph.
    algorithms::C45CandidateOne actually evaluated continuous threshold, with entropy in bits. Candidates appear in node preorder, then increasing feature and distinct-value boundary order. Threshold is a finite separating midpoint, falling back to the lower value if rounding reaches the upper value. selected marks the first strict positive maximum ratio at this node. The records belong to their owning trace.
    algorithms::C45NodeTraceActual selected rows, depth, entropy and stopping reason of one node. Vector position equals the corresponding DecisionTree node id. rows preserves original input order, with owned indices; labels and feature values are not copied. candidate_begin/count delimit this node's records in C45Trace::candidates.
    algorithms::C45OptionsGrowth controls for the restricted continuous gain-ratio learner. Root depth is zero. A zero depth cap is unlimited; min_samples is a node-size stopping rule, not a minimum child size. Zero/one both allow any impure node. max_candidates bounds the whole call before an excess candidate is partitioned; zero means unlimited. No partial model is returned on any exception.
    algorithms::C45TraceOwned continuous model and actual training provenance from a shared kernel. No training is replayed. Ordinary c45_train() omits row/candidate records. Input values/labels are borrowed only during the call and are never mutated. Empty aligned inputs give empty vectors. Trace storage includes O(n*h) row indices and one record per evaluated candidate, h the largest reached depth.
    nn::CachedSpectralKernelOwn a live normalized kernel and its signed bilinear denominator estimate.
    nn::models::CachedTransformerLMOwn initialized source decoder parameters and validate explicit caller K/V appends.
    cad::CadDocument
    geometry::CaliperEventOne actual support-pointer decision or farthest-pair test.
    CallbackBase class for user-defined callbacks invoked by datamunge functions.
    cad::CameraA camera value independent of a window or graphics device. Camera units match the scene; up need not be normalized. A valid camera has distinct position/target and an up direction not parallel to its view.
    game::CameraPerspective camera with right-handed local -Z view and zero-to-one depth.
    nn::models::CamOutputOwn Grad-CAM and explicit locally-affine exp-score Grad-CAM++intermediates.
    algorithms::CannonRoundOne actual round's source-block ownership and accumulated global output. Arrays a_sources/b_sources have q*q row-major cells. Each entry identifies the original input block by row*q+column, not a scalar offset. partial has n*n row-major values after this round's block products, before the next shifts. Values/indices are owned and independent of inputs and later rounds.
    algorithms::CannonTraceOwned product, actual carried source ids, snapshots and loop work counters. The shared ordinary/traced kernel records without replaying multiplication or deriving source ids from a closed-form round formula. Source ids travel through the same source-cell selection as numeric shift buffers. Inputs are borrowed only during the call and never mutated; input values are not copied into this result. With q rounds, snapshots use O(q*(n*n+q*q)) storage. Empty input has no rounds.
    algorithms::CannonWorkCounts of scalar arithmetic and buffer assignments in this Cannon implementation. A multiply-add counts one multiply-and-accumulate expression, not two measured machine instructions. Copies count double assignments, including the final closing shift and self-copies when the mesh has one cell. These are not network messages, bytes, timings, allocations or hardware performance counters.
    algorithms::CanopyOwned canopy centre index and loose-radius member indices. Members generated by canopy_clustering() are unique, ascending original indices. Overlap is permitted. Removing a point from seed eligibility does not remove it from subsequent membership searches. The default centre is zero, without points.
    algorithms::CanopyCoverageOwned inverted memberships and unique unordered candidate pairs. point_canopies[i] contains ascending canopy ids that include point i. shared_pairs is lexicographically sorted with each first id smaller than its second id. pair_visits counts all within-canopy pairs before deduplication, so it may exceed shared_pairs.size(). These describe candidate retention, not a clustering accuracy or speed guarantee. Copies are independent and own all indices.
    algorithms::CanopyStepActual seed-pool transition for one complete canopy construction. Vector position is the corresponding canopy id. newly_removed is ascending and includes the selected seed, so every step consumes at least one point even at t2=0. Visit offsets delimit this step's full original-index-order distance scan.
    algorithms::CanopyTraceOwned result and actual Euclidean canopy construction provenance. Inputs are not retained. Each of m seeds scans all n original points, including previously consumed seeds: distance_evaluations=n*m, coordinate_differences=n*m*d. Ordinary canopy_clustering() omits visits/steps. A trace needs O(n*m) additional storage, with no replay or shared mutable state. Empty points give empty records.
    algorithms::CanopyVisitOne actual seed-to-point distance evaluation and its resulting decisions. already_removed describes eligibility before this canopy started, not membership. newly_removed includes the selected seed itself even when tight radius is zero. Flags are from the shared kernel; they are not reconstructed from final canopies.
    algorithms::CantorZassenhausOptionsSeed and complete-call work caps for odd-field squarefree factorization. Zero caps mean unlimited. Trials include constant candidates; modular products count multiply-then-reduce calls in polynomial powering/character construction, including DDF. Caps throw before excess work and never return a partial factor list. They do not bound coefficient operations, primality validation, gcd/division or time.
    algorithms::CantorZassenhausTraceOwned input normalization, factors and actual DDF/EDF provenance without replay. input is normalized but retains its leading coefficient. monic_input is the divided-by-leading-coefficient polynomial. Product(factors)=monic_input; multiply by leading_coefficient to recover input. residual is the final DDF remainder; if nonconstant it is emitted directly as the last irreducible factor. Constants have no factors and residual=[1]. Invalid/zero/repeated-factor inputs throw.
    algorithms::CantorZassenhausWorkActual high-level work counts from the shared factorization kernel. Counts do not measure scalar field operations or wall time. Gcd calls include squarefree validation, DDF and EDF; modular products count only multiply/reduce requests in powering/character computation. Ordinary calls keep these counters internally but allocate no DDF/EDF records.
    nn::models::CapsNetOutputsPrimary/digit capsules, scores and an optional true/predicted-mask decoder.
    rl::environments::CartPoleCartPole-v1-style explicit-Euler cart/pole dynamics with observations[x,xdot,theta,thetadot].
    rl::foundations::CategoricalPolicyPathLive endpoints of an explicit two-layer categorical policy graph.
    nn::models::CategoricalQPathLive categorical return-distribution endpoints.
    nn::models::CbamOutputsSequential channel and spatial attention tensor results.
    nn::models::CenterNetConfigConfigure CenterNet feature-only ResNet, learned upsampling and three prediction heads.
    nn::models::CenterNetOutputsRetain stride-four CenterNet features, heatmap logits, sizes, offsets and local peaks.
    nn::models::CenterTargetsOwn detached CenterNet Gaussian, size, offset and retained-centre targets.
    random::ChaCha20Buffered RFC 8439 ChaCha20 engine emitting little-endian 64-bit words. Uses a fixed 256-bit key, 96-bit nonce and checked 32-bit block counter. Eight next_u64() calls consume one 64-byte block; unused words remain buffered. The counter never carries into the nonce. Copies preserve raw position and the inherited normal() cache: copying duplicates a stream, not an independent key. Separate instances share no state; concurrent mutation needs external locking. Raw calls take constant amortised time/storage with no allocation. This wrapper supplies no entropy acquisition, nonce management, authentication, reseeding, backtracking resistance, key erasure or machine-code constant-time assurance. Public fixed keys are for conformance checks; a 64-bit seed is for simulation.
    random::ChaCha20DrawOwned location, capacity and value of one actual ChaCha20 raw draw. The location describes the consumed word, not the next draw. No key or nonce is copied into a record; values are still raw keystream and may be sensitive.
    algorithms::ChaChaBlockTraceOwned actual state setup, 80 quarter rounds, 20 round states and serialization. Trace factories populate the record in the same kernel used by ordinary blocks; no round is replayed. initial contains the key, and later fields contain key-derived state/keystream. Use public test material for exposed diagnostics; records do not erase their memory. Default construction alone does not execute a block.
    algorithms::ChaChaEncryptTraceOwned one-shot output and actual block/counter/offset/keystream records. Contains sensitive keystream and output material; no erasure/authentication is performed. Source input/key/nonce are borrowed only during the call. O(n+64*b) storage for n bytes and b=ceil(n/64) blocks; empty input has no block records.
    algorithms::ChaChaQuarterStepOne actual quarter-round application inside a full block. before/after use the indices order; round zero is the first column round. Owned values and indices remain independent of the live working state.
    algorithms::ChaChaQuarterTraceOwned four-word input, four actual compound ARX stages and final quarter round. Each stage follows an add/xor/rotate group, with rotation amounts 16,12,8,7. Arithmetic is modulo 2^32. No replay or shared state; this record may contain key-derived material. It performs no memory erasure or security certification.
    algorithms::ChaChaXorBlockOne actual block used by one-shot XOR, retaining the full keystream. bytes may be less than 64 for the final block; unused tail bytes are retained here but discarded by the one-shot stream position. No source-data reference is held.
    algorithms::ChakravalaChoiceActual congruence class, bracketing candidates and minimum-norm multiplier. Admissible positive m satisfy m=residue mod modulus, with modulus=abs(k). below is the largest such m<=floor(sqrt(N)), or zero when none exists; above is the smallest such m>floor(sqrt(N)). Errors are abs(m*m-N), computed exactly in unsigned 128-bit arithmetic. A missing below has error zero but is never eligible. Equal errors select the smaller positive m.
    algorithms::ChakravalaStateOwned auxiliary triple satisfying a*a-N*b*b=k in an executed cyclic solve. The kernel keeps positive a,b and a signed nonzero k for nonsquare N. Default construction is only a record, with no invariant validation.
    algorithms::ChakravalaStepOwned before, multiplier decision and after records from one actual cyclic update. The ordinary and traced solver share arithmetic. Records are captured during execution; neither multiplier choices nor coordinate updates are replayed.
    algorithms::ChakravalaTraceOwned initial triple, chronological cyclic steps and final Pell solution. Square inputs have initial={floor(sqrt(N)),1,0}, no steps and found=false. Nonsquares begin at the legacy floor-root triple and stop at k=+1, without the historical shortcuts for norms -1, +/-2 or +/-4. Their path therefore differs from variants starting at the nearest square or stopping at |k|=1.
    geometry::ChanOptionsOptions for chans_algorithm_trace.
    geometry::ChanResultHull plus the per-round trace of Chan's algorithm.
    geometry::ChanRoundOne round of Chan's algorithm with guess \(m\).
    nn::models::CharacterConfigConfigure the six-convolution raw-character classifier and fixed onehot depth.
    nn::models::CharacterOutputOwn raw-character onehot ingress,nine temporal activations and binary logits.
    nn::models::CharacterSplitsOwn genuine raw-character source partitions and compact six-convolution configuration.
    nn::CheckpointOptionsOptions for checkpoint.
    algorithms::CheneyCopyOwned symbolic evacuated heap with rewritten slots and packed integral size offsets. heap ids are new slots; its roots and fields are rewritten during the actual traversal, preserving duplicate fields, duplicate roots, cycles and sharing. heap.sizes contains one positive size per survivor, including default ones. offsets[new] is the prefix sum of those sizes, in caller-chosen units, without alignment/header padding. This models layout and references, not raw allocation, object payload copying, deallocation, mutator suspension or an arena swap.
    algorithms::CheneyEventOwned actual forward or scan-completion record, without replay or queue snapshots. For Root, source=-1 and field is the root-slot index. For Reference, source is the scanned old id and field its original reference-slot index. For Scan, source=target is the scanned old id, field=0, destination=scan, copied=false. scan is the current object-slot head; completed scans cover [0,scan) before the event. free_before/free_after count allocated object slots. At scan events they span that entire object's field processing; at forwards they span only that request. used_before/after measure packed units with the same convention. After Scan, [scan+1,free_after) is the pending queue. Records own all values.
    algorithms::CheneyResultOwned breadth-first old-id order and dense old-to-new slot map, retaining the legacy layout. Each reachable object occurs once, ordered by first discovery from the ordered roots and reference fields. Unreachable old ids have forwarding=-1. Slots are object indices, not byte addresses; sizes are ignored by cheney_copy().
    algorithms::CheneyTraceOwned evacuated heap plus every actual forward and scan-completion event. Uses the ordinary kernel; no discovery, forwarding or rewriting is replayed. There are R+E_live+L events on success. Input graphs are unchanged, and copied trace records can be modified independently. Trace memory is additional to the dense forwarding table and evacuated graph; it is not constant workspace.
    algorithms::CheneyWorkActual validation, forward requests, completed scans and forwarding outcomes. root_probes includes duplicate root slots; reference_probes includes every live field, including repeated/shared/cyclic edges. Each forward request is either one copy or one reuse, so root_probes+reference_probes=copies+reuses. Validation visits the entire input, including garbage fields and supplied sizes.
    algorithms::ChienGeneratorTestOne actual generator power test, retaining rejected candidates without replay. q is a distinct prime divisor of p-1; candidate passes this test iff value!=1. A primitive root must pass every distinct-factor test. Records own their values.
    algorithms::ChienOptionsWhole-call limits for Chien enumeration and generator discovery; zero means unlimited. Point/term caps are checked from the normalized degree before generator work or sweep allocation. Generator steps count trial divisors plus primitive-root power tests, checked before each such operation; scalar arithmetic within a test and repeated division by an accepted factor are not separate steps. All shortcut paths use zero field-point and generator steps. Limits bound these named operations, not primality validation, normalization or elapsed time.
    algorithms::ChienStepOwned actual coefficient-state vector and evaluation at one nonzero point. terms[j]=input[j]*point^j mod p immediately before the next update; value is their modular sum. The first record has exponent zero and point one. Recording does not re-evaluate the polynomial with Horner's method.
    algorithms::ChienTraceOwned normalized input, actual generator/recurrence records, roots and work. Zero, constant and linear shortcuts leave generator, multipliers, zero-check and recurrence records empty/default; path identifies them explicitly. For Incremental, zero is checked separately, steps covers p-1 nonzero points, and the retained final update returns final_point=1 and final_terms=input. This is a prime-field implementation, not arithmetic over GF(2^m) for m>1. All records are independent of the input and other calls; nothing is replayed.
    algorithms::ChienWorkActual named operations, including the legacy constant/closing state updates. Excludes prime testing, coefficient normalization, allocations and integer division/modulo work in factoring p-1. Each modular scalar multiplication is counted once, regardless of its bit cost; additions count all accumulator updates, including zero coefficients. Counters are checked size_t values.
    linalg::CholeskyDecompositionThe factor of \(A=LL^\top\) returned by cholesky().
    algorithms::ChristofidesOptionsComplete-call storage limits for the exact odd-vertex matching subproblem. max_odd_vertices may be 0..22, defaults to the legacy limit 22, and is a hard vertex cap (zero permits only an empty odd set). max_matching_states counts allocated table entries, including odd masks; zero is unlimited. Limits are checked after the actual MST and before matching-table allocation. No partial result escapes a cap failure. These do not bound the complete graph's storage.
    algorithms::ChristofidesTraceOwned actual tree, exact-matching choices, Euler circuit and shortcut result. All stages come from one execution without replay. tree edges are in Kruskal acceptance order, odd_vertices in ascending order, and matching in bitmask reconstruction order. Euler edge ids index tree followed by matching, retaining parallel copies as distinct identities. kept_positions indexes each first visit in euler_vertices; the final closing start is appended separately to result. Costs use long double accumulation for diagnostics and double for the legacy result. They describe rounded arithmetic, not an exact-real certificate.
    algorithms::ChristofidesWorkActual named construction counts, distinct from timing or bit complexity. Every nonempty even mask is evaluated once; matching_candidates counts partner relaxations for its least set bit. Odd masks occupy table storage but are never evaluated. An empty odd set needs one table entry and no relaxations. Empty input bypasses all graph/matching work. No sort comparisons are counted.
    algorithms::ChudnovskyStepOwned actual term, accumulation and estimate from the executing double kernel. term is a_k=(-1)^k(6k)!(A+Bk)/((3k)!(k!)^3 C^(3k)), with A=13591409, B=545140134 and C=640320. The estimate is K/sum_after, K=426880*sqrt(10005), in double arithmetic. ratio_to_previous is zero at index zero, where no ratio was evaluated. sum_changed tests actual equality, not mathematical convergence; term can remain nonzero after additions stall.
    algorithms::ChudnovskyTraceOwned actual Chudnovsky prefix records, stop reason and operation counts. Ordinary and traced calls share one kernel without replay. Positive requested counts are honoured through the first underflowed term; stagnation alone does not stop the loop. The first underflowed zero is included and suffix terms are skipped. first_unchanged_index is -1 if every addition changed the sum. No input or shared mutable state is retained. Default construction performs no evaluation. Trace records add O(m) storage for m actual evaluated terms.
    nn::ChunkedAttentionResultOutput and first derivatives of a weighted attention output sum.
    nn::study::Cifar10StudyOwned training/validation tensors, original row IDs and fitting-only channel statistics.
    nn::data::CifarDatasetRaw CIFAR image/label tensors with optional coarse labels.
    algorithms::CipollaCandidateActual tested auxiliary value, difference and Euler residue. w=a^2-n modulo p. euler_value is w^((p-1)/2) modulo p, equal to zero, one or p-1; p-1 marks acceptance. Every rejected test is retained in a trace.
    algorithms::CipollaElementOwned coefficients of x+y*s in one Cipolla call's quadratic extension. The call supplies p and s^2=w; this plain record stores neither and does not validate manually assigned coefficients. Returned coefficients are canonical uint64 residues. The basis symbol s is formal, not the complex number i.
    algorithms::CipollaOptionsWhole-call actual-candidate and extension-product limits; zero is unlimited. Candidate order is 1,2,...,p-1,0, fixing the missing-zero case while retaining previous successful nonzero choices. Validation precedes limits and shortcuts. Products count result multiplications plus every base square, including the final unused square retained from the legacy loop. Primality and scalar Euler powers are outside the extension-product cap. No partial result escapes a cap.
    algorithms::CipollaPowerStepOwned actual state transition of one right-to-left exponent bit. If remaining_exponent is odd, result is multiplied by base; otherwise result stays unchanged. Base is always squared, including the final unused square. Captures the executing arithmetic, not a recomputed explanation.
    algorithms::CipollaResultOwned exact modular-root verdict and both unsigned root representatives. root follows deterministic auxiliary search/powering order, not size order. other_root is -root modulo p. They are distinct for nonzero residues at odd primes; zero and p=2 have one distinct root. Failure has exists=false, root=other_root=0 and legacy_root=-1. Default storage is not a completed solve. legacy_root equals root when it fits long long; otherwise it uses other_root, which fits because one of two complementary uint64 roots is at most p/2.
    algorithms::CipollaTraceOwned actual prime-field path, candidate tests, bit states and full-range root result. The ordinary, unsigned-result and traced calls share a kernel without replay. input_n is the caller's uint64; normalized_n is input_n modulo the validated prime. residue_euler is zero when the p=2/zero paths skip its computation. a,w,final_element and both record arrays stay zero/empty off the extension path. No shared state or input mutation. Trace storage is O(T+log p) for T actual candidates; no allocation is reserved from the modulus magnitude.
    algorithms::CipollaWorkActual named operation counts, excluding arithmetic inside primality validation. Scalar Euler powers retain a square in every bit iteration, including the closing unused square. Each extension product performs exactly five modular scalar products and two reduced additions, even for zero coefficients. Counts are executed operations, not timing, secret-independent work or bit complexity.
    geometry::CircleOwned planar center and nonnegative radius in coordinate units. Storage alone does not validate geometry; checked producers require finiteness.
    algorithms::Circle2DOwned planar disk with an independently stored centre and radius. Defaults retain centre (0,0), radius one and the original field order. This plain record does not enforce positivity, finite coordinates or non-overlap; circle_packing_metrics() validates data before measuring it. Returned layout radii are expressed in the returned coordinate units.
    cad::Circle3
    algorithms::CirclePackingFrameOwned actual unnormalised working disks and measured relaxation energy at one snapshot. Working disks have radius one. Raw edge target is two; nonedge repulsion uses clearance target 2.15. energy=(edge_stress+nonedge_penalty)/2, where the latter squares only positive clearance deficits. These are diagnostic measurements of the captured state, not a replay or a promised decreasing objective. The force distance floor 1e-9 can modify the gradient interpretation near coincidence. max_displacement is the largest actual committed vertex movement in the last sweep, zero for the initial snapshot. Postprocessed disks are stored separately.
    algorithms::CirclePackingMetricsOwned tolerance-based contact, overlap and edge-error diagnostics for supplied disks. For each pair, gap=distance-radius_i-radius_j. Overlap means gap<-tolerance; contact means |gap|<=tolerance. Contacts can therefore include tiny tolerated overlaps. Edge stress is the sum of squared gaps on distinct nonloop edges; overlap penalty is the sum of squared negative gaps on every pair, independent of the overlap-count tolerance. Empty/singleton min_gap is zero; no-edge maximum error/stress is zero. Zero radii are counted separately and are not disk-packing certificates. These measurements do not establish planarity, optimality or an exact-real contact representation. All numeric aggregates use long double.
    algorithms::CirclePackingOptionsExplicit fixed-sweep controls and preflight work/record limits for the legacy relaxation. Finite nonnegative step_size scales simultaneous pair displacements. There is no adaptive step, line search or early convergence test. Empty/singleton inputs execute no sweeps. snapshot_stride is positive and applies only to traced calls: record the initial state, every stride, and the final state without duplication. Zero caps mean unlimited. Positive caps reject the complete forecast before adjacency/snapshot allocation; validation precedes those caps. Snapshot controls do not limit untraced storage. The dense adjacency matrix remains O(V^2).
    algorithms::CirclePackingTraceOwned actual relaxation snapshots, normalization map and returned fixed-radius disks. Ordinary and traced entry points share the executing kernel without replay. Raw snapshots precede postprocessing: subtract normalization_center, divide by normalization_scale, then RESET every radius to 0.45. The radius is not scaled with the centres. This can destroy tangencies or produce overlapping disks. The name is legacy: no Koebe packing, planarity test or convergence guarantee is supplied. Default storage alone performs no layout. Calls share no state.
    algorithms::CirclePackingWorkActual named validation, relaxation and diagnostic work, excluding sort/allocator costs. Pair visits count all unordered pairs in every requested sweep for V>=2, even when their force is zero. Position updates count actual vertex commits, including unchanged values. Diagnostic scans are separate from the relaxation work cap. Graph input is validated in full; loops are ignored and duplicate/reversed edges collapse to one unweighted adjacency. Counts are not elapsed time.
    dstruct::CircularBuffer
    algorithms::ClarkeWrightOptionsComplete-call preflight limits for savings storage, endpoint scans and optional recording. With m customers there are C=m(m-1)/2 candidate pairs and exactly C*m route-slot inspections. All input validation precedes forecast/cap checks, which precede route/candidate allocation. Zero means unlimited. max_decisions applies only to traced calls; no partial routes or trace escape a failure. These logical counts exclude sorting comparisons, geometric arithmetic and allocator work.
    algorithms::ClarkeWrightStepOwned actual sorted-pair decision, endpoint lookup and accepted concatenation. Stable route slots refer to the initial ascending customer order, excluding the depot. A merge retains route_i and clears route_j. Missing optional slots mean an interior customer. Loads are meaningful only for present slots. Reversal flags indicate executed reverse calls, even on singleton routes. merged_customers excludes depot visits and is empty on rejection. No replay.
    algorithms::ClarkeWrightTraceOwned actual parallel-savings decisions, final routes, loads and distance accounting. Ordinary/traced entry points share the executing kernel without replay. initial_star_distance is twice the sum of cached depot distances. Accepted savings telescope in exact arithmetic; accounting_residual measures the actual widened final distance minus (initial_star_distance-accepted_savings). Rounded sums need not cancel exactly. No optimality, fleet-count or approximation guarantee follows. Calls share no state; no borrowed input references survive.
    algorithms::ClarkeWrightWorkActual named routing operations, not elapsed time or a complete instruction count. Every sorted pair scans all initial route slots, including cleared slots. Geometric evaluations include cached depot distances, customer-pair distances and final output edges. Comparator counts depend on the standard library sort. Appended customers count elements copied into surviving routes, not reversals.

    algorithms::ClippedSegmentOwned visible endpoint coordinates with the historical field order and types. A rejected result has visible=false and four zero coordinates.     geometry::ClippedVoronoiActual bounded Voronoi cells and selected clipping work.
    geometry::ClosestPairImprovementOwned actual strict incumbent improvement from the executing pair scan. The first comparison initializes the incumbent and is included. No candidate evaluation is replayed to build these records.
    geometry::ClosestPairOptionsPair-work and optional actual-improvement recording limits. Zero means unlimited. Its required count depends on data/order and is not forecast as every pair. Failed work/record/range/allocation checks expose no partial result or trace.
    geometry::ClosestPairResultOwned closest-point coordinate copies and legacy finite-double distance. Original field order/types are retained.
