    geometry::ClosestPairSelectionOwned closest input identities, copied coordinates and widened measured distance. first<second refer to original input positions, including distinct records with identical coordinates. Distances are rounded long-double hypot evaluations, not exact predicates. Equal measured distances keep the lexicographically first index pair. Default storage alone is not a valid search result. Calls own copies.
    geometry::ClosestPairTraceOwned actual improvements and final indexed result from one all-pairs execution. Shares the executing kernel with ordinary search without replay. Stores only K strict improvements, not a full candidate history: O(K) additional storage, with K at most n(n-1)/2. The final improvement is the returned selection. Input coordinates are copied into result only; records retain ids and distances. No borrowed input references survive and calls share no mutable state.
    geometry::ClosestPairWorkActual validation, distance and incumbent work, excluding allocator costs. All unordered pairs are visited in i-major/j-minor ascending order, even after finding zero distance. Ties count candidates equal to the current incumbent, excluding initialization; zero_pairs counts every measured zero-distance pair. Counts are not elapsed time and do not measure exact-real arithmetic costs.
    algorithms::ClosureOptionsOwn ClosureOptions values for one independent native execution. Fields describe actual producing values or policy units. In-class initializers define defaults. Containers own their values; constructing a record alone performs no algorithm work and retains no caller storage or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::ClosurePhaseOwn ClosurePhase values for one independent native execution. Fields describe actual producing values or policy units. In-class initializers define defaults. Containers own their values; constructing a record alone performs no algorithm work and retains no caller storage or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::ClosureRunOwn ClosureRun values for one independent native execution. Fields describe actual producing values or policy units. In-class initializers define defaults. Containers own their values; constructing a record alone performs no algorithm work and retains no caller storage or shared mutable state.
    stats::ClusterAgreementExternal partition agreement, with explicit DBSCAN noise coverage. Labels are compared to reference classes after fitting, not used to train or choose parameters. Purity excludes noise; adjusted Rand treats all -1 rows as one category. The latter convention measures a partition including noise, not successful assignment of those rows. Scores are invariant to arbitrary cluster/class renaming. Value-owned result; no shared mutable state. See cluster_agreement() for input validation.
    optim::CMAESCMAES on the ArbitraryFunction callback interface. Unbounded covariance-adaptation evolution strategy with weighted elites, evolution paths and global step-size adaptation. Default offspring count is 4+floor(3*log(p)). Covariance eigensolve is dense with numerical eigenvalue floors. Stops on search-scale/axis tolerance or generation budget; stochastic results depend on seed and population, not a global certificate. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    rl::CmaEsFull covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy for maximization.
    optim::CMAESOptionsConfiguration for CMAES; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    nn::models::CnfDensityOutputOwn all four quarter-trajectory checkpoints and the final continuous-flow density path.
    nn::models::CnfFieldOutputOwn a live velocity field, selected trace and all exact/paired trace diagnostics.
    algorithms::CNFGrammarEpsilon-free binary-normal-form grammar with arbitrary integer nonterminal ids. The original three-field layout is retained. unary maps one terminal byte to the ids A with A->byte; it does not represent nonterminal unit rules. binary entries {A,B,C} mean A->BC. Negative and sparse ids, including signed extremes, are valid. Repeated productions are semantically idempotent for recognition. No epsilon, unit-production or general-CFG conversion is supplied. The start may appear on a right-hand side because no epsilon rule exists. Public containers own their data; subsequent analyses own their results.
    stats::CNNClassifierA small convolutional neural network image classifier, trained by backpropagation with mini-batch stochastic gradient descent. The architecture is the classic LeNet-style stack for a single-channel (grayscale) image:
    stats::CNNClassifierOptions
    stats::CNNClassifierPrediction
    nn::models::CnnZPlusExplanationActual forward logits and each detached signed-relevance redistribution endpoint. Target scores include output bias, while redistribution denominators exclude all biases and negative weights. Seeds can be negative; the maps then need not be nonnegative. Actual max-pool winners route pooled relevance back to the map. Epsilon and zero positive paths can lose mass; compare layer sums explicitly. This is a model-inspection heuristic, not proof that pixels caused a prediction. No borrowed input references or learnable-gradient history are retained.
    nn::CoatnetDigitOutputScores and intermediate features of the digit CoAtNet.
    algorithms::CocktailSortPassOwned state after one actual directional pass of cocktail shaker sort. Bounds are inclusive before/after the pass. A forward pass with swaps lowers hi by one; every backward pass raises lo by one, including a stopping pass. A zero-swap forward pass keeps both bounds. next_lo>next_hi means an empty remaining window. A final zero-comparison pass is retained, matching the legacy kernel. Only strict adjacent inversions swap; equal keys keep identity.
    algorithms::CocktailSortTraceOwned input/output, stable original identities and actual directional passes. Empty/singleton inputs have no passes and zero work. Larger inputs include the final zero-swap pass even if its window has one item and no comparisons. Counts exclude copying, index initialization and loop control. Swaps equal strict inversions in the original input. No input references or shared state survive. Snapshot storage is O(n*p), where p<=n is the actual pass count; output-only sorting uses constant auxiliary state beyond its owned input copy.
    nn::models::CodecPacketHold all values needed by a bounded TFLCODE1 decoder, without encoder state.
    nn::models::CodecQuantizerOwn explicit per-coordinate Float32 ranges for a uniform byte quantizer.
    cad::CoEdge
    algorithms::CohenSutherlandStepOwned pre-decision endpoints/codes and the actual selected edge intersection. Endpoints/intersections are long double working values before final double conversion. Bit values are left=1,right=2,bottom=4,top=8; boundary points are inside their half-plane. Terminal records use replaced_endpoint=2, new_code=0 and zero intersection coordinates, which are not geometric data.
    algorithms::CohenSutherlandTraceOwned final result and at most five actual decisions from one executing clip. There are at most four intersections, because each processed closed half-plane contains both remaining endpoints and stays satisfied. Interpolation keeps each free intersection coordinate between the current endpoint values; the selected coordinate is pinned to its rectangle boundary. These are floating computations, not exact predicates: near-corner decisions can differ from real arithmetic. Counts exclude validation, coordinate comparisons and presentation. No references, global state or replay are retained.
    nn::models::CollapseSummaryOwn host-side analytic and sampled finite-mixture posterior diagnostics.
    sim::ColliderImmutable local convex geometry and its transform within a rigid body. Dimensions are full extents in metres. ConvexHull uses vertices instead. Shared vertex storage must remain immutable for the lifetime of bodies/snapshots.
    nn::models::ColorDataOwn lightness-only observations,chroma targets and original RGB.
    algorithms::ColoringAnalysisOwned producing result, actual degree ordering and selected work, without event history. order sorts multigraph degree descending, then vertex ID ascending. Degrees exclude self-loops. Inputs are not retained. Copying owns all vector storage.
    algorithms::ColoringEventOne actual constant-size first-fit event, without marker-array snapshots. vertex is always the vertex being processed. For neighbor events, neighbor is the actual adjacent vertex; colored states whether its label exists, color is that label or zero placeholder, and flag states whether a true marker write occurred. For probes color is the tested label and flag its blocked value. For assignments color is the committed label. Other fields are placeholders.
    algorithms::ColoringGraphOwned undirected graph fixture with explicit vertex count, including isolates. Edges retain their order and may be edited; family builders produce simple loopless graphs. No coloring or optimality certificate is implied by storage.
    algorithms::ColoringOptionsComplete input caps and online actual-event cap for analysis/capture. All endpoints are validated before caps or adjacency allocation. Vertices include isolates; edges count original records, including loops/duplicates. Event units are whole neighbor/probe/assignment records, not bytes or peak RAM.
    algorithms::ColoringResultOwned legacy greedy labels and contiguous palette size. Empty graphs use no colors; each nonempty edgeless graph uses color zero. The output is proper for the graph after deleting loops, not an optimality certificate or a proper coloring of an original graph containing a loop.
    algorithms::ColoringTraceOwned actual preparation, output and chronological constant-size sweep events. Capturing performs no replay or extra degree sorting. Online admission occurs before each neighbor read/marker write, availability read or assignment. Default cap is one million records; zero disables it. Preparation, ordinary output/work, capacities and allocation overhead are excluded. No truncation or partial trace escapes failure. History is O(n+m) records, not full marker arrays.
    algorithms::ColoringWorkSelected actual preparation and first-fit work, excluding validation and CPU costs. Degrees and adjacency entries include parallel edges, but not loops. Marker initialization is measured in logical slots; writes count every actual assignment of true, including repeated writes from duplicate edges.
    nn::models::ColorizationResultOwn predicted chroma and all colorizer stages.
    nn::models::ColorMetricsOwn color-regression diagnostics and decoded RGB. Host presentation view.
    algorithms::CombSortPassOwned state and work after one actual comb-sort gap pass. Pair indices increase from zero; each pair is (i,i+gap). One pass costs n-gap key comparisons. A zero-swap scan stops only at gap one. Original positions follow actual exchanges: their equal-value order need not remain stable.
    algorithms::CombSortTraceOwned original values, final work and actual comb-sort pass states. work is identical to comb_sort_work() for the same input. Empty/singleton inputs have no records and identity final indices. Each record owns two length-n snapshots; p passes require O(np) snapshot work/storage. Output-only and work-only calls use constant auxiliary storage beyond their owned input. Equal-value identities may cross indirectly during a gapped exchange.
    nn::models::CompactMaskRcnnOutputsOwn shared stride4 features and RPN outputs for the compact64px Mask R-CNN.
    stats::TukeyHSD::ComparisonOne pairwise comparison: group1 - group2 with its family-wise interval.
    nn::models::CompetitiveAeOutputOwn training and deployment endpoints of a hard-competition autoencoder.
    algebra::ComplexA complex number, used to report polynomial roots that are not real. Plain re/im fields (no arithmetic operators exposed) matching Polynomial's convention of a member operator== over a free one (SWIG's Python backend maps a free operator== to a single module-level __eq__ that collides across every type that defines one).
    nn::ComplexTensorA complex tensor stored as two real float tensors of equal shape and dtype.
    algorithms::ComponentLabelAnalysisOwned final labelling and work, without history allocation. count equals labels_created minus successful_unions. Only foreground cells query representatives during renumbering; both scans visit background too.
    algorithms::ComponentLabelCellOwned actual first-pass foreground decision with its union-record range. earlier_labels[0..earlier_count) follows up, left, upper-left, upper-right, omitting background/out-of-bounds positions and retaining duplicate labels. assigned is their minimum or a newly created ID. The union range is half-open.
    algorithms::ComponentLabelOptionsComplete-image and actual-history budgets; zero means unlimited. Full shape validation precedes the complete max_cells cap and allocation. max_events counts foreground-cell plus union-attempt records online; analysis and output-only calls ignore the event cap.
    algorithms::ComponentLabelTraceOwned actual two-pass history, without prefix reruns or synthetic decisions. provisional is the map after scan one. parents is the actual forest after scan two, including dummy zero; halving need not flatten it fully. root_to_dense is the actual remap, zero at non-root/unused entries. Input, snapshots and results own independent storage.
    algorithms::ComponentLabelUnionActual union operands, pre-attachment roots and resulting attachment. Rank determines attachment; equal ranks choose the smaller root and increment its rank. Redundant attempts have merged=false, winner=root_a and loser=0. Internal root IDs are distinct from the final dense component labels.
    algorithms::ComponentLabelWorkActual two-scan and balanced disjoint-set operation counts. Neighbor probes count in-bounds earlier positions for foreground cells only; admitted labels retain duplicates. find_steps counts path-halving iterations, not original edges. parent_writes counts union/halving assignments, including idempotent halving writes, excluding initial set creation. Snapshots and later measurements perform no counted operations. All counters are checked.
    algorithms::ComputusGregorianTraceOwned actual Meeus/Jones/Butcher integer steps and the resulting date. All divisions are floors of nonnegative integers for supported positive years. a is a zero-based Metonic index; the golden number is a+1. h is a nominal lunar offset, not an unconditional observed or corrected full-moon date. l+1 is the nominal following-Sunday offset. m subtracts one week in the two exceptional Sunday cases. No iteration, replay, allocation or shared state.
    nn::models::CondenseContextBorrowed stores, condensing progress and optional penalty/output logs.
    nn::models::CondensedConvGather indices and packed grouped kernel for a converted learned group convolution.
    nn::models::CondenseNetConfigDense-stage dimensions, group condensation and regularization settings.
    nn::models::CondenseNetConvertedCostAnalytical RGB inference-form count metadata, without allocating a converted model.
    nn::models::CondenseNetOutputsFinal features/logits, arithmetic metadata and explicit group-lasso penalty terms.
    nn::models::ConditionalGanOutputOwn seven live conditional GAN endpoints with separate logistic objectives.
    nn::models::ConditionalVaeOutputOwn Gaussian VAE endpoints plus the exact condition and both concatenated inputs.
    geometry::ConeDirectionOwned original neighbour identity, location, distance and computed direction. Angles use atan2 in [-pi,pi]; equal computed angles sort by original index. Repeated nonzero directions remain separate records. Coincident query/other locations are excluded, since their direction is undefined. No input reference.
    geometry::ConePointSummaryOwned actual largest-gap witness and classification for one original point. At least two directions select the first strict largest gap in sorted adjacent order, then the wrap gap last. Empty/single-direction queries use a full-turn score by convention and are flagged for every valid threshold. For no directions, gap endpoint ids are n (the input size), not valid point ids. gap_start and largest_gap describe an open angular sector; its bounding neighbour rays are allowed. Wrap arcs can extend beyond pi. Rounded gaps are confined to [0,2pi]; this is floating geometry, not an exact predicate.
    cad::ConeSurface
    geometry::ConeSurfaceAnalysisOwned binary mask, per-point witnesses and actual work from one executing scan. Mask entries align with original indices, including coincident queries. No references or shared state survive. The radius criterion is local, but this implementation visits every ordered pair: O(n^2+sum(k log k)) time, bounded by O(n^2 log n), and O(n) scratch/output storage without retained directions.
    geometry::ConeSurfaceLimitsComplete pair-work and optional actual-direction storage limits. All finite coordinates and controls validate before the n(n-1) forecast. Zero means unlimited. The direction cap is online and applies only to traces; analysis/output-only calls do not retain all directions. Failures expose no partial return. No spatial index is implied by a small geometric radius.
    geometry::ConeSurfaceTraceOwned per-query sorted direction records from the same scan as the analysis. Total direction storage is O(sum k), at most n(n-1), in addition to O(n) analysis/scratch storage. No candidate distance/angle is replayed. Sorted records retain original identities and copied coordinates.
    geometry::ConeSurfaceWorkActual all-pairs and angular work, excluding allocator, sort-comparator and rendering costs. Pair visits include coincident records; distance evaluations exclude them. Angle evaluations count admitted noncoincident directions. sort_calls counts std::sort invocations with at least two records, not sort comparisons. gap_tests counts k circular gaps for each query with k>=2; sparse conventions add no gap tests. Complete pair preflight and checked increments prevent wrap.
    nn::models::compact_bert::ConfigOwn Config source graph endpoints or configuration.
    nn::models::ConfiningEnergyPathOwn the live ConfiningEnergyPath mathematical endpoints.
    stats::ConformalClassifierOptionsSettings for SplitConformalClassifier.
    stats::ConformalCoverageThe exact coverage law of split conformal prediction with n calibration points.
    stats::ConformalRegressorOptionsSettings for SplitConformalRegressor.
    nn::ConfusionMatrixCounts of true-class rows and predicted-class columns, with SVG rendering.
    nn::ConfusionMatrixPlotOptionsPresentation settings for an annotated confusion-matrix SVG.
    optim::ConjugateGradientConjugateGradient on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Nonlinear Polak-Ribiere-plus directions with negative beta truncated to zero, periodic/descent restarts and an Armijo line search. It is not linear CG with exact line minimisation and does not imply termination in p steps. Returns when gradient/change/search conditions stop progress. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    algorithms::ConjugateGradientOptionsAbsolute stopping and optional actual-snapshot storage controls for CG. Zero iterations is valid; zero max_trace_values means unlimited. Positive trace caps count four vector entries per unknown per completed step, checked online before completing the next step. A failing call can already have requested A p. Solve-only calls ignore this storage cap.
    optim::ConjugateGradientOptionsConfiguration for ConjugateGradient; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    algorithms::ConjugateGradientRunCG output with honest stop reason, counted products and optional owned steps. solution.residual is the recomputed absolute norm; solution.converged is true exactly for stop == CGStop::converged. Starting point is zero. There is one A p product and one diagnostic A x product per completed step, with no replay. A curvature failure also counts its attempted A p. Initial zero needs no call. No initial snapshot is stored; initial_residual is ||b||. Returns own storage.
    algorithms::ConjugateGradientStepOwned actual CG step, including its used direction and resulting iterate. x and r are the resulting iterate and recursively updated residual; p and ap are the direction and A p actually used. beta is the next-direction coefficient only when has_next_direction is true. Norms/coefficients use long double; vector storage and each recurrence assignment use checked double rounding.
    algorithms::ConnectedComponentsOwned dense component IDs, ordered by first row-major component occurrence. Zero is background; IDs are independent of internal union-find roots. Original fields and layout are preserved. All nonzero input ints mean foreground.
    algorithms::ConnectedComponentStatsPixel-index area, bounds, centroid and exposed-edge measurements for one label. Bounds are inclusive; centroids average zero-based pixel-centre indices. perimeter4 counts exposed orthogonal edges including holes/image edges, regardless of label connectivity; it is not a smooth Euclidean perimeter.

    geometry::ConvexHullAnalysisOwned strict hull, earliest original identities and actual work without history. Vertices start at the lexicographic minimum and run counterclockwise, without repeating the first. Collinear edge points are omitted. Empty gives no points; one distinct point gives one; a collinear set gives its sorted two endpoints. Identity vector aligns one-for-one with hull vertices.
    geometry::ConvexHullOptionsLimits for complete input storage and actual optional hull trace events. Full finite validation precedes max_points preflight; max_events is an online count of actual test/pop/push records, ignored by untraced calls. Zero disables either cap. No partial result escapes a failed cap.
    geometry::ConvexHullTraceOwned actual sorted identities, compact stack edits and completed scan chains. lower/upper contain indices into sorted and include their endpoints. Inputs with fewer than two distinct points take no scans and have empty chains/events. Trace capture performs no extra sorting or orientation replay. All storage is independent of the caller, result and other snapshots; O(n) extra space.
    geometry::ConvexHullWorkActual sorting, deduplication and two-scan work, with checked counters. Comparison counts depend on the standard-library sort and original order. For at least two distinct points each pass pushes each point once. Tests count exact orientation requests; every nonpositive test causes one pop. max_stack is the greatest length of either separate chain, not their sum.
    sim::ConveyorEnvironmentA headless, single-payload conveyor and two physical sorting bins. Uses the native rigid-body solver at 240 Hz, SI units and Y-up coordinates. A friction-driven belt stops when the centre crosses X=0.10 m; the next fruit cannot spawn until the current one is sorted, missorted or lost. Basic apples use a 78 mm sphere proxy; bananas use a 160 by 46 mm capsule proxy. Diverse selects six meshes per class and scales/rotates the corresponding proxy; entry X is [-1,-.7] m, across-belt Z is [-.065,.065] m, yaw is [0,2*pi), and pitch/roll are [-.12,.12] rad. Appearance draws are shared across classes. Payload rotation is locked as a stable initial manipulation approximation. Bins are centred at (0.10, 0.44, +/-0.42) m; the negative-Z bin is for apples. The workcell includes a pedestal at X=0.62 m, ready for a Z-up URDF visual translated to CAD (0.62,0,0.72). Robot actuation, grasping and arm collision geometry belong to the external controller; this class does not infer them from visual CAD. world() exposes forces/body edits for later control tasks. Instances are single-writer; reset(seed) repeats the same fruit sequence.
    sim::ConveyorObservationOwned observation, using physics coordinates X along belt, Y up, Z across belt. CAD scene methods convert to X along belt, Z up, Y across belt.
    nn::models::ConvFeatureCarry an NHWC feature map together with its positive channel-count metadata.
    nn::ConvGeometryGeometry of one convolution or pooling layer along one axis.
    nn::ConvLayerOptions
    nn::models::ConvNeXtBlockOutputsResidual branch before dropout and complete ConvNeXt block output.
    nn::models::ConvNeXtConfigConvNeXt V1/V2 layout, stem, classifier and branch-dropout metadata.
    nn::models::ConvNeXtOutputsAll stage maps and classifier logits from a complete ConvNeXt.
    nn::models::ConvNeXtSizeStage depths and channel dimensions for a ConvNeXt layout.
    nn::models::ConvNormConfigSettings for rectangular convolution followed by batch normalisation.
    nn::models::ConvolutionalAeOutputOwn all six activation endpoints of a convolutional autoencoder.
    nn::models::ConvolutionalDecoderOutputOwn the hidden map and reconstructed image from a spatial decoder.
    nn::models::ConvolutionalVaeDecoderOutputOwn all decoder stages from a Gaussian sample to Bernoulli pixel probabilities.
    nn::models::ConvolutionalVaeOutputOwn Gaussian posterior endpoints and all seven spatial encoder/decoder stages.
    optim::CoordinateDescentCoordinateDescent on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Each epoch visits coordinates in index order. Every partial update requests a full gradient and an Armijo-backtracked value sequence; this is not exact one-dimensional minimisation. An exhausted search restores that coordinate. Stops on the full end-of-epoch gradient norm. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::CoordinateDescentOptionsConfiguration for CoordinateDescent; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    datasets::CoraCitationGraphOwn normalized features, sparse graph entries, and label splits for Cora.
    algorithms::CordicAnalysisOwned actual approximation and final folded-frame recurrence state. result includes half-turn restoration; raw_x/raw_y and residual refer to the folded frame, initially (1,0,reduction.reduced). inverse_gain is the product actually accumulated for exactly iterations stages, initially one. No field certifies error to the true original angle. Zero stages is a valid unrotated approximation. The model uses double arithmetic, including multiplications.
    algorithms::CordicConstantOne actual cached circular-stage constant, copied on request. shift=2^-index, angle=atan(shift), inverse_gain_step=1/sqrt(1+shift²), all rounded doubles. The shared immutable table is lazily built with libm calls; the subsequent recurrence performs lookups and floating multiplications.
    algorithms::CordicErrorRowMeasured worst errors for one requested iteration count against the host libm. Empty angle inputs set has_samples=false and leave zero placeholders for errors/worst_angle. Positive samples select the first input with the largest max(abs(sine error),abs(cosine error)); norms measure abs(hypot(result)-1). Values are diagnostics against std::sin/cos, not certified mathematical bounds.
    algorithms::CordicReductionOwned actual rounded-period reduction and optional half-turn fold. principal is remainder(theta,period), with period=2*pi_double. reduced lies within [-pi_double/2,pi_double/2]; flipped means a half turn was removed and both final coordinates must be negated. This does not perform high-precision reduction modulo mathematical 2*pi: large input angles can have large phase error.
    algorithms::CordicStepOwned actual circular update, including before/after state and normalized direction. Constants are copied from the producing table. direction is +1 at residual >=0 (including either zero), otherwise -1. Before/after coordinates are raw; unit_x/unit_y divide the actual after-state by hypot and remain in the folded frame, without half-turn restoration. They reproduce the former report's plotted normalization; they are not a rerun or a compensated-output snapshot.
    algorithms::CordicTraceOwned actual rotation sequence and the result it produced, without replay. Exactly one constant-size record per completed stage; zero stages is empty. Caller inputs, constants returned elsewhere, steps and result own independent values. Theta(1+N) work and O(N) extra trace storage for N<=1075.
    algorithms::CordicWorkBounded actual per-call operations, excluding one-time shared table construction. These are algorithmic evaluations, not machine-instruction/throughput counts. Every requested stage executes even at zero residual. Trace normalization calls are additional diagnostics and do not change the producing recurrence.
    cv::CornerA detected corner: its pixel location and a detector-specific response score (higher is a stronger corner). Meant to be independently sortable/filterable by the caller.
    rl::environments::CorridorLocal slipping corridor with80-percent intended direction and separate terminal/time-limit outcomes.
    algorithms::CosineLSHOwn an immutable finite index with seeded Gaussian hyperplanes and insertion-order buckets. Input data are copied, fixing the historical borrowed-pointer lifetime hazard and stale buckets after caller mutation. Bit agreement has probability1-theta/pi for nonzero vectors and an isotropic continuous plane; finite sampled Gaussian arithmetic is the implementation. Zero vectors use cosine0 and nonnegative sign bits. Query still initializes N dense marks: O(N+L*k*d+V+C*d), with V actual member visits and C distinct candidates. There is no worst-case sublinear guarantee. Copies own all data/planes/buckets; const queries share no mutable state.
    CountPipeline step created by count(); counts rows per group.
    algorithms::CountingSortAnalysisOwned sorted values, stable original identities and bucket boundaries. For nonempty input, bucket b denotes min_value+b. Its output interval is [starts[b],ends[b]); counts[b] is its length. original_indices[j] identifies the input item copied to output[j], and increases within each equal-key block. Empty calls allocate no buckets: automatic bounds are both zero, explicit bounds retain the supplied values. No references or shared mutable state survive.
    algorithms::CountingSortPlacementOne actual right-to-left assignment using a predecremented end cursor. Events appear in execution order, with input_index descending. The chosen output slot is cursor_before-1. No snapshot or report-side replay is needed.
    algorithms::CountingSortTraceComplete owned counting-sort analysis and actual placement events. The same kernel drives legacy sorting, analysis and tracing. Storage and time are O(n+k), including n events; no partial trace is returned on failure.
    algorithms::CountingSortWorkLogical operations actually performed by the counting-sort kernel. Excludes validation, allocation/zeroing, copies, cursor decrements, loop tests and hardware timings. Range discovery examines n items only in automatic calls; count/prefix/place work is n,k,n for nonempty accepted input.
    dstruct::CountMinSketch
    algorithms::CrankNicolsonHeatTraceComplete owned initial/step states and actual reusable Thomas factors. One kernel drives final-only and traced calls. Factors are prepared once when steps>0; pivots are the actual eliminated diagonal and multipliers[0]=0. States include the initial sample plus all requested steps, never a partial history. Work/storage is O(nx*(steps+1)); final-only storage is O(nx). All vectors are owned and no callbacks/references survive. Independent calls are thread-safe subject to the supplied callback's own behavior.
    algorithms::Crc32ByteStepOne actual byte-at-a-time reflected CRC register update. raw_before precedes byte injection; lookup_index=(raw_before XOR byte)&255; raw_after=(raw_before>>8) XOR table_value. Raw registers exclude final XOR.
    algorithms::Crc32FlipOne independent single-input-bit corruption and its finalized CRC difference. Bit numbering is byte-major, least-significant bit first inside each byte: bit b toggles byte b/8 with mask 1<<(b%8). syndrome is changed XOR baseline.
    algorithms::Crc32FlipScanOwned complete census of each independent one-bit corruption of one message. For fixed length, CRC differences are linear in the error pattern and independent of payload. Output-bit counts are not collision probabilities or cryptographic avalanche guarantees. Empty input has no flips, false has_flips and zero summary placeholders. Independent calls share no mutable state.
    algorithms::Crc32TraceOwned complete actual byte folds from the same kernel as crc32(). Input bytes are consumed in order; no view/reference survives. Initialization is FFFFFFFF and final XOR is FFFFFFFF. Empty input has raw FFFFFFFF, checksum zero and no events. O(n) time/storage for n bytes.
    nn::models::bilstm_crf::CrfLive source Crf endpoints with owning tensor handles.
    nn::CrfDecoded
    algorithms::CristianAnalysisOwned nominal receipt-time estimate and admissible return-delay interval. network_round_trip=RTT-processing; return delay lies in [minimum,network-minimum] in the ideal model. The interval midpoint is minimax for absolute error. All fields are double evaluations, not outward-rounded certificates. Large epochs can collapse absolute endpoints; the separate delay fields retain information that an absolute timestamp addition may round away. No clock is read/set and no references or shared mutable state are retained.
    algorithms::CristianExchangeOwned controlled exchange separating actual path asymmetry from an uncertainty bound. The generated RTT includes both network legs and known processing. The server timestamp is at reply departure. model_error=(outbound-return)/2 is calculated from durations, rather than subtracting rounded epoch timestamps. It describes ideal midpoint error; fields are floating approximations, not certificates.
    algorithms::CristianProbeOne ideal-rate request/reply observation using one consistent time unit. server_time is stamped at reply departure, after server_processing has elapsed. RTT includes outbound delay, processing and return delay. The common one-way lower bound applies to both network legs, not processing. All quantities are finite; durations are nonnegative. The server is assumed accurate and elapsed client durations calibrated to the same ideal rate.
    algorithms::CristianSelectionOwned complete per-probe analyses and the first smallest stored error radius. Empty input has has_probe=false and index zero as an unused placeholder. Selection is by stored error_bound, not raw RTT when assumptions/processing differ. The chosen estimate refers to that probe's own receipt instant; it is not extrapolated to a later present and does not set an operating-system clock.
    nn::models::CrnnConfigConfigure exact convolution-width division and recurrent hidden size.
    nn::models::CrnnOutputOwn CRNN time-major logits and every convolution stage.
    optim::CrossEntropyMethodThe Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) for derivative-free continuous optimization on an ArbitraryFunction within a box constraint. A diagonal-covariance Gaussian search distribution is repeatedly refit from the best ("elite") fraction of each generation's samples, with the new distribution parameters exponentially smoothed against the previous generation's for stability (Rubinstein 1997; Rubinstein & Kroese 2004).
    optim::CrossEntropyMethodOptions
    nn::ml::CrossValidationScoreSample-weighted validation mean and individual fold means.
    algorithms::CrtMergeOwned actual certificate and wide candidate for one sequential CRT merge. before is the last representable compatible prefix. Bezout coefficients obey before.modulus*bezout_first+input_modulus*bezout_second=gcd. difference is the normalized input residue minus before.remainder. Inconsistency leaves the correction/candidate fields zero and emits no hypothetical merged pair. Compatible attempts retain the actual signed correction product, normalized multiplier and wide candidate, even when the period cannot fit int64.
    algorithms::CrtOptionsNamed complete-call limits for attempted merges and actual Euclidean divisions. Zero means unlimited. Limits count operations until the first inconsistency or period overflow, not the unvisited suffix. All moduli are validated before these limits apply. No partial result/trace escapes when a work cap is reached.
    algorithms::CrtSolutionOwned representable generalized CRT result, retaining the legacy field order and defaults. A successful solve has 0<=remainder<modulus, with modulus the lcm of the processed input moduli. Inconsistency returns {false,0,0}; the default record {false,0,1} is merely unverified storage. Empty input solves to {true,0,1}. Period overflow throws in chinese_remainder(), rather than masquerading as mathematical inconsistency. Manually constructed records are not validated.
    algorithms::CrtTraceOwned actual sequential CRT path with an optional complete int64 verdict. Complete and Inconsistent runs fill solution with their legacy result; Overflow leaves solution empty. prefix always retains the last representable compatible prefix, including on failure. steps includes the first rejected attempt and omits the unvisited suffix. Inconsistency/overflow are actual mathematical/range outcomes; work caps and allocation failures still throw, exposing no partial trace. Default construction alone performs no solve. Ordinary and traced entry points share the executing kernel without replay.
    algorithms::CrtWorkActual validation visits, attempted merges and named arithmetic operations. Euclidean steps include an initial zero quotient when the first modulus is smaller. Products count the correction product, period product and residue product separately, including compatible overflow attempts and redundant/unit congruences. Validation covers every modulus even if arithmetic stops early. These are fixed-word counts, not elapsed time or arbitrary-precision bit cost.
    nn::models::CspContextBorrow parameter stores and normalization settings during a CSP forward.
    nn::models::CspOutputsOwn transformed, bypass, concatenation and fused CSP feature tensors.
    datasets::CsvOptionsHow CSV text is split into cells and typed. Every field has a usable default.
    CsvReaderSWIG-friendly streaming CSV reader: returns a big file as DataFrames of at most batch_size() rows each, so only one chunk is in memory at a time.
    datasets::CsvReaderStreams a CSV file as DataFrames of at most batch_size() rows each.
    nn::data::CsvTableOwned rectangular string table with a unique nonempty header.

    nn::CtcLossResultLoss and TF CTCLoss's second output: d loss[b] / d logits, in the logits' layout, before any reduction over the batch. The loss is recorded as in ctc_loss; the gradient has no history.

    algorithms::CubicSplineOwned local-power coefficients S_i(x)=a_i+t*(b_i+t*(c_i+t*d_i)), t=x-xs[i]. Preserves the original five-vector layout. For n>=2, xs contains n finite increasing knots and each coefficient vector has n-1 finite entries. Empty models have all vectors empty; singleton models have one xs/a entry and no b/c/d entries. Public mutation is permitted; evaluators validate the shape. A manually supplied model need not be natural or C2 merely because it is structurally valid. Coefficient units are y, y/x, y/x² and y/x³.
    optim::CuckooSearchCuckoo Search (Yang & Deb, 2009) on an ArbitraryFunction within a box constraint: a population of nests is perturbed by heavy-tailed Levy flights (via Mantegna's algorithm) and a fraction of the worst nests is abandoned and rebuilt each iteration, mimicking brood parasitism. Derivative-free.

    nn::CudaHalfMatmulRun dense products on CUDA with packed binary16 inputs and Float32 accumulation.
    cad::CudaRendererExplicit NVIDIA CUDA offscreen CAD renderer with persistent device resources. Uses the existing compute CUDA kernel backend. Primary, shadow and AO rays, materials/maps, transparency, sampling and wire overlays execute on the GPU. Geometry/BVH preparation stays on the CPU. Float32 device arithmetic and scale-aware ray bias can differ from the CPU reference; this is not a bit-exact replacement. Inputs must be representable in float32. The last base snapshot and its uploaded geometry are retained until replaced or this renderer is destroyed. Calls on one instance serialize; separate instances own separate contexts. No silent fallback is performed. CPU render() remains available in builds without CUDA; select fallback explicitly in the application.

Logistic evaluation uses a stable inverse link. Callback coordinate dimensions and finiteness are checked.

    algorithms::CuthillMcKeeStepOne actual CM queue removal and the neighbours it discovers. Owned values; steps are in forward BFS order even for a reversed result. Newly enqueued vertices use increasing (degree, original id), separately for each removed vertex, rather than sorting a whole BFS level.
    algorithms::CuthillMcKeeTraceOwned complete output and actual queue history of one CM traversal. No input references survive. Arrays degree, parent and level use original ids; roots parent themselves at level zero. Each new component resets its level. Steps and forward_order always describe the forward run; order and position describe the requested final direction. Empty graphs have empty arrays and zero work. Adjacency scans count normalized directed entries, not raw duplicates.
    nn::models::CycleDomainsOwn disjoint A/original-B rows, transformed B and each domain's original source IDs.
    nn::models::CycleGanOutputOwn both translations/cycles/identities, four patch maps and all explicit CycleGAN terms.
    algorithms::CycleOptionsOptional completed-transition-call limit for diagnostic cycle finding. Zero means no caller limit. A positive limit stops before the next call that would exceed it; completed callback calls are not undone. It is not a timeout.
    algorithms::CycleResultOwned least positive period lambda and least cycle-entry index mu. The historical layout/types are unchanged. Successful detection has lambda>=1; a default zero record is a placeholder, not a detected cycle.
    algorithms::CycleSortPlacementOne actual final-cell placement in a cycle rotation. Each target occurs once in the complete trace. A placement stores the held value and its displaced value/identity before the value-cell write. The displaced item becomes the next held item until target==cycle_start closes the cycle; that final displaced duplicate of the original start is discarded. rank_begin is the first destination for this key in the remaining suffix; equal values may advance target. No full array snapshot is stored.
    algorithms::CycleSortTraceOwned input, actual aggregate work and complete ordered placement records. Original identities travel with the same moves as values, exposing instability on equal keys. Final original_indices is output-to-input; intermediate array states must be interpreted with the held item because a cycle's start remains unchanged until closure. Empty/singleton traces have no placements and identity final indices. At most n records and O(n) extra storage, with no snapshots.
    algorithms::CycleSortWorkOwned sorted values and actual operations from the canonical cycle-sort kernel. array_writes counts assignments to working value-array cells only. It excludes argument/output copying, the held item, counters, trace identities, allocation and physical device writes. Rank comparisons count strict less-than tests; equality comparisons include the final false duplicate-skip test. Loop/index tests are excluded. Empty/singleton inputs have zero counts. Values and counts are owned; no input references or shared mutable state survive.
    algorithms::CycleWorkOwned cycle, its entry state and exact completed-call/equality counts. Evaluations are the sum of the four phase counters, including initial calls. Comparisons count only state-equality tests, excluding loop/limit checks. Entry is obtained by the canonical recovery phase without replaying the orbit.
    algorithms::CykAnalysisComplete owned CYK result, triangular chart and actual work. cells is ordered by increasing length, then begin; all cells, including empty ones, are retained. nonterminals lists all grammar ids, including unreachable ids and start, in ascending order. First witnesses try increasing left length then original binary-rule order. Duplicate terminal/binary rules do not create duplicate memberships. No input/grammar views or shared mutable state remain. Empty input rejects and has an empty chart; no epsilon convention is inferred. Public edits are possible; helper access/reconstruction checks local structure rather than certifying an edited result against the original grammar.
    algorithms::CykCellOwned membership and first witnesses for a nonempty half-open byte span. entries is sorted by original nonterminal id and contains at most one entry per id. Empty entries means no nonterminal derives the span. Storage contains no references into grammar/input; begin is zero-based and length is positive.
    algorithms::CykEntryFirst actual derivation establishing one nonterminal in a chart cell. left_length=0 denotes a length-one terminal rule; terminal is then the input byte, left/right are unused zero placeholders and binary_rule is SIZE_MAX. Otherwise the children have original ids left/right, with lengths left_length and cell.length-left_length. binary_rule indexes the original ordered binary vector. Length, start and input live in the containing cell/analysis. A first witness does not count or exclude alternative parses.
    algorithms::CykParseNodeOne node of an owned first-witness parse in preorder. A leaf has length one, terminal equal to its input byte and both child indices SIZE_MAX. A binary node's children partition its half-open span and follow their parent in preorder; terminal is unused zero. Nodes contain original ids. The returned vector's indices remain valid until the caller mutates it.
    algorithms::CykShapeChecked CYK geometry and worst-case dense-state/rule-loop sizes. cells=n(n+1)/2, splits=n(n-1)(n+1)/6, state_slots=cells*m, max_rule_tests=splits*r. These are potential capacities/work, not counts of successful derivations. Empty input has all four counts zero. No ownership beyond scalar values and no shared state.
    algorithms::CykWorkChecked actual operations from the same CYK kernel that recognizes the input. Terminal candidates count raw matching unary-list entries, including duplicates. split_points includes every split, even when an empty child skips the binary rule loop. binary_rule_tests counts rules entered; matching_rules counts those whose two children are present, including repeated/already-known conclusions. new_states counts distinct (span,nonterminal) insertions. No replay or timing estimates; empty input has zero work. Counters exclude grammar preparation, dense initialization, chart extraction, allocation and witness reconstruction.
    cad::CylinderSurface
    algorithms::CZDistinctDegreeStepOne actual distinct-degree step on the current remaining monic polynomial. frobenius is x^(p^degree) modulo remaining_before. bucket is the monic gcd with frobenius-x, possibly the unit [1]. remaining_after is the exact quotient. Previously removed degree buckets are absent. Records own all coefficients.
    algorithms::CZEqualDegreeTrialOne actual random equal-degree splitting attempt, including rejected constants. Candidate coefficients come from the legacy seeded xorshift stream modulo p; they are deterministic and slightly biased, not ideal independent uniform samples. A constant candidate is rejected without gcd/powering (all following polynomials empty). Otherwise initial_gcd is computed first. A proper gcd is accepted directly; else used_character=true and character is h^((p^d-1)/2) mod target. split_gcd then comes from gcd(character-1,target). quotient is set only for an accepted split.

    D

    causal::DAGAn owned directed acyclic graph indexed by node numbers from zero.
    algorithms::DagLongestPathTraceOwned input edges, actual topological order, final paths and every reachable-edge attempt. topological_order covers all n vertices. Initial zero-indegree vertices are queued in ascending id; newly ready vertices are appended in original outgoing edge order. This FIFO policy is deterministic for fixed input, not a global smallest-id order. Original edge order and ready timing determine first ties. predecessor_edge uses m as the source/unreachable sentinel; result's vertex sentinel remains n. No input references or shared mutable state survive. Public edits are possible; witness recovery validates local chains rather than certifying arbitrary edited graphs for optimality or acyclicity.
    algorithms::DagLongestPathWorkActual operation counts for the canonical DAG ordering and relaxation phases. Topological work includes the entire graph, even unreachable components. Relaxation work includes only edges leaving source-reachable vertices. Counts exclude input validation, adjacency construction, output copying, allocation and later path recovery. They count logical visits, not elapsed instructions or wall time. No shared state or borrowed storage.
    algorithms::DagPathOwned source-to-target vertex/edge witness with its stored rounded total. Unreachable paths have found=false, empty arrays and negative-infinite weight. The source's empty-edge path has one vertex and weight zero. Edge indices select the exact original parallel edges. No input references survive.
    algorithms::DagRelaxationOne actual candidate evaluated from a finalized reachable vertex. edge_index identifies the original directed edge. from_distance is final at evaluation; previous_distance may be negative infinity on first discovery. candidate is its checked finite double sum. improved uses strict > without a tolerance, so equal stored values preserve the earlier witness.
    algorithms::DamerauCellAll actual candidates and the selected move at one positive-prefix cell. Prefixes i,j are one-based lengths. last_source is the previous source row holding the current target byte; last_target is the earlier column of this row matching its source byte, captured before the current equality update. Candidate costs are clipped to bound=n+m; an unavailable bridge has bound. This cannot change an interior minimum, which is at most max(i,j)<n+m.
    algorithms::DamerauShapeChecked rectangular capacities and finite sentinel for Lowrance–Wagner. rows=n+2, columns=m+2, cells=rows*columns, interior_cells=n*m, bound=n+m. Empty inputs still have the sentinel/prefix borders. Values are capacities, not operation counts or allocated bytes; no references or shared state.
    algorithms::DamerauTraceOwned inputs, full sentinel table and actual Lowrance–Wagner cell records. table is row-major with shape.columns columns. Ordinary prefix distance D(i,j) is table[(i+1)*columns+j+1]. cells is row-major over positive prefixes, at index (i-1)*target.size()+j-1. Every cell is retained; no replay or snapshots. Strings are literal bytes, including NUL/high bytes, without Unicode decoding, normalization or case folding. Public edits are possible; helper checks are local consistency checks, not a certificate of edited-table optimality.
    algorithms::DamerauWorkActual checked operations of the shared unrestricted-distance kernel. Byte matches count all equal-byte cells, not matches in one recovered script. Eligible bridges have both earlier occurrence indices positive. Selected bridges count winning DP cells, not necessarily edits on the final traceback. Counts exclude initialization, allocation, input copying and script recovery.

They are approximations to real errors, not directed interval bounds. Owned values have no caller lifetime dependency or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::DdaTraceOwned ordinary DDA points, actual accumulators and checked work diagnostics.     geometry::DelaunayAnalysisCoordinate-deduplicated topology counts and exact local empty-circle checks. Counts are independent of triangle order. Duplicate-coordinate ids are mapped to earliest originals. Triangle indices must be valid, distinct in coordinate, exactly CCW, with no duplicate face and at most two incident faces per edge. These checks do not certify global nonoverlap, hull coverage or planar embedding of an arbitrary supplied mesh. minimum_angle_degrees is a scaled floating diagnostic, NaN for no faces and potentially zero after extreme scale loss; it never controls topology. Empty-circle signs are exact for stored binary64.
    geometry::DelaunayInsertionOwned actual cavity removal, directed boundary and replacement for one site. removed/added may contain ghosts, identified by c=the original input count. boundary is ordered by canonical undirected endpoint key but retains the first directed occurrence; shared interior edges are cancelled. Actual face scans precede this event. No full before/after mesh snapshot or geometric replay is retained. All vectors own their entries and have no input lifetime dependency.
    geometry::DelaunayTraceComplete owned sites, earliest-identity mapping, finite mesh and actual events. Numeric coordinate equality coalesces duplicates and signed zeros. Representatives retain earliest input indices in input order. Seed is the first two distinct sites and first later noncollinear site; remaining distinct sites are inserted in input order. Strict positive incircle conflicts retain an existing diagonal on an exact cocircular tie; permutations may therefore select another valid mesh. Final finite triangles rotate their smallest id first and are lexicographically sorted, independent of map/hash traversal. All-collinear/fewer than three distinct sites have no seed, faces or insertion events. All fields own data; public edits are unchecked and independent calls share no mutable state.
    geometry::DelaunayWorkActual seed and cavity operations, excluding validation, sorting and copies. A conflict test is either an incircle test on a finite face or an exact half-plane test on a ghost. Counters exclude CCW checks on newly created faces, between-endpoint comparisons, map operations, allocation, trace copies and final sorting. Initial seed plus three ghosts are excluded from creation/removal counts. No counts are estimates of time or fixed-predicate internal arithmetic.
    stats::DeleteDJackknifeOptionsDelete-d subset budget and deterministic engine seed. Enumerates lexicographic sorted deletion indices if exact C(n,d)<=max_subsets; otherwise draws max_subsets uniform size-d sets independently with replacement across draws. Each draw has no repeated index, but duplicate sets across draws are allowed. Uses retained partial Fisher-Yates permutations, MT19937-64 and std::uniform_int_distribution, so sequences can depend on standard library. Finite B Monte Carlo dispersion uses denominator B to retain legacy semantics; B=1 therefore gives zero dispersion, not evidence of zero sampling variance.
    stats::DeleteDJackknifeResultDelete-d standard-error estimate and actual subset count/mode. Complete variance uses (n-d)/d times population variance over all subsets. In Monte Carlo mode this same formula uses the B sampled replicate values; it is a conditional approximation with a (B-1)/B finite-B variance factor. Larger d alone does not guarantee valid inference for nonsmooth statistics. Original field layout kept; no retained sample/callback or shared mutable state.
    stats::DeleteDJackknifeTraceActual same-execution delete-d sets, replicate statistics and summary. Each sorted deletion set pairs with its actual callback value; no RNG replay or repeated statistic fits. All vectors are owned. Mean/variance describe subset statistics conditional on this input, not the statistic's sampling law.

    algorithms::DepthFirstTraceOwned goal-search or complete source-component DFS state and actual events. n is the parent/depth sentinel; edges.size() is the absent parent-edge marker; 2*n is the discovery/finish-time sentinel, checked representable before graph allocation. Times tick only at discoveries and genuine finishes, starting zero. Seen-but-unfinished vertices therefore have a valid discovery and missing finish. Parent/edge/depth are set on first entry only. preorder contains all entries, postorder only actual finishes. Successful goal search keeps its path active; it does not fabricate unwinding. Full traversal sets goal_requested=false, goal=n, result.path empty and result.found=false, while expanded/preorder exhaust all source-reachable vertices. Every examined arc has exactly one target-state category; unseen arcs cause discovery, active arcs close a directed ancestor cycle (including self-loops), finished arcs need no descent. Counters exclude domain validation, adjacency construction, allocation/copies, result-path extraction and timestamp/event bookkeeping. They are not timings.

    algorithms::DepthRectInclusive integer-pixel rectangle with one constant camera depth. Larger depth is farther; equal-depth objects retain input order, so the later input wins an overlap. Reversed bounds paint nothing. No 3D geometry or depth interpolation is performed. Instances own no external resources.
    nn::models::DepthSplitsOwn custom56-room fitting,validation and test sensor pairs.
    nn::DescriptorKNNResultOwn detached predictions and the neighbors used for each query.
