    stats::DesignMatrixData
    nn::models::DetectionClassEvaluationRetain AP scalars and the precision envelope for one category.
    nn::models::DetectionDatasetEvaluationRetain all-area AP means across categories with selected nonignored truth.
    nn::models::DetectionEvaluationPredictionStore one scored detection before AP matching.
    nn::models::DetectionEvaluationTruthStore one annotated box and dataset ignore flags.
    nn::models::DetectionPyramidLevelDescribe one feature level of a P2–P5 RoI pyramid.
    nn::models::DetectionRoiInputsOwn normalized and pixel RoIs with feature-minibatch indices.
    nn::models::DetectionRoiOutputsRetain class probabilities and class-specific box regression tensors.
    nn::models::DetectionRpnTargetsOwn detached objectness and box targets for a selected scene minibatch.
    nn::models::DetectionSceneConfigConfigure quantized MNIST digits placed on grayscale detection canvases.
    nn::models::DetrConfigConfigure source post-norm DETR backbone, encoder/decoder and learned query set.
    nn::models::DetrOutputsRetain DETR auxiliary logits/boxes from every decoder layer and encoder memory.
    nn::models::DetrTargetsOwn tensor one-hot classes, normalized boxes and matched-query mask for one DETR layer.
    algorithms::DeutschJozsaClassicalResultSequential classical promised decision and actual callback count. Agreement of 2^(n-1)+1 values implies constant only under the promise. n=0 needs one observation. The full table is not certified.
    algorithms::DeutschJozsaResultOriginal two-field numerical Deutsch–Jozsa decision. constant is the compatibility threshold p0>0.5, not a promise certificate. Probabilities are unclipped and may slightly exceed one through rounding.
    algorithms::DeutschJozsaTraceOwned executing-circuit snapshots and observed promise evidence. No replay or repeated oracle evaluation. Basis bit q is qubit q, with q=0 least significant. mean_phase is count-derived (zeros-ones)/2^n in binary64, independently of gate accumulation. No shared mutable state; all arrays own their data. Stateful callbacks describe an observed table, whereas a physical Boolean oracle must describe a fixed function.
    algorithms::DeutschJozsaWorkCircuit oracle, callback, gate and amplitude-pair counts. Excludes allocation, copying, probability extraction and callback internals. A butterfly updates one pair per single-qubit Hadamard.
    sim::DevArmPickEnvironmentHeadless DevArm pick-and-place environment with a caller-selected bin objective. Nine actions operate a bounded Cartesian lattice; numerical IK drives the six real URDF joint coordinates, clamped to limits and limited to 1.5 rad/s. IK accepts up to 12 mm position residual and uses a soft wrist-down preference. The grasp point is end_link local (-.02,0,0) m, between the finger tips. Tool and carried-payload collision guards reject moves through workcell solids. The grasp is an ideal proximity latch with size-dependent jaw aperture and payload orientation stabilization; opening restores dynamic gravity/contact physics. Robot servos are kinematic: this is not torque control, a full mesh-collision robot simulator, or hardware deployment. Observations are privileged state, not image observations. Instances are single-writer and own independent worlds.
    sim::DevArmWristCameraFixed wrist camera with native CPU RGB rendering, matching the real URDF pose. The mount is end_link local (-.09,-.075,.045) m, viewing local (.13,0,0), with local +Z as image-up. These extrinsics never track fruit coordinates. Intrinsics are square pixels, configurable vertical field of view, and a 2 mm near plane. capture() includes real arm self-occlusion and static geometry. Simple backgrounds are cached while joint/finger coordinates stay identical. The attached owner's Realistic visual profile renders complete scenes with shared materials and studio lighting, including cross-object shadows. Validated static/robot triangles are retained while joint/finger coordinates are unchanged; moving actors are always prepared from the supplied frame. The realistic base-only RGB/depth/ID image is retained at that exact pose. Empty actor captures return independent copies; registered references reuse those same base pixels when no non-fruit objects remain. Other reference actors are always rendered afresh. Caches do not alter samples or lighting. The borrowed environment must outlive this single-writer camera.
    compute::DeviceAn explicit backend and ordinal, with no hidden current-device state. CPU accepts index zero only; GPU indices refer to backend enumeration order.
    compute::DeviceInfoDescribe one backend without treating missing support as an available GPU.
    algorithms::DFAOwned deterministic finite automaton with optional missing transitions/start. delta has num_states rows of num_symbols entries, and accept has num_states bytes. Each target is -1 or a valid state. -1 denotes an implicit rejecting sink, which loops on all symbols; start=-1 denotes the empty language. A zero-state DFA requires start=-1. Zero symbols permits only the empty word. Aggregate field order/types remain unchanged; default construction is now a valid empty zero-alphabet machine. Containers own their storage. Read-only calls share no mutable state, provided the aggregate is not concurrently changed.
    algorithms::DFAEquivalenceResultExact whole-language comparison result, optionally with a shortest counterexample. equivalent=true means all reachable product pairs were exhausted, not a bounded word test. If false, witness is a shortest distinguishing word, lexicographically first among that length; an empty witness then denotes epsilon. No witness is provided when equivalent=true. Counters include the implicit rejecting sinks when reached. Containers own their storage.
    algorithms::DhExchangePublic values and raw shared residues from one deterministic toy exchange. Retains supplied g/p and four computed residues, not private exponents. Does not certify a group or protocol. No shared state; raw residues are exposed.
    algorithms::DhPowerCycleComplete cyclic subgroup generated by a validated nonzero prime-field element. values[x]=g^x mod p for x=0..order-1, starting at1. The next product closes back to1; exactly order products are performed. Values are distinct, owned and ordered by exponent. This small-cycle enumeration is not a strength estimate.
    cad::Diagnostic
    graphics::DiagramEditable native method diagrams, exported as standalone SVG without external renderers. Coordinates have equal scales on both axes and y points upwards. Nodes own their labels, wrap words and size themselves from the plotting library's embedded Computer Modern font metrics. Text supports UTF-8 and explicit newlines (not TeX markup). Visible labels use native glyph outlines so viewers cannot substitute a differently sized font; selectable source text and accessible labels are retained. Unicode digit scripts, superscript plus/minus/T and script ell use native base glyphs. Other characters absent from the embedded font render as question marks; accessible labels retain the original text. Arrows join node boundaries. Paths, polygons, ellipses and free labels share one coordinate system. Export fits all primitives, labels, stroke widths and arrowheads, leaving a pixel margin. A diagram wider than max_width is scaled uniformly, retaining its aspect ratio. Mutation is not thread-safe; const export may be called concurrently on an unmodified object. Rendering and storage are linear in the number of primitives and their text/path lengths.
    graphics::DiagramNodeStyleNode appearance and minimum size; text expands the box when necessary. Explicit newlines are retained; long lines wrap at word boundaries within width. An unbreakable word may expand the box. Padding is applied on all sides. Nodes are rounded rectangles, or circles when circle is true. Numeric values must be finite; dimensions and font size are positive, padding and corner radius nonnegative.
    graphics::DiagramPointA diagram coordinate; x grows rightwards and y upwards, in diagram units.
    graphics::DiagramStrokeAppearance of a native diagram path, polygon or ellipse. Values are owned; widths are pixels and RGB opacity is respected. All numeric values must be finite. Width must be positive; RGB channels and opacity are clamped on export.
    geometry::DiameterOptionsComplete input, actual-event and retained-event policies; zero disables a cap.
    geometry::DiameterResultOwned actual farthest endpoints and finite Euclidean separation.
    geometry::DiameterRunOwned actual hull/diameter and selected rotating-pointer work.
    algorithms::DiceBigramCountOne unsigned-byte bigram and its actual left/right/shared multiplicities. key=(first_byte<<8)|second_byte. All 65,536 byte pairs are distinct, including NUL and bytes 128–255. Native trace rows are sorted by this unsigned key.
    algorithms::DiceConsumeEventActual remaining-count transition for one right-hand bigram occurrence. One record per ascending right byte offset, including failed matches. Before and after refer only to this key's unconsumed left count. A miss has both zero.
    algorithms::DiceOverlapChecked multiset sizes, intersection/union counts and normalized overlap. Counts are occurrence counts, not numbers of distinct keys. For a nonempty combined multiset, Dice=2*shared/total and Jaccard=shared/union_count. For two empty multisets both values use the caller's explicit empty-equality convention. Scores use binary64 rounding; integer fields retain exact checked counts.
    algorithms::DiceTraceOwned actual bigram counts, consumed occurrences, inputs and scores. No replay or independent reconstruction: sorted rows and events come from the executing dictionary kernel. Rows include keys seen on either side. The rich trace scans even identical/short inputs, unlike the scalar early-return paths. Containers own their values, including byte strings; no shared mutable state. There is no case folding, trimming, padding, UTF-8 decoding or normalization.
    algorithms::DiceWorkActual occurrence-level operations of the shared consuming kernel. One left dictionary update per left bigram and one right lookup per right bigram. Counts exclude hash collisions/probes, reserve/rehash, equality checks, copies, trace-only row insertion/counting, sorting and score arithmetic.
    algorithms::DifferenceMapResultOriginal result layout with a decoded B-side cross-projection estimate. After positive iterations solution is P_B(f_A(x_before)), not P_B(x_after). At a true fixed point it equals P_A(f_B(x_before)) and lies in both sets if callbacks are actual projections. converged retains only the strict numerical step<tol rule: small beta can hide a large projection gap. It is not a feasibility certificate. With zero iterations, solution=P_B(x0), residual=0 is an unevaluated historical sentinel, and converged=false. Containers own data; defaults are empty/zero.
    algorithms::DifferenceMapStepOwned vectors from one actual four-projection difference-map update. Calls occur in order A(x), B(x), A(f_B), B(f_A). f_A=(1-1/beta)A(x)+x/beta; f_B=(1+1/beta)B(x)-x/beta. estimate_a and estimate_b are the cross projections; x_after=x_before+beta*(estimate_a-estimate_b). Eight n-vectors are retained.
    algorithms::DifferenceMapTraceOwned initial/final iterates, actual steps, decoded result and stop metadata. No replay or independent reconstruction. Callback side effects occur only during the recorded execution; a thrown call returns no partial trace but prior external effects remain. The iterate, B-side estimate and cross-projection gap are distinct. No shared mutable state except what callbacks capture. Empty vectors are valid zero-dimensional states if both callbacks return empty vectors.
    algorithms::DifferenceMapWorkActual callback/update counts and retained-history entry count. Each completed update calls A and B twice and updates n coordinates. A zero budget calls only B once. Counts exclude callback internals, validation, norm arithmetic, copying and allocation. History entries count one per record plus its eight n-vectors, excluding initial/final/result vectors and transient buffers.
    optim::DifferentiableFunctionAn objective function that additionally supports exact gradient evaluation. Optimizers that consume this type (GradientDescent, Adam, LBFGS) use the full gradient at every step.
    nn::DifferentiableKalmanResultFiltered states and innovation diagnostics from a scalar linear Gaussian model.
    optim::DifferentiableSeparableFunctionA function that is both differentiable and separable – the common case for machine learning loss functions (a sum of per-example losses). Optimizers that consume this type (SGD) can update coordinates from a single term's gradient without evaluating the full objective.
    optim::DifferentialEvolutionDifferentialEvolution on the ArbitraryFunction callback interface. Box-constrained differential mutation/crossover with greedy trial replacement. Supports the declared rand1/best1/current_to_best1/rand2 and binomial/exponential strategies. Coordinates seed one clamped member; more than twenty small-best-improvement generations can stop the run. O(population_size*p) storage; no global certificate. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    nn::models::DiffusionGuidanceOutputOwning live class-conditioned predictor endpoints.
    nn::models::DiffusionImageOutputOwning live image predictor endpoints, independent of caller store lifetime.
    DiffusionMapsSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::DiffusionMaps — embeds points via the leading eigenvectors of a dense, alpha-normalized heat-kernel Markov transition matrix, scaled by eigenvalue^diffusion_time. Distinct from LaplacianEigenmaps (sparse k-NN graph Laplacian, no density normalization).
    stats::DiffusionMapsDense Gaussian diffusion maps with alpha degree correction and right Markov eigenvectors. Coordinates are lambda^time D^-1/2 v, where v has Euclidean norm one. Degree weighting, feature units, null handling, time and eigenvalue conventions follow diffusion_maps_trace(). Density independence at alpha one is an asymptotic manifold result under regularity and sampling conditions, not an exact finite-data guarantee. Fit work O(n*n*p+n^3), temporary storage O(n*n+n*p), retained storage O(n*k+n+p). The object owns its results; concurrent const reads are safe. No prediction on new rows.
    stats::DiffusionMapsOptionsDense Gaussian diffusion-map controls, with raw feature units and no automatic scaling. Defaults retain two coordinates, epsilon one, alpha one half and time one. Validated by DiffusionMaps and diffusion_maps_trace().
    stats::DiffusionMapsTraceValue-owned matrices from the actual dense diffusion fit, without replay. All square matrices are n by n in kept-row order. Right eigenvectors have D-weighted norm one, not stationary-probability norm one. Multiply coordinates by sqrt(sum(degrees)) to obtain the latter convention. No input references survive.
    nn::models::DiffusionMlpOutputOwn live compact-MLP prediction and hidden endpoints. Fields retain graphs/storage after this record and the original store are collected; no cached model or optimizer.
    nn::models::DiffusionScheduleOutputOwn all nine detached Double tables of a cosine diffusion schedule.
    nn::models::DiffusionSignalDataOwning detached periodic-waveform fixture with exact source provenance.
    nn::DigitTransducerCompact GRU encoder, label predictor and joint network for spoken digits.
    algorithms::DijkstraPopOwned state of one actual heap removal, fresh or stale. A fresh removal settles the vertex before its outgoing arcs are inspected. Its relaxation_begin/count index this pop's contiguous range in DijkstraTrace::relaxations. A stale pop has zero relaxations. Heap_after is the size after the whole expansion.
    algorithms::DijkstraRelaxationOwned operands and outcome of one actual outgoing-edge inspection. Original edge identity is retained for multigraphs. Equal candidates do not update either the predecessor or heap; no decrease-key or hidden replay occurs.
    algorithms::DijkstraTraceOwned actual removals, relaxations, chosen edge identities and logical work. No input views survive. Histories use O(V+E) storage without full distance/heap snapshots. The trace cap counts pops plus edge inspections, not result arrays or adjacency storage.
    algorithms::DijkstraWorkLogical operation counts of the actual lazy binary-heap execution. Counts exclude validation, adjacency construction and binary-heap comparator calls. Heap pushes include the source; every pushed entry is eventually popped, including stale ones.
    algorithms::DinicAugmentationOwned actual path push, with residual operands copied before mutation.
    algorithms::DinicPathArcOwned before/after values for one oriented residual pair on an actual pushed path. Arc ids 2*i and 2*i+1 denote the forward and cancellation arcs of input edge i. A reverse use decreases the original edge flow. Self-loop pairing remains unambiguous.
    algorithms::DinicPhaseComplete BFS levels and actual blocking-flow work of one search, including termination. Levels stay fixed during a blocking phase. Unreachable vertices have sentinel vertex_count. The final record has unreachable sink, no augmentations and unchanged flow.
    algorithms::DinicTraceValue-owned original input and actual phases/path pushes, captured without replay. Ordinary graph/work storage is O(V+E). Histories add C=P*(V+1)+A+L entries, where P includes final BFS, A counts augmentations and L sums path lengths. Each level, phase, augmentation and path-arc record counts one entry; owned original edges/results/work arrays are outside this optional history budget. No input views survive.
    algorithms::DinicWorkLogical operations in one actual Dinic execution, excluding validation/allocation. BFS scans include zero-capacity, reverse and self arcs of reached vertices. DFS scans include repeated use of a current arc after successful pushes. A pointer advance is permanent within its phase. Path updates count oriented residual pairs, not both writes.
    dstruct::DirectedAcyclicGraph
    algorithms::DirectedArborescenceOwned original-vertex parent and input-edge identities of an optimum arborescence. Success has one entry per original vertex: the root parents itself and has kNoBranchingEdge; every other entry names its selected original incoming edge. Failure leaves both arrays empty and result={0,false}, with no partial tree. Parallel edges retain distinct input identities. Calls own all returned data.
    algorithms::DirectedBranchingResultLegacy owned minimum rooted-arborescence cost and existence verdict. Field types/order/defaults are retained. Success spans all vertices from the prescribed root with outgoing paths; finite negative weights are supported. Failure returns {0,false}; default storage alone has not solved a graph. Manually assigned values are not validated or optimality certificates.
    dstruct::DirectedGraph
    DirListingThe result of dir(): a class's public members, printable and queryable.
    DirMemberOne public member in a dir() listing.
    bayes::DiscreteBayesianNetworkA categorical Bayesian network with one conditional probability table per node.
    rl::DiscreteEnvironmentBorrowed single-writer callbacks; their owners must outlive train_discrete(). Neither callback may mutate a policy concurrently. Exceptions propagate after any already completed progress. Reset seeds are derived independently of action draws.
    algorithms::DiscreteLogThe result of a discrete-logarithm search: whether a solution exists and, if so, an exponent x with base^x ≡ target (mod p).
    algorithms::DiscreteLogOptionsSelected primitive-call and actual-history policies.
    algorithms::DiscreteLogResultVerified discrete logarithm or an explicit unsuccessful bounded search. Legacy aggregate order/types preserved. Success means g^x=h modulo p; failure is not proof of nonexistence. A valid generator has a logarithm for every nonzero target; bounded relation/rank/query work may still fail.
    algorithms::DiscreteLogRunOwned actual exponent outcome and selected work.
    algorithms::DiscreteLogWorkActual selected primitive-call counts; these are not timings or all bit operations.
    rl::DiscreteModelArchitecture and initialization for a native CPU policy.
    rl::DiscreteObservationOwned observation with finite features, a binary feasibility mask and optional table row. Masks have exactly model.actions entries and at least one allowed action, except a true terminal successor may have none. No true class/future state is required.
    rl::DiscretePolicyOwned inference policy; copies require clone(), which never shares learnable storage. Neural scores are native nn tensors internally. Inference is single-writer; optimizer/replay/RNG training state is not part of an inference checkpoint.
    rl::DiscreteTrainingOptionsMatched-window controls for tabular, replay-based and on-policy learning. Checkpoints occur at powers of two from window 128 and at completion. The trainer bootstraps time-limit/window boundaries, never true terminal states. Forced-action chains can be coalesced with exact composed reward/discount; every underlying environment step still runs and sees new arrivals.
    rl::DiscreteTrainingResultTraining evidence and independent inference checkpoints, without optimizer resumption.
    rl::DiscreteTransitionOne actual environment option, preserving terminal versus time-limit semantics.
    rl::DiscreteWindowComplete measured work for one independent training window.
    dstruct::DisjointSet
    geometry::DistanceTransformTraceOwned column-pass intermediates and final feature field from one execution. No full per-line histories are retained. Storage and work are O(rows*columns), plus O(rows+columns) line scratch. The optional cell cap excludes caller input storage.
    geometry::DistanceTransformWorkLogical work of actual one-dimensional envelope sweeps, aggregated for a grid. Counts exclude validation, output initialization, copying and square roots. Empty-site lines scan inputs but evaluate no finite parabola. All counters are checked against wrap.
    nn::models::DistortedMnistOutputsTensor-generated distorted MNIST images and their known output-to-input maps.
    algorithms::DitherRegionStatsColumn-band input/output means and actual binary density. Empty bands have zero means/fraction and pixels0. These are arithmetic summaries, not perceptual fidelity scores or proof of an algorithm having produced the output.
    algorithms::DivisionAnalysisActual exact result and selected producer work, excluding formatting/guards/loop control.
    algorithms::DivisionWideValueExact signed magnitude using two unsigned64-bit words.
    algorithms::DivResultExact unsigned quotient, remainder and actual bit count.
    algorithms::DivResultExLegacy field-order quotient/remainder and algorithm-specific iteration count. Divisor0 retains the historical{0,0,0}sentinel, which is NOT a defined quotient/remainder. Use analyzed/trace valid_divisor to distinguish it.
    algorithms::DixonCollectionOwned positive smooth relations and actual scan progress for a fixed modulus. Input candidates are consecutive integers from floor(sqrt(n))+1, even for perfect squares. Only accepted relations are retained; zero residues are counted separately. This is a deterministic scan, not uniform random sampling.
    algorithms::DixonDependencyAn actual zero row of the eliminated parity matrix and its square congruence. Owns original relation indices and full exponent sums, all even. Both GCDs are retained; the solver selects a proper minus factor first, then plus. A factor need not itself be prime. No combinations of different zero rows are searched, and a trivial congruence can therefore leave the run unsuccessful.
    algorithms::DixonRelationOne positive factor-base-smooth square residue from the actual scan. Owns exponents in the collection's prime order. The empty product is one; residue zero is excluded. No references into solver storage survive return.
    algorithms::DixonTraceOwned actual collection, tested dependencies and logical elimination work. No replay: the same kernel implements dixon_factor(). Collection stops at base_size+1 relations or the candidate budget. All-row GF(2) elimination uses dynamic 64-bit word vectors, so bases and relation sets can exceed 64 bits. Only dependencies visited up to the first proper factor are captured. Captured scalar cells equal base.size()+sum(exponents.size()+3) over relations +sum(relation_indices.size()+exponent_sums.size()+4) over dependencies. The optional cap excludes vector objects and transient elimination storage. Scratch space is O(k*k), in addition to captured output; no shared mutation.
    nn::DLinearOutputFitted projections and the two observed-history components.
    linalg::DMatDense storage policy for la::Mat<DMat, T>.
    nn::models::DncAccessOwn the live DncAccess endpoints of the four-slot DNC preset.
    nn::models::DncLinkOwn the live DncLink endpoints of the four-slot DNC preset.
    nn::models::DnCNNResultOwn predicted signed noise,restored image and every DnCNN stage.
    nn::models::DncStateOwn the live DncState endpoints of the four-slot DNC preset.
    nn::models::DncStepOwn the live DncStep endpoints of the four-slot DNC preset.
    nn::models::DnDataOwn aligned clean,noisy and signed residual tensors.
    nn::models::DnMetricsOwn raw and clipped denoising diagnostics. Host presentation view.
    algorithms::DominoCoverProblemOwned exact-cover encoding of adjacent domino placements on a rectangular board. Cells use row-major IDs r*board_columns+c with row zero at the top. Each placement has exactly two orthogonally adjacent cells. The canonical builder visits cells row-major, adding horizontal then vertical placements. Identical dominoes need no piece-identity column. Public mutable fields are validated by domino_tiling_diagram(); exact_cover() separately validates general incidence.
    algorithms::DoomsdayAnchorOwned monthly anchor with its one-based day of year and computed weekday. All twelve anchors for one year share its doomsday; differences between their ordinal days are multiples of seven. All fields are values, without references.
    algorithms::DoomsdayTraceOwned actual year terms and signed monthly offset for a validated date. No replay: doomsday_weekday() calls this same executing kernel. The monthly reference is January3/4, February28/29, March14, April4, May9, June6, July11, August8, September5, October10, November7 or December12. All fields are values; no allocation or references into caller storage.
    algorithms::DoomsdayYearOwned actual year terms of Conway's Doomsday rule. Uses astronomical year numbering, including zero and negative years, and floor division for centuries. All weekday codes are Sunday=0 through Saturday=6. The dozen decomposition is an equivalent mental-arithmetic identity evaluated alongside the direct offset, not a second weekday solver. Default fields are an uncomputed placeholder, not the terms of year zero. O(1), no allocation, input references or shared mutable state.
    dstruct::DopeVector
    algorithms::DoubleDabbleStepOne owned actual correction-and-shift stage, with padded most-significant-first nibbles. before and after contain decimal digits0..9. corrected can contain8..12 and is an intermediate binary nibble field, not decimal text. carry_out[i] moves from nibble i toward i-1; the rightmost nibble receives input_bit. All four vectors have trace.capacity entries. Default fields are an uncomputed placeholder.
    algorithms::DoubleDabbleTraceOwned actual binary-to-BCD result, steps and logical work from the shared kernel. Captures at most64 stages of at most20 nibbles, without replay. Four nibble snapshots per stage use O(B*D) storage; ordinary conversion/work calls keep O(D) scratch. This finite uint64_t domain needs no optional history cap. Default fields form an uncomputed placeholder, not a computed zero-width result. Caller inputs are unchanged, no borrowed references or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::DoubleDabbleWorkLogical work of the shared fixed-capacity shift-and-add-three kernel. Counts nibble-level operations, excluding validation, allocation, zero trimming, output formatting and trace copies. With B requested bits and D capacity, digit_checks=nibble_shifts=B*D. Corrections and decimal carries depend on the selected value and are equal; these are not CPU timings or hardware cycles.
    dstruct::DoubleEndedQueue
    dstruct::DoublyLinkedList
    nn::DpEpsilonAn (ε, δ) guarantee and the Rényi order that gave it.
    algorithms::DpllEventOwned actual partial assignment at a search event, with original clause identities. assignment has num_vars+1 values: index0=0; other values0(unassigned),+1,-1. node ids start at0 in entry order. Root parent uses SIZE_MAX. Unit/conflict clause is the original zero-based index; all other kinds use clauses.size(). No formula normalization, assignment replay or borrowed state is represented.
    algorithms::DpllMeasurementOwned actual model/verdict and work without search-history capture. Carries no borrowed input references. Defaults are an uncomputed placeholder.
    algorithms::DpllTraceOwned original CNF, actual search events, total result and work from one solve. No replay: the same executing iterative kernel implements ordinary/work calls. Trace entries count1 per formula plus1 per clause plus1 per input literal, then1 per event plus1 per captured assignment element. The cap excludes scalar metadata, working stack, allocator bytes and elapsed time. Root/event capacity is checked before the affected capture; all input validation precedes limits. Zero disables only the optional cap. A cap exception returns no partial verdict.
    algorithms::DpllWorkChecked logical work of the shared DPLL kernel, excluding validation/copies/allocation. nodes counts root and branch entries. decisions counts split points, branches counts attempted children; nodes=branches+1. Clause visits count outer clause-loop iterations of status/unit/pure scans. Literal visits count each inspected occurrence, including both passes over unsatisfied clauses in the pure scan; a second literal pass does not add another outer clause visit. Counters are operations for this implementation, not CPU timings or CDCL work.
    nn::models::DPNBlockOutputsProjected input paths, learned updates and resulting dual-path representation.
    nn::models::DPNConfigDPN release depth, exact width/increment scaling, group override and stem/BN settings.
    nn::models::DPNLayoutReference stem, bottleneck, cardinality and per-stage dual-path metadata.
    nn::models::DPNOutputsStem, four dual-path stages, every unit and final classifier outputs.
    nn::models::DPNPathsFixed-width residual and growing dense tensors, with explicit channel metadata.
    algorithms::DpStepOwned result of one actual unit, pure or resolution elimination. after is the complete normalized formula: ascending distinct literals per clause, lexicographically ordered distinct clauses, no tautologies. Empty after means true; a contained empty clause means false. No subsumption is performed. Adjacent snapshots are related by existential elimination of abs(literal), not equivalence with that variable left free. All counts refer to this transition; positive/negative/pairs/tautologies/duplicates are zero for unit/pure steps. No views into the caller or previous states remain.
    algorithms::DpTraceComplete owned normalized input, eliminating history and SAT verdict. Native ordering is deterministic: check empty clauses/sets first, then first unit, then smallest signed pure literal, then smallest absolute variable. All formulas are canonical as in DpStep. num_vars is a domain bound, not an array allocation: unused and very large sparse ids cost no dense storage. Every step eliminates at least one occurring variable; at most that many steps exist. No satisfying assignment or independent proof certificate is returned. Independent calls share no mutable state; public edits are unchecked.
    algorithms::DpWorkActual rule applications and parent-pair work from one eliminating solve. Pair counts include tautological and duplicate conclusions. Peak counts distinct non-tautological clauses in normalized input or any completed state; excludes old/new coexistence, temporary unions and retained history. Counters exclude validation, sorting, normalization, scans, allocation and snapshot copies. Owned scalar values have no shared state; they are not elapsed-time estimates.
