    nn::models::DreamEvaluationOwn one scalar feature objective and its ordinary Float32input derivative.
    nn::models::DreamStepOwn one bounded input-ascent result and its explicit line-search diagnostics.
    nn::models::DropPathOutputsMasked branch, sampled gate and broadcast scaling multiplier.
    algorithms::DStarLiteGridPersistent D* Lite for a rectangular four-neighbor unit-cost occupancy grid. Owns g/rhs labels and an indexed binary heap with at most one entry per vertex. Planning runs backward from a fixed goal; Manhattan priorities and a checked movement modifier let changed edges/new starts reuse prior state. Cell bounds must fit int and total cells<=INT_MAX. A shortest simple route has at most N-1 edges; backups at N or more are saturated to infinity, retaining every possible optimum and bounding integer labels. Priorities use exact uint64_t arithmetic; modifier headroom of4*N is reserved before moving the start. Blocked goal has rhs=infinity; unblocking restores its zero boundary. Blocked endpoints yield no route. No diagonals, weighted terrain, moving goal, sensor inference or automatic movement are included. Copying owns an independent full planner. Concurrent mutation of one instance needs synchronization. Each repair can touch the whole grid; there is no guaranteed speedup over fresh search. Heap operations are O(log N), backup degree<=4, persistent storage O(N), plus caller-requested trace.
    algorithms::DStarRepairOwned route and actual interval work from one successful repair call. Default fields are an uncomputed placeholder. All caller data remain owned by the planner or this return value; no borrowed references are retained here.
    algorithms::DStarStepOwned scalar operands/results of one actual popped vertex, without replay. rhs_after includes any self update; predecessor backups may affect other vertices.
    algorithms::DStarTraceOwned initial/final labels, original live queue and actual repair pops. Entry accounting is5*N+initial_open.size()+steps.size(): grid cells,four label arrays,one per initial queue record and one per pop record. Scalar metadata, planner working storage, paths and allocator bytes are excluded. The complete base cost is checked before copies; each new pop entry before queue/label mutation. On a trace cap exception completed earlier pops remain in the planner; a later repair resumes correctly. work_before distinguishes already pending work from pops captured in this call. Initial/final labels outside the needed frontier can remain stale/infinite; only current-start optimality is guaranteed at termination.
    algorithms::DStarWorkLogical work since construction or the previous successful repair. Includes pending map/start updates and current repair. Counts exclude input validation, heap comparisons/swaps, snapshots and final route extraction. Neighbor checks count actual Bellman backup neighbors, including blocked ones. Work is not elapsed time; a resumed capped repair may include prior completed pops.
    algorithms::DtmfPeaksOwned eight-frequency results and first-maximum keypad candidate, not a validated detection. In results from dtmf_peaks(), the first four targets are rows697/770/852/941Hz, then columns1209/1336/1477/1633Hz. Default construction leaves the target array zero-filled; dtmf_peaks() fills the grid and all responses. row/column index their own four-element groups. Equal powers retain the first index. Empty input and silence choose candidate '1' by ties. No energy, duration, frequency tolerance, level ratio, speech or noise validation is performed. Finite negative raw powers remain visible. All fixed-size results own scalars; no input aliases or mutable shared state survive.
    geometry::DTWComputationOwned ordinary result and logical work, without retained cost-table history. Scratch consists of two cost rows and one predecessor byte per positive cell. No input references survive return. Copies own independent result paths.
    geometry::DTWResultOwned unrestricted scalar DTW result, preserving the original three-field layout. Distance is the unnormalized sum of absolute differences along the returned inclusive path. Default construction is an uncomputed placeholder. Copies own independent buffers. Positive lengths fit int; steps advance a, b or both by one.
    geometry::DTWTraceOwned input, actual accumulated costs and chosen predecessors from one DTW run. Positive cells are row-major at i*b.size()+j; sentinel border is implicit. Costs and predecessor codes are captured during the original recurrence, not reconstructed afterward. Infinite cells mark unrepresentable costs. Logical capture entries are a.size()+b.size()+2*a.size()*b.size(): one per input scalar, cost and direction. Result paths, rolling scratch rows, scalar metadata and allocator bytes are excluded. Copies are independent.
    geometry::DTWWorkLogical work of the shared DTW recurrence and actual traceback. These are counts, not time. Validation, allocation, copies, comparisons and rendering are excluded. Each positive cell reads three predecessor slots, including infinite boundary slots. Every returned pair counts one traceback step.
    nn::dtype_ofMaps a C++ element type to its dtype: dtype_of<float>::value == DType::Float32.
    nn::dtype_of< bool >Maps C++ bool storage to the tensor boolean dtype.
    nn::dtype_of< double >Maps C++ double elements to tensor Float64 storage.
    nn::dtype_of< float >Maps C++ float elements to tensor Float32 storage.
    DualSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::autodiff::Dual – a first-order forward-mode dual number. Build an expression out of named operations (starting from a seed with derivative=1) to read off an exact derivative alongside the value.
    autodiff::DualA first-order forward-mode dual number: tracks a value together with its derivative with respect to a single seed variable through every operation. Evaluating a function on a Dual seeded with derivative=1 computes both the function's value and its exact derivative in one forward pass.
    cad::Dual
    nn::models::DuelingQPathLive endpoints of mean-centered dueling action values.
    dstruct::DynamicArray
    nn::DynamicLossScaleHost loss-scale policy, advanced only after explicitly applied/skipped updates. A good-step interval doubles the scale up to maximum. overflow() halves it down to minimum and clears the good-step count. Neither call changes a model/optimizer. Value-owned state; serialize it separately for exact dynamic-scale resume. Do not mutate one instance concurrently. No GPU or automatic optimizer integration.
    nn::models::DynamicsGaussianLive per-member Gaussian prediction of state delta and reward.
    nn::models::DynamicsPredictionLive next-state and reward endpoints of an explicit model prediction.

    E

    algorithms::EarleyItemOne dotted original production and its origin column. In chart column k, prod names an original production, dot counts matched RHS symbols and 0<=origin<=k. Equal triples in a column are deduplicated; duplicate input productions retain distinct prod ids. Standalone default fields are a placeholder, not a claim that a production exists. Copies own their scalars.
    algorithms::EarleyLocationNumeric location of an item in an owned Earley chart. Both default coordinates are earley_no_item, denoting no parent. Validity depends on the containing trace; copying does not retain a pointer into it.
    algorithms::EarleyReasonOwned first-insertion evidence attached to one actual chart item. Parents are numeric chart locations, always lexicographically earlier than the target. This gives an acyclic first-witness deduction graph even for nullable cycles. Duplicate attempts do not replace the first reason. It is not a packed parse forest and does not enumerate all derivations. Default is a placeholder.
    algorithms::EarleyResultOwned recognition verdict, legacy-compatible column sizes and actual work. The temporary chart/indexes are discarded; no input or provenance is retained. Default is an uncomputed placeholder. A computed chart_sizes has N+1 entries, including empty columns, even for an undefined start or rejected input.
    algorithms::EarleyTraceOwned actual chart and first-insertion reasons from one Earley recognition run. Copies own independent grammar/token/chart buffers. Items keep insertion order and original production ids; reasons[k][i] explains chart[k][i]. Full chart closure supports epsilon, unit cycles, left recursion and ambiguity, but returns no parse forest or count of parses. Empty RHS means epsilon; symbol strings, including empty strings and embedded NUL, are opaque atomic names. A symbol is nonterminal exactly when it occurs on a LHS. A missing start production rejects. Logical capture cost is base+2I, where base=2N+P+sum(rhs lengths)+2 and I is the number of unique items. Base counts start/LHS/RHS/token strings and one column metadata record per boundary; each item and its reason count once. String bytes, runtime indexes, scalar fields and allocator overhead are excluded. Editing returned records may invalidate numeric references; no automatic repair occurs.
    algorithms::EarleyWorkActual logical recognition work, excluding compilation, hashes, allocation and capture copies. Every item is processed once. Predictions run once per requested nonterminal per column; completion joins each waiter with each distinct completed span once. Counts are not execution time and checked uint64 arithmetic cannot wrap.
    nn::EarlyStoppingTracks a validation metric and decides when to stop (tflow nn::EarlyStopping).
    algorithms::EasterDateOwned Gregorian Easter month/day with the historical field order and types. Computed dates lie from March 22 through April 25. Value-initialized zeros are a placeholder, not a computed date. No year, timezone, input reference or historical calendar-adoption information is retained.
    algorithms::EasterRangeSummaryOwned first-tie extrema and 35 date counts for an inclusive year range. Bins zero through 34 mean March 22 through April 25 on a fixed March axis. Counts describe deterministic Gregorian ecclesiastical rules over the selected years, not an astronomical forecast or a random-sampling probability model. Earliest/latest compare month/day, not chronology; equal dates keep the first ascending year. Storage is constant, with no per-year records or allocation. Default storage alone is not a valid summary.
    algorithms::EclatResultCanonical frequent itemsets and work, without retained intersection history.
    algorithms::EclatStateOne observed singleton or actual conditional intersection in an Eclat run.
    algorithms::EclatTraceOwned evidence captured during the actual iterative Eclat traversal.
    algorithms::EclatWorkChecked logical work counters for one sorted-tidset Eclat run.
    algorithms::ECMAdditionActual affine addition operands, denominator GCD, inversion and resulting point.
    algorithms::ECMAnalysisOwned actual bounded-search result and work; n means failure or no proper factor, never a prime certificate.
    algorithms::ECMCurveOwned actual generated curve and its final observed outcome.
    algorithms::ECMHasseStudyExact uniform integer count of B-smooth candidates in a small prime Hasse interval. This is not a distribution of elliptic-curve orders or a measured ECM success probability. Prime-power divisibility by the stage1 multiplier is stricter than B-smoothness alone. Counts include1 as the empty prime product.
    algorithms::ECMOptionsExplicit bounded stage1 search settings; no stage2 or primality certificate.
    algorithms::ECMPointOwned normalized affine residue coordinates or the point at infinity.
    algorithms::ECMTraceOwned complete actually generated curves and evaluated slope denominators; no replay. Complete result or exception: each record quota is admitted before appending; unknown future curve/denominator counts are not reserved as invented work. Default one million actual records;0 disables optional cap. Excludes fields, point components, capacities, output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM.
    algorithms::ECMWorkActual selected stage1 operation counts; excludes validation, sieve, allocation and elapsed time.
    cad::Edge
    nn::EdgeWhere a gradient goes: input slot input_nr of node.
    algorithms::EdgeBetweennessActual raw and conventional undirected edge betweenness on canonical edges.
    algorithms::EdgeBetweennessTraceAn owned ordinary result and complete online primitive event history.
    algorithms::EdmondsKarpAugmentationOne actual bottleneck push along a recorded BFS parent path. path runs from source to sink. search identifies its complete pre-push BFS; amount is the minimum positive residual on that path. Copies own all records.
    algorithms::EdmondsKarpPathArcBefore/after values of an actual oriented residual pair on a pushed path. Input edge i owns arc ids 2*i (forward) and 2*i+1 (cancellation). Reverse use decreases that edge's original flow, preserving independent identities for parallel, antiparallel and self edges. Values are copied during the actual push.
    algorithms::EdmondsKarpResultOrdinary owned flow result and work, without retained search/path history. Inputs remain unchanged and independent calls share no mutable state. No optional capture quota applies; ordinary working storage is O(V+E).
    algorithms::EdmondsKarpSearchFull actual BFS levels and first-discovery parents before a path push. Unreachable level is vertex_count; source and unreachable parent ids are SIZE_MAX. Every successful search has exactly one augmentation at the same vector index. The last search fails to reach the sink and supplies the returned source cut.
    algorithms::EdmondsKarpTraceOwned original network and search/path evidence captured without replay. Logical capture C=E+1+P*(1+2V)+A+L: E input records, one network header, P full BFS headers/levels/parents (including failure), A augmentation headers and L path-arc records. Result copies, runtime arrays, scalars, vector capacity and allocator bytes are excluded; this is not a peak-RAM limit. Histories add O(C) work/storage. Mutable records are inspectable data, not self-certifying proofs.
    algorithms::EdmondsKarpWorkChecked logical operations from the actual complete-BFS Edmonds-Karp run. Counts exclude validation, allocation, copying, certificate checks and CPU time. Each BFS scans every outgoing residual arc of every reached vertex, including zero, reverse and self arcs. The final failed search is included.
    nn::models::EfficientDetConfigConfigure EfficientDet source variant and explicit compact geometry overrides.
    nn::models::EfficientDetSpecRetain EfficientDet compound backbone/pyramid/head/resolution metadata.
    nn::models::EfficientNetConfigEfficientNet B0 through B7 forward configuration.
    nn::models::EfficientNetScalingReleased EfficientNet width/depth/resolution/dropout coefficients.
    nn::models::EfficientNetV2ConfigEfficientNetV2 S/M/L or base B0 through B3 forward configuration.
    nn::models::EfficientNetV2VariantReleased EfficientNetV2 block table and scaling coefficients.
    algorithms::EigenPairOwned real Rayleigh estimate and a normalized represented vector. Shared with fixed-shift inverse iteration; no convergence certificate is implied.
    nn::EighResultEigen decomposition of a symmetric matrix.
    nn::EigResultEigen decomposition of a general real square matrix (TF Eig).
    ElasticNetSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::ElasticNet — regularized linear regression fit by coordinate descent (alpha=0 is ridge, alpha=1 is lasso); see also the Ridge and Lasso convenience facades below.
    stats::ElasticNetElastic-net penalized least squares via cyclic exact-coordinate descent. Accepts Formula numeric/categorical main effects and interactions. Rows with a null formula value are dropped; retained design entries and responses must be finite. With an intercept, centre X/y; without one, use a zero origin. Optional predictor scaling uses sqrt(sum((x-mean)^2)/n), including for indicator/interaction columns; exact zero scales become one. Response is never standardized. Published slopes and intercept are restored to raw formula-design units; penalties apply to scaled slopes. Automatic paths share a grid derived from the full training set. Each validation fold fits its own predictor/response offsets and predictor scales on training rows, using the fixed full-data Formula schema, and pools held-out squared errors by row. Selection minimizes this MSE, retaining the first (largest lambda) on exact ties. The selected full-data path fit supplies coefficients; exhausted fits are retained and flagged, not silently removed from selection. Inspect fold and path status. Cyclic descent uses actual column norms, including zero/constant columns. Stopping requires max_change<=tol and KKT<=tol*max(1,max_j(abs(X_j^T*y/n))) in preprocessed coordinates. A finite iteration limit returns a partial fit, with converged=false. Positive lambda*(1-alpha) gives a strictly convex slope objective; lasso/OLS can have nonunique coefficients on dependent designs. No covariance, p-values or confidence intervals are inferred from selected coefficients. Unlike the rescaled 2005 elastic net estimator, this implements the direct glmnet-style penalized objective. Owns fitted state, leaves input unchanged; const methods have no mutable caches. One t-sweep fit costs O(t*n*p); a length-L, F-fold path costs O((F+1)*L*t*n*p), plus Formula expansion, with numerical storage O(n*p+L*p+F*L).
    stats::ElasticNetOptionsGaussian elastic-net controls in glmnet's lambda/alpha parameterization. The objective is RSS/(2*n)+lambda*(alpha*L1+(1-alpha)*L2_squared/2), applied to preprocessed slope coefficients. The intercept is unpenalized; response is not scaled. CV-only path/fold controls are ignored for a fixed nonnegative lambda.
    nn::models::ElementaryFlowOutputOwn a live elementary planar/radial map and its per-row determinant diagnostics.
    rl::MapElites::EliteCandidate retained as the elite of one cell.
    cad::Ellipse3
    algorithms::EllipsoidCutOne actual factored central cut, without an objective or convergence claim. support_bound=||lower^T*g|| is computed at the input state. Log volumes are measured from the input/output positive diagonals. center_changed is false if rounding left every coordinate unchanged; an optimizer treats that as stagnation.
    algorithms::EllipsoidIterationActual subgradient query at one recorded sample, with its accepted-cut decision. No callbacks are retained and no explanation is replayed. A terminal iteration has updated=false. state_index identifies the pre-cut objective sample.
    algorithms::EllipsoidOutcomeDetailed finite outcome with best point, last state and an explicit stop reason. last_support_bound belongs to the most recent subgradient query, which can precede the final state if the last allowed iteration performed an update. has_support_bound is false when max_iter=0. Ordinary/work calls retain no input or iteration history, have no optional capture quota, and own their output.
    algorithms::EllipsoidResultBest evaluated point, its objective and attempted oracle iterations. Retains the original three-field layout. iterations counts subgradient calls, including a terminal zero/tolerance/stagnation check; it is not the number of successful cuts. A best point alone does not certify convergence. Copies own x.
    algorithms::EllipsoidSampleActual objective evaluation at an owned ellipsoid state. Initial sample is followed by exactly one sample for each committed cut. objective is the center value; best_value is the smallest evaluated value so far. The ellipsoid algorithm need not decrease the current center objective.
    algorithms::EllipsoidStateOwned ellipsoid E={center+lower*u : ||u||<=1} with a triangular shape factor. The lower matrix is n by n, finite, exactly zero above the diagonal, with positive diagonal. Thus P=lower*lower^T is positive definite mathematically; forming P explicitly may lose this property through floating cancellation. Public values are mutable; entry points validate shape before access.
    algorithms::EllipsoidTraceOwned actual objective samples and subgradient attempts from the same optimizer run. For dimension n, each sample costs S=1+n+n*n entries (record, center and all stored factor entries) and each iteration I=1+n (record and gradient). Thus C=samples*S+iterations*I. The returned outcome, callbacks, runtime buffers, row/container metadata, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded; quota is retained history, not peak RAM. No input/callback views survive.
    algorithms::EllipsoidWorkChecked logical counts from the actual callback/cut execution. Counts exclude validation, geometry preparation, allocations, copying, logs, candidate arithmetic and CPU time. support_products counts lower-factor terms in L^T*g for nonzero oracle gradients, including terminal tolerance attempts. factor_entries_updated counts committed lower-triangle entries, not all writes.
    stats::EmbeddingSeparationUnnormalised class-centroid sums and their external separation ratio. Total scatter equals within plus between, up to floating-point error. Ratios use no degrees-of-freedom correction and are not F statistics.
    nn::models::EmpiricalTcOutputOwn exact finite-mixture log densities and signed pointwise total-correlation ratios.
    nn::EnableGradGuardTurns recording on for its lifetime (inside a NoGradGuard).
    nn::EnasControllerBernoulli architecture controller and moving reward baseline. The second decision has a separate logit for each possible first choice.
    geometry::EnclosingCircleCheckTolerance-aware distances and containment diagnostics for a supplied circle. Residual is hypot(point-center)-radius. A point passes when residual is at most1e-9*max(1,radius). Counts describe tolerance, not exact support identities.
    geometry::EnclosingCircleEventActual containment test and optional immediate boundary rebuild. Depth0 tests the next outer point,1 tests a preceding point under one fixed boundary point,2 tests under two. A failed test immediately rebuilds from one/two/three points respectively. Later nested events can rebuild again.
    geometry::EnclosingCircleTraceOwned original/order data and actual seeded incremental history. Capture units count original points, shuffled point copies, permutation IDs and event records. Scalar final/initial circle fields are not additional units.
    nn::models::seq2seq::EncodedOwn Encoded source graph endpoints or configuration.
    nn::models::EncoderClassifierOutputOwn frozen-code, standardized-feature and linear-head endpoints.
    nn::models::bert::EncoderPathOwn EncoderPath source graph endpoints or configuration.
    filter::EnsembleKalmanFilterThe (stochastic, "perturbed observations") Ensemble Kalman Filter: represents the state distribution as a finite ensemble of sample state vectors rather than an explicit mean/covariance, propagating each member through the true nonlinear f (plus sampled process noise) and estimating the covariances the Kalman update needs from the ensemble's own sample statistics. Like UnscentedKalmanFilter, needs no Jacobian; unlike it, scales to very high-dimensional states (the classical use case this filter was designed for – e.g. geophysical data assimilation with millions of state variables) since its cost scales with ensemble size, not state dimension squared/cubed. Statistical, not exact: converges toward the optimal (linear-Gaussian case: KalmanFilter's) estimate as ensemble_size grows, with Monte Carlo sampling noise at any finite size.
    game::EntityOwned scene components; spatial is the single source of transform and velocities. spatial.position/rotation/dimensions describe the entity even when physics is disabled. Enabling physics uses all spatial fields as the rigid-body settings. No Lua source is executed: behavior names refer to explicitly registered native factories.
    cad::EntityName
    rl::environments::EnvOwn the Env simulation state or interface.
    rl::environments::EnvBaseOwn the EnvBase simulation state or interface.
    nn::EpisodeScoresFeatures and class predictions for one episode.
    rl::EpisodicNoveltyScore novelty relative to a memory of states visited this episode.
    optim::EqualityConstrainedFunctionSmooth equality-constrained objective for constrained optimizers.
    optim::EqualityQuadraticEuclidean projection onto sum(x)=total, with exact KKT control. The optimum is target-(sum(target)-total)/dimension in every coordinate. Raw gradients at a constrained optimum generally do not vanish. Pure owned fixture.
    algorithms::EqualizationOptionsComplete rectangular row/pixel caps for the owned diagnostic entry point. Each zero disables its policy; row objects and pixels are separate units. Limits are not bytes/peak RAM and exclude fixed256-entry diagnostics/capacities. Shapes and representability are checked before policy caps or output allocation.
    algorithms::EqualizationTraceOwned output and actual fixed-size CDF/mapping tables from one producing execution. No replay or per-pixel history. Integer counts are exact size_t values; the map retains the legacy double formula and half-up conversion, not a rational certificate. Constant/empty input uses the identity mapping; the output still clamps any out-of-range input. All arrays and image rows copy independently.
    algorithms::EqualizationWorkSelected actual producing histogram/CDF/map/output visits, not elapsed time. clamped_pixels counts distinct input locations outside0..255, once in the histogram pass, not both clamp reads. Other fields exclude validation, allocation and diagnostic storage/bookkeeping; counts are not total FLOPs.
    optim::EstimationOfDistributionEstimation of Distribution Algorithm (EMNA-style, full-covariance Gaussian) on an ArbitraryFunction within a box constraint. Unlike explicit-operator methods (GA, DE) or covariance-adapting methods (CMA-ES), EMNA builds an explicit multivariate Gaussian model of where the good solutions are each generation – re-estimating its mean and covariance from scratch as the empirical mean/covariance of the current generation's elite, with no smoothing or evolution paths – and samples the next generation directly from that model. Derivative-free.
    optim::EstimationOfDistributionOptions
    geometry::EuclideanDistanceFieldOwned distances, squared distances and nearest-site coordinates on a rectangular unit grid. Nonzero input cells are sites. Ties choose smaller column, then smaller row, following column-first separability. Without sites, both distance fields are positive infinity, nearest_row uses row count and nearest_column uses column count. Rows are numbered downward. Distances are between cell centres; no padding, outside sites, obstacles or path-cost model.
    nn::EuclideanGraphStepUpdated coordinates and scalar node features.
    algorithms::EuclideanMstOutcomeOwned planar minimum spanning tree and actual complete-graph work. Point indices are preserved, including separate vertices at identical coordinates. The output owns its edge records; no inputs or optional trajectory are retained.
    algorithms::EuclideanMstTraceOwned points and actual Kruskal trace on their complete Euclidean graph. Pair edges are generated lexicographically (i,j), i<j, with stable ties in that order. Captured entries C=N+M+S count N point records plus the nested M input-edge and S actual scan records. N+M is checked before any generated graph/copy; nested steps reserve online before scanning. Default one million; zero disables only quota. Output tree, runtime graph/sort/DSU state, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded, so this is not a peak-memory bound. Points, nested trace and output are all owned; exceptions expose no partial result. No independent optimization replay is performed.
    algorithms::EuclideanMstWorkActual distance and stable Kruskal work from a complete planar graph. Each unordered point pair is measured once with hypot, before sorting. Logical counts exclude coordinate validation, allocation, sorting and CPU time.
    algorithms::EuclidOutcomeOwned unsigned-range Bezout certificate and work from one actual kernel execution. Ordinary/work calls keep only running scalar states and this result; they do not allocate optional row history or apply a capture quota. Certificate follows the same signed-truncation ordering as the legacy API, with exact widened intermediates. No borrowed input, shared mutable state or explanatory replay.
    algorithms::EuclidRowOne actual raw Euclidean remainder and its signed-wide Bezout row. remainder=s*a+t*b holds mathematically for the trace inputs. Initial rows are (a,1,0) and (b,0,1), with divided=false and quotient=0 unused. Each derived row has divided=true and the actual truncation-toward-zero quotient that produced it. The terminal zero row is retained. Signed compiler-supported128-bit fields allow quotient2^63 and terminal coefficients beyond int64 without wrapping. These raw rows are not rewritten by the separately reported final sign normalization.
    algorithms::EuclidTraceOwned actual raw rows and unsigned-range outcome from the shared extended-Euclid loop. For D actual divisions, rows/captured_entries=2+D WHOLE ROW RECORDS, including two initial rows and the terminal zero row when a division occurs. Input scalars, result/work metadata, vector capacity, runtime and allocator bytes are excluded; this is not peak RAM. Initial two records are quota-checked before allocation; each next record is admitted before its division and append. Default max_rows one million; zero disables only quota. Arithmetic/container checks remain. Exceptions expose no partial trace. Every returned container owns its values; ordinary calls retain no optional history. Final sign normalization lives in outcome, while raw rows preserve the actual signed-truncation computation.
    algorithms::EuclidWorkActual Euclidean divisions, coefficient updates and final normalization flag. Each quotient/remainder iteration counts one division and two coefficient updates, including an initial zero quotient when input magnitudes are reversed and the terminal zero-remainder update. sign_normalized records the actual final three-value sign flip. Counts exclude validation, copies, allocation, CPU time and arbitrary-precision bit cost; native input width bounds these counters.
    algorithms::EulerOutcomeOwned intrinsic trajectory, nominal step size and actual work. Every Euler call returns N+1 samples, including both endpoints. Ordinary/work calls keep the intrinsic trajectory but no optional derivative history or capture quota. step_size is the finite rounded nominal h; sample times follow euler_method()'s documented grid rounding. A successful run is not an error estimate or a guarantee of stability/accuracy for the supplied ODE.
    algorithms::EulerTraceOwned actual derivative vectors alongside the same execution's intrinsic trajectory. derivatives[i] is the exact callback vector at solution.t[i], solution.y[i]. The final sample has no derivative query. No callbacks are retained or replayed. Logical capture C=(2N+1)(d+1) counts N+1 sample slots with d state entries and N derivative slots with d derivative entries. All C is checked before history copies or callbacks. Default one million; zero disables only that quota. Other outcome metadata, runtime state/callback storage, vector headers, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded: C is not peak RAM. Copies own all samples/derivatives. Failures return no partial trace; callback side effects before a later callback/arithmetic failure remain the caller's responsibility.
    algorithms::EulerWorkLogical work from the actual fixed-step Euler execution. Counts exclude validation, time-grid construction, allocation, history copying and CPU time. rhs_calls counts actual callback invocations; scalar_updates counts committed component updates, not floating instructions. Complete results have steps=rhs_calls=N and scalar_updates=N*d. Exceptions expose no partial result.
    rl::planning::EvaluationPolicy prior and current-player value returned by a leaf evaluator.
    stats::SplitConformalClassifier::EvaluationCoverage and set-size statistics on a labelled test set.
    stats::SplitConformalRegressor::EvaluationCoverage and width statistics on a test set.
    nn::EvidentialRegressionPredictionNormal-inverse-gamma parameters for one continuous response per row.
    nn::EvidentialRegressionVariancePredictive variance components for the normal-inverse-gamma model.
    optim::EvolutionStrategyClassic self-adaptive (mu, lambda) / (mu+lambda) Evolution Strategy with a single global step size mutated log-normally each generation (Rechenberg 1973, Schwefel 1981). This is the pre-CMA-ES form – no covariance matrix adaptation – and is the foundational lineage CMAES (also in this module) descends from. Derivative-free, box-constrained.
    optim::EvolutionStrategyOptions
    algorithms::ExactCoverNodeOwned snapshot of one actual index-linked dancing-links node. Node IDs are indices into a trace mesh. Root is zero; required-column headers are 1..C and data nodes follow input row/entry order. column is a HEADER NODE ID, not a zero-based problem column. Root column/row are -1; header column points to itself and row is -1. Data row is the original input row ID and size is zero. Header size is its current vertical list length. Mutable records do not validate their own links; they own integers rather than pointers into another object.
    algorithms::ExactCoverOutcomeOwned first-cover result and actual search/restoration work. Uses the same deterministic search as exact_cover(). The runtime mesh is fully restored even after success; the first selected-row result is retained separately. Ordinary/work calls retain no optional input, event or mesh-snapshot history.
    algorithms::ExactCoverResultFirst exact-cover verdict and selected original row indices. Preserves the original bool/vector field layout. A solved result covers every required column exactly once; an unsolved result has an empty row vector. Empty universes are solved by the empty selection. Row order is actual search order, not sorted order. Copies own rows; default construction is unsolved.
    algorithms::ExactCoverStepOwned actual residual-column and selected-row state at a search event. column_sizes has C entries: -1 for a covered column and actual nonnegative vertical-list size for an active column. partial_rows is the actual selected-row stack at this event; depth equals its length. column/row use zero-based problem IDs, or -1 when inapplicable. At unselect_row, the pivot column is still covered even though that candidate has been popped. These are live captures, not replay.
    algorithms::ExactCoverTraceOwned actual search states and initial/final dancing-links meshes. All inputs, nodes, events and output rows are owned. Initial/final nodes are copied from the actual runtime mesh; every successful/failed search unwinds fully, so those arrays agree exactly. No explanation is reconstructed by another solver. Let R be input row count, I total incidences and K=1+C+I nodes. Known base capture B=R+I+2K counts row records/incidences plus two NODE RECORD snapshots (each entire seven-field node counts as one record). Each event costs 1+C+depth: event record, column sizes and selected-row IDs. B is reserved before graph/copy allocation; events are reserved before snapshot copies. Default one million; zero disables only quota. Ordinary output/work, runtime mesh/stack/validation, vector headers, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not peak RAM. Any failure returns no partial trace; caller input is never mutated.
    algorithms::ExactCoverWorkChecked logical operations from the actual iterative dancing-links execution. Initialization, validation, allocations, snapshots, copying and CPU time are excluded. Column scans count every active header visited by the minimum-size heuristic. Link writes count assignments even if their value is unchanged. Every completed successful or failed search restores its mesh: covers=uncovers and row_attempts=row_restorations. Search remains exponential in the worst case.
    nn::ExactImageShapleyOwned exact-enumeration fixed-baseline Shapley values and actual coalition scores. patch_values is Float64 [R,C]; coalition_scores is Float64 [2^P], indexed by ascending integer masks with patch zero the least significant bit. All retained tensors are detached independent storage. Base/full are actual endpoints, and efficiency_residual=sum(patch_values)-(full-base), including rounding error. Exact means no coalition sampling, not exact real arithmetic or causal evidence. Attributions may be signed; changing baseline, partition or score changes the game.
    algorithms::ExchangeSortWorkOwned sorted values and actual key-operation counts for exchange sorts. Key comparisons count evaluations of left>right, excluding loop control, copying, index initialization and gap arithmetic. Passes include the final zero-swap scan. Empty/singleton inputs perform no passes. Counters are checked before increment. No references or shared state are retained.
    cad::Expansion
    rl::replay::ExperienceOwn one discrete or continuous transition with terminal-only bootstrap suppression.
    algorithms::ExpGolombDecodedOwned complete decoded values, consumed prefix length and actual work. The count argument is an upper limit. A complete frame ending earlier returns fewer values; hitting the limit leaves any tail unread. consumed_bits identifies that exact boundary. A malformed attempted word throws instead of returning partial output. No input, optional span history or capture quota is retained.
    algorithms::ExpGolombEncodedOwned bit-vector payload and actual encoding work. bits follows vector<bool> specialised storage, with no byte serialization or endianness format defined. Order k and outer framing are supplied by the caller. Empty input produces empty bits and zero work. No optional history/quota is kept.
    algorithms::ExpGolombSizeExact coded bits and a positive-common-width binary payload comparison. For nonempty input fixed_width=max(1,bit_width(maximum)); all-zero values thus use one bit per field by this convention. Empty input has zero width/counts and maximum zero. fixed_bits=values*fixed_width. Order/count/width framing and storage overhead are excluded. Computing a count does not promise available output memory.
    algorithms::ExpGolombTraceOwned actual bit vector, values and spans from the shared Exp-Golomb execution. Encoding owns the complete output bits and copied input values. Decoding owns the entire input vector, including unread tails, plus actual complete values. There is no explanatory replay. consumed_bits equals output size for encoding and actual prefix length for decoding. Logical C=B+2N counts retained bit positions, value entries and whole word records. Encoding reserves known C before copies or emission; decoding reserves whole input B before copying, then two entries online before each value/span append. Default one million; zero disables only quota. Other metadata, runtime/capacity/container headers/allocator bytes are excluded: C is not peak RAM and is not a byte-packing format. Exceptions expose no partial trace; every returned container owns its values. Caller mutation is independent.
    algorithms::ExpGolombWordActual emitted/parsed word with zero-run, quotient and low-bit boundaries. All half-open indices address the trace bit vector. [begin,payload_begin) is the zero run; [payload_begin,suffix_begin) is binary(q+1), including its leading one; [suffix_begin,end) contains k raw low bits. At UINT64_MAX,k=0 the quotient payload is a real 65-bit sequence, not a wrapped uint64 value. Records own scalars.
    algorithms::ExpGolombWorkLogical values and emitted/consumed bits from the actual Exp-Golomb kernel. zero_prefix_bits counts only leading zeros; quotient_bits includes the leading one and remaining quotient-plus-one binary digits. suffix_bits counts the k raw low bits per value. bit_visits is their sum, excluding preflight, allocation, copies, validation and CPU instructions. Unread input tails are not visits.
    nn::ExplicitRatingOne centered rating between a row and a column of a sparse matrix.
    stats::ExponentialSmoothingExponential smoothing (Holt-Winters family): simple exponential smoothing (no trend, no seasonality), Holt linear trend (with optional damping), and seasonal Holt-Winters (additive or multiplicative), unified under one class the way R's HoltWinters() and statsmodels' ExponentialSmoothing() are – which components are active is controlled entirely by ExponentialSmoothingOptions::trend/seasonal.
    stats::ExponentialSmoothingOptions
    algebra::ExprA symbolic expression tree over +, -, *, /, ^ (power) and sin/cos/exp/log, supporting symbolic differentiation, basic algebraic simplification, and numeric evaluation. Value type wrapping a shared, immutable node tree – copies are cheap and structural sharing across copies is always safe since nodes are never mutated after construction.
    vector_expr::ExpressionShared read-only range and materialisation API for lazy numeric nodes. Lvalue Vector leaves are borrowed; temporary Vectors and all child nodes are owned. Borrowed leaves must outlive evaluation. Reads see their current values and lengths. Copies of a node copy any temporary vectors that it owns.
    stats::ExprNode
    algorithms::ExtendedGcdLegacy signed gcd and Bezout coefficients, preserving the three-int64 field layout. For returned results, gcd>=0 and the mathematical identity a*x+b*y=gcd holds. Evaluate products in a wider type: int64 products can overflow even when the identity is small. Actual legacy gcd(0,0) returns {0,1,0}; this corrects the old comment claiming zero coefficients. A gcd of2^63 cannot fit this record and extended_gcd() throws instead. Manually constructed records are not validated.
    algorithms::ExtendedGcdCertificateUnsigned gcd and signed canonical Bezout coefficients for the entire int64 input range. gcd is at most2^63, so INT64_MIN magnitudes are representable. Actual final coefficients fit signed int64; intermediate/terminal-zero coefficients need wider arithmetic. Mathematical a*x+b*y=gcd requires widened evaluation, not unchecked int64 multiplication. The returned zero-pair certificate is {0,1,0}. Default or manually assigned fields do not prove a solve; bezout_certificate_valid checks both the identity and common-divisor conditions without overflowing.
    filter::ExtendedKalmanFilterThe Extended Kalman Filter: the standard first-order generalization of KalmanFilter to a nonlinear model x_k = f(x_{k-1}) + w_k, z_k = h(x_k) + v_k – linearizes f and h (via numerical Jacobians, see detail::numerical_jacobian()) about the current state estimate at every step and otherwise runs the exact same predict/update algebra as the linear filter. Exactly reproduces KalmanFilter's result when f and h happen to be linear (their Jacobian is then the same constant matrix everywhere).
    nn::models::ExtendedRecurrentOutputFlat live endpoints of the compact recurrent extension presets.
    cad::ExtrusionSurface
    algorithms::EytzingerLayoutTraceOwned complete-tree layout and chronological placements from its actual construction. Empty input gives empty vectors and zero capture. Logical optional capture C=N counts whole placement records only; ordinary output layout, metadata, vector capacities and allocator/runtime bytes are excluded. This is not peak RAM. O(N) output/history storage plus O(log(N+1)) recursion; no replay or input alias.
    algorithms::EytzingerPlacementOne actual in-order assignment from sorted input to a complete-tree node. Owns its integer value and both zero-based positions; retains no input pointer.
    algorithms::EytzingerProbeOne actual element inspection and chosen transition in an exact-match tree search. Owns its snapshot, with no input alias. Match terminates immediately. A missing chosen child terminates an unsuccessful search without accessing outside layout.
    algorithms::EytzingerSearchTraceOwned exact-match answer and actual chronological probe snapshots from one execution. Empty layout has no probes. Logical optional capture C=P is whole probe records, with P=result.probes=probes.size(); input, metadata/capacity/allocator/runtime bytes are excluded. No peak-memory claim. Stored values survive input mutation.

    F

    cad::Face
    nn::models::FaceNetConfigConfigure eleven NN1 convolutions,two maxout layers and128D output.
    nn::models::FaceNetOutputsOwn raw128D embeddings,normalized embeddings and13 stage maps.
    cad::FaceSurface
    stats::FactorAnalysisExploratory common-factor covariance model fitted by iterative principal axes. For centred rows Z, models C approximately as Lambda*Lambda^T+diag(Psi), with unit-variance uncorrelated latent factors and diagonal variable-specific variance. This is PAF, not R factanal's maximum-likelihood estimator or a minres optimizer. Each reduced matrix replaces C's diagonal with clipped communalities; negative retained eigenvalues become zero. SMC initialization and regression scores use an eigenvalue-floored inverse, floor 1e-8*max(diag(C)); this is not a pseudoinverse. Orthogonal varimax preserves the common covariance, not the identities of factors. Factors are ordered by squared loading sum, signs by largest-magnitude loading. Rows with any null selected feature are dropped; other retained values must be finite, with positive sample variance in every selected column. Repeated names, invalid options and unrepresentable arithmetic are rejected. Negative parameter- count df is allowed for exploration, not certified identification. Boundary fits can converge: check diagnostics(), raw_uniqueness and covariance residuals. Existing uniquenesses() remain clipped nonnegative; reported communalities remain actual squared loading norms and may exceed observed variance (Heywood violation). Owns fitted state; inputs unchanged; const operations share no mutable caches. For t extraction steps, bounded Jacobi sweeps and small k, main work O(np^2+t*p^3), plus bounded rotation work; storage O(np+p^2+t*p) including the iteration history.
    stats::FactorAnalysisOptionsControls iterative principal-axis factoring (PAF), not maximum likelihood. Both extraction and optional pairwise varimax use max_iter/tol. Extraction's absolute tolerance is in fitted variance units; rotation uses its normalized objective.
    algorithms::FactorizationRunOwned complete prime multiset and selected work, without historical records.
    algorithms::FactorizationTraceOwned actual complete prime multiset and recursive producing histories.
    rl::foundations::FactorizedDensityOwn independent categorical density factors with symmetric Dirichlet priors.
    nn::models::FactorVideoConfigConfigure full-depth R(2+1)D-18 or P3D-199.
    nn::models::FactorVideoOutputOwn full-depth factorized video logits,pooled features and residual endpoints.
    algorithms::FalsePositionEvaluationOne owned actual callback evaluation from endpoint initialization or a trial. Records the returned finite value without retaining or calling the function again.
    algorithms::FalsePositionOptionsIndependent policy, function-unit and coordinate-unit controls for secant bracketing. Zero residual or coordinate tolerance disables that test; callback zeros always stop. Endpoint zeros are checked before sign rejection; endpoint residual-only acceptance is not performed. All controls are validated before callbacks/capture.
    algorithms::FalsePositionOutcomeOwned result, terminal reason, actual work and true-versus-weighted bracket state. For a trial stop, a/b and their values/weights describe the bracket used to compute the returned estimate, before its terminal update. Endpoint zero collapses that state to the zero endpoint; same-sign rejection keeps original inputs, default RootResult and infinite radius. Input order is retained, so a need not be less than b. Radius is the rounded maximum estimate-to-endpoint distance, possibly infinity for a full-width interval; not an outward-rounded certified error bound. Small residual does not imply small coordinate error. No callback or input reference is retained; independent calls share no state.
    algorithms::FalsePositionStepActual pre-update bracket, true values, artificial weights and one evaluated trial. Pre-update terminal tests leave replaced=0; weight underflow can follow an actual replacement/halving. Raw signs certify the bracket under caller assumptions; weights only choose the secant. Snapshots own all values and are never reconstructed by another solve.
    algorithms::FalsePositionTraceOwned outcome and callback/step records captured during the same actual solve. Logical optional capture C=evaluations.size()+steps.size() counts WHOLE records: both endpoints cost2 and each evaluated trial adds2. Metadata, ordinary result, capacities and allocator/runtime bytes are excluded; this is not peak RAM. Quota is admitted before both endpoint calls and before each trial's arithmetic/ callback; zero disables quota only. No partial trace escapes an exception.
    nn::models::FcnConfigConfigure released FCN stride variants or a compact all-stage VGG adaptation.
    nn::models::FcnOutputsOwn FCN linear logits and coarse/skip/fused score features.
    nn::models::FcosConfigConfigure FCOS backbone, shared group-normalized towers and distance units.
    nn::models::FcosOutputsRetain five-level FCOS logits, positive distances and centerness logits.
    nn::models::FcosTargetsOwn detached FCOS classes, ltrb targets, positives and centerness.
    cad::Feature
    nn::data::FeatureOne tf.train.Feature: exactly one of the three lists is used.
    nn::data::FeatureColumnsFit immutable numeric/categorical feature state on selected training rows.
    nn::models::FeatureObjectiveOwn selected-feature response and the two explicit image-prior penalties.
    nn::models::FeaturePyramidOutputsRetain unsmoothed top-down maps and separately smoothed pyramid outputs.
    cad::FeatureResult
    nn::models::bilstm_tagging::FeaturesLive source Features endpoints with owning tensor handles.
    nn::data::FeatureSpecNamed input column and its encoding kind.
    nn::FeatureStandardizerFrozen population moments for column standardization.
    cad::FeatureTree
    fem::FEM1DSolve steady or transient one-dimensional divergence-form problems with P1 Galerkin FEM. Models -(p*u')'+q*u=f and u_t-(p*u')'+q*u=f on a caller-supplied mesh. Requires at least two finite strictly increasing nodes, finite coefficient/ boundary/source data and finite assembled arithmetic with nonzero Thomas pivots; those mathematical/geometry preconditions are not fully validated. Positive p, nonnegative q/Robin data and adequate constraints give the usual coercive model. Piecewise-constant p/q can be scalar or one per element. Results own their values; input mesh/data are unchanged. Calls share no mutable global state, while callback side effects/concurrency belong to the caller.
    fem::FEM1DResultOwned nodal P1 steady solution, with checked scalar accessors for language bindings. The continuous finite-element field is the piecewise-linear interpolant of these values; nodal agreement alone does not imply agreement between nodes. Copies own their arrays, with no mesh/callback alias. Public edits can break array consistency; accessors check the actual requested vector bounds.
    fem::FEM1DTimeSeriesOwned initial state and actual strictly advancing backward-Euler time slices. Solver output has one u row per time and one value per spatial node. Initial time zero/u0 are retained as supplied; later rows satisfy imposed boundary data. Times retain rounded nominal-step products with a shortened final interval; an already reached endpoint is not appended twice. Copies retain no mesh/source alias. Public edits may break consistency; accessors check actual vector bounds.
    fem::FEM2DGalerkin finite-element solver for the 2D Poisson equation -k * (u_xx + u_yy) = f(x, y) on a triangular mesh, using piecewise-linear (P1) Lagrange elements and Dirichlet boundary conditions only (this "basic" 2D solver does not offer FEM1D's Neumann/Robin options). Internally assembles a sparse stiffness system and solves it with the conjugate-gradient solver (datamunge::linalg::cg) – the assembled matrices themselves are never exposed, matching this codebase's rule that linalg's sparse/dense matrix types are never SWIG-bound.
    fem::FEM2DResultThe nodal solution of a 2D FEM Poisson solve.
    dstruct::FenwickTree
    algorithms::FermatBaseCensusExact exhaustive counts over a specified half-open Fermat base interval. Counts are integer census results, not samples or posterior probabilities. Passes are necessarily coprime, so passes/coprime is the conditional pass fraction only when coprime>0. Passes/total is the unconditioned interval fraction only when total>0. Empty intervals have all counts zero; no fraction is fabricated. Owned scalars and constant driver storage, with no shared state.
    algorithms::FermatBaseResultOwned exact result of one Fermat congruence and its actual gcd. Tests base^(n-1) modulo n using canonical mod_pow, plus std::gcd. A failure proves n composite; a pass does not establish primality. Noncoprime bases cannot pass. No shared state, retained references or floating arithmetic.
    algorithms::FermatOutcomeOwned result and actual work counts of bounded Fermat splitting. For odd n, start_a is the exact ceiling root; last_a and last_b are the last actual trial and its exact floor root of a squared minus n. Trials count square tests, including a hit; increments count moves between tested a values, hence trials-1. An even input has zero trials, increments and a/b metadata. Returned_factor matches fermat_factor(); cofactor is n/returned_factor when a square or even branch completes, and zero at TrialLimit. Proper_split requires both factors greater than one. Results own their scalars and share no state.
    algorithms::FermatPrimalityOutcomeOwned result, actual round count and last state of seeded Fermat testing. Requested rounds stay separate from completed rounds; early filters perform zero congruences. Last base/gcd/residue are zero for filters, otherwise actual values from the last tested round. True means prime for SmallPrime and only probable prime for RoundLimit. Scalar ownership has no shared mutable state.
    algorithms::FermatPrimalityTraceOwned actual seeded round records captured during one Fermat test. C=captured_entries=rows.size() counts whole FermatBaseResult records. The solver admits a record before drawing its base or computing gcd/power; no replay and no nested exponent-bit history. Input/output scalars, capacity, allocators and runtime storage are excluded, so C is not peak RAM. Copies are independent; editing rows does not recompute the stored outcome.
    algorithms::FermatStepOne actual odd Fermat square test, owned without input references. Difference is computed in unsigned 128-bit arithmetic before its exact integer root b. Square reports equality of b squared and difference; b is not rounded from floating arithmetic. Rows come from the solver, never a replay loop.
    algorithms::FermatTraceOwned same-pass Fermat outcome and optional actual trial history. C=captured_entries=rows.size() counts whole FermatStep records, not scalar fields or bytes. Quota admission occurs before square/root work and storing each row. Input/output scalars, vector capacity, allocator and runtime storage are excluded: C is not peak RAM. Copies are independent; editing a row does not recompute outcome. Even inputs capture nothing. Ordinary/work calls store no optional history and impose no history quota.
    algorithms::FibonacciDecodedOwned complete positive values and work from strict whole-frame parsing. Every input bit must belong to a complete representable codeword; unfinished tails are errors, not padding. Empty bits give no values. No borrowed input references survive, and no partial result is returned on a parse error.
    algorithms::FibonacciEncodedOwned packed-bool encoded payload and actual emission work. Empty values give empty bits. Output uses vector<bool> storage; no byte order, serialization, padding or external frame metadata is defined. No optional history/capture quota; copies own their buffers independently.
    algorithms::FibonacciSearchOutcomeSearch result and actual logical work of the shared Fibonacci kernel. Result.probes counts element inspections including a possible final equality fallback and repeated clamped indices. Comparisons counts executed key-value <, > or == tests: upper main branch one, lower/equal main branch two, fallback one. Transitions counts nonmatching main-loop schedule updates. These exclude index/bound checks, instructions, cache events and timings. No optional history.
    algorithms::FibonacciSearchProbeOne actual read and pre/post schedule transition in Fibonacci search. Main decisions are+1 for key above value,-1 for key below value,0 for match. Fallback performs only equality and uses decision2 for a miss; it does not compute an unexecuted ordering comparison. Match and fallback preserve sizes and offset. Fields are owned snapshots, never replayed or borrowed.
    algorithms::FibonacciSearchScheduleInitial exact consecutive Fibonacci sizes for a sorted-array search. For positive length, starts at small=0,middle=1,large=1 and grows until large>=length. Growth_steps counts actual additions, excluded from probes. Empty length has all-zero sizes/counts. Length is checked against ptrdiff_t maximum before arithmetic, making the first covering Fibonacci sum fit size_t. Owns scalar state, no allocation or shared mutation.
    algorithms::FibonacciSearchTraceOwned actual Fibonacci outcome and chronological element-read records. C=captured_entries=probes.size()=outcome.result.probes counts whole optional records, including repeated positions and final fallback. Metadata, input, capacities, allocators and runtime storage are excluded: C is not peak RAM. No input copy or retained reference. Copies are independent and edits do not recompute outcome. Ordinary/work calls keep no optional history or quota.
    algorithms::FibonacciTraceOwned same-pass Fibonacci bits, values, spans and work. Logical capture C=B+2N counts B retained bit positions, N value entries and N whole FibonacciWord records. Scalars, vector capacity/headers, allocators and runtime temporaries are excluded: C is not peak RAM. Encoding admits complete C before copies/emission. Decoding admits B before copying, then two entries online per complete word before its value/span append. Copies are independent; edits do not recompute work/spans. No nested digit history.
    algorithms::FibonacciWordActual half-open span and overlapping delimiter of one complete word. Begin and end address FibonacciTrace::bits. Payload is [begin,end-1); the two-bit delimiter occupies [delimiter_begin,end) with delimiter_begin=end-2. Its first one is also the highest payload digit. Indices are owned scalars, not iterators. Spans are captured during emission/parsing without replay.
    algorithms::FibonacciWorkLogical complete-value and bit counts from the actual Fibonacci codec. Payload_bits counts Zeckendorf digits, including their highest one. Each word adds one terminator bit; bit_visits is their sum. Counts exclude table lookup, preflight, greedy candidate checks, copying, allocation and CPU instructions. Empty inputs give zero counts; scalars are owned without shared state.
    graphics::FigureA finished figure of any kind (a single plot or a grid of panels) with one output interface: title(), size(), to_svg()/to_png()/to_pdf(), save*(), and show().
    FilterPipeline step created by filter_rows(); keeps rows where the predicate is true.
    algorithms::FiniteDifferencePoissonResultOwned grid, assembled Poisson system and numerical residual from one native solve. Arrays own their storage; no source callback or caller references are retained. source[i], rhs[i] and residual[i] refer to interior node x[i+1]; x and u include both boundary nodes. The residual is A*u_interior-rhs for the stored binary64 matrix and RHS, evaluated with long-double intermediates, then rounded to double. It measures the discrete solve, not PDE accuracy.
    optim::FireflyAlgorithmThe Firefly Algorithm (Yang, 2008/2009): a population of fireflies is pairwise attracted toward brighter (better) neighbors, with attractiveness decaying with squared distance and a shrinking random-walk term for exploration. Derivative-free, O(n^2) per iteration in the population size.
    optim::FireflyAlgorithmOptions
    nn::models::FireOutputsSqueeze activations, both Fire expand branches and their concatenation.
    optim::FISTAFISTA on the ProximalFunction callback interface. Classical t recurrence (1+sqrt(1+4*t^2))/2 and extrapolated gradient points, followed by the supplied proximal map. Stops on successive accepted-coordinate displacement. No adaptive restart, backtracking or monotonicity safeguard. Supply the correct proximal dimensions and a rate at most 1/L for the standard convex bound. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::FISTAOptionsConfiguration for FISTA; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    algorithms::FitchAnalysisSame-run minimum score, actual node masks and one minimum-change witness.
    algorithms::FitchEdgeOne actual top-down witness child-state assignment.
    algorithms::FitchStepOne actual postorder state-set write and score update.
    algorithms::FitchTraceOwned inputs and actual complete scoring/witness history.
    algorithms::FitchWorkActual checked postorder and witness-assignment counts.
