    game::FixedClockFixed-step accumulator; callers execute returned ticks in their own application loop. This library owns no window, process main loop or wall clock. Each instance is single-writer and stores only the unconsumed fraction of a fixed tick.
    algorithms::FlashsortClassGroupConsecutive class-index range and its total original occupancy.
    algorithms::FlashsortMoveOne actual carried-value exchange before the finishing insertion sort.
    algorithms::FlashsortTraceOwned original, class-grouped and sorted states plus actual class/carry evidence. A nonshortcut capture admits C=5n+2m entries before copying: input, output, grouped values, original assignments, at most n carry records and two m-entry class arrays. Shortcut C=2n stores only input/output; other arrays are empty. Counts are entries, not bytes or peak RAM. No sorting/assembly is replayed.
    algorithms::FlashsortWorkActual work and class occupancy from one native Flashsort, without a history. Min/max comparisons count two ordered tests per element after the first; classifications counts every actual value-to-class call, including leader searches. permutation_writes counts carried-value exchanges, including cycle closure. Insertion comparisons count predecessor>key evaluations (including false ones), shifts count successful predecessor moves, and placements count final key stores. Loop-bound/finite-validation tests and allocations are excluded. n<=INT_MAX keeps these whole-run uint64 counters representable. No timing claim.
    algorithms::Fletcher16ByteStepOne actual modulo-255 byte fold from the production Fletcher-16 kernel. Residues use the canonical representation 0..254; byte 255 contributes zero modulo 255. Before/after values describe the actual sequential fold, not replay.
    algorithms::Fletcher16FlipOne independent single-input-bit corruption, recomputed by the same full-message fold. Bit numbering is byte-major, least-significant-bit first within each octet. delta_a and delta_b are modular differences, not XOR popcounts or probabilities.
    algorithms::Fletcher16FlipScanOwned complete one-bit census and its exact full-message byte-fold budget. Every candidate toggles/restores one owned scratch message. The original view is unchanged and never retained. Empty input has zero records and counters.
    algorithms::Fletcher16ReplacementOne replacement candidate at a fixed byte position, including the unchanged control.
    algorithms::Fletcher16ReplacementScanOwned exact 256-candidate single-position replacement census. There are 255 changed candidates and one unchanged control. A zero/255 original has one changed candidate that aliases; other originals have none. Records are complete actual folds, not an assumed detection theorem.
    algorithms::Fletcher16TraceOwned complete actual byte states for zero-initialised raw Fletcher-16. No input view survives. Empty input has checksum/residues zero and no events. The packed raw tag is B in the high byte and A in the low byte; it is not a protocol-specific pair of complemented check bytes.
    algorithms::FloodFillNeighborOne ordered neighbor slot; invalid slots have zero row and column. Four directions are up/down/left/right; eight are NW/N/NE/W/E/SW/S/SE.
    algorithms::FloodFillNeighborhoodFixed-capacity ordered neighborhood without allocation or grid storage. Unused slots are zero initialized; count is zero for an invalid center.
    algorithms::FloodFillProbeOne actual direction attempt and its value before any discovery paint. Outside slots have value zero; accepted means an in-bounds target match.
    algorithms::FloodFillTraceOwned input, output and evidence recorded during the actual fill. No retained views or replay; modifying caller storage cannot change this result.
    algorithms::FloodFillVisitOne actual LIFO pop and its contiguous range of neighbor probes. Stack sizes exclude/include the current scan's discoveries respectively.
    algorithms::FloodFillWorkOwned scalar measurements of one actual iterative fill. Each discovered cell is painted when pushed and popped once. Neighbor slots include outside probes; in_bounds_neighbors counts actual value reads. A preexisting replacement-valued cell is a barrier, not a traversal bridge.
    algorithms::FlowCertificateNumerical primal/dual checks for a public maximum-flow result. Feasibility and cut equality are tested separately. A nonzero tolerance gives numerical agreement, not an exact proof; every error and the signed gap remain visible.
    nn::models::FlowDataOwn paired observed frames,published flow and provenance metadata.
    nn::models::FlowerDataOwn observed flower RGB images,zero-based class labels and original source IDs.
    nn::models::FlowerSplitsOwn disjoint fitting,validation and test flower subsets.
    nn::models::FlowInverseOutputOwn a live inverse map and its analytic log absolute determinant.
    nn::models::FlowMatchingStepOutputOwning live Euler or RK4 stage endpoints, with no full trajectory.
    nn::models::FlowMetricsOwn endpoint,angular and strict optical-flow outlier diagnostics. Host presentation view.
    algorithms::FlowNetworkOwned directed capacitated fixture, with explicit terminals and isolated vertices. Generators validate capacities and checked output counts before allocation.
    nn::models::FlowPreparedOwn observed flow data and its cached multiscale supervision.
    nn::models::FlowResultOwn full-resolution flow,pyramid fields and internal activations.
    nn::models::FlowScaleOutputOwn a live transformed point batch and accumulated scalar or per-row log determinant.
    nn::models::FlowSplitsOwn fitting,validation and held-out scene-family splits.
    nn::models::FlowStudyDiagnosticsOutputOwn all three flow-study sample diagnostics, independent of fitted family.
    nn::models::FlowStudyPointsOutputOwn detached two-dimensional observations and their audited component labels.
    nn::models::FlowSupervisionOwn five tensor pyramid targets in fixed input-image displacement units.
    nn::models::FlowVaeOutputOwn all eighteen Gaussian, conditional-flow, density and reconstruction endpoints.
    cv::FlowVectorThe estimated motion of one tracked point between two frames. valid is false when the point's window was too close to the image border, or too textureless/aperture- ambiguous (the same "does the structure tensor have two strong eigenvalues" criterion shi_tomasi_corners() uses to pick good points to track in the first place – Lucas-Kanade windows should generally be centered on such points).
    nn::models::FlowWarpResultOwn backward-warped image and detached full-window coverage.
    algorithms::FloydCycleStepOne actual Floyd pair after a complete movement or a no-call phase reset. Detection pairs are x_t and x_(2t), with t starting at one. Locate resets tortoise to x0; measure holds tortoise at the recovered entry. Original-orbit indices distinguish equal labels reached at different times. Each row precedes that pair's equality test; phase resets are not callback evaluations.
    algorithms::FloydCycleTraceOwned actual Floyd pairs and work from the ordinary detector kernel. Recording adds O(mu+lambda) storage and no callback calls or orbit replay. No retained callback/input views. Failure returns no partial trace.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergNeighborOne guarded future-neighbor slot and its fixed numerator over16. Outside coordinates are zero placeholders. Direction order is right, down-left, down, down-right with numerators7,3,5,1. No grid storage is retained.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergResultOwned binary integer output and actual native work. Values are0or255; storage is an int grid, not a packed one-bit bitmap.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergStencilOwned fixed-capacity future-neighbor geometry. A valid center has four slots, including outside ones; an invalid center has none.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergStepOne actual raster quantization and its update range. Boundary loss uses the missing numerator over16 in long double. Values already include all prior diffusion; they are not clamped to the nominal grayscale range.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergTraceOwned original/output grids and actual raster/update evidence. Records are captured during the ordinary kernel, without replay. Caller storage is never retained or modified; failures return no partial result.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergUpdateOne actual floating-point update to a future cell. Only in-bounds updates are stored, in the original direction order. The transfer is computed as error*numerator/16.0 in double, preserving the historical order.
    algorithms::FloydSteinbergWorkActual raster counts and signed tone-balance diagnostics. Nominal grayscale units are0..255; finite values outside that range are accepted without clamping. Boundary loss is the sum of error times discarded weight in long double, not an absolute error. Balance residual includes floating rounding. Empty images have zero counts/sums/extrema. Diagnostics are not perceptual scores.
    algorithms::FloydWarshallOutcomeOwned ordinary matrices and actual work without history. Uses the same seeding and k/i/j kernel as the original API; no replay.
    algorithms::FloydWarshallRelaxationOne actual strict improvement in k/i/j execution order. The left/right entries are read immediately before the update; in a negative cycle sweep they can change within that same k stage. A record is not a failed comparison or an edge seed. The selected hop is the actual next[from][k].
    algorithms::FloydWarshallStageOwned actual matrices at one admitted-intermediate boundary. Admitted0 is the seeded state. Admitted k+1 follows the complete k sweep. Snapshots are raw execution states; affected negative-cycle entries do not have shortest-path meaning. No negative-cycle flag is fabricated before its final scan.
    algorithms::FloydWarshallTraceOwned graph, raw matrices and evidence captured during the executing sweep. Contains seeded and every post-k matrix, plus only strict successful improvements. No input views, rerun or independent alternative algorithm is retained.
    algorithms::FloydWarshallWorkActual seeding, guarded sweep and final diagonal-scan counts. Counts refer to the executing kernel, excluding input validation, allocations and optional snapshot copying. Each finite candidate costs one addition and one strict comparison; equal-cost candidates keep the existing next hop. All counts are checked by representable full sweep bounds before matrix allocation.
    algorithms::FNVBucketProfileCounted bucket occupancy and distinct-key integer-hash collisions. All fields own their values. Bucket pairs count unordered INPUT RECORD pairs sharing a bucket, including duplicates. Hash pairs count unordered DISTINCT byte-key pairs with equal full-width integer hashes. These are different events. Numeric dataframe columns convert counters to double, exact up to 2^53.
    algorithms::FNVStepActual before/XOR/after state for one consumed byte, in integer hash order. Owns primitive values, not a view into the input. Unsigned word arithmetic wraps.
    algorithms::FNVTraceOwned hash value and one complete actual record per consumed byte. Empty input retains zero records and its offset basis. Copying owns independent history; input and ordinary scalar state are excluded from the record quota. This is O(n) retained storage, unlike the ordinary hashes' O(1) state.
    nn::ml::FoldOne complementary training/validation partition with zero-based row positions.
    nn::FoldedLinearA linear layer's weight and bias after folding a batch norm into it.
    algorithms::ForceDirectedFrameOwned state of one actual sweep. Repulsion is captured before attraction; displacement is the actual net accumulator after attraction. Positions follow all vertex moves. No replay or separately rounded force sums.
    algorithms::ForceDirectedMetricsIndependent widened geometry and regularized force potential. Diagnostics use long double, O(n squared + m) work and O(1) auxiliary storage. They do not run the layout or mutate input. Potential is an integral of this implementation’s regularized law, not a monotonicity or optimality certificate.
    algorithms::ForceDirectedOutcomeOwned ordinary coordinates with actual work. No history is allocated; the shared kernel performs each sweep once.
    algorithms::ForceDirectedTraceOwned initial, raw, normalized and per-sweep states. All arrays own storage; caller mutation is independent. There are no frames for n<2 or zero sweeps. Final centering/scaling changes units and potential.
    algorithms::ForceDirectedWorkActual kernel counts and final normalization metadata. Counts exclude validation, allocation, capture copies and optional metrics. Uniform values count distribution invocations, not raw engine words. Inactive n<2 returns without normalization.
    nn::ForecastBaselinesFits, forecasts, and lead-wise errors for four point baselines.
    nn::ForecastWindowBatchA batch of observed histories and their subsequent forecast targets.
    stats::FormulaA parsed model formula such as "y ~ x1 + x2", R's formula object.
    algorithms::ForwardBackwardOutcomeOwned inference tables and actual work from the same kernel. All arrays own storage; caller edits are independent. There is no additional phase-history copy because the result already contains the actual tables.
    algorithms::ForwardBackwardResultOwned actual scaled forward/backward tables and smoothed state marginals. Historical field layout retained. For positive representable evidence, alpha rows are filtering distributions; beta uses terminal beta[T-1]=scale[T-1] and is not a probability distribution. In exact arithmetic sum(alpha[t]*beta[t])=scale[t], so gamma is explicitly normalized. Impossible sequences have log_likelihood=-infinity and zero gamma placeholders, not defined posteriors. Empty observations have empty arrays and log likelihood0.
    algorithms::ForwardBackwardWorkActual once-only inference counts, excluding validation and allocations. Transition terms count pair visits: one product plus accumulation in the forward pass, two products plus accumulation in the backward pass. Support probes run only on the first zero predictive mass to distinguish a mathematically impossible prefix from numeric underflow. No replay or diagnostic arithmetic is included.
    algorithms::FourierGateOne actual gate call and its immediately resulting complete state. For Hadamard the control equals target and angle is zero; for Swap control/target are the swapped bits.
    algorithms::FPGrowthHeaderOwned node-link indices for one observed item in a captured tree. Headers are returned by ascending item ID; each node-index list preserves actual creation order. It replaces a linked-chain view with independent owned indices. Sum the referenced node counts for item support in this conditional tree.
    algorithms::FPGrowthNodeOne actual FP node in creation order, with a checked full-width parent ID. Node0 is the dummy root with item SIZE_MAX, count0 and parent SIZE_MAX. Other nodes may legitimately carry item SIZE_MAX; root identity comes from index0, never the item value. Counts are weighted prefix occurrence totals, not edge probabilities.
    algorithms::FPGrowthResultOwned canonical frequent sets and actual work without history. Uses the same executing kernel as capture. The ordinary output is never counted as retained trace-history quota. No input mutation or shared state.
    algorithms::FPGrowthStepOne actual DFS emission followed by its conditional pattern base. Step order is the original depth-first mining schedule. Pattern is the emitted unsorted suffix sequence. Empty ancestor paths are omitted from base. A nonempty base always builds a child tree, even if filtering leaves only its root. SIZE_MAX child means no nonempty base and no child build; no replay is used.
    algorithms::FPGrowthTraceOwned raw baskets, actual trees, emissions and weighted conditional bases. Retained history is admitted online before each associated copy/move. Base entries are N+raw occurrences. Each tree costs1+prefix+nodes+order+sum(1+header node IDs); each step costs1+pattern+sum(1+path items). Node/step/tree/header aggregates count one record each; arrays add their item/index entries. Root nodes and pruned child trees count. This quota excludes ordinary canonical output, work, normalized input, active trees, conditional buffers and allocator bytes; it is not bytes or peak RAM. Working records may be formed before their size is known. No partial result escapes failure.
    algorithms::FPGrowthTreeOwned actual fully built tree, including conditional trees pruned to a root. Trees occur in actual build order. Prefix stores the current DFS suffix sequence, not sorted canonical output. Order is frequency descending with ID-ascending ties; header rows are ID ascending. Nodes/headers own storage. Only the frequent-item projection is compressed; raw rows, infrequent items and empty projections are not recoverable from this tree alone.
    algorithms::FPGrowthWeightedPathOne actual nonempty conditional prefix path with its target-node count. Items run from the nearest ancestor toward the root, excluding the target and root. The child builder sorts them again using its own conditional frequency order. Weight is the target node count, not an ancestor count or number of path records.
    algorithms::FPGrowthWorkActual build, insertion, header, parent-walk and DFS counts. Counts exclude validation, allocation, sort comparisons, hashing internals and capture copies. Weighted counts contribute one visit per stored item, not weight visits. Root creation is counted through trees_built; nodes_created excludes roots. Peak node records include only trees resident in active DFS frames, excluding temporary child/conditional buffers and retained history.
    nn::models::FpnDigitDetectorFeaturesOwn source compact FPN detector maps and one shared multi-level RPN result.
    cad::Frame
    algorithms::FrankWolfeOptionsOptions for frank_wolfe.
    algorithms::FrankWolfeResultResult and trace of frank_wolfe.
    dstruct::FreeList
    algorithms::FreivaldsBinaryAuditExhaustive supplied-binary-vector counts for the numerical verifier. Enumeration uses column0 as the low bit. This audits the double tolerance test, not exact algebraic equality. Incompatible matrices have vectors0 and no kernel work.
    algorithms::FreivaldsCountsActual kernel work, excluding validation, allocation and capture. A term means one multiply and accumulate, not a hardware instruction. All three matvecs finish before row comparisons. Failed rounds count as completed.
    algorithms::FreivaldsCurveRowOne requested prefix length and its deterministic seed count. Rows retain caller order and duplicates. Trials0 has accepted0; no undefined fraction is stored.
    algorithms::FreivaldsExampleMatricesOriginal40x40 integer fixture and its exact representable product. A and B use mt19937 seed3 and uniform integers[-9,9], all A then all B in row order. Product reuses strassen_multiply(); bounded integer arithmetic is exact for this fixture. Generator distribution mapping follows the C++ standard library implementation.
    algorithms::FreivaldsResultA numerical verdict with actual work and first failure. SIZE_MAX failure indices mean no failed round. Compatible nonpositive-round calls accept vacuously; incompatible calls reject without rounds.
    algorithms::FreivaldsRoundOwned values from one actual performed round. Differences contain only the tested row prefix, as absolute values; all matvec output rows exist even after a row0 mismatch. No replay or fabricated unchecked differences.
    algorithms::FreivaldsSeedSweepDeterministic once-per-seed experiment and actual aggregate counts. These fixed pseudorandom seeds are not an IID sample or a statistical confidence interval. Empty round requests produce no rows or seed executions. Incompatible requests retain rejecting seed records with no kernel work.
    algorithms::FreivaldsSeedTrialActual maximum-prefix outcome for one seed. Each seed executes once at the largest nonnegative requested prefix. A requested prefix K passes iff compatible and K<=0, or no failure, or K<=failed_round.
    algorithms::FreivaldsTraceOwned inputs and actual round frames from one kernel execution. All input matrices and frame vectors own storage independently. No partial result escapes an exception. Entry admission is conservative for all requested rounds, before input copies and RNG draws.
    algorithms::FreivaldsWorkActual counts and input/RNG metadata for one call. State advances modulo2^64. Supplied probes set seeded=false and states/seed=0; incompatible calls draw nothing.
    algorithms::FrequentItemsetA set of items found frequent, with the number of transactions containing it.
    nn::models::FrozenEncoderClassifierCopy frozen encoder/scaling state and evaluate a caller-owned linear classifier head.
    nn::FrozenGraphOwn an immutable frozen GraphDef and execute its supported numeric subgraphs natively.
    nn::models::FrozenVgg16Own all13 imported VGG16 convolution pairs as detached fixed constants.
    nn::models::FrozenVgg19Import all16 genuine-shape VGG19 convolution pairs as frozen constants.
    sim::FruitAppearanceSeeded rendering/shape parameters, independent of camera or policy predictions. Prototype IDs 0..5 have separate apple/banana geometries. The skin palette is shared by both classes to prevent a red-versus-yellow color shortcut.
    sim::FruitStreamEnvironmentNative continuing multi-fruit conveyor, real-URDF servos and asynchronous outcomes. The belt always runs at .22 m/s. Independent exponential inter-arrival times are scheduled even during arm motion, and insertion is quantized by at most one 1/240-second physics tick. Fruit passing X=.30 m is missed. There is no between-pick reset, teleport, stopped belt or hidden queue at the source. An opt-in training_proxy accelerates empty/servo intervals using analytic belt transport and a .4 s bin-settling approximation, omitting fruit-fruit contacts. Arrivals and task rewards are shared, but the proxy is incompatible with articulated dynamics and is not physics evidence. Use articulated_physics for contact-based learning/evaluation; it imports link inertias/collision hulls and simulates finite actuator effort, free payload rotation, slip and physical release momentum. Interception options target the oldest/second-oldest observed fruit, inspect it through a supplied classifier, time a descending grasp, lift, traverse and release. Fixed IK servos are not learned torques; the scheduler is trainable. The default perception channel is explicitly SYNTHETIC and intended for fast RL training, with configured class-error probabilities. Supply set_perception() for actual RGB evaluation; unknown predictions never use true-label fallback. With watch_infeed enabled, reset starts at a camera-aimed entry observation pose. Empty-queue waits return there via guarded, rate-limited waypoints; the next decision can interrupt after 0.125 seconds. This orients the real rigid camera, not a virtual pan. Queue state still uses privileged tracking, not RGB detection. Instances are single-writer; callbacks must not mutate the environment.
    sim::FruitStreamOptionsConfiguration of an unbounded-time, bounded-memory sorting workcell. Arrivals are never postponed for a busy arm. At capacity, arrivals are counted as overflow misses. Outcomes are removed after two seconds (self-emptying bins). Legacy mode stabilizes orientation and uses ideal latches. Articulated mode integrates free rotation, force-limited servos and physical grasps. Motor geometry remains privileged state; nominal physics is not a hardware calibration.
    nn::FtTransformerRegressionLive outputs from a tabular feature transformer.
    nn::FunctionA reusable custom function (TF: an op plus REGISTER_GRADIENT_OP).
    nn::models::FusedBlockTensor-packed kernels and summed bias of one inference RepVGG block.
    algorithms::FuzzyCMeansFrameOwned actual center update, distances and membership update for one iteration. Numerators and denominators are the actual ordered accumulations, not reconstructed weighted means. Distances precede membership assignment. Objectives bracket each coordinate block; exact block descent does not promise strict finite-precision descent with the near-coincidence shortcut.
    algorithms::FuzzyCMeansPartitionMean partition coefficient and natural-log entropy of membership rows. These describe concentration, not calibrated probabilities or evidence for the number of clusters. Entropy uses0log0=0. No sample correction or label mapping.
    algorithms::FuzzyCMeansResultOwned centers, updated memberships and final numerical objective. Field order and layout are retained. Centers use the incoming memberships of the last iteration; returned memberships use those centers. No final center refresh. A zero-iteration fit has initialized memberships and zero centers; iterations0 does not mean convergence.
    algorithms::FuzzyCMeansRunFit plus actual work and stopping information. Strict max_change<tol controls early stopping; tol0 runs the cap. max_change0 is only a placeholder when no iteration occurred. There is no global-optimum or probability-calibration guarantee.
    algorithms::FuzzyCMeansTraceOwned inputs, initial state and actual once-only iteration history. No replay, caller mutation, shared state or partial result. Whole conservative admission precedes initialization draws and input copies. Extra phase objectives may overflow even when an ordinary final fit is representable.
    algorithms::FuzzyCMeansWorkActual executed fit work, excluding validation, allocation and copying. Draws count uniform distribution calls, not engine words. Ratio powers occur only on rows without a near-coincident center. Diagnostic objectives are additional trace work, distinct from the final objective.

    G

    algorithms::GabowEventOwned actual state after one traversal primitive, without replay. Kinds are enter,edge,collapse,close-root,assign,finish. Enter follows first preorder/S/B pushes; edge follows neighbor-index increment before edge action; collapse/close-root follow one B pop; assign follows one S pop and component write; finish follows frame pop and any component counter increment. Intermediate assignment states need not satisfy quiescent boundary invariants. S contains every discovered-unassigned vertex, including finished DFS calls, and can exceed the active DFS path.
    algorithms::GabowResultRaw component IDs and actual work from one SCC execution. IDs are contiguous0..C-1, assigned in sink-first closure order. For a cross-component edge u->v, id[u]>id[v]. Neighbor order can change labels for incomparable components; equality of partitions is the stable meaning.
    algorithms::GabowTraceOwned graph and actual primitive snapshots from one kernel execution. Whole-request conservative admission precedes graph copy and state allocation. No replay, shared state, caller mutation, truncation or partial output. Captured entry accounting excludes ordinary final labels/work/scalar root metadata, working state and allocator bytes.
    algorithms::GabowWorkActual traversal operations and peak stack lengths. Excludes validation, history copies, allocation, rendering and partition summaries. Each vertex enters/finishes once, is assigned once and is pushed/popped once on each stack. Individual edges can collapse many boundaries; total root pops is N. Event count is E+4N, including root-close pops and collapse pops.
    algorithms::GaleShapleyEventOwned actual proposal decision and before/after FIFO state. Captured after the actual acceptance/replacement/rejection. next_choice and both maps are post-decision; queue_before is before removing this proposer, queue_after is after any append. decision is accept-free,replace or reject. No regenerated history. kUnmatched denotes no prior incumbent or no newly freed proposer.
    algorithms::GaleShapleyRunOne matching with actual kernel work. Both ordinary and diagnostic fitting use the same FIFO traversal without replay. The theorem concerns submitted strict complete rankings and stable matchings, not maximum total utility or real-world program constraints.
    algorithms::GaleShapleyTraceOwned inputs, actual reviewer ranks and actual FIFO proposal events. Whole-request conservative admission follows full preference validation, which may allocate O(n) scratch. Admission precedes quadratic rank tables, matching state and history/input copies. No replay, partial trace, truncation, caller mutation or shared state.
    algorithms::GaleShapleyWorkActual rank construction and FIFO decision counts. Excludes input validation, allocation, history copies, checking stability, rank summaries and enumeration. rank_entries counts only the reviewer rank table used by the matcher. A queue push occurs initially or after rejection/displacement; each real proposal pops one free proposer.
    rl::environments::GameTwo-player perfect-information game interface with current-player observations.
    algorithms::GameNodeA node of a two-player game tree: a leaf carrying a heuristic value, or an internal node with children. Levels alternate between the maximizing and minimizing player.
    algorithms::GameResultThe outcome of a game-tree search: the minimax value of the root and the number of leaves_evaluated to obtain it (the work done).
    algorithms::GammaDecodedOwned strictly decoded positive values and actual parse work, without history. Every input character must belong to one complete representable codeword; trailing zeros are not padding. Empty input yields no values. No input views survive.
    algorithms::GammaEncodedOwned encoded characters and actual emission work, with no optional history. bits uses one char per bit, not packed bytes. No input view survives; ordinary work calls have no optional capture quota. Empty input gives empty bits and zero work.
    algorithms::GammaSizeSummaryExact gamma and minimal common fixed-width payload sizes for positive values. Empty input has zero sizes and maximum zero. Fixed width is the binary width of the largest value; it does not include framing or a transmitted width/count. These are theoretical bit counts. The string codec stores one char per bit.
    algorithms::GammaTraceOwned values, bit characters and spans captured during the actual codec run. Retained logical entries C=B+2N count B bit characters, N values and N word records. Scalar fields, result/runtime temporaries, string/vector capacity and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not a peak-memory bound. Encoding knows complete C before copies/emission; decoding knows B first and reserves two entries per complete word online. Copies own independent buffers, with no input views.
    algorithms::GammaWordActual half-open bit spans of one emitted or parsed gamma codeword. The prefix occupies [begin,payload_begin), and the binary payload including its leading one occupies [payload_begin,end). Spans refer to GammaTrace::bits, which owns its data; numbers are indices, not borrowed iterators or views.
    algorithms::GammaWorkLogical value and bit counts from actual gamma emission or parsing. Each successful codeword contributes its zero-prefix and full binary payload lengths. bit_visits counts emitted characters for encoding or consumed characters for decoding; validation, preflight, allocation/copying and CPU instructions are excluded. Full input validation is an additional pass, not hidden in this count.
    stats::GAMMOptionsGaussian random-intercept prior and additive fit controls.
    stats::GAMOptionsControls additive term structure and penalized IRLS.
    stats::GAMSmoothSpecifies a centered cubic P-spline or a centered linear term.
    algorithms::GanttSegmentOne owned half-open contiguous busy interval.
    optim::GAOptionsConfiguration for GeneticAlgorithm; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

    nn::models::GatedPixelOutputOwn the seven live boundaries of the three-block dual-stream gated context.
    nn::models::GateOutputsA differentiable channel gate and its rescaled feature map.

    datasets::GaussianBlobsOwned numeric features and zero-based centre labels for Gaussian clouds. Rows are grouped by centre, then draw order; coordinates are unscaled. Copies are independent. The generator stores no references to centres or shared RNG state.
    causal::GaussianCITestA Gaussian conditional independence test using Fisher's transform.
    nn::GaussianConditionalJoint conditional Gaussian moments.
    nn::GaussianCovarianceFitFit state for a zero-mean Gaussian model, in Float64.
    algorithms::GaussianEliminationEventOne actual accepted/rejected pivot, completed elimination or back-substitution step. kind is pivot, reject, eliminate or back. column is zero-based; row is selected current pivot row (before swapping), eliminated row or solved coordinate. value is selected pivot, actual factor or assigned solution coordinate. matrix/rhs/row_order are post-event owned copies, except reject precedes any rejected swap. x is empty before back substitution and a full n-vector after each back step; unsolved earlier coordinates are zero placeholders.
    algorithms::GaussianEliminationRunOwned ordinary solve output, actual upper state, row order and element-growth evidence. solution preserves the legacy LinearSolution layout. A rejected pivot leaves solution.x empty and accepted_pivots identifies its zero-based column. This is a computed cutoff failure, not a rank/conditioning certificate. upper/rhs are actual stored doubles, including cancellation residues; row_order[i] is the original row now at i. They remain available on rejection. Successful empty input has accepted_pivots0 and solved=true. max_coefficient includes the input and every stored coefficient assignment; RHS is excluded. growth is max_coefficient/initial_max, or the placeholder1 for all-zero/empty A. The scalar double recurrence is not widened; finite stored assignments are checked, while rounding and underflow remain possible. No shared state.
    algorithms::GaussianEliminationTraceOwned inputs, actual elimination history and ordinary run from one shared execution. Inputs and all event vectors are independent of caller and other snapshots. captured_entries counts input rows/cells/RHS, plus each event's one metadata record and matrix rows/cells/RHS/x/row_order. Ordinary final outputs, root/work metadata, working storage and allocator bytes are excluded. Entries are not bytes or peak RAM. Worst-case history costs O(n^4), ordinary work O(n^3).
    algorithms::GaussianEliminationWorkActual arithmetic work in one partial-pivot solve, excluding validation and copies. Counts record executed comparisons, nontrivial swaps and stored updates, even on a pivot rejection. A coefficient update is one multiply-subtract, not one floating operation. Checks, allocation, diagnostics and history are excluded.
    nn::GaussianEnsembleSummaryMoments of an equal-weight mixture of Gaussian predictions.

    algorithms::GaussianResidualSummaryWidened infinity-norm residual and normwise backward error for a supplied candidate. These describe the candidate, not solver success, conditioning or forward accuracy. residual is b-Ax in long double. backward_error is its infinity norm divided by matrix_inf*x_inf+b_inf, with0/0defined0; empty givesallzeros. Units differ from linalg::backward_error(), which uses Frobenius/2-norms.
    nn::GaussianSmoothingCertificatePointwise certificate for a Gaussian-smoothed classifier.

    nn::models::GaussianVaeOutputOwn Gaussian posterior parameters, explicit samples and beta-weighted VAE objectives.
    nn::models::GaussianValuePathLive source continuous-PPO actor and separate critic endpoints.
    algorithms::GaussJordanEventOwned actual accepted/rejected pivot, normalization or completed other-row update. kind is pivot/reject/normalize/eliminate. column is the current zero-based pivot column; row is selected pivot row before swapping, normalized pivot row or updated row. value is selected pivot, normalization divisor or raw f. A pivot event follows all row swaps; reject precedes any rejected swap. transform starts as I and undergoes exactly the same row operations as matrix and rhs: it is a partial row transformation, not yet an inverse certificate. Every full matrix/RHS/permutation snapshot is independently owned.
    algorithms::GaussJordanResultOwned legacy Gauss–Jordan result: computed cutoff success, solution and inverse. Both arrays are empty on cutoff failure. Successful arrays contain floating approximations, not exact arithmetic certificates. Field order and aggregate layout are preserved. Empty valid square input succeeds with empty arrays.
    algorithms::GaussJordanRunOwned final reduction state and legacy result from a single checked execution. result.inverse and result.x exist only on success; no duplicate final inverse is stored. reduced/rhs are the actual final coefficient/RHS state on success or cutoff failure. Partial transformation matrices on failure are available through trace events, not result.inverse. accepted_pivots is n on success or the rejected zero-based column. row_order records cumulative row interchanges (row combinations mean rows no longer equal the original equations). max_clear_factor is the largest raw f used against a normalized pivot row; it is not the Gaussian pre-normalization ratio and need not be at most1. Empty valid input succeeds with empty outputs. No accuracy/rank certificate.
    algorithms::GaussJordanTraceOwned original system, actual-time events and final run, without replay. captured_entries counts input matrix row records/cells and RHS plus one metadata record and all matrix row records/cells/RHS/permutation per event. Ordinary final outputs, root/work metadata, working storage and allocator bytes are excluded. Entries are not bytes or peak RAM. Successful full histories attain their admission bound; early rejection may retain much less. O(n^4) worst-case history/copy cost versus O(n³) ordinary arithmetic/O(n²) storage.
    algorithms::GaussJordanWorkActual full-block Gauss–Jordan work, excluding validation, allocation and snapshots. A block update counts one stored multiply-subtract, not one floating operation. Zero factors and already-processed columns are still updated, preserving the legacy recurrence. Identity zero-fill is allocation; diagonal writes count.
    algorithms::GaussLegendreRunOwned fixed-count analysis result and actual initial/final states. Executes exactly iterations stages, without replay or early stopping. Flags record first equality of successive computed estimates and of (a,b,t), not exact convergence or correct rounding; p is deliberately excluded from that mean-state comparison. a and b can stall one ULP apart. Final unused p may be infinite at the maximum iteration, while the estimate remains finite. O(iterations) work/O(1) result storage; no shared mutable state.
    algorithms::GaussLegendreStateActual arithmetic-geometric means, correction accumulator and doubling weight. Default values are inert storage, not the initialized pi system. Produced states start at a1,b1/sqrt2,t1/4,p1. At the maximal supported iteration the final unused p overflows to infinity; no subsequent stage may use it.
    algorithms::GaussLegendreStepOwned actual stage, including the used correction and before/after states. correction is the actual left-associated (p*delta)*delta used in t-=correction; it need not equal the subsequently rounded difference t_before-t_after. estimate_changed compares rounded estimates; mean_state_changed compares actual a,b,t, excluding p. Neither flag certifies mathematical accuracy.
    algorithms::GaussLegendreTraceOwned actual fixed-count history and final run, admitted as complete records. captured_records counts one initial-state record plus each fixed-schema stage record, not scalar entries or bytes. Ordinary final output, root/work metadata, working state and allocator bytes are excluded; this is not a peak RAM limit. All state copies are independent. O(N) history/copy cost, no numerical replay.
    algorithms::GaussLegendreWorkActual arithmetic counts, excluding diagnostics, allocation and snapshots. Initial sqrt is included in square_roots. Each stage executes both means, left-associated p*delta*delta subtraction and p*=2. Legacy scalar calls evaluate only the final estimate; run/trace evaluate the initial estimate and every stage to observe changes. One estimate is one quotient expression, not one floating operation. No early stop is triggered by stagnation.
    algorithms::GaussNewtonIterationOne evaluated parameter state, including its proposed next step. The initial state is iteration zero. step_norm is the norm of the incoming completed update (zero initially), while next_step_norm and linearized_sse describe the proposed outgoing update. Diagnostics are calculated at these params, not the preceding state.
    algorithms::GaussNewtonLinearizationOne local residual/Jacobian least-squares problem and its undamped step. All values are owned. J is observations by parameters, r=model-y, and step minimizes ||r+J*step||_2. Columns are scaled to unit norm internally, then the solution is restored to parameter units; no normal equations, regularization or bounds are used. A numerically rank-deficient Jacobian is rejected, not assigned an arbitrary solution.
    algorithms::GaussNewtonResultOwned full-step Gauss-Newton fit and its evaluated parameter trajectory. The original params/iterations/sse fields remain first for aggregate compatibility. iterations counts completed updates, including on budget exhaustion. sse and residuals always describe the returned params. step_tolerance_met only certifies that the next proposed step has norm <= tol: it does not prove stationarity, a minimum, global optimality or parameter identification. Check the gradient and model assumptions too. No early rejection or line search hides an increase in the objective.
    algorithms::GaussSeidelCoordinateOne actual in-place coordinate assignment with its mixed read state. row is zero-based, sweep is one-based. before contains new lower-index values and old higher-index values; after changes only row. numerator is the widened b[row] minus ordered off-diagonal products immediately before division. Snapshots are independent owned copies, not reconstructions of the solver.
    algorithms::GaussSeidelHistoryOwned initial vector, actual coordinate events, sweep states and final run. captured_entries counts initial.size()+1 for the initial residual, then one metadata record plus both n-vectors per coordinate and one metadata record plus its n-vector per completed sweep. Record metadata includes scalar fields and work. Units are entries, not bytes or peak RAM. Original input A/b, root metadata, final ordinary run, working vectors and allocator storage are excluded. All vectors are independent of caller and other records. O(kn²) history.
    algorithms::GaussSeidelRunOwned final Gauss-Seidel result and work from the same execution. Zero start; inclusive absolute tolerance. No history or hidden replay. solution retains IterativeSolution's legacy layout. Inputs are never changed; no global state is used. O(kn²) work and O(n) extra storage for k sweeps.
    algorithms::GaussSeidelSweepOne actual completed sweep and its recomputed residual. residual uses widened A x row sums rounded to double, then widened b-A x differences and hypot, finally checked to double. It is not an exact residual or forward-error certificate. work is cumulative, including this residual.
    algorithms::GaussSeidelTraceOwned actual residual history for the forward in-place Gauss-Seidel baseline. residuals[0] is ||b|| and each subsequent entry follows a completed sweep. Empty and zero RHS converge initially. The legacy result layout is preserved.
    algorithms::GaussSeidelWorkActual dense arithmetic counts from a forward Gauss-Seidel execution. Counts include zero coefficients. One product is a multiply-subtract or multiply-add, not one floating operation. Validation, copies, allocation and norm arithmetic are excluded. The initial residual evaluation uses b alone.
    GBMClassifierSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::GBMClassifier — multiclass gradient boosting (a sequence of shallow trees, one per class per round, fit to the current multinomial-deviance gradient).
    stats::GBMClassifierMulticlass additive trees fitted to one-hot-minus-softmax residuals. Starts from log empirical class priors. At each round, all K residual targets use the same pre-round probabilities, then one least-squares CART tree per class is fitted. A scalar learning_rate multiplies its leaf means. There is no Newton leaf correction, (K-1)/K multiplier, centring constraint, line search or built-in early stopping; this is not numerically identical to sklearn GradientBoostingClassifier/LogitBoost. Formula supplies finite encoded predictors (including categorical/interaction terms) and a string response. Complete cases define sorted classes and priors; null formula rows are dropped. Needs at least one expanded predictor and two retained classes. All prior trees remain fixed. Subsampling selects rows without replacement once per round, shared across its K trees. The seed does not affect full-sample deterministic CART fits; greedy split ties follow predictor/threshold order and absolute tolerances. training_deviance is mean multinomial negative log likelihood, without factor two, computed with log-sum-exp rather than flooring probabilities. Prefix zero is the prior model. Evaluation is explicit, never used to fit or alter trees. Training accuracy or loss cannot diagnose generalization or select a stopping round without held-out data. Model owns the Formula schema, trees, encoded training data and row maps. Inputs are unchanged; const operations share no mutable caches. This CART implementation scans all candidate thresholds: conservative fit work O(M*K*p*n^2*(D+1)), with storage O(np+M*K*(n+nodes_per_tree)) including each tree's stored training predictions. Numeric inference traverses fitted trees; no query preprocessing is learned.
    stats::GBMClassifierOptionsControls the number, shrinkage, shape and row sampling of residual trees. max_depth must be positive; unsplittable nodes remain constant. Rates above one are allowed, but no monotone training-loss guarantee is asserted for arbitrary rates or stochastic samples.
    stats::GBMClassifierPredictionOwned labels and softmax probabilities in original query-row order. Missing predictors produce an empty string and empty probability row. A complete row has K probabilities in GBMClassifier::classes() order; ties use the first sorted class. Probabilities can underflow to zero and are not post-hoc calibrated.
    GBMRegressorSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::GBMRegressor — a sequence of shallow regression trees, each fit to the residuals of the current ensemble (gradient boosting on squared error).
    stats::GBMRegressor
    stats::GBMRegressorOptions
    stats::GBMValidationResultOwned learning-rate/round search result, including a possible prior-only choice. selected_options can refit on the caller's chosen data. If selected_rounds is zero, selected_options.n_trees is one solely to satisfy the fit constructor; use explicit prefix zero when evaluating/predicting that selected model.
    nn::Neat::GeneDirected connection indexed by its population-wide innovation ID.
    algorithms::GeneralMatchingResultOwned maximum-cardinality matching, with symmetric mates and an explicit unmatched sentinel. mate has one entry per input vertex. Matched endpoints refer to each other; size counts pairs, not matched vertices. A maximum need not be unique and its selected edges can depend on input order. No graph storage is borrowed.
    algorithms::GeneralMatchingTraceOwned final matching, actual contraction sets, lifted paths and search work counters. Root searches are numbered chronologically; contraction/augmentation vectors each preserve their own execution order. Edge scans count visited adjacency entries, including entries then skipped as matched or already contracted. Ignored self-loops add no adjacency entries; duplicates do add entries. Recording can require O(V^3) storage for expanded contraction sets, in addition to O(V+E) graph/work storage. The unrecorded function allocates no event records.
    algorithms::GenerationalEventOne primitive collector event with actual object, decision and stack size. kind is root/old_field/remember/seed/mark/visit/young_field/promote/free or full_root/full_mark/full_visit/full_field. object is source/current id; target is the referenced id or the same id, except remember uses -1. accepted records young membership for root/old_field, a newly marked candidate for seed/young_field/full_root/full_field, false for free, true otherwise. stack_size is actual current size (after mark-push or visit-pop); discovery and classification events use zero. No per-event vector or path is replayed.
    algorithms::GenerationalHeapOwned fixed-age graph with an exact maintained set of old-to-young reference slots. Construction validates once and indexes young ids and every boundary slot. Only checked existing-field replacement is permitted; ages, roots, object ids and field counts stay fixed. set_reference maintains the slot invariant as a modeled write barrier. It is not a concurrent/runtime collector: collect only proposes retention/reclamation, with no age changes, copying or deallocation. Copies own all data. Concurrent collect calls are safe absent concurrent writes.
    algorithms::GenerationalInputOwned graph and binary ages for a generated generational example. Sizes are absent and references use dense slots; no real memory is allocated for modeled objects. Vectors are independent of later calls.
    algorithms::GenerationalResultOwned legacy minor-analysis flags, candidates and full-trace comparison. promoted[i] names a retained young object proposed for promotion; young_freed names unretained young objects. No real objects, ages or references are changed. All old objects conservatively supply boundary references, including unreachable old garbage, so promoted need not imply full-root reachability. Counts are object visits, not total collector work. Legacy field order/types are stable.
    algorithms::GenerationalRunOwned legacy result, actual full marks and work from one executing analysis. Full marks distinguish true root reachability from conservative minor retention. Same values as minor_gc; includes boundary discovery and a full comparison, O(N+E+R) work/storage bounds, with no caller mutation or hidden replay.
    algorithms::GenerationalTraceOwned input graph/ages, ordinary run and chronological actual collector events. The online quota counts complete event records, not numeric entries or bytes. Owned input/name vectors, root/work/final output, working tables/stacks and allocator storage are excluded; it is not a peak RAM limit. Invalid inputs are rejected before copies/capture. No partial/truncated trace is returned.
    algorithms::GenerationalWorkActual selected validation, discovery, tracing and output-loop work. Counts include stored duplicate fields/roots. They are visits, not timings or a complete instruction count; allocation, container internals, copies and trace capture are excluded. Full-comparison fields are zero for young-only collection. preparation_work() records construction only, not later writes.
    nn::Generatorxoshiro256** stream with convenience draws.
    optim::GeneticAlgorithmGeneticAlgorithm on the ArbitraryFunction callback interface. Real-valued box-constrained selection, crossover, Gaussian mutation and optional elitism. Initial coordinates seed a clamped population member. Returns the best visited point and can stop after more than twenty small-best-improvement generations. O(population_size*p) storage; strategy/rate choices affect results, with no global certificate. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    geometry::GeoHashBinA floor-quantized signed grid cell and its lossless packed key.
    algorithms::GeohashBitOne actual coordinate comparison and axis-endpoint update. bit_in_symbol is zero-based 0..4 before the group count increments. symbol_value is the actual accumulator after shifting in this bit. longitude=true selects the longitude interval. Exact equality to midpoint chooses upper. No input is borrowed and no event is reconstructed from a final key.
    algorithms::GeohashBoundsOwned latitude/longitude bounds in degrees, initially the whole world rectangle. These are actual ordered double-bisection endpoints, not certified exact-real bounds at arbitrary precision. Long runs can stagnate or collapse an interval. Longitude is not normalized across the date line. No shared state or mutation.
    geometry::GeoHashBuildRunAn ordinary table build together with its actual operation counts.
    geometry::GeoHashBuildTraceAn owned ordinary result and complete online primitive history.
    algorithms::GeohashCellOwned decoded double cell bounds, unrounded center and actual angular spans. latitude_bits/longitude_bits count decoded bit positions, not significant coordinate bits. limited is true if any update stagnated or ended collapsed. Long keys may have degenerate/unchanged bounds; no physical-distance or exact real-cell certificate is implied. Center is (lo+hi)/2 without decimal rounding.
    algorithms::GeohashEmissionOne actual base32 emission with endpoints at that control-flow point. Records the appended character before the executing kernel resets its group counter/accumulator. Owns its bounds; no prefix string is copied per record.
    geometry::GeoHashEventA copied fixed-schema record from the executing hashing kernel.
    geometry::GeoHashFrameOne actual double quotient in an ordered two-point frame.
    algorithms::GeohashResolutionIdeal dyadic angular resolution rounded to double, separate from actual endpoint arithmetic. Ideal widths use 360*2^-longitude_bits and 180*2^-latitude_bits. At high counts these rounded spans can underflow to zero; spans_positive reports both positive. This is neither a metric-distance estimate nor a guarantee the actual encoder endpoints retain that width beyond floating precision. No allocation or mutation.
    algorithms::GeohashRunOwned encoded key, actual final bounds, work and first precision-limit flags. first_unchanged_bit/first_collapsed_bit are one-based actual bit indices, zero if absent. A repeated interval need not have zero width; these flags do not claim additional geographic accuracy, true convergence or unique ownership of a shared boundary. Ordinary result needs O(p) output bytes, O(1) other storage.
    geometry::GeoHashRunAn ordinary recognition candidate together with actual work.
    geometry::GeoHashTableAn owned quantized-bin index of ordered model bases.
    algorithms::GeohashTraceOwned initial-coordinate record, actual bit/emission records and final ordinary run. captured_records counts 1 initial fixed-schema coordinate/bounds record, one per GeohashBit and one per GeohashEmission. These are records, not numeric entries or bytes. Root/work/final ordinary output, working state and allocator storage are excluded; this is not a peak RAM limit. Vectors are independent.
    geometry::GeoHashTraceAn owned ordinary result and complete online primitive history.
    algorithms::GeohashWorkActual bit and character operations from one ordered encoder execution. Counts include all requested steps even after interval stagnation. They are selected operations, not timings or total floating-operation counts. Allocation, copying, validation and trace capture are excluded.
    geometry::GeoHashWorkSelected actual kernel operation counts for one build or recognition.
    geometry::GeoMatchA highest-vote candidate and its first-hit geometric verification.
    algebra::GfFactorizationComplete factorization over GF(p) from factor_gf_p().
    GGPlotSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::graphics::GGPlot — a ggplot2-style grammar-of-graphics builder. Geom/theme/scale/facet calls are chainable, mirroring ggplot2's own layered ggplot(df, aes(...)) + geom_point() + ... style as closely as C++ method chaining allows.
    graphics::GGPlotA ggplot2-style grammar-of-graphics builder: layers of geoms are accumulated against one Aes mapping and replayed at save() time (once per facet panel, if facet_wrap() was used), each replay producing an RPlot so rendering reuses the exact same SVG/PNG/PDF engine as the R-base graphics library.
    nn::models::GhostBlockOne released GhostNet bottleneck specification before width scaling.
    nn::models::GhostModuleOutputsIntrinsic and cheaply generated maps plus a possibly trimmed concatenation.
    nn::models::GhostNetConfigGhostNet width, stem, classifier dropout and normalization settings.
    bayes::GibbsOptionsSettings for GibbsSampler.
    bayes::GibbsResultOutput of GibbsSampler::sample().
    bayes::GibbsSamplerMetropolis-within-Gibbs: updates one coordinate at a time, each via a scalar random-walk Metropolis step evaluated against the SAME joint log-density with every other coordinate held fixed – mathematically equivalent to a Metropolis step targeting the exact full conditional p(x_i | x_-i), since the joint-density ratio with everything else held fixed IS the full-conditional-density ratio. This is the standard fallback used whenever a full conditional isn't conjugate/directly sampleable (what BUGS/JAGS call "Metropolis-within-Gibbs"), not exact Gibbs sampling via closed-form conditional samplers – those are necessarily model-specific (they need to know each conditional's actual distributional family) and aren't something a generic engine driven only by a joint log-density can provide. Updating one coordinate at a time (rather than proposing the whole vector jointly, as RandomWalkMetropolis does) can mix substantially better when parameters live on very different scales or are only weakly correlated.
    algorithms::GirvanNewmanEventOne fixed-schema copied state from the actual native kernel.
    algorithms::GirvanNewmanRunThe legacy final BFS components with actual work and numeric diagnostics.
    algorithms::GirvanNewmanTraceAn owned ordinary result and complete online primitive event history.
    algorithms::GirvanNewmanWorkSelected actual operations of a betweenness or community run.
    geometry::GjkEventOne owned fixed-size GJK state record emitted during the actual kernel. point is the new support point only for support records; otherwise it is the current/returned closest point. direction is the search direction (initial direction for initial, zero for empty). value is squared norm for direction, actual support improvement for support, returned norm for progress/limit and zero otherwise. support_a/b are the most recent selected input indices, not simplex provenance for all retained points; they are zero placeholders for empty input. At each support query strict greater-than retains the first tie. Unused simplex array slots are zero. Copies own data and retain no input aliases.
    geometry::GjkRunAn owned GJK approximation, final working feature and actual stop reason. distance is in input coordinate units. closest/simplex describe the final working Minkowski feature, with at most three points; they are zero/empty for empty input. A near-origin return reports distance zero even if closest is nonzero. A triangle-inside return stores the routine's zero and three points. No closest pair on the original shapes, exact containment, penetration depth or rigorous floating error bound is supplied. Copies own every value.
    geometry::GjkTraceAn owned ordinary GJK result and its complete online state records. Input vectors, root object, ordinary result/final feature, constant working simplex/feature storage and allocator overhead are outside the record quota. A quota counts complete GjkEvent objects, not scalar entries, bytes or peak RAM. All metadata and stopping records count. No replay, partial return or truncation occurs. Copies own event storage; independent calls share no mutable state.
    geometry::GjkWorkSelected actual operations of one GJK execution, initially all zero. Counts exclude input validation, arithmetic FLOPs, allocation and wall time. Each Minkowski query scans both complete clouds, including duplicates, with first-index ties: support_dots equals the scanned vertex count and support_comparisons equals support_dots-support_calls. All counters are owned; overflow throws length_error. Concurrent independent calls share no state.
    GLMSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::GLM — a generalized linear model (gaussian, binomial, poisson, or Gamma family with its canonical link, matching R's glm() defaults) fit by iteratively reweighted least squares.
    stats::GLMMaximum-likelihood canonical-link regression by iteratively reweighted least squares.
    GLMMSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::GLMM — a generalized linear mixed model fit by penalized quasi-likelihood, with a single grouping factor, e.g. "success ~ x1 + (1 | school)" with family="binomial".
    stats::GLMMFits binary or count mixed models by a maximum-working-likelihood PQL approximation.
    stats::GLMMOptionsPQL relinearization and bounded covariance-search controls.
    stats::GLMOptionsControls canonical-link IRLS; defaults follow R's glm.control().
    stats::GLMPredictionOwned prediction vectors aligned to query rows; omitted rows contain NaN. Confidence limits describe the conditional mean, never a future observation.
    nn::GloVePairsOwn the nonzero directed pairs and harmonic co-occurrence counts.
    nn::GloVeResultOwn GloVe log-count predictions, weights and embeddings.
    nn::models::GlowDensityOutputOwn all four compact Glow stages and their live density intermediates.
    datasets::GMLGraphAn owned graph topology with explicit original-to-native vertex mapping. node_ids are ascending unique original signed decimal ids; native index i corresponds to node_ids[i]. edges preserve input order, direction, loops and multiplicity. directed records graph metadata, default false. Weights, labels, layout and other attributes are skipped: this is a topology reader, not a weighted/labeled GML round trip. Copies own all vectors independently.
    algorithms::GnomeSortEventOne owned fixed-size record from the executing pointer loop. Step ordinal is zero-based among loop bodies. Pair values and original ids describe the pair BEFORE the comparison/exchange, only when compared is true. Boundary visits have compared/swapped false and unused pair fields zero. Initial/stop metadata have unused ordinal/pair/flag fields zero. Metadata pointer fields are both zero for initial and both n for stop. Copies retain no references; unused fields are placeholders, not input observations.
    algorithms::GnomeSortRunOwned sorted values, identities carried by the actual swaps and selected work. Original indices are zero-based positions in the supplied input. Equal keys retain increasing original indices, including repeated signed extremes. The identity output and its initialization cost O(n); sorting has constant other working state. Copies own both vectors and share no mutable state or aliases.
    algorithms::GnomeSortTraceOwned ordinary result and every online fixed-size state record. No full array snapshots are retained per visit: history storage is O(H) complete records, in addition to O(n) owned values/identities. Inputs, root, ordinary output/identities, constant working state and allocator overhead are outside the record quota. It is not a numeric-entry, byte or peak RAM limit. No replay, truncation or partial trace is returned on quota failure. Copies own all storage; independent calls share no mutable state.
    algorithms::GnomeSortWorkSelected actual operations of an executing gnome sort, initially zero. Counts exclude input copying, identity initialization, allocations, loop tests, FLOPs and wall time. A boundary visit at index zero advances without a key comparison. Every strict adjacent swap moves the pointer backwards once. Diagnostic counters are checked before increment and own no references.
    algorithms::GoertzelEventOne owned fixed-size actual recurrence record, without numerical replay. For sample records index is zero based, input is x[index], before_s1/s2 are the actual prior states and value is the evaluated s0. State assignments then make s1=value and s2=before_s1. For stop, index=N, before fields are final states and value is raw power. For initial index/before/input are zero and value is the actual coefficient, or zero for empty input. Metadata input is unused zero.
    algorithms::GoertzelRunOwned actual selection, terminal states and unnormalized raw squared-magnitude estimate. For bin_indexed calls bin holds the supplied size_t index, never reduced mod N; frequency_mode/selected_bin are then unused placeholders. For legacy frequency calls selected_bin is the actual signed int; for unrounded calls it is unused zero. Empty input has has_coefficient=false, zero omega/coefficient/states/power and zero updates; no frequency grid is evaluated. The supplied bin is still retained for empty bin-indexed calls. All unused fields are placeholders. power is not normalized by sample count, a PSD, calibrated watts or mean-square signal power. Cancellation can produce a FINITE NEGATIVE value, retained without clamping. Very long blocks, large unreduced angles and cancellation can lose accuracy even when all states are finite. Copies own every scalar.
    algorithms::GoertzelTraceOwned ordinary result plus all fixed-size records captured online. Complete initial/sample/stop records are charged, not numeric entries, bytes or peak RAM. Input, root, ordinary result/selection metadata, constant working states and allocator overhead are excluded. No input aliases, replay, truncation or partial return survive. Copies own their history vectors.
    rl::GoExploreResultResult of deterministic archive exploration.
    algorithms::GoldenEventOwned before/after states and the actual new callback for one search event.
    algorithms::GoldenResultMidpoint estimate, evaluated objective and iteration count from golden-section maximization.
    algorithms::GoldenRunOwned ordinary result plus actual final bracket, callback count and stop reason.
    algorithms::GoldenStateActual endpoints, two cached probes and their evaluated values.
    algorithms::GoldenTraceOwned run and complete online initial/update/stop records.
    algorithms::GoldschmidtRunOwned scalar output, normalization states and selected loop-operation counts. No callbacks, input references or histories are retained. The ordinary double-returning API uses the same kernel with no record allocation.
    algorithms::GoldschmidtStateActual normalized numerator and denominator, not a mathematical quotient certificate. Owns two doubles; a scaled numerator may underflow to zero or overflow to infinity.
    algorithms::GoldschmidtStepOne complete actual before/factor/after update captured during execution. All values own primitive storage. The same rounded factor feeds both products.
    algorithms::GoldschmidtTraceOwned run plus one whole record per actual update, without replay. Initial normalization lives in run.initial and is not a history record. Copying duplicates the vector. Ordinary state/output, allocation overhead, inputs and the initial/final scalar records are excluded from the quota. O(t) retained history; quota units are records, not bytes or peak RAM.
    algorithms::GolombTraceOwned actual bits, complete spans and selected bit-visit counts. Encoding owns emitted bits; decoding owns only the consumed prefix, excluding any unread tail. Each word owns its value; no input references survive. Unary counts include terminators. Remainder counts include actual short/long payload positions. These selected visits exclude preflight, copies and CPU costs. The quota counts words only, not bits, bytes, capacity or peak RAM.
    algorithms::GolombWordActual complete codeword boundaries and decoded/emitted integer parts. Owns scalars; indices are half-open bit positions in the associated trace.
    nn::models::GoogLeNetConfigReference or compact dimensions and dropout settings for GoogLeNet.
    nn::models::GoogLeNetOutputsIntermediate activations and logits from GoogLeNet.
    nn::GradcheckOptionsFinite-difference step and element-wise Jacobian comparison tolerances. Use deterministic functions and suitably precise floating inputs; options are not validated.
    nn::GradcheckResultWhether checked derivatives agree and diagnostics for the first failed comparison.
    nn::GradientAccumulatorSums gradients over several micro-batches.
    optim::GradientDescentGradientDescent on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Velocity is momentum*velocity-step_size*gradient. Updates before testing the gradient just used or absolute objective change. Equal objective values can stop an oscillation away from stationarity. O(p) reset velocity state; no line search. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::GradientDescentOptionsConfiguration for GradientDescent; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    cv::GradientFieldPer-pixel image derivatives, row-major like the input.
    nn::GradOptionsOptions for grad.
    geometry::GrahamAnalysisOwned strict hull, earliest original identities and actual selected work. With at least three distinct points, output starts at the lowest-y then lowest-x pivot and runs counterclockwise without repeating the first vertex. Collinear input returns the pivot and farthest endpoint. Empty/singleton/two distinct points retain the legacy lexicographic shortcut, with no scan work. Exact coordinate equality merges signed zeros; the earliest matching original record supplies the coordinate representation. No caller storage is retained.
    geometry::GrahamEventOne actual test, pop or push, referring to trace.ordered indices. Constant-size edits avoid quadratic stack snapshots. A test leaves the stack unchanged; a,b and turn describe its actual operands/sign. On edits those fields are zero placeholders. point is the edited point, or candidate on tests.
    geometry::GrahamTraceOwned actual angular order, strict hull and complete chronological stack edits. ordered starts with the chosen pivot for at least three distinct points; the legacy small-input shortcut instead retains lexicographic order and no events. Each indexed point owns its earliest original coordinate representation. Capture performs no extra sorting or orientation replay. Copying owns storage.
    geometry::GrahamWorkSelected native preparation and scan work, excluding validation and allocation. Sort counts depend on the standard library and input order. Angular and sweep tests call the exact binary64 orientation predicate; other comparisons do not. The scan pushes each distinct point once when there are at least three.
    algorithms::GramSchmidtOptionsAbsolute residual acceptance and complete input/optional capture limits. The threshold is an order- and scale-dependent heuristic, not a numerical rank certificate. Pass two repeats the modified projection sweep before one final normalization; it does not change the threshold or promise exact orthogonality.
    algorithms::GramSchmidtProjectionOne actual modified projection, with owned complete before/after residuals. coefficient is the dot of before with the current accepted basis row, not a replay from the original input. Pass indices are zero based. All vectors own their values; basis identifies a row in trace.run.basis.
    algorithms::GramSchmidtRowActual final residual and acceptance decision for one original row. residual is stored before normalization. accepted_rows counts basis rows immediately after the decision, including this row if accepted.
    algorithms::GramSchmidtRunOwned accepted row vectors, their original row identities and actual work. Rows are accepted when their computed residual norm is strictly above the absolute tolerance. They approximate an orthonormal set; one pass can lose orthogonality or accept dependent rounding noise. No exact span/rank guarantee. Empty input returns empty; rectangular zero-width rows are all skipped. No references to caller input survive. Copying owns all nested storage.
    algorithms::GramSchmidtTraceOwned actual projections, row decisions and result from one shared execution. Capture performs no arithmetic replay. Floating-value quota units are 1+2d per projection (coefficient, before and after) and 1+d per row decision (norm and residual). Metadata, ordinary basis/output/work, capacities and allocation overhead are excluded: this is not a byte or peak-RAM budget. Online admission precedes each dot request and capture vector copies; zero disables the policy cap. Failure returns no partial trace. With full rank, O(k²d) retained history can be much larger than O(kd) ordinary working/output storage. Caller inputs are never retained or mutated.
    algorithms::GramSchmidtWorkSelected operations in the producing native loop, not timings or all CPU work. Dot products count one request per projection plus one residual self-dot per input row. Products/additions count d terms per dot, including the initial zero addition. Updates count d products and d subtractions per projection; divisions count normalization coordinates of accepted rows only.
    nn::GraphAttentionHeadOwn the score, attention, and output tensors of a graph attention head.
    nn::GraphDiffusionForecastFeatures from each diffusion order and the associated direct predictions.
    nn::GraphForecastWindowsNode-major histories and their immediately subsequent observations.
    nn::GraphPoolOwn pooled features, coarsened adjacency and node assignments.
    geometry::GraphSearchResultResult of proximity_graph_search().
    nn::GraphSessionOwn a trusted local GraphDef loaded into a CPU TensorFlow session.
    nn::GraphTraceEventOne operation interval from TensorFlow RunMetadata.
    algorithms::GraspCandidateActual scores and RCL membership for one unplaced candidate. Scores concern assigned neighbors only; side zero wins exact g0/g1 ties.
    algorithms::GraspConstructionOne actual construction step, owning all candidate scores and chosen RNG state. pick is an index into candidates, not a vertex ID or RCL rank. Quota admission precedes scores, candidate snapshots and the one modulo RNG draw.
    algorithms::GraspCutCheckSeparately evaluated supplied partition, not a producing GRASP trace. Floating gains use the same sequential incident sums and 1e-12 comparison as local search. tolerance_local certifies only those computed tests. It is not a global or exact-real optimum certificate. All storage is owned.
    algorithms::GraspExactCutOwned exact-enumeration result and actual examined complement classes. Exact refers to exhaustive partitions, not exact arithmetic on arbitrary floating weights. Values use sequential double sums; integer fixtures with exact representable sums admit exact comparisons. Side zero is fixed at vertex zero, removing complement symmetry; strict value ties keep the first.
    algorithms::GraspFlipOne actual vertex-flip test in a cyclic immediate-improvement scan. before_side is the label read before possible mutation; delta is the sequential signed incident-weight sum. Later tests in the same pass see earlier flips.
    algorithms::GraspMaxCutResultLegacy owned feasible partition and producing final cut value. side contains zeros/ones by vertex; value sums u<v crossing adjacency entries once, including parallel entries. This is a feasible value, not an optimum certificate. Empty graphs return zero with an empty partition.
    algorithms::GraspOptionsComplete input, local-pass and actual optional capture limits. Basic shape/endpoint/finite/no-loop/parameter validation precedes input caps; reciprocal-multiplicity validation allocates only after those input caps. A local pass includes a full cyclic scan, including the terminal no-flip scan.
    algorithms::GraspRestartActual completed restart with owned pre/post-local partitions and best-so-far value. constructed_side is captured before local search, final_side after its terminal scan. No constructed objective is evaluated by the producing kernel.
    algorithms::GraspRunOwned ordinary best result and actual selected work without retained histories. Copying owns the partition; no input references or callback state survive.
    algorithms::GraspTraceOwned actual construction, flip and completed-restart histories from one execution. Logical capture units: 1 per construction step plus 1 per candidate record; 1 per flip test; 1 per restart plus 2n retained partition labels. A restart's whole 1+2n requirement is admitted before its construction; step and flip requirements are admitted online before their producing score/delta work. Excludes record fields, allocation overhead/capacities, validation and ordinary result/work. This is not a byte/peak-RAM bound. No replay or partial result. Histories own storage; ordinary/run calls allocate no optional histories.
    algorithms::GraspWorkSelected actual construction, local-search and objective work, excluding validation/copies. Construction candidates are scored once per unplaced vertex per step. Neighbor visits count every inspected adjacency entry, even if unassigned or not crossing. RNG words count exactly one modulo draw per placement.
    graphics::GrayscaleImagePanelOwned rectangular grayscale values and a panel title. Rendering requires finite values in0..255; the source values are never changed.
    optim::GreyWolfOptimizerGrey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) on an ArbitraryFunction within a box constraint: a population of wolves is guided each iteration by its three best members (alpha, beta, delta), moving every wolf to the elementwise average of three independently randomized pulls toward those leaders. Derivative-free. Mirjalili, Mirjalili & Lewis (2014), "Grey wolf optimizer", Advances in Engineering Software, 69, 46-61.
    optim::GreyWolfOptimizerOptions
    rl::environments::GridBaseOwn the GridBase simulation state or interface.
    algorithms::GridCellUpdateOne validated occupancy change, applied in input order by update_cells(). Repeated coordinates are allowed; the last value wins. Default is an unblocked origin update, not a request to initialize a planner.
    rl::environments::GridGameOwn the GridGame simulation state or interface.
    algorithms::GridPathResultOwned grid route preserving the historical field order and failure convention. Coordinates are(row,column), endpoints included, four-neighbor unit steps. On failure path is empty,cost zero,found false; cost is meaningful only if found.
