    bayes::GridPosteriorPosterior summaries computed on a grid.
    nn::GridSampleOptionsOptions of grid_sample (PyTorch grid_sample semantics, NHWC).
    rl::environments::GridWorldSource5x6 wall grid with negative unit step rewards.
    nn::models::GrnOutputsGlobal response normalization map and differentiated output.
    GroupByPipeline step created by group_by(); frame | step yields a GroupedDataFrame.
    dstruct::GroupedDataFramedplyr-style grouped-DataFrame handle returned by DataFrame::group_by(): pairs a copy of the source DataFrame with a set of key columns, deferring aggregation until summarise()/count() is called. Holding the source by value (rather than a reference or pointer) keeps chains like df.select(...).group_by(...).summarise(...) safe, since the intermediate select() result is a temporary that would otherwise dangle.
    nn::GroupFairnessGapsPairwise absolute differences in binary classifier rates.
    nn::GroupFairnessRatesBinary decision counts and rates for one group.
    algorithms::GroverOptionsComplete state and full-phase-capture caps, each zero disabling its policy limit. State units are complex amplitudes, not bytes. Capture counts the initial N amplitudes and 2N+1 per iteration (oracle state, diffused state and oracle mean). Metadata, ordinary final state, capacities and allocation overhead are excluded.
    algorithms::GroverResultLegacy deterministic summary, without sampling or state collapse. measured retains its historical name but is an argmax; success_prob is the actual squared target amplitude, unclamped and not renormalized. Roundoff can make the state norm differ from one. No quantum device or hidden-target search is performed: the simulator is given the marked index.
    algorithms::GroverRunOwned final native state, deterministic summary and selected producing work. State preparation uses the existing Hadamard gate arithmetic; iterations use actual complex-vector reflection loops. No analytic probability substitution, normalization, probability clamping, sampling or input references.
    algorithms::GroverStepActual oracle and diffusion states captured during one iteration. before is the preceding step's after_diffusion, or trace.initial on step one. oracle_mean is the actual sequential complex mean used by diffusion. Each vector owns storage; no second execution reconstructs these phase states.
    algorithms::GroverTraceOwned initial state, actual full-phase snapshots and final producing result. Known complete requirement N+K(2N+1) is preflighted before state allocation or gates. No truncation, replay, partial result or retained references. Capture adds O(KN) owned complex values to ordinary O(N) working/output storage; units exclude metadata, final ordinary output, capacity and peak RAM. Copying is deep.
    algorithms::GroverWorkSelected actual state-operator visits, excluding snapshots and probability extraction. One oracle call is one known-target phase flip in this simulator. It is not a gate synthesis, physical device timing or a classical black-box query count. Hadamard pairs count the actual two-amplitude gate pairs, not scalar FLOPs.
    nn::models::GumbelCategoricalAutoencoderOutputOwn categorical posterior, soft/hard sample, decoder and objective endpoints.
    nn::models::GumbelCategoricalSampleOwn posterior categorical probabilities, a relaxed draw and hard Gumbel-max indices.
    nn::models::GumbelNoiseBankOwn the source-compatible uniform/Gumbel banks and their Float32 model inputs.

    H

    algorithms::HalleyRunOwned final legacy summary, precise stopping reason and producing callback counts. No callback or input references survive. Legacy iterations count loop inspections, including the successful residual inspection, rather than updates; with cap zero the final callback is evaluated but iterations remains zero.
    algorithms::HalleyStepOwned actual callback inspection and optional Halley update from one execution. Derivative and denominator fields are meaningful only when derivatives_evaluated; next is x unless updated. The final budget inspection evaluates only f, even if its residual is not accepted. No extra callback evaluations reconstruct records.
    algorithms::HalleyTraceOwned chronological actual inspections and producing run; no replay or truncation. One record per f call, including final budget check, is admitted before that callback. Default cap one million records, zero disables it. Record counts are not bytes, capacities or peak RAM. Copying is deep; no retained callable state.
    algorithms::HalleyWorkActual selected callback calls and applied updates, not FLOPs or elapsed time. Callback bodies can have arbitrary costs; no timing comparison follows from these counts.
    nn::HamiltonianNetworkOutputHamiltonian and corresponding canonical time derivatives.
    algorithms::HamiltonianSearchResult of a Hamiltonian-path search.
    algorithms::Hamming74AuditFixed exhaustive codebook and decoder outcomes grouped by actual channel error weight. Totals include all16 transmitted codewords and128 masks (2048 decodings). Results describe this deterministic decoder, not an assumed real-channel law. No heap, random draws or caller references; weight arrays have indices0..7.
    algorithms::Hamming74DecodedOwned decoded data and the applied syndrome correction, without a recovery certificate. corrected means a flip was applied. Only an at-most-one-bit channel error assumption makes that flip correct; two errors are miscorrected. A zero syndrome can also hide three or more errors. No input references retained.
    algorithms::Hamming74ParityOwned actual inputs and running XORs of one even-parity check. Positions are one-based. Prefix0 is the first input bit; prefix1..3 use exactly three producing XORs. No replay, heap storage or borrowed state.
    algorithms::Hamming74TraceOwned fixed-size actual parity checks, syndrome and correction from one decoding. All arrays own values; copying is deep. No heap, optional history, replay or truncation is needed for this fixed7-bit/3-check trace. Work excludes snapshot copies, validation and weighted syndrome assembly. Input remains unchanged.
    algorithms::Hamming74WorkSelected actual decoder visits and XORs, excluding validation/capture/assembly. Fixed-size input uses12 parity bit visits,9 parity XORs,0or1 correction flips and4 final data reads. These counts are not timing or total machine work.
    optim::HarmonySearchHarmony search on an ArbitraryFunction within a box constraint: a fixed-size harmony memory of candidate solutions is improvised one new vector at a time, mixing memory consideration, pitch adjustment, and random selection per dimension, with greedy replacement of the worst memory member. Derivative-free.
    optim::HarmonySearchOptions
    algorithms::HashAvalancheOwned actual single-input-bit hash sensitivity summary.
    nn::HashedDenseMapFixed row-major map from dense connections to signed bucket values.
    algorithms::HeapPermutationOptionsComplete output/history policy caps, each zero disabling that policy. Output values count integers across all rows, not bytes or peak memory. Trace entries count swap records only; ordinary output/fields/capacity and allocation overhead are excluded. All known requirements precede copies and swaps.
    algorithms::HeapPermutationRunOwned complete rows in legacy Heap order with selected producing work. Arbitrary integers and repeated values are allowed. Positions are permuted, so equal values produce repeated rows; no sorting or deduplication occurs. Input and output rows own separate storage, including the single empty row.
    algorithms::HeapPermutationSizeChecked exact logical size of a complete Heap enumeration, without generation. Counts include one empty permutation for n=0. Copied values exclude the initial working copy and snapshots; recursive calls include the initial call. This is a count model, not bytes, peak RAM, timing or an allocation guarantee.
    algorithms::HeapPermutationSwapActual swap event preparing the next emitted row, with zero-based indices. before values come directly from the producing array immediately before the swap. No pre/post state replay or copied snapshots; ordinary output owns rows.
    algorithms::HeapPermutationTraceOwned complete rows and actual swap records captured in their producing execution. Complete n!-1 records are preflighted before any working copy, allocation or swap. No replay, truncation or partial result; copying is deep. Ordinary output has O(n*n!) values plus O(n!) row objects; capture adds O(n!) records.
    algorithms::HeapPermutationWorkSelected actual producing recursive calls, emissions, swaps and output value copies. Excludes validation, reserve/allocation, initial working copy and trace writes. Equal-valued swaps still count as actual swaps, although values do not change. Counts are not FLOPs, byte traffic or elapsed time.
    algorithms::HeapSortOptionsComplete input cap and complete-snapshot plus online-swap capture policy. Zero disables either optional policy, not count/container representability. Capture units are one per swap record plus1+n per full snapshot (one record and n integer values). Fields, capacity, allocation overhead and ordinary output are excluded; this is not bytes or peak RAM.
    algorithms::HeapSortRunOwned sorted output and actual selected build/extraction work from one execution. Input values are copied once into working/output storage. Arbitrary int64 values and ties are supported, no references retained or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::HeapSortSnapshotOwned actual state at input, completed build or completed extraction repair. Build/extraction snapshots have a valid heap in[0,heap_size), and an ascending suffix at least as large as every heap value. Input snapshots need not be heaps. swaps_done ties the snapshot to a prefix of actual swap events, without replay.
    algorithms::HeapSortSwapActual exchange recorded immediately before the producing swap. Indices are zero-based; before-values are read from the producing array. Root parking records the old heap size; sift swaps record the reduced active heap size. A swap can exchange equal values and remains an actual exchange.
    algorithms::HeapSortTraceOwned actual checkpoints/exchanges and producing result, without a second sort. Always captures input and completed build, including empty/singleton inputs, then n-1 post-repair states for n>=1. Known snapshot units are preflighted before allocation/copy; online whole swap records are admitted before swaps. No truncation or partial result. Copies are deep. Snapshot storage is O(n²) values and events O(n log n), in addition to ordinary O(n) output, unlike the O(1) extra space of the legacy in-place algorithm.
    algorithms::HeapSortWorkSelected actual sift visits, strict key comparisons and swaps. Excludes child-index tests, allocation, snapshots, validation and byte traffic. A sift visit includes the terminal leaf/order check; root swaps count the extraction exchange separately. These are not elapsed time or total FLOPs.
    algorithms::HeatGridValidated uniform heat-grid configuration with homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries. nx interior points lie at rounded i*dx for i=1,...,nx; endpoints are exactly 0,L. Rounded interior coordinates must remain strictly inside the domain. r=D*dt/(2*dx*dx). Coefficients and final time must fit finite double storage.
    algorithms::HeatSineModeOwned unit sine-mode controls separating continuous, spatial and time errors. For mode m=1,...,nx, initial[i]=sin(m*pi*i/(nx+1)). continuous solves the continuous heat equation at the grid points; semidiscrete uses the exact central-difference eigenvalue; discrete applies the ideal CN amplification factor steps times. These are floating evaluations of modal formulas, independent of the Thomas recurrence, not arbitrary-precision certificates. Boundary values are set to exact zero. Negative amplification alternates sign.
    algorithms::HeatStepOwned actual state and uneliminated right-hand side at one heat time level. Initial state has index/time zero, an empty rhs and zero scaled_residual. profiles include both exact zero endpoints; rhs holds nx interior entries. RMS uses the nx interior values. scaled_residual is the maximum rowwise |A*u-rhs|/(|rhs|+|A|*|u|), with zero/zero defined as zero. It is a backward-error diagnostic of the stored tridiagonal solve, not a PDE error.
    algorithms::HermiteEvaluationOwned actual basis and weighted terms from the producing Hermite evaluation. No second computation, references, allocations or symbolic substitution. Terms are in h00*y0,h10*h*m0,h01*y1,h11*h*m1 order; value uses the retained left-associated sum. Slopes have dy/dx units, so width factors matter. Roundoff remains visible; this is not an interval bound or exact rational result.
    optim::HessianFunction
    algorithms::HiddenMarkovModelOwned finite-alphabet hidden Markov model parameters in state-major order. Initial has N entries, transition N rows of N entries, emission N equal rows of M>0 entries. Forward-backward and path-query APIs validate all shapes first, then finite weights in[0,1] and each distribution's long-double sum within absolute1e-12 of1. They never normalize caller parameters. The entirely empty model is accepted with empty observations. Other legacy consumers may assume valid parameters. State and symbol IDs are zero based; arrays own their storage.
    nn::ml::HiddenMarkovModelRun scaled categorical HMM inference and one expectation/maximization update.
    fda::HierarchicalBSplineClassical (overlay) hierarchical B-spline in the style of Forsey and Bartels: every cell of a dyadic tree may carry its own local "detail" TensorBSpline.
    bayes::HierarchicalNormalPosteriorExact posterior summaries of the hierarchical Normal model.
    nn::models::HierarchicalVaeOutputOwn all nineteen spatial/posterior/prior/reconstruction/objective hierarchy endpoints.
    nn::models::HierarchyGaussianOwn the mean and log variance of a diagonal conditional Gaussian posterior.
    nn::models::HierarchyPriorOutputOwn all stages of an image-free ancestral sample from a learned Gaussian hierarchy.
    nn::HiFiGanCriticScores and two feature maps from one waveform critic.
    nn::HiFiGanLossScalar HiFi-GAN objectives for alternating updates.
    algorithms::HighWaterMarkResult of high_water_mark().
    nn::models::HighwayClassifierOutputsProjection, every coupled-gate hidden layer and classifier logits.
    nn::models::HighwayOutputsTransform activations, sigmoid gates and their coupled-carry mixture.
    algorithms::HillClimbOptionsNative coordinate-search and selected-execution policies.
    algorithms::HillClimbResultLegacy owned best point/value layout.
    algorithms::HillClimbRunOwned best value and actual selected search work.
    algorithms::HillClimbStepOne actual initial evaluation or signed coordinate proposal.
    algorithms::HillGridOwned samples of a one-dimensional objective and its largest visited grid value.
    algorithms::HirschbergOptionsComplete input admission and online producing-work/history policies. Counts are not bytes/peak RAM: input counts bytes of both strings, work counts rolling DP cells and base-case pair scans, capture counts one record plus three score arrays per split. Fields/capacity/output/frame overhead excluded. Zero disables each optional cap. Orientation can change tied optimal rows.
    algorithms::HirschbergRunOwned alignment, actual work and orientation from the producing execution. Aligned output rows are always in original caller order, even if internal orientation transposes the inputs. No references retained; copies are deep.
    algorithms::HirschbergSplitActual forward/reverse profiles and first maximizing split from one recursive call. Ranges and midpoints are zero-based offsets in internally oriented inputs. reverse[j] scores the suffix beginning at column j, already reindexed. All vectors own actual values; total is the producing split sum, not replay.
    algorithms::HirschbergTraceOwned complete split histories and producing run, with online whole-record admission. Only nonbase split calls have records, in actual preorder. Input views and temporary score rows are not retained. Capture failure returns no partial trace. Additional retained histories do not obey the untraced row-space bound.
    algorithms::HirschbergWorkSelected actual producing work and live rolling score-value peak. Peak excludes output, stack frames, views, trace copies, capacity and bytes. Left result row is held during the reverse sweep, so up to three rows live, then all score rows are destroyed before either recursive child is entered.
    HistogramAn owned histogram plot with equal-width bins and chainable heading setters, like R's hist(x, breaks = bins).
    algorithms::HitsOptionsComplete input and online whole-iteration capture caps, each zero disabling policy. Capture counts2n initial score values, then1+4n per complete iteration: one record and raw/normalized authority/hub vectors. Scalar fields, ordinary output, capacity and allocation overhead excluded; not bytes/peak memory.
    algorithms::HITSResultOwned historical hub/authority vectors and actual completed iteration count. Ordinary nonzero updated vectors have approximately unit Euclidean norm; edgeless updates are zero, and zero budget returns uniform initialization. Nonempty initialization uses1/sqrt(n). No input references are retained.
    algorithms::HitsRunOwned actual HITS result, stop branch and selected producing work. last_change is meaningful only when has_step; otherwise it is zero sentinel. A small update change does not certify a unique principal direction, graph relevance, convergence rate or absence of competing dominant components.
    algorithms::HitsStepActual sequential authority-then-hub update captured during its producing pass. Hub raw sums use this iteration's normalized authorities. Norms are actual sequential sum-of-squares roots, not analytic substitutions or rescaling certificates. All vectors own storage and copy independently.
    algorithms::HitsTraceOwned actual initialization, complete update records and producing result. Initial2n values admitted before output allocation; each known1+4n update record admitted before that iteration's allocations/edge work. No truncation, replay, partial result or retained references. Capture adds O(Kn) score values beyond O(n) ordinary working/output storage; fields/capacity excluded.
    algorithms::HitsWorkSelected actual update visits, excluding validation, initialization and capture copies. Duplicate edges count repeatedly. Norm visits are squared-value sum terms; divisions occur only for nonzero norms. Change visits compare both score vectors at each vertex. Counts are not timing, FLOPs or total memory traffic.
    algorithms::HmacKeyAvalancheOwned complete experiment, not a randomness or unforgeability certificate. All supplied key bits are flipped once, least-significant bit first within each byte. Histograms cover every possible distance without clipping.
    algorithms::HmacOptionsComplete combined key/message input policy before copying or hashing. The cap counts input bytes once, not allocations, bytes hashed or peak memory.
    algorithms::HmacReferenceCaseOwned public RFC4231 HMAC-SHA-256 input and expected full/prefix hex. expected_hex contains 64 characters except case 5's 32-character 128-bit prefix. The full-tag API remains 32 bytes for every case. No references are retained.
    algorithms::HmacRunOwned tag and producing call-boundary diagnostics; no input references retained.
    algorithms::HmacTraceFixed-size owned intermediates captured during the actual producing HMAC. This educational record contains key material; example keys are public fixtures. No replay, message-history copy or input references. Arrays occupy 256 byte values beyond run (three 64-byte blocks plus two 32-byte digests), excluding metadata/padding. key_digest is meaningful only when run.key_hashed; otherwise its zero initialization is a sentinel. This is not secure-erasing storage.
    algorithms::HmacWorkSelected work recorded at actual SHA-256 invocation boundaries. Block counts use SHA-256 padding length, not a captured round/compression trace. Excludes pad generation, copying, allocation, hex formatting and trace copies.
    bayes::HMCHamiltonian Monte Carlo with a fixed leapfrog trajectory length and Nesterov dual-averaging step-size adaptation during warmup (Hoffman & Gelman 2014), using an identity mass matrix. Samples from the distribution proportional to exp(log_posterior) over unconstrained real parameters.
    bayes::HMCOptionsSettings for HMC.
    bayes::HMCProposalA fixed HMC proposal and its log acceptance diagnostic.
    bayes::HMCResultOutput of HMC::sample().
    algorithms::HmmPathEnumerationOwned widened path sum, state marginals and best joint path. A bounded small-model reference, not a fast inference method or exact arithmetic. Time0 is the least significant base-N digit; strict best-weight updates keep the first enumerated tie. Impossible evidence yields probability0, log_likelihood=-infinity, zero marginal placeholders and no best path. Empty observations enumerate one empty path of weight1. Long-double positive product underflow throws.
    nn::ml::HmmResultOwn detached smoothing, best-path and one-update HMM results.
    algorithms::HmmSampleA sampled path of a discrete HMM.
    nn::ml::HmmStateinitial [K], transition [K,K], emission [K,V]; all float64 probability rows.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpGraphOwned bipartite graph descriptor with separate zero-based side labels. Repeated edges and order are retained; algorithms validate endpoints on use. Default construction gives the empty graph. No references or shared state.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpOptionsComplete graph and online logical-history policies, each zero disabling its cap. Input caps count all supplied vertices/edge entries, including isolated or repeated entries. Trace counts records and retained vertex/distance values, not bytes/capacity/peak memory. No sampling or truncation.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpPathOwned actual shortest augmenting path immediately before its producing flip. left[i]->right[i] are the path's forward unmatched edges. Before the flip, right[i] is matched to left[i+1] except for the final free right vertex. The root is free and all path vertices are distinct. k pairs mean2k-1 graph edges; flipping gains one matched pair. No replay or input references.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpPhaseOwned actual BFS labels and subsequent shortest-path flips, including terminal BFS. left_distance counts matched-right-to-left hops from free left roots, before DFS dead-end pruning; SIZE_MAX means undiscovered. BFS stops expanding labels at/above the shortest free-right distance, though already discovered frontier labels can remain. Every augmentation has shortest_pairs forward pairs. Terminal BFS has shortest_pairs=0 and no augmentations; its complete reachable sets produce the run's minimum cover. Records own all arrays.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpRunOwned actual matching, terminal-BFS minimum vertex cover and selected work. cover_left/cover_right use their own side indices in ascending order. They cover every supplied edge and their combined size equals matching size, certifying optimality independently of tie choices. No references retained.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpTraceOwned producing BFS/path history from an initially empty matching. Each BFS admits1+n_left record/distance units before its work; each known path admits1+2k record/vertex units before copies and flipping. Working buffers, ordinary output, metadata/capacity/byte peak memory are excluded. No partial result, truncation, post-hoc reconstruction or retained references.
    algorithms::HopcroftKarpWorkSelected actual producing visits, excluding validation/copy/allocation/certificate/capture costs. Duplicate edges count repeatedly when visited. Pair writes count matched-pair assignments along paths, each of which writes both orientation arrays. These counters are not timing, FLOPs or complete memory traffic.
    algorithms::HopcroftOptionsComplete projected graph and online logical history policies, each zero disabling its cap. Counts include a materialized sink and unreachable states. Trace units count records and retained state IDs, not bytes/capacity/peak memory. Input validation precedes caps and completed graph/predecessor allocations.
    algorithms::HopcroftPassOwned actual preimage and splits from one producing splitter/symbol pass. Empty preimages retain an empty split list; a zero-symbol machine has no passes despite actual splitter pops. Splitter labels refer to the copied set popped at this pop index, even if later passes refine its original block.
    algorithms::HopcroftRunOwned reachable quotient, completed-state partition labels and selected producing work. blocks index completed states, including any sink and unreachable input states. Their IDs describe the final internal partition, not the quotient's reachable BFS numbering. result starts at0 and retains only reachable quotient blocks.
    algorithms::HopcroftSplitOwned actual block split and its producing worklist branch. Every vector is ascending in original completed-state labels. inside and outside partition parent exactly. Both means an existing pending parent was replaced; it does not mean two additional pushes.
    algorithms::HopcroftTraceOwned actual initial partition, chronological producing passes and final run. Initial units are one per block plus one per retained state ID. Each pass adds 1+|splitter|+|predecessors|; each proper split adds 1+|parent|+|inside|+|outside|. Counts are admitted before history copies, after their triggering sets are known. Working sets and ordinary output are outside this capture policy. No truncation, replay, partial result or retained input references.
    algorithms::HopcroftWorkSelected producing visits of the ordered-set worklist implementation. These exclude validation, completion, set insertion/comparison internals, copying, allocation, quotient construction and history; not timing or FLOPs.
    algorithms::HopfieldExperimentOwned public original100-neuron/three-memory fixture and actual complete noise study. Retains three extra random states before ten with-replacement probe toggles, preserving the original data RNG stream. Those ten draws need not change ten distinct positions. Stored weights, actual trace/trials and summaries are owned.
    algorithms::HopfieldNetworkOwned symmetric zero-diagonal Hopfield weight matrix with its historical aggregate layout. Nonempty models require square finite weights, exact symmetry and zero diagonal when used by energy/recall. Hebbian storage does not guarantee every supplied pattern is stable, nor recall of the nearest stored pattern. No references or shared state are retained; do not mutate weights concurrently with a call.
    algorithms::HopfieldNoiseSummaryFinite-trial observed noise summary, with bit agreement distinct from exact recovery. No population accuracy or confidence claim. Each trial has100 neurons; zero trials is a default-construction sentinel, not produced by the study helper.
    algorithms::HopfieldNoiseTrialOwned actual corruption/recall trial from the original fixed-size noise study. The noise parameter is a per-bit selection percentage, not an exact Hamming distance. Full input/output states and the actual seeded run remain available.
    algorithms::HopfieldOptionsComplete neuron/weight and online logical-history caps, each zero disabling policy. Input validation precedes these policies and internal working copies. History units count records/state/index values, not bytes/capacity/peak memory.
    algorithms::HopfieldRecallRunOwned actual final state, completed sweeps, stop branch and selected work. No nearest-memory or stored-pattern guarantee. NoChange certifies only the computed local-field update rule, not an exact-arithmetic energy certificate.
    algorithms::HopfieldRecallTraceOwned actual initialization and producing sweep/update history, without replay. Initial1+N units count one record and its state. Each sweep admits1+3N before shuffle/copies: one sweep record, N order IDs, N end-state values and N update records. Scalar record fields/metadata/capacity/working/output/byte peak memory excluded. Histories add O(S*N+1) storage; diagnostic energies add O((S+1)N*N) work beyond ordinary recall. No truncation/partial result/input references.
    algorithms::HopfieldSweepOwned actual shuffled sweep and its end-state/energy observations. Energy observations are extra sequential full-matrix calculations at actual states, not replayed dynamics or exact/compensated arithmetic. They can round.
    algorithms::HopfieldUpdateActual local field and sign decision at its producing asynchronous update. Later updates in the same sweep see this decision immediately. Exact zero, including negative zero, chooses+1, preserving historical code behavior.
    algorithms::HopfieldWorkSelected actual recall and separate diagnostic-energy visits. Excludes validation, copies, RNG/shuffle, allocation and history bookkeeping. Fields include all diagonal zero terms. Counts are not timing or total traffic.
    algorithms::HorspoolAlignmentActual right-to-left comparison outcome and window-end shift for one Horspool alignment. Ending byte is always text[position+m-1], even if a different text byte caused a mismatch. Full matches use mismatch_index=m rather than a valid pattern index.
    algorithms::HorspoolTraceOwned Horspool shifts, actual alignment records and the shared scan result. Tables and records contain no borrowed bytes. Empty/oversized patterns have no alignments; empty patterns have zero shifts. Metadata and all positions count bytes.
    cv::HoughCircleA detected circle: center, radius, and the raw vote count that found it.
    cv::HoughLineA detected line in the classical (rho, theta) normal-form parameterization: every point (x, y) on the line satisfies x*cos(theta) + y*sin(theta) = rho. Represents an INFINITE line, not a segment – see line_endpoints() to clip it to an image.
    nn::models::HourglassConfigDescribe square stacked-hourglass architecture metadata.
    nn::models::HourglassResultOwn raw intermediate-supervision heads and every retained graph stage.
    nn::models::HRNetConfigConfigure HRNetV2 widths,residual depths and repeated fusion module counts.
    nn::models::HRNetOutputsOwn HRNet logits,fused coarse scores and persistent final branch maps.
    algorithms::HSPOwned ungapped segment pair with zero-based starts and half-open ranges. The same length applies to both sequences. Score is the sum of match/mismatch contributions; it is not a bit score, probability or E-value. No strings are borrowed.
    image::HSVA pixel color in HSV space: h in [0, 360), s and v in [0, 1].
    algorithms::HuffmanBuildRunOwned byte code and the shared exact-weight integer construction that produced it. Integer symbols are unsigned byte values0..255; ordinary topology/lengths accompany the byte model. No references or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::HuffmanBuildTraceOwned actual byte frequencies, merge records and producing byte model. No source-text copy or retained references. Merge quota excludes fixed256 frequency entries and ordinary output; it is not a memory-byte limit.
    algorithms::HuffmanCodeOwned byte codebook and full decoding tree, preserving historical aggregate layout. Codes contain nonempty binary words; a single leaf uses"0". Empty code has root=-1 and empty map/tree. Nonempty root may be any valid index. Unique byte leaves, full binary structure and exact map/path agreement are required by codecs. Containers own storage; do not mutate during a concurrent call.
    algorithms::HuffmanCountNodeActual generic construction topology, with original integer symbol indices at leaves. Node IDs are compact positive leaves in ascending symbol order, then actual parent creation order. Leaf child indices use kHuffmanNoNode.
    algorithms::HuffmanCountsRunOwned exact-weight construction result for an integer-symbol alphabet. All uint64 counts are accepted without restricting their sum to uint64. Exact totals/costs use decimal strings to avoid exposing an arithmetic backend. Zero-count lengths are0; a lone positive symbol uses length1. For m>=2, weighted_bits equals merge_cost; for m=1 they are count and0 respectively.
    algorithms::HuffmanCountsTraceOwned count input, actual complete merges and producing construction result. Merge admission is complete before heap work: m-1 records for m>=1, else0. No truncation/replay/partial return/input references. Input copy and ordinary output are covered separately by complete input admission, not record count.
    algorithms::HuffmanMergeOwned actual two minimum removals and parent insertion from one producing merge. Decimal weights are exact, including values beyond uint64. IDs refer to the producing compact node array, not a reconstructed heap or canonical code.
    algorithms::HuffmanOptionsComplete borrowed-input and whole-merge-record policies, each zero disabling its cap. Input entries are count-vector positions, including zeros, or source text bytes depending on the entrypoint. Merge cap counts records only; owned input copies, ordinary output/nodes/lengths, decimal/scalar metadata, capacity and byte/peak memory are separate. Known m-1 records are admitted before heap work.
    algorithms::HuffmanSummaryComputed entropy, weighted mean and Kraft diagnostics for supplied counts/lengths. Values use long-double accumulation then double conversion, not exact certificates or proof of optimality/prefix validity. Empty support gives zeros.
    algorithms::HuffmanWorkActual selected construction visits, excluding validation/copies/allocations/decimal conversion. Heap comparison internals and multiprecision limb operations are not counted. Counts are not timings, FLOPs or complete memory traffic.
    geometry::HullEventActual scan event, referring to indices in the trace's sorted unique points. candidate is the pending point; point is the pushed/popped point, or candidate for a test. a,b,turn are meaningful only for test events and otherwise zero. stack_size is the actual size after the event (unchanged for tests). Together these compact edits describe every stack state without quadratic snapshots.
    geometry::HullIndexedPointOwned distinct coordinate with the earliest matching input identity. Exact equality coalesces duplicates and signed zeros; sorting ties by original index retains the earliest coordinate representation. Output owns the point.
    nn::models::HybridReachPathLive source two-choice hybrid reaching policy endpoints.
    HyperDualSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::autodiff::HyperDual – a second-order forward-mode dual number carrying two independent derivative directions plus their exact mixed second partial, for computing Hessian entries.
    autodiff::HyperDualA second-order forward-mode dual number carrying a value along with derivatives along two independent seed directions and their exact mixed second partial – i.e. x = x0 + eps1*dx1 + eps2*dx2 + eps1*eps2*dx12 with eps1^2 = eps2^2 = 0. Seeding eps1 along e_i and eps2 along e_j and evaluating f yields d^2f/dx_i dx_j exactly (to machine precision, unlike finite differences).
    stats::HypothesisTestResultOwned hypothesis-test result, analogous to R's htest list. Each test documents which fields it populates and what its interval estimates. Unused numeric fields retain zero; this default is storage, not a claim of zero effect. Read bounds only when has_conf_int is true; one-sided intervals may be unbounded. p_value is a null-model tail probability, not a posterior probability of the null. Objects own their method string and contain no borrowed references or shared state.

    I

    nn::models::I3dConfigConfigure the complete RGB Inception-v1 inflated3D graph.
    nn::models::I3dOutputOwn complete I3D endpoints,pooled features and categorical logits.
    nn::models::IafDensityOutputOwn all compact IAF recovered inputs, autoregressive stages and density intermediates.
    stats::ICADeflationary FastICA with population whitening and frozen new-row transforms. Fits centered x=A*s under the modelling assumption of mutually independent sources and a full-column-rank instantaneous linear mixture. At most one source may be Gaussian for identifiability up to sign/scale/permutation; Gaussian subspaces remain rotationally unidentifiable. Finite-sample contrast optimization does not certify statistical independence, non-Gaussianity or true-source recovery. PCA truncation discards information before ICA. No standardization of original feature units occurs. Null feature rows are dropped jointly during fitting; retained nonfinite values are rejected. Uses 1/n covariance and matching 1/n fixed-point averages. Eigenvalue rank threshold is max(n,p)*epsilon*largest eigenvalue after a common feature-scale factor. Returned sources have population covariance identity to numerical precision, even when a finite iteration budget is exhausted. Final signs make the first largest- absolute training value positive; component order is extraction order, not variance. Owns means, retained rows, PCA whitening, rotation, training arrays and diagnostics. Inputs remain unchanged; const inference has no shared mutable caches. Same seed/STL reproduces initialization, but normal_distribution is not bit-identical across STLs. Fit work O(n*p^2+p^3+sum(iterations)*n*k+sum(iterations)*k^2); retained storage O(n*(p+k)+p^2+k^2+k*sum(iterations)). Jacobi eigensolver uses at most 100 sweeps.
    stats::ICAFixedPointStepOwned raw projected FastICA update, normalized direction and sign-invariant angle change. raw_update is E[z*g(z dot w)]-E[g']*w after projection off previous rows. A zero/nonfinite update is an error, not a convergence certificate.
    stats::ICAOptionsControls retained PCA dimensions, contrast, iterations, angle tolerance and initialization. Whitening uses population covariance (divisor n), matching the fixed-point expectations.
    geometry::IcpOptionsOptional complete input and actual-history admission policies. Zero disables each optional cap. A step costs 1+5*N logical entries: one record, two coordinates for each before/after point, and one match index per source point. Excludes input copies, ordinary/transient arrays, final aligned cloud/result/work, scalar metadata and vector capacity; not byte/peak RAM.
    geometry::IcpResultAccumulated planar rigid pose, update count and final working-cloud RMSE. Legacy aggregate field order/types are preserved. Angle is an unwrapped sum in radians; translation composes incremental rotations/translations. RMSE now measures final updated working points, correcting the old pre-update value. Applying the accumulated pose once can differ from repeated updates by rounding. Empty-cloud RMSE zero is a convention, not a registration-quality claim.
    geometry::IcpRunOwned final working points and explicit stop/work information. The result pose is accumulated during production. Aligned points are the actual repeated-update cloud; applying that pose once has ordinary rounding differences. No caller mutation, retained references or shared state.
    geometry::IcpStepActual owned match/update boundary from a single ICP iteration. Before/after preserve evolving working coordinates, rather than reconstructed accumulated-pose points. Correspondences allow many source points per target; strict-less ascending target ties choose the first. Post-update errors are additional observations and never influence the preserved legacy stop rule.
    geometry::IcpTraceOwned original clouds, actual steps and their final producing result. No repeated-prefix solves or reconstructed intermediate states. Storage adds source/target copies and O(K*N) captured step values to ordinary workspace.
    geometry::IcpWorkSelected producing work, separate from extra error-observation passes. Counts exclude validation, centroids, covariance, trigonometry, copies, allocations and comparisons. Ordinary final RMSE adds one nearest pass; traced steps add fixed-match and nearest error observations after each update.
    algorithms::ID3DataOwned integer-coded categorical teaching data and predictor names.
    algorithms::ID3FrameClassifierID3 with frozen categorical encoding of named numeric or string DataFrame columns. All predictor values are categories, including numeric columns: no thresholds, scaling or ordering assumptions. Dictionaries are learned only on training rows, assigning nonnegative codes in first-occurrence order. New levels map to -1 and use the native local-majority fallback. Nulls and nonfinite numeric predictors are rejected, rather than silently omitted or imputed. Labels are numeric ints. Models own their tree/schema/dictionaries. Const inference has no shared mutation.

This is not the legacy scalar wrapper sampling sequence. samples>=P+1 and at least two; kernel_width and ridge must be finite positive. Kernel exp(-(fraction_off/kernel_width)^2); intercept is unpenalized. A Float64 tensor Cholesky solve fits all coefficients at once, without an optimizer or explicit inverse. Very ill-conditioned fits may fail.

Every patch must contain pixels. Produces a weighted i.i.d. sample in one shot rather than a Markov chain – no warmup, nothing to check for mixing – but accuracy depends entirely on how well the Gaussian proposal covers the target's mass; effective_sample_size is the diagnostic to check before trusting the result.

    algorithms::IndexCalculusModelPointOne illustrative logarithmic asymptotic-model comparison, not measured work. Bits denotes log2 of a hypothetical modulus, including sizes outside uint64. These formula values omit hidden constants/lower-order terms and do not predict this implementation's capped factor base, finite budgets or crossover timing.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusOptionsFinite work budgets and complete allocation/history admission policies. Attempt budgets are exact counts, zero means no attempts. Optional allocation caps use zero to disable. A trace relation/stage costs 1+K logical entries, one record plus the complete K-dimensional slot budget, also reserved for a failed stage with an empty solution. No rejected trial is retained. History cap excludes ordinary matrices, table/output arrays, seed/scalar metadata, vector capacity and byte/peak RAM. Untraced preparation ignores it.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusPreparationTraceOwned table plus actual accepted relation and linear-stage histories. Records are captured inside the producing precomputation, not by replay. Additional history storage is O((accepted rows+stages)*K); logical caps and exclusions are documented by IndexCalculusOptions.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusQueryActual bounded target-search result and its successful smooth relation. Trivial h=1 or h=g uses no random trial, leaves relation fields empty/zero. An unready valid table gives failure for other targets. Each call copies the stored query RNG state; queries do not mutate a table or each other.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusRelationOne accepted smooth relation captured at its actual collection boundary. g^exponent modulo p equals residue and the ordinary integer product of factor-base primes raised to powers. Failed nonsmooth trials are not stored.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusStageActual prime-field or lifted prime-power solution boundary. Each stage solves modulo the prime field; modulus names the resulting q^j solution modulus after a successful correction lift. A failed rank stage has empty solution. No elimination is performed by dividing nonunits modulo p-1.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusTableReusable verified factor-base logarithms and deterministic query-start state. Public value storage owns all arrays. Query validates group-factor data, factor-base ordering/primality, dimensions and every supplied logarithm before use, so editing values does not bypass domain checks. Validation has its own cost and is not counted as target search. No hidden cache or shared state.
    algorithms::IndexCalculusWorkSelected actual precomputation operations, excluding validation/factorization. Modular exponentiation internals, RNG shifts, sieve work, allocations/copies, comparisons and final exponent checks are outside these selected totals. Counter overflow throws. They are operation observations, not CPU time.

    filter::InformationFilterThe Information Filter: the algebraic dual of KalmanFilter, tracking the information matrix Y = P^-1 and information vector y = Y x instead of (x, P) directly. Its measurement update is purely ADDITIVE (Y += H^T R^-1 H, y += H^T R^-1 z) – the classical advantage of this form is that fusing several independent sensors, or distributing a filter across nodes that each see part of the measurement stream, is just summing information contributions, with no matrix inversion per sensor. The time-update (predict) step has no equally simple additive form for general F, so this implementation converts to covariance form, applies the ordinary KalmanFilter-style predict, and converts back – mathematically exact, and produces IDENTICAL results to KalmanFilter given the same model (the two are the same estimator in a different parameterization, not an approximation of each other).
    algorithms::InformedSearchExpansionOne non-stale queue removal, recorded before its outgoing edges are relaxed. Values are snapshots owned by InformedSearchTrace; goal removals are included.
    algorithms::InformedSearchResultWeighted path-search output, distinct from the sorted-array SearchResult type. Owns its path. Unreachable answers have found=false, cost zero and an empty path.
    algorithms::InformedSearchTraceOwned multi-goal search answer and chronological expansion snapshots. Recording adds O(k) storage for k expansions; no mutable state is shared.
    nn::InformerForecastDirect forecast and encoder and decoder diagnostics.
    nn::InformerSparseTraceProjected operands, sampled keys, and selected-query contexts from a sparse encoder stage.
    nn::models::InfoVaeOutputOwn all sixteen Gaussian, decoder, MMD and objective endpoints of a compact InfoVAE.
    bayes::INLAGaussian-strategy integrated Laplace inference for a latent Gaussian field. Model: eta=D*x, x|theta~N(0,Q(theta)^-1), with conditionally independent observations. At each theta, Newton finds x's mode and inverse Hessian. The Laplace log integrand is log prior(theta)+.5 log|Q|+log likelihood-.5*x'Q*x-.5 log|H|. Grid integration forms a mixture of these Gaussians; there is no simplified/full marginal Laplace skew correction and no sparse GMRF solver. Non-Gaussian conditional modes are used as approximate means. Use only modest dense latent dimensions. Borrowed callbacks run synchronously; result owns everything. Const calls have no shared mutation, but user callbacks must themselves be thread-safe when shared.
    bayes::INLAConditionalOne converged Gaussian approximation at fixed hyperparameters. Mode equals conditional mean only when the conditional posterior is Gaussian. Covariance is inverse negative Hessian at the mode; all arrays own their storage.
    bayes::INLALikelihoodPointLog likelihood and its first derivative and negative second derivative in eta. Curvature must be finite/nonnegative for the concave conditional model. Owns values.
    INLAMixedModelSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::INLAMixedModel — a mixed model (same formula grammar as GLMM/LMM) fit by Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation instead of penalized quasi-likelihood/REML: a genuinely Bayesian alternative returning real posterior means/sds (including for the variance components) rather than point estimates + asymptotic standard errors. See datamunge::bayes::INLA (C++-only, not exposed to bindings – same reasoning as AutodiffModel) for the underlying algorithm.
    stats::INLAMixedModelApproximate Bayesian mixed model using dense Gaussian-strategy INLA. Supports one lme4-style random term, e.g. y~x+(1+x|group). Latent coordinates are fixed effects followed by one random-effect block per group. At each theta the conditional Gaussian is centered at the mode; hyperparameter integration combines those Gaussians. No marginal skew correction, sparse solver or exact posterior sampler is supplied. See INLAMixedModelOptions for the proper priors. Complete cases across response/fixed predictors/group/random slopes are fitted; nonfinite retained numeric inputs are rejected. All fitted storage is owned. Units/centering change the meaning of the independent fixed-effect priors.
    stats::INLAMixedModelOptionsPrior and numerical controls for a single-grouping-factor mixed model. Factor entries have independent proper uniform priors inside the declared box: diagonal Lambda in [epsilon,bound], off-diagonal Lambda in [-bound,bound]. Gaussian residual log sigma is uniform on a finite, data-centered interval; this empirical prior construction limits interpretations of evidence across datasets. These are priors on factor entries/log sigma, not uniform priors on variances.
    bayes::INLAOptionsNumerical controls for dense Gaussian-strategy INLA; no sparse or skew correction. Grid work grows as points^theta_dim. DE is a seeded mode search, not a global certificate.
    bayes::INLAResultGaussian-mixture posterior summaries and the full retained hyperparameter grid. These are approximate moments, not exact posterior draws. Within variance is the weighted conditional variance; between variance is variance of conditional modes. Their sum is total variance; neither term alone orders total variance against EB. All members own their data. Conditional covariance storage costs O(K*p^2).
    nn::models::InpaintDataOwn aligned clean targets,masked observations and center patch targets.
    nn::models::InpaintMetricsPresent tensor inpainting metrics as legacy host scalars.

Excludes original/working/final arrays, scalar metadata, vector capacity and byte/peak RAM; untraced calls ignore the history cap.
    algorithms::InsertionSortProfileRowOne actual original-workload input and its three producing work records. Random means one permutation from an evolving std::mt19937/std::shuffle stream, not an empirical mean or a portable permutation specification.
    algorithms::InsertionSortRunOwned stable sorted values, corresponding original indices and producing work. Identities distinguish equal records; equal keys preserve original index order. No input mutation, retained references or shared state. Value-only legacy calls omit identity/history storage while sharing the same executing loop.
    algorithms::InsertionSortStepActual completed insertion and its owned working-array snapshot. Each step follows exactly one insertion, including zero-shift insertions; no repeated-prefix sorting is used to reconstruct a state.
    algorithms::InsertionSortTraceOwned original input and actual insertion states from one execution. Empty/singleton inputs have no insertion records. The original input supplies the initial state; no synthetic initial insertion is added.
    algorithms::InsertionSortWorkSelected actual key tests and array-cell assignments, not elapsed time. Key comparisons include the final false key test when j>0; index-bound tests are excluded. Shifts count successful > tests and rightward cell writes. Placements include unchanged destinations. Input copies, identity bookkeeping, key temporary reads, allocation and observations are excluded.

    optim::InteriorPointInteriorPoint on the InequalityConstrainedFunction callback interface. Gradient steps on f-mu*sum(log(-c)) with c<0. Backtracks only for strict feasibility, not barrier-objective decrease, then decays mu after each fixed inner budget. Requires a strictly feasible start and can fail later when feasible steps underflow. No KKT or barrier-stationarity stop test; no phase-I feasibility search. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::InteriorPointOptionsConfiguration for InteriorPoint; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    algorithms::InterpolationErrorScanOwned finite-query error census for two scalar functions, with sampled extrema only. Predictions and references are evaluated once each per query, in that order. Empty input has has_samples=false and zero max/RMS/index placeholders. Worst index is the first maximum absolute error, including first-zero ties. A grid maximum is not a certified supremum between queries. RMS uses scaled differences to avoid squaring large errors directly. All arrays are owned.
    algorithms::InterpolationSearchOptionsOptional complete input count and actual probe-record ceilings. Zero disables each optional cap. Element admission precedes reads; retained probe admission precedes its candidate inspection/append, but endpoint guards have already executed. Excludes borrowed input, scalar work/result, vector capacity and byte/peak RAM. Untraced calls ignore max_probes; no partial trace is returned on an error. Sortedness remains an unchecked precondition.
    algorithms::InterpolationSearchProbeOne actual closed interval and exact-floor candidate before its update. Flat intervals have numerator=denominator=offset=0 and position=lo; no division. For nonflat intervals position=lo+floor(numerator*(hi-lo)/denominator), using an exact widened product. All fields are owned scalar snapshots.
    algorithms::InterpolationSearchRunOwned ordinary search result and selected actual work from one execution. Does not copy/own input values. No mutation, retained input references or shared state.
    algorithms::InterpolationSearchTraceActual scalar probe history from the same executing interpolation loop. Empty and out-of-endpoint-range queries retain no probes. No repeated-prefix search or reconstructed intermediate states. Input lifetime ends with the call.
    algorithms::InterpolationSearchWorkSelected actual endpoint guards, flat-range tests and candidate key tests. Index checks, arithmetic, allocation, records and physical memory/cache reads are excluded. result.probes counts logical candidate inspections, not all endpoint accesses; a flat-range answer counts one logical probe without a separate candidate comparison, because its successful guards certify equality.

All snapshots are owned scalars.
    algorithms::ItpTraceOwned same-execution scalar history and final ITP diagnostics. No callback replay or repeated shorter runs. Endpoints are not step records; every actual projected/final-midpoint candidate call has one record.

    stats::JackknifeLimitsOptional complete input/retained-scalar ceilings checked before callbacks/copies. Zero disables either cap. Delete-one counts 2*n output doubles; delete-d traces count B*(d+1) deletion-index/replicate entries. These are element counts of mixed scalar types, not bytes. Excludes borrowed sample, summaries, temporary kept/permutation vectors, vector capacities and byte/peak RAM. No partial result returns on error. Legacy convenience functions disable caps.
    stats::JackknifeResultOwned delete-one statistics, estimated bias/SE and actual leave-one-out values. Order matches original observation indices; pseudo-values are algebraic transforms of actual callback results, not independent observations. Bias correction and variance estimation need statistical assumptions beyond finite callbacks. No sample/callback references retained. Original field layout kept.

Occupied candidate slots have compared=false and both byte fields zero; no extra input byte reads are introduced for recording. Other events have compared=true and equal records actual byte equality. Candidate equal events are actual accepted matches. Order pairing can differ from match partners.
    algorithms::JaroWinklerOptionsComplete byte admission and optional actual event-record ceiling. Complete first.size()+second.size() is checked before flags/input copies. Events are admitted online before each candidate/order/prefix inspection; zero disables either optional cap, and untraced calls ignore max_events. Counts exclude flag workspace, scalar summaries, vector/string capacities, and byte/peak RAM; the byte count admits borrowed inputs and their trace copies once, not as a total allocation quota.
