    algorithms::JaroWinklerRankedNameOne owned ranked name and its actual single-pass scoring result. index is original input row. Name is copied only for returned rows. No input lifetime dependency, identity/probability assertion or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::JaroWinklerRankLimitsComplete candidate-count and input-byte policies for native name ranking. All candidates and query bytes are admitted before scoring/copying. Zero disables either optional cap. Excludes working scores/flags, returned name copies, capacities and byte/peak RAM; no partial top-k prefix on error.
    algorithms::JaroWinklerRunActual Jaro ingredients, unconditional prefix score and selected work. No input ownership/references. Scores are numerical similarities, not identity probabilities or a metric distance. Odd ordered-mismatch counts retain a half-integer t=mismatches/2, not integer division. Bytes are case sensitive, include NUL/high bytes, and receive no Unicode decoding or normalization.
    algorithms::JaroWinklerTraceOwned original bytes and chronological events from the producing loop. Inputs are copied once for a self-contained trace, preserving NUL/high bytes. No repeated-prefix scoring or reconstructed matching decisions. Events cover candidate slots, ordered comparisons and actual prefix tests in execution order.
    algorithms::JaroWinklerWorkSelected actual inspections, excluding bounds/arithmetic/flag writes/allocation. Candidate slots include occupied skips, which do not execute byte equality. Order tests equal matched count; prefix tests include a terminating mismatch. These are logical operations, not physical memory/cache accesses or time.
    geometry::JarvisAnalysisOwned strict unclosed hull, earliest source identities and selected work. Starts at lexicographically least coordinate and runs counterclockwise for noncollinear inputs. Collinear input returns its two extremes; empty/singleton/ two-distinct inputs use the lexicographic shortcut. Signed zeros coalesce, keeping the earliest input coordinate representation. No input references.
    geometry::JarvisEventScalar actual wrap state using indices into JarvisTrace::sorted. Test contains its actual incumbent before/after inspection and exact sign; farther is meaningful only for a zero turn. Start/Select have examined=0, turn=0 and farther=false placeholders, with equal before/after candidate. No full hull snapshots or search replay; all state is owned scalar metadata.
    geometry::JarvisTraceOwned actual lexicographic distinct input and chronological wrapping events. No caller references, repeated-prefix runs or reconstruction of candidate decisions. Copying owns storage. Empty/small shortcuts retain sorted points with no events. With u>=3, exactly u events per actual hull edge are captured.
    geometry::JarvisWorkSelected actual preparation and wrapping work, not time or memory accesses. For u>=3 distinct points and h returned vertices, orientation_tests=h*(u-2) and wrap_steps=h. The fewer-than-three shortcut performs no wrapping tests. Sorting counts depend on input and standard library. Collinear comparisons use sorted index order along a ray, never squared floating distances.
    algorithms::JohnsonAllPairsResultLegacy aggregate of owned all-pairs distances and global negative-cycle status. Rows/columns are original vertices; unreachable entries are positive infinity. A detected negative cycle anywhere invalidates the entire problem: all entries remain positive infinity, including the diagonal. Empty graphs return an empty matrix and false. Field order and types retain the legacy aggregate contract.
    algorithms::JohnsonAnalysisOwned output, terminal potentials, reduced edges and actual selected work. Potentials/reduced weights use long double arithmetic on finite binary64 inputs. These are rounded machine values, not exact-real certificates. A negative-cycle result retains terminal potentials but has no reduced edges. Edge order matches input, including parallel edges/loops. No borrowed storage.
    algorithms::JohnsonEventOwned scalar actual operation without repeated solver runs or full snapshots. Unused size_t fields are zero. Potential uses source=0 placeholder; pass is zero-based and meaningful only there. Edge is original input identity and is meaningful only for Potential/Reweight/Relax. Stale is false outside Pop. Seed/Pop use u=v; Restore uses u=source. Infinity denotes an absent old label only; finite arithmetic results are checked. After records the committed value.
    nn::models::JohnsonFeaturesOwn selected frozen VGG16 content and style activation handles.
    algorithms::JohnsonOptionsOptional complete input/output and online event ceilings, measured in records. Zero disables a ceiling, never arithmetic/container representability checks. Validate endpoints and finite weights before admission; input count is n+m, matrix count is n*n. No partial result is returned on failure. These limits exclude vector capacities, allocator overhead, byte counts and peak RAM.
    nn::models::JohnsonOutputsOwn generated RGB and every retained transformation stage.
    algorithms::JohnsonTraceOwned same-execution analysis, original graph and chronological scalar history. Default event cap is a million records; no truncation, replay or input views. Recording adds O(K+m) owned storage for K actual events and copied m edges.
    algorithms::JohnsonWorkSelected logical work from the producing execution, excluding validation/allocation. Heap counts are operations, not internal comparator calls or elapsed time. Passes include a final unchanged pass. Matrix cells count n*n initialization; restored_cells counts reachable entries only. All counters are checked.
    sim::JointA joint from a dynamic child to a parent body or the fixed world. Anchor/axis are in the child's rotated local frame; coordinate zero is its authored pose. Connected bodies do not collide. Each child has at most one joint.
    fda::JointAdaptiveSplineOptionsControls for alternating mesh growth and smoothing-parameter selection. Every accepted tree is retuned using the supplied validation observations. Validation therefore influences subsequent growth; independent test data are required to assess this complete procedure. The original fixed-lambda API remains available when growth must depend on training responses alone.
    sim::JointStateJoint coordinate/rate pair in radians/radians per second or metres/metres per second.
    image::JpegDecodeOptionsDecoding options; the defaults match TensorFlow's DecodeJpeg(channels=0).
    image::JpegInfoHeader-level facts about a JPEG stream.
    algorithms::JumpSearchAnalysisOwned scalar search answer, exact schedule and producing selected work. No references to caller input. result.probes equals block_reads+scan_reads.
    algorithms::JumpSearchProbeOwned actual inspected value, active block and resulting branch. Half-open block bounds are before this inspection. Select followed by a scan can move the read index backward or inspect the same endpoint twice.
    algorithms::JumpSearchScheduleExact integer schedule for a possible sorted-array length, without allocation or reads. Positive length uses floor(sqrt(n)), at least1. Empty input has all-zero fields. max_probes is ceil(n/block_size)+block_size for positive n, a conservative read bound including possible repeated block-end/scan inspection.
    algorithms::JumpSearchTraceOwned same-execution analysis and chronological reads, without replay/input copy. History costs O(probes) storage. The optional ceiling counts complete records, excluding capacities, byte counts and peak RAM. No partial result on failure.
    algorithms::JumpSearchWorkSelected actual logical comparisons/reads, not machine memory traffic or time. A block read performs one >=key test. A scan read performs ==key, then >key only on inequality. One value is captured per logical probe; repeated visits to the same array element count again. Preparation/sortedness checks excluded.

    K

    algorithms::KabschAnalysisOwned same-execution paired fit, normalized covariance/key matrix and actual observations. Normalize each input set by its max(1,absolute coordinate), then center in long double. Covariance is the mean outer product in those normalized units. Divide it by covariance_scale to build the dimensionless Horn key matrix; scale zero uses an all-zero key. Eigenvalues are descending and quaternion is the actual normalized principal eigenvector, scalar-first. No second fit or iteration replay. Eigen residual/gap are additional diagnostics, not exact certificates of rank, uniqueness or convergence in exact arithmetic. All vectors own data.
    algorithms::KabschResultOwned proper-rotation/translation fit mapping source onto corresponding target points. Original field order/types retained. No scale/reflection/permutation fitting. RMSD evaluates the returned double transform on the original paired inputs. Degenerate data can admit multiple equally optimal rotations; one is returned.
    algorithms::KadaneStepOwned actual local/global recurrence states after one original input element. Seed has running_before0 and best_changed=true by convention. Later best_changed is the actual strict > decision. No repeated-prefix runs or full array copies.
    algorithms::KadaneTraceOwned same-execution answer and one actual state record per input element. O(n) history, no caller views or input copies; empty input has no records.
    algorithms::KahanAccumulatorLocal owned Kahan stream state with the original sequential arithmetic order. Empty stream sum/correction/count are zero. Does not guarantee exact sums, order independence, a relative-error bound for ill-conditioned cancellation, or sensible compensation after infinity/NaN. No dynamic allocation/shared state.
    algorithms::KahanStepOwned actual rounded arithmetic from one Kahan update. correction_after=(total-sum_before)-adjusted; it estimates rounding loss, not an exact expansion/certificate. Values follow normal double IEEE operations; nonfinite values propagate and fast-math reassociation invalidates the method.
    algorithms::KahanTraceOwned actual one-record-per-value arithmetic and final stream sum. Trace is not a higher-precision sum and retains no input references. O(n) history; optional complete record ceilings exclude capacities/bytes/peak RAM.
    filter::KalmanFamilyStudyOwned actual outputs of every original model-family run on the same admitted data. Linear Kalman/RTS uses one actual forward pass plus native backward pass. EKF/UKF/EnKF/PF each run independently on the same nonlinear observations; information form and alpha-beta use original linear observations. Alpha-beta- gamma uses the separate acceleration sequence. No full-prefix replay, callbacks or filter objects retained. Native exceptions propagate without partial output.
    filter::KalmanFilterOwned fixed-model linear covariance Kalman filter with optional full RTS smoothing. Models x_k=F*x_(k-1)+w and z_k=H*x_k+v with caller-supplied Q/R covariance. Inputs are copied; predict/update mutate this instance, independent copies evolve separately. Concurrent mutation requires synchronization. Shape checks do not establish finite values, covariance PSD, noise independence or valid probability assumptions: those remain caller preconditions. Uses explicit LU inverses and simplified covariance updates, not a Joseph/square-root method. Under a valid linear Gaussian model the mean is conditional MMSE; floating output is approximate. No universal realized-error or numerical PSD guarantee.
    filter::KalmanStageOwned actual prior, predicted and corrected state/covariance from one native step. Captures getter outputs around the producing predict/update, with no replay. Snapshot storage is O(n^2); no model/input references are retained.
    filter::KalmanStateOwned state mean and covariance, shared by the native filter-family outputs. Units follow the model; covariance is state-unit products. No input references. Public edits are unchecked and do not mutate the producing filter.
    filter::KalmanStudyDataOwned original synthetic observations/truth for all report filter families. Linear/nonlinear sequences have50steps, dt1/true velocity2, seed42 mt19937. Position-only SD2 observations are drawn first, then monotonic2x+sin(x) observations with SD.5 using the same engine/new distribution. Acceleration control has40noiseless steps from rest with acceleration.5. Exact normal mapping is standard-library dependent. No external dataset or caller views.
    filter::KalmanStudyOptionsNative study populations/sigma parameter and complete input/population ceilings. Limits count original input steps and ensemble+particle members, excluding multiple method outputs, matrix capacities, byte counts and peak RAM. Zero disables optional ceilings only; counts/UKF sigma-scale representability checked.
    algorithms::KangarooCollisionOne actual successful trail lookup and candidate check.
    algorithms::KangarooJumpOne actual tame or wild group jump and exact distance. The native-only unsigned128 distance avoids b+distance wrap at uint64 limits.
    algorithms::KangarooJumpSizeOne actual seeded jump-table entry, as used by both kangaroos.
    algorithms::KangarooOptionsActual-jump and retained-record policies; zero disables each cap.
    algorithms::KangarooResultHistorical owned verified candidate and actual total jump count.
    algorithms::KangarooRunSelected actual call-boundary and working-trail diagnostics.
    algorithms::KangarooTraceOwned actual native tables, jumps and matched-lookup outcomes.
    stats::KaplanMeierEstimateOwned product-limit results in ascending time order.
    stats::KaplanMeierPointKaplan–Meier estimate at a distinct observed time.
    algorithms::KaratsubaCallActual digit-vector operand lengths, split and result length for one invocation. Calls are entered preorder; parent is an earlier record except root's sentinel parent=size_t max. Low/high/sum roles preserve actual call order. The base case is min(left_digits,right_digits)<=32, Root zero has one digit; recursive zero slices can retain their original widths. No operands/products are re-multiplied to construct the tree.
    algorithms::KaratsubaOptionsOptional complete input-digit and actual recursion ceilings. Zero disables an optional cap, not size arithmetic. Depth counts root0; a positive ceiling is the largest admitted depth, while0 disables that ceiling. Caps count digits/calls/depth, excluding capacities/temporary vectors/bytes/RAM.
    algorithms::KaratsubaTraceOwned original operands, actual decimal result and producing recursive call records. Complete original bytes are owned, including leading zeros/empty conventions. Recursion records store lengths/roles rather than full intermediate big integers. O(calls) extra history in addition to kernel digit temporaries and owned input/output.
    algorithms::KaratsubaWorkSelected actual recursive calls and schoolbook digit products, not total arithmetic/time. Excludes validation, digit additions/subtractions, carries, shifts, copies, allocations and formatting. A zero operand still runs the actual one-digit leaf.
    algorithms::KargerOptionsComplete input/trial ceilings and online owned-history record admission. Zero disables an optional cap, not size arithmetic. History charges n+1 records per contraction snapshot or completed trial partition; edges copied once are covered by complete n+m admission. Capacity/bytes/peak RAM are excluded.
    algorithms::KargerStepActual selected original edge and owned canonical components after its contraction. Labels are minimum original vertices, not union-find root ids. Crossing list preserves original edge order and parallel multiplicity; chosen_rank is the unbiased accepted word modulo crossing_count. No union/search replay.
    algorithms::KargerTraceOwned original multigraph, actual contraction histories and every completed trial. No borrowed graph storage or replay. Extra storage O(m+B*n*n) worst case for B trials of n vertices; complete record caps can reject large captures.
    algorithms::KargerTrialActual completed trial cut/partition and range of contraction records. If no crossing edge remains before two groups, the graph is disconnected; choose component0 against the rest, giving a nontrivial zero cut. First strict best retained on ties; best_changed marks that actual decision.
    algorithms::KargerWorkSelected actual logical work, excluding validation, union-find internals and trace copies. Edge scans include every original record when rebuilding candidates and counting final cuts, including loops. Random draws include rejected modulo- bias words. Counts are operations, not elapsed time or allocation traffic.
    algorithms::KarnEstimatorEducational Jacobson/Karels RTT smoother with Karn's ambiguity and backoff rules. Clean first sample R sets SRTT=R,RTTVAR=R/2,RTO=3R. Subsequent clean samples update RTTVAR=.75*oldvar+.25*abs(oldSRTT-R), then SRTT=.875*oldSRTT+.125*R, RTO=SRTT+4*RTTVAR. Retransmitted ACKs do nothing; timeouts double current RTO. No timestamp exception, clock granularity, RFC minimum/maximum, TCP sender, packet sequence tracking or scheduling is modeled. Therefore not a complete RFC6298 implementation. Preserves original ordinary-double operation order. Local owned state, no allocation/shared state; mutation requires external synchronization if one instance is used concurrently. Failed updates leave all state unchanged; copied instances evolve independently.
    algorithms::KarnEventOwned actual pre/post estimator states from one producing transition. Sample is caller-provided for ACK events, zero placeholder for Timeout. No replay, retained input views or inference of network elapsed time.
    algorithms::KarnStateOwned current RTT smoothing and timeout values in seconds. Uninitialized state has SRTT/variation0 and the positive configured initial RTO. A zero clean sample may produce zero RTO because this educational model has no clock granularity or RFC minimum/maximum clamp. No caller references.
    dstruct::KaryTree
    algorithms::KBRewriteStepOwned actual rule application from deterministic first-rule/leftmost reduction. Rule index is in the original supplied rule order, not an inferred canonical system. before/after strings are actual producing values, not prefix replay.
    algorithms::KBRewriteTraceOwned actual finite reduction and complete original word/rules. captured_entries counts one initial word, one per input rule and one per application; excludes individual bytes/inner strings/capacities/runtime copies. A trace step stores two whole words, so this record quota is not a byte or peak-memory bound. Rules are validated before copies, and applications admitted before replacement. No second reduction or partial returned trace.
    geometry::KDNearestProbeOwned actual point or branch decision from the producing nearest traversal. Visit.measure is point distance; FarPlane.measure is absolute split-coordinate difference. Only FarPlane has a meaningful child index/explore_far flag. best indices use size_t max before any candidate; best distance initially infinity.
    geometry::KDNearestTraceOwned original points, actual answer and chronological nearest-query operations. Trace copies original points in input order and captures actual visits/far decisions, without replay. Adds O(n+records) copy/storage beyond query work; no tree/input references survive. Long-double distances are rounded metrics, not exact-real nearest oracles for arbitrarily close inputs.
    geometry::KDSearchWorkSelected actual nearest-query work, not input copying, comparisons or elapsed time. One point-distance computation per visited node; plane tests only for nonnull far children. Pruned subtrees need not contain only one point.
    geometry::KDTree2DOwn a balanced alternating-axis median tree for planar nearest/k/radius queries. Finite points required. Stable deterministic build ties use other coordinate, then original input index; each node retains original identity. Nearest and k-nearest equal computed distances prefer earliest input index, including duplicates. Distances use widened coordinate subtraction and hypot, avoiding the old double square overflow/underflow; they remain rounded machine values. Construction expected O(n log(n+1)) work/O(n) owned storage; tree height O(log n). Queries can visit every node: no universal average O(log n) guarantee without distribution assumptions. No insertion/removal. Const queries use local state and share no mutable state; original caller data are not retained.
    stats::KendallTauOwned pair counts and coefficients from kendall_tau().
    KernelPCASWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::KernelPCA — principal component analysis generalized to a nonlinear feature space via the kernel trick. With a linear kernel it reproduces plain unscaled PCA's scores (up to a sign flip per component).
    stats::KernelPCAKernel PCA in the training-centred feature space, as sklearn.decomposition.KernelPCA.
    stats::KernelPCAOptionsKernel-PCA geometry, without automatic predictor standardization or gamma selection.
    KernelRegressionSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::KernelRegression — Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression, a nonparametric fit where each prediction is a kernel-weighted average of training responses.
    stats::KernelRegressionNadaraya-Watson regression: nonnegative local averages on a frozen formula design.
    stats::KernelRegressionOptionsLocal-mean geometry and conditional leave-one-out bandwidth search.
    stats::KernelRidgeCVResultComplete-case, fold-refitted validation for explicitly fixed KRR candidates. Each fold fits its own Formula schema, predictor offsets/scales, response offset and kernel centering. No internal auto selection is allowed. Candidate/fold order is retained; pooled validation SSE divided by all retained rows determines the first strict minimum. Scores tune the candidates and do not estimate selected-model performance without another holdout. No shared mutation; dense repeated fits. Labelled input rows incomplete under the full Formula are omitted jointly. The formula has a numeric response and supported predictors. Candidates use fixed lambda>=0 and positive nonlinear gamma. Fold IDs align with original rows; labels on omitted rows are ignored. Nonnegative contiguous 0..F-1 IDs, at least two folds; every fold needs at least two fitting rows. Results name the candidate to refit on all supplied fitting rows. Invalid folds/options or missing finite validation rows cause std::invalid_argument. Formula, level and numerical failures within a fold propagate to the caller.
    stats::KernelRidgeRegressionDense RKHS least squares with a genuine optional unpenalized intercept. Minimizes sum_i(y_i-b-f(x_i))^2+lambda*||f||_H^2. With a free intercept, center both K and y: alpha=(C*K*C+lambda*I)^-1*C*y and predict with the consistently centered query kernel plus mean(y). This enforces sum(alpha)=0; the equivalent raw-kernel intercept is b=mean(y)-mean_kernel'alpha. Without an intercept, neither K nor y is centered and b=0. Formula intercept markers do not add kernel features; fit_intercept controls b explicitly.
    stats::KernelRidgeRegressionOptionsKernel, penalty, training metric and finite candidate grids for KRR. Lambda multiplies the RKHS penalty beside a sum of squared errors, not their mean: an objective mean loss + rho*norm^2 corresponds to lambda=n*rho. Gamma is inverse squared length in standardized design units when enabled.
    compute::KernelSourceNative program source and its explicit, backend-neutral argument layout. Vulkan takes SPIR-V words; CUDA takes null-terminated PTX text. Programs have buffer parameters first, followed by one by-value parameter block when nonempty. Vulkan uses descriptor set zero with sequential storage-buffer bindings and a push-constant block. CUDA uses the equivalent pointer parameters and packed block.
    cv::KeyPointA detected blob keypoint: its pixel location, the Gaussian scale (sigma) at which it was found, and the Difference-of-Gaussians response at that scale (higher magnitude is a stronger blob).
    nn::models::KfacActorPathLive manual-actor endpoints needed for caller-computed K-FAC statistics.
    nn::models::KfacNaturalPathOwning/live endpoints of source factored Tikhonov preconditioning.
    nn::models::KimConfigConfigure random-embedding Kim sentence-CNN token and branch widths.
    nn::models::KimOutputOwn raw sentence logits,the complete zero-PAD table and all branch features.
    KMeansSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::KMeans — k-means clustering (Lloyd's algorithm with k-means++ initialization) fit from a DataFrame and a list of numeric feature columns.
    nn::ml::KMeansProvide seeded centre selection and a single tensor Lloyd update.
    stats::KMeansK-means clustering (Lloyd's algorithm with k-means++ initialization) fit from a DataFrame and a list of numeric feature columns. Rows with a null value in any feature column are dropped before fitting.
    stats::KMeansOptions
    nn::ml::KMeansStepRetain one Lloyd update and diagnostics for the supplied centres.

Records follow medoid-slot then original-point order and exclude existing medoids. best_changed is the actual strict trial_cost<incumbent-1e-12 test. These are evaluations, not accepted trajectory states or replayed objectives.
    algorithms::KMedoidsResultOwned selected input identities, cluster assignments and distance objective. Cluster ids index medoids, not original points. Equal computed distances keep the first medoid slot; coincident medoids can therefore have empty clusters. iterations counts accepted swaps, not candidate evaluations or convergence tests.

    algorithms::KMPSearchAnalysisOwned exact matches and actual selected work from one shared search execution. No input/history copies retained. Empty pattern or longer-than-text returns no matches and zero work, preserving historical early-exit behavior.
    algorithms::KMPSearchTraceOwned original byte strings, actual table, matches and chronological comparisons. Input bytes admitted before copies, table before allocation, each comparison before evaluation and each match before append. Excludes capacities, private runtime table/output copies, struct fields and bytes/RAM. Default million, zero disables optional quota. No partial trace escapes an exception.

Does not count border-integer tests, table accesses, output writes, validation, allocation or total machine work.

Integer profits permit pruning with its exact floor integer_upper; relaxation_value is a rounded double for display only and never controls pruning.

    algorithms::KnapsackResultOptimal 0/1 knapsack value, original-index choices and actual visited-node count. The historical field types/layout are retained. Ownership is independent of input storage. Only strict improvements replace an incumbent solution.
    algorithms::KnapsackTraceOwned optimal result, sorted original indices and actual search/pruning records. Nonpositive-profit items are excluded from the active order and remain unchosen. Empty original input has no nodes; a nonempty input with no active items has one root leaf. Recording adds O(N+k) storage for N visited nodes and k active items; no input is borrowed.
    KNNClassifierSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::KNNClassifier — k-nearest-neighbors classification. Since a training point's nearest neighbor is always itself, training_accuracy()/confusion_matrix() report leave-one-out performance rather than a trivial resubstitution fit.
    stats::KNNClassifierk-nearest-neighbour classifier from a formula class ~ x1 + x2 + ....

    stats::KNNClassifierPredictionPredicted classes with the vote shares behind them.

    stats::KNNNeighborsThe neighbours of a set of query points, as returned by the kneighbors() methods.
    KNNRegressorSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::KNNRegressor — k-nearest-neighbors regression. As with KNNClassifier, fitted_values()/r_squared()/rmse() report leave-one-out performance.

    stats::KNNRegressorOptionsSettings for KNNRegressor.

    algorithms::KnuthBendixResultOwned generated shortlex rules and actual finite completion status. complete=true means the final exhaustive ordered overlap/containment scan joined every critical pair. With strict terminating shortlex rules this gives confluence and a canonical form for the supplied presentation. false means a rule/round ceiling stopped the procedure: equality of reductions is sound, but unequal reductions do not decide inequivalence. Initial rule-limit exits may have processed only a prefix of the supplied equations. No group/monoid finiteness or convergence promise follows from a finite test of words.
    algorithms::KosarajuAnalysisOwned component labels and actual same-execution selected work without history. Labels are0..c-1 in reverse-finish transpose-root order, not minimum-vertex ids. Cross-component original edges go from a lower to a higher returned label.
    algorithms::KosarajuTraceOwned original graph, actual transpose/finish order/labels and chronological events. No second DFS/replay. Capture quota counts complete original n vertex records, E adjacency records and each actual event. Excludes actual transpose/order/ labels/output copies, individual event fields, capacities and bytes/RAM. Complete original count admitted before copies, each event before its producing mutation/examination. Default million, zero off, no partial result on failure.
    algorithms::KosarajuWorkActual selected DFS operations excluding graph validation/transpose construction/copies/time. Every original and transpose adjacency entry is examined once, including duplicates/loops. Each vertex finishes and is assigned once. Root counts are actual forest roots; second_roots equals the number of SCCs.
    algorithms::KruskalOutcomeOwned minimum spanning forest and actual work counts. No graph/history is borrowed or retained. Edges keep caller endpoint orientation. Equal finite weights preserve input order; output total sums accepted weights in that order.
    algorithms::KruskalStepOne actual sorted edge scan with pre-merge roots and post-decision components. input_index identifies the owned input edge in KruskalTrace. Roots follow actual path halving and rank ties, not canonical component labels. No DSU replay is used.
    algorithms::KruskalTraceOwned input edges and actual scanned-edge decisions from the shared forest kernel. Capture C=M+S counts M input edge records and S actual step records, not their individual scalar fields. The complete M is checked before copying input; each additional step is reserved before scanning it. The default quota is one million, zero disables only that quota. Output forest, runtime sort/DSU storage, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not peak RAM. Failure returns no partial trace. Copies own input/steps/result. No callbacks or replay are involved.
    algorithms::KruskalWorkLogical counts from one actual stable Kruskal execution. Validation, sorting, path-halving steps, allocation, copying and CPU time are excluded. find_calls is exactly twice scanned_edges, including cycles and self-loops.
    nn::KvCacheKeys and values of the positions decoded so far, [N, heads, T, dh] each, grown by append one step (or chunk) at a time. Without autograd history the cache writes into a buffer with doubling capacity and hands out views (no per-step copy of the whole cache); tensors that need gradients are concatenated instead, so gradients flow through the cache.
    nn::models::KvState< Native operations spelling used by source cache methods.

    L

    optim::L1LeastSquaresObjectiveMean-loss lasso objective with an exact soft-threshold proximal map. No hidden standardisation. Unpenalised coefficient zero supports an explicit intercept column. Stationarity uses the proximal-gradient mapping, not raw smooth-gradient zero. Dense calls own no mutable caches.
    graphics::LabelImagePanelOwned rectangular nonnegative label grid and its panel heading. Zero is background; positive IDs may have gaps, allowing provisional maps. Storage is independent of the labeller. Colours repeat after eight positive IDs.
    cv::LabelMapThe result of connected_components(): a per-pixel label image (row-major, same layout as image::Image::data() but one int per pixel rather than per channel byte). Label 0 is always background; foreground components are numbered 1..count.
    nn::models::LadderGaussianOwn the mean and log variance of a precision-fused diagonal Gaussian.
    nn::models::LadderPriorOutputOwn all six explicit ancestral Ladder endpoints without an image or inference state.
    nn::models::LadderVaeOutputOwn sixteen Gaussian evidence, hierarchy, decoder and loss endpoints of a Ladder VAE.
    random::LaggedFibonacci64Own an additive lagged-Fibonacci ring x[n]=x[n-j]+x[n-k] modulo2^64. Require0<j<k. SplitMix64(seed) fills k initial words in physical order; index0 is oldest. Each output overwrites the oldest slot by its sum with the actual short-lag word. Unsigned wrap is intended. This is not cryptographic; parity follows a linear recurrence, and arbitrary lag pairs do not guarantee maximal period or statistical quality. Scalar seeding explores at most2^64 states. Construction/storage O(k), each raw update O(1), observations do not replay. Objects own state and inherited distribution cache; copies preserve both. Independent objects share no state; concurrent mutation requires synchronization.
    random::LaggedFibonacciParityOrbitOwned normalized oldest-first parity masks until the first repeat or explicit cap. Bit i denotes parity of the i-th oldest ring word, eliminating physical index rotation. This is an exact finite-state projection, not the full64-bit engine period or a randomness certificate. complete=false has no inferred period. All masks are distinct; the repeated closing mask is identified by offset.
    random::LaggedFibonacciStepOwned operands/output from one actual modular64 ring update. value=long_word+short_word modulo2^64, overwriting write_index; short_index identifies the other actual ring operand. No replay or engine references.
    random::LaggedFibonacciTraceOwned complete before/after physical rings and every actual consumed modular transition. captured_entries=2*k+count counts both full boundary-ring words and scalar transition records, not fields/capacities/bytes/RAM. Allocation/admission of both rings and all records finishes before the caller engine is advanced. No input engine references or replay; normal cache is left intact.
    algorithms::LagrangeAnalysisOwned direct interpolation value and actual same-execution selected work.
    algorithms::LagrangeFactorActual ratio and pre/post product from one non-diagonal factor application. term_index identifies the original node term; excluded_node identifies its k!=j factor. widened_differences marks fallback when a double subtraction overflowed; ordinary finite-difference arithmetic retains historical order.
    algorithms::LagrangeTermActual final node contribution and sequential sum boundary values.
    algorithms::LagrangeTraceOwned actual original nodes, factor products, term sums and final evaluation. captured_entries=2*n+n+n*(n-1)=n*n+2*n counts original x/y values plus term and factor records, excluding scalar fields/capacities/runtime copies/bytes/RAM. Complete input/count/optional quota admitted before copies/evaluation. No second interpolation or reconstructed products; all histories own their data.
    algorithms::LagrangeWorkActual selected direct-product operations excluding validation, allocation and time. On complete n-node evaluation, terms=sum_additions=n and ratio_evaluations= term_multiplications=n*(n-1). Empty uses the historical zero convention.
    nn::LagrangianNetworkOutputDynamics and differential terms, each shaped [batch,1].
    algorithms::LamportClockOwn one process's nonnegative signed64 scalar Lamport logical clock. Starts0. Internal/send events increment once; receive commits max(current,message_stamp)+1. Scalar order respects happened-before when the caller records every local event and attaches actual send stamps to receives. Converse false: ordered timestamps need not imply causality. This class does not authenticate messages, model a network, synchronize threads or produce a unique total order across processes. Pair with process ids externally if needed. All transitions O(1), no allocation; invalid/overflow failures leave state unchanged. Copies own values, independent objects share no mutable state.
    algorithms::LamportEventOwned actual before/message/after values of one producing clock update. message_time is the caller's actual nonnegative stamp for Receive, zero placeholder otherwise. No process/message identity, network validation, physical duration or happened-before relation is inferred by this record.
    algorithms::LanczosProjectionActual same-pass coefficient subtracted during full reorthogonalization. A coefficient is computed on the residual after all earlier projections in this iteration, not on the original three-term residual or a replay.
    algorithms::LanczosResampleAnalysisOwned actual query result, raw sums and selected producing work. position is the original query, effective_position is clamped to[0,n-1]. raw_sum/weight_sum are actual original-order sums. value=raw_sum for legacy raw mode or raw_sum/weight_sum for explicitly normalized mode. No replay.
    algorithms::LanczosResampleTapOwned original identity, weight and actual accumulation boundary for one producing tap. virtual_index is the window lattice position; sample_index is its actual boundary-clamped stored identity. Product/sum fields are unnormalized even when the final analysis value divides by total weight.
    algorithms::LanczosResampleTraceOwned complete original samples, every actual window tap and actual query analysis. captured_entries=n+2*a counts original sample values and tap records, not individual fields, capacities, output/runtime copies or bytes/peak RAM. Complete input, integer geometry and count/quota are checked before copying samples or evaluating weights. No second query or synthetic history.
    algorithms::LanczosResampleWorkActual selected finite-window tap work, excluding validation, trig internals, copies and time. Every complete query evaluates2*a candidate weights and reads their clamped samples, including zero weights. Negative weights can cause ringing/overshoot.
    algorithms::LanczosResultOwned producing tridiagonal coefficients and basis vectors, preserving legacy field layout. V[j] is basis vector j, not matrix row j of Q. The leading m=alpha.size() diagonal and first m-1 beta entries define T. Historical beta may additionally contain the actual terminal residual norm on early stop when requested steps exceeded m; that extra value is not a T off-diagonal. No eigenvalues computed.
    algorithms::LanczosRitzAnalysisOwned actual native tridiagonal eigensystem and explicit full-matrix Ritz diagnostics. values are descending native Jacobi approximations; coefficients[j][i] is mode i's coefficient of actual basis vector V[j]. vectors[i] is the formed full Ritz vector. Residuals explicitly evaluate A*y-theta*y, rather than using only terminal_beta*last_coefficient, which omits reorthogonalization/roundoff defects. Orthogonality/projection errors are observed widened maxima, not exact certificates or evidence the supplied result originated from A.
    algorithms::LanczosStepOwned actual matrix-product, three-term and final reorthogonalized residual boundaries. Full vectors are producing snapshots, not repeated prefix runs. alpha and beta_previous are actual recurrence values; residual_norm follows the one full reorthogonalization pass and controls the absolute stopping decision.
    algorithms::LanczosTraceOwned complete original matrix/start, actual output/stages and same-execution selected work. captured_entries counts n*n+n original scalar values, then1+3*n per step and one record per projection. Excludes original row records, scalar fields, result basis/coefficients, runtime copies/capacities/bytes/RAM. Admit complete original geometry before copies, each step before matrix work and each projection before its inner product. No replay or partial returned trace.
    algorithms::LanczosWorkSelected actual dense Lanczos operations, excluding validation/copies/allocation/time. dot_products counts alpha and reorthogonalization inner products, excluding sum-of-squares norm work. matrix_products counts actual scalar A*v products. Full reorthogonalization is one sequential pass over all current basis vectors.
    geometry::LaplacianAnalysisOwned actual final points and same-execution selected smoothing work.
    geometry::LaplacianCurveStudyOwned original41-vertex path, actual noisy points, pin flags and noiseless reference. Synthetic reference data, not a mesh-quality or ground-truth guarantee for arbitrary graph smoothing. No caller/RNG state retained.
    LaplacianEigenmapsSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::LaplacianEigenmaps — embeds points via the smallest non-trivial eigenvectors of a heat-kernel-weighted, sparse k-nearest-neighbor graph Laplacian. Distinct from DiffusionMaps (also heat-kernel-based, but dense and alpha-normalized).
    stats::LaplacianEigenmapsLaplacian Eigenmaps (Belkin & Niyogi, 2003): builds a SPARSE symmetric k-nearest- neighbor graph with heat-kernel-weighted edges, forms the graph Laplacian L = D - W, and embeds points via the n_components eigenvectors of the generalized eigenproblem L f = lambda D f associated with the smallest non-trivial eigenvalues (the trivial constant/all-ones-in-D-metric eigenvector at eigenvalue 0 is discarded). Solved via the symmetric normalized Laplacian L_sym = I - D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2} trick. Distinct from Diffusion Maps (also heat-kernel-based, but uses a dense all-pairs kernel with alpha-normalization and a diffusion-time-scaled Markov-matrix eigendecomposition instead of a sparse k-NN graph Laplacian). Rows with a null value in any feature column are dropped before fitting.
    stats::LaplacianEigenmapsOptions
    geometry::LaplacianTraceOwned graph, full actual Jacobi states/energies and actual vertex updates, without reruns. fixed is normalized to n flags; states[0] is the complete original geometry, followed by each actual complete sweep. energies are widened sums over actual states, not an exact monotonicity/mesh-quality certificate. Captured count is 2*n+E+1 + iterations*(n+1+R): original vertices/normalized flags/adjacency entries/ initial energy, then each state/energy and R actual free nonisolated updates. Counts point/record identities, not their coordinates/fields/capacities/bytes; result/runtime copies excluded, not peak RAM. Complete quota admitted before graph/state copies or smoothing. No replay or partial returned trace.
    geometry::LaplacianUpdateActual free nonisolated vertex centroid and before/after state from one Jacobi pass. centroid reads only the old complete state, never an earlier update in the same pass. Widened flags identify actual overflow-avoiding coordinate fallbacks; normal finite double accumulation/update order follows historical arithmetic.
    geometry::LaplacianWorkSelected actual smoothing work, excluding complete graph validation, copies and time. neighbor_reads counts point records used in actual free nonisolated centroids, not scalar coordinates. energy_edges counts undirected edge multiplicities visited by trace-only energy diagnostics; ordinary/count-only smoothing has0.
    LassoSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::Lasso — pure L1-penalized ("lasso") regression, a special case of ElasticNet with alpha fixed to 1. Can shrink coefficients exactly to zero, performing variable selection.
    stats::LassoLasso convenience model using the shared coordinate-descent/CV engine. Fixes alpha=1; all ElasticNet contracts apply. L1 thresholding permits exact zero slopes. Dependent designs can have nonunique coefficients; predictions may still be unique.
    stats::LassoOptionsLasso controls forwarded to ElasticNet, fixing alpha=1. Same defaults/constraints as ElasticNetOptions; no alpha field.
    nn::models::LatentDiffusionReverseOutputLive unclipped latent posterior endpoints, without a sampler or model.
    nn::LatentOdeDecodedLatent states at the query times and the scalar readouts.
    nn::LatentOdeOutputDiagonal Gaussian posterior and its decoded trajectory.
    algorithms::LaxWendroffAnalysisOwned actual final grid, computed Courant coefficient and selected same-execution work. allow_unstable records explicit opt-in to abs(Courant)>1, not a stability certificate. Ordinary API and default analysis enforce the CFL domain.
    algorithms::LaxWendroffCellOwned actual old-state stencil and producing new value for one periodic cell. General terms give value=center-advective_term+diffusive_term, with actual double terms widened for storage or actual widened fallback terms. Copy paths have unused term placeholders0 and use the identified original operand directly. Every cell reads the complete old state, never a previously updated new value.
    algorithms::LaxWendroffStateActual complete-state time, mass, L2 and extrema observations. Time/mass/L2 use long double arithmetic and are observations, not exact conservation/stability/positivity certificates. L2=sqrt(dx*sum(u*u)).
    algorithms::LaxWendroffTraceOwned complete original/every actual state, producing stencils and explicit diagnostics. states[0] is original input, followed by every real completed step; no prefix reruns. captured_entries=n+1+steps*(2*n+1): original n values/diagnostic, then n next-state values, one diagnostic and n cell records per step. Excludes fields/capacities/final-result/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Complete count and quota admitted before copies/evaluation, default million, zero off.
    algorithms::LaxWendroffWorkSelected actual stencil/update work, excluding validation, copying, allocation and time. stencil_reads counts the three original operand point identities initialized per cell, not physical machine loads. diagnostics_cells counts additional trace-only state observations; ordinary/count-only calls retain0 there.
    optim::LBFGSLBFGS on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Limited-memory BFGS with weak-Wolfe bracket/bisection search, descent fallback and positive-curvature pair retention. If the search budget ends, a previous Armijo step can be used; if none was found, returns. Tests gradient norm or absolute objective change. O(history_size*p) state; history_size must be positive. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::LBFGSOptionsConfiguration for LBFGS; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    algorithms::LBGAnalysisOwned actual LBG result, requested/rounded target and same-execution producing work.
    algorithms::LBGIterationOwned actual producing Lloyd assignment/update evidence for one real iteration. No post-update distortion is invented for this record; stage final consistency evaluation and the next real iteration provide separate observed objectives.
    algorithms::LBGQuantizationOwned actual nearest-codebook predictions, mean squared distortion and selected distance work.
    algorithms::LBGResultOwned actual final codebook, nearest assignments and mean squared Euclidean distortion. Final assignment/distortion are re-evaluated against each actually returned stage codebook, correcting the old pre-update objective/stale labels. The multiplicative split can leave zero centroids unchanged and retain empty codewords, so requested size does not imply that many distinct used centers.
    algorithms::LBGStageOwned actual initial/final codebooks and final nearest consistency result for one size.
    algorithms::LBGTraceOwned original data and every actual split-stage/assignment/update record from one execution. Complete trace or exception. Actual quota counts n*d input coordinates; each stage record plus2*k*d codebook coordinates+n final assignments; each iteration record plus2*k*d coordinates+n assignments+k counts. Admitted before each record/copy; unknown convergence length is not fabricated. Excludes fields/row headers/capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Default million actual logical records;0 optional cap off.
    algorithms::LBGWorkActual selected producing distance, assignment, centroid and split work. Excludes complete validation, copying/allocation/capture and elapsed time. Trace adds no distance recomputation; final consistency passes occur in all modes.
    random::LCG64JumpOwned actual logarithmic affine-power evaluation, separate from any engine mutation. This evaluates affine composition, not count raw steps. Stages are actual composition evidence, not a fabricated raw-word trajectory. All products/adds use defined unsigned wrap; no modular inverse/division by a-1 is required.
    random::LCG64JumpStageActual one exponentiation-loop state after optional bit composition and power squaring.
    random::LCG64LowBitOrbitOwned actual autonomous reduced-modulus orbit or explicitly incomplete finite prefix. Projection obeys the same recurrence modulo2^bits, independently of hidden high bits. This helper does not consume an engine or empirically traverse its2^64-state period. Prefix exhaustion is not a period certificate.
    random::LCG64StepActual low64 multiply/add transition from one LCG recurrence execution. product and after use defined unsigned wrap modulo2^64. Wrap flags describe exact unsigned range overflow, not a CPU flag/instruction or quality metric.
    random::LCG64TraceOwned actual raw transitions consumed from the caller engine, preserving its inherited normal cache. Complete count+1 quota/geometry and vector reservation precede caller mutation. Afterwards trivial record appends do not allocate. Default million records, 0 optional cap off. Excludes field/capacity/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM.
    algorithms::LCSAnalysisOwned actual selected optimal subsequence and same-execution work.
    algorithms::LCSStepActual prefix coordinate and direction chosen during one producing traceback move.
    algorithms::LCSTraceOwned original inputs, actual producing full DP table and complete actual traceback moves. Table contains (n+1)*(m+1) cells including zero boundaries. Steps stop when either prefix is empty, so the implicit remaining boundary moves are absent. Complete conservative capture admission counts n+m+table_cells+n+m before allocation/evaluation: input records, table cells and at most n+m moves. captured_entries reports the actual logical count using steps.size instead of that admitted upper bound. Excludes fields/capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Default million-entry cap; zero disables it only.
    algorithms::LCSubstringAnalysisOwned longest contiguous shared run and the actual first row-major maximizing occurrence.
    algorithms::LCSubstringCellOne actual cell write and its strict running-maximum decision.
    algorithms::LCSubstringTraceOwned original inputs, actual completed rows and all producing cell writes.
    algorithms::LCSubstringWorkActual common-suffix DP work, excluding guards, allocations and copies.
    algorithms::LCSWorkActual selected full-table and traceback operations; excludes validation/allocation/copies.
    LDASWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::LDA — R-MASS::lda()-style linear discriminant analysis.
    stats::LDAFit pooled within-class covariance linear discriminant analysis from a categorical formula. Owns fitted design, means, precision terms and training observations; no borrowed dataframe lifetime. Class order is alphabetical. Null predictors/response rows are dropped while fitting; finite usable numerical designs and positive-definite within-class scatter are required, with at least2 classes, at least2 rows per class and n>classes+predictors. Formula transforms/interactions are supported; intercept is ignored. No regularization or posterior calibration is performed. Fitting uses scatter W and Sigma=W/(n-classes), not the maximum-likelihood W/n. Bayes scores use the full design; discriminant plots use at most two axes. Const inference borrows no mutable global state; mutable fitting is constructor-only.
    stats::LDAOptionsOptional positive class priors in alphabetically sorted class order; absent means observed proportions. Priors must have one value per observed class and sum to1 within1e-6.
    stats::LDAPredictionOwned predictions aligned to every original input row. Missing-predictor rows have empty labels and empty posterior/discriminant rows.
    algorithms::LeakyBucketLazy leaky-bucket meter, algebraically dual to a token bucket with complementary storage. Starts empty at time0 and therefore allows an immediate burst up to capacity. This is an admission meter, not a shaping queue; accepted arrivals have no delayed release schedule. Capacity must be positive finite, rate nonnegative finite; timestamps finite, nonnegative and nondecreasing, amounts finite and nonnegative. Same-time arrivals preserve caller order. O(1) per event, no borrowed input/shared global state; concurrent mutation requires synchronization.
    algorithms::LeakyBucketArrivalOne proposed admission in caller time units and amount units.
    algorithms::LeakyBucketEventActual producing meter event with old state, lazy leak and final admission state. The operation has no queue and schedules no release time. Rejection still commits the elapsed leak and timestamp. Negative/backward/nonfinite inputs throw before mutation. Unused excess drainage is not banked below level0.
    algorithms::LeakyBucketTraceOwned complete actual meter event sequence and selected real decisions. One captured logical record per arrival owns its time, amount and actual transition. Field scalars/capacities/bytes/RAM are excluded from the quota.
    nn::models::LearnedGroupConvOutputsNormalized features, masked convolution output and the exact mask used by this call.
    algorithms::LearnedIndexAn owning lower-bound index for sorted signed 32-bit integer keys.
    nn::LearnedQuadraticRolloutRetain coordinate trajectories and objective histories from an optimizer rollout.
    linalg::LeastSquaresAccuracyAccuracy of the three least-squares methods on one problem, from least_squares_accuracy().
    optim::LeastSquaresObjectiveFull-sum linear least squares with inspectable per-row components. evaluate/gradient are sums. SGD and SAGA use mean component gradients; SVRG uses the full gradient divided by n as its mean snapshot. All share the same unpenalised minimizer, but a step size must name its loss convention.
    linalg::LeastSquaresResultResult of least_squares().
    LegendAn owned, reusable legend layer created by legend(), the pipe-friendly form of R's legend(legend = labels, col = colors).
    LegendArgsNamed options for a manually labeled legend, used as legend().with(LegendArgs{{"labels", ...}, {"col", ...}}) (R's legend() arguments).
    graphics::LegendEntryOne manually specified legend row, as drawn by R's legend().
    nn::models::LeNetOutputsIntermediate tensors from LeNet-5, retaining their autodiff graphs.
    optim::LevenbergMarquardtLevenbergMarquardt on the ResidualFunction callback interface. Forms J transpose J plus scalar damping*I and solves by unpivoted elimination. Accepts only strict reductions of half residual SSE, multiplying damping by .3 on acceptance and 10 on rejection. Tests proposed step norm even after rejection. A small rejected step is not a gradient certificate; no parameter constraints. O(np^2+p^3) work. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::LevenbergMarquardtOptionsConfiguration for LevenbergMarquardt; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    algorithms::LevenshteinAnalysisOwned actual byte distance and same-execution selected work.
    algorithms::LevenshteinCodeBlockOne actual emitted/read binary block after its implicit leading1.
    algorithms::LevenshteinCodewordActual value, stream span, unary count and producing binary blocks.
    algorithms::LevenshteinCodingTraceOwned full stream, actual word/block evidence and prefix progress from one execution. Complete trace or exception, never a silent partial parse. Capture cap counts full owned stream bits, values, word records and actual block records. Fields, capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM excluded; default million,0 off.
    algorithms::LevenshteinCodingWorkActual selected complete values and written/read bits, excluding validation/copies/allocation.
    algorithms::LevenshteinEditOne actual optimal traceback move selected from the captured producing DP table. Diagonal is preferred if optimal, then up, then left; costs are0 for equal diagonals and1 otherwise. Coordinates are original actual row/column prefix lengths before moving toward the origin, not necessarily a/b order.
    algorithms::LevenshteinTraceOwned actual rolling-row snapshots and additional native optimal traceback, no DP rerun. Rows hold the longer original byte string and columns the shorter; ties put original b in rows. The full table is copied from each actually computed rolling row, never independently rebuilt. Additional native traceback reads this table once and records its actual optimal moves, without claiming that the ordinary scalar API performs traceback. Complete conservative admission counts input bytes, all table cells and at most a.size+b.size path records before copying/evaluation. captured_entries records actual input/table/path count. Excludes fields/capacities/runtime rows/output copies/bytes/RAM. Default million logical records,0 cap off.
    algorithms::LevenshteinWorkActual selected rolling-row operations; trace-only traceback is separate work.
    algorithms::LevinsonAnalysisActual complete or explicitly partial prefix solution and exact-zero breakdown status.
    algorithms::LevinsonAttemptActual three error sums and denominator of one attempted leading-order extension.
    algorithms::LevinsonResidualIndependent widened residual observations for a caller-supplied full solution. This is an observed normwise backward-error ratio, not a rigorous rounding bound, conditioning estimate or forward-accuracy certificate.
    algorithms::LevinsonStateOwned actual completed leading-order forward/backward basis and solution.
    algorithms::LevinsonTraceOwned input and every actual attempted/completed prefix from a single recurrence execution. Complete conservative admission assumes every prefix completes:2*n inputs, sum(k=1..n)(1+3*k) state/vector records and n-1 attempts. Actual returned count can be smaller on breakdown. Fields/capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM excluded; default million records,0 optional cap off.
    algorithms::LevinsonWorkActual selected recurrence work, excluding validation, capture, residuals and elapsed time.
    algorithms::LexBFSAnalysisOwned actual deterministic Lex-BFS ordering and same-execution selected work.
    algorithms::LexBFSClassificationOne actual membership test made while refining a real remaining block.
    algorithms::LexBFSStageOwned actual initial or post-refinement ordered partition snapshot.
    algorithms::LexBFSTraceOwned actual normalized matrix, original adjacency, every partition and real membership tests. Exact complete capture admission is E+2*n*n+n+1 before copies/matrix work. Counts original adjacency entries, n*n matrix cells, n+1 stage records, n*(n+1)/2 member slots and n*(n-1)/2 classifications. Excludes row/block container headers, fields/capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Default million logical records;0 disables only optional cap. No prefix reruns.
    algorithms::LexBFSWorkActual selected matrix/refinement work, excluding guards/copies/allocation/time.
    algorithms::LibrarySortAnalysisOwned actual sorted values and same-execution fixed-shelf work.
    algorithms::LibrarySortInsertionActual input identity, predecessor and chosen gap/placement branch.
    algorithms::LibrarySortShelfOwned actual fixed-capacity shelf state, with explicit occupancy distinct from placeholder zero values.
    algorithms::LibrarySortTraceOwned original input, actual insertion branches and every real shelf snapshot. For n>=2 exact complete capture counts n original values, n insertion records and(n+1)*(1+2*(2*n+2)) shelf/slot/flag records. For n<=1 only n original values are captured, matching the actual trivial-copy branch. Admitted before copies/algorithm. Excludes fields/capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM; default million records,0 optional cap off.
    algorithms::LibrarySortWorkActual selected fixed-shelf operations; no timing or amortized-paper complexity claim.
    cad::Light
    stats::LimeImageExplainerLIME (Ribeiro, Singh & Guestrin, 2016): explains one prediction by fitting a simple, interpretable linear model in the neighborhood of the instance. It perturbs the image by randomly switching superpixels on (original) or off (baseline), asks the black-box model for each perturbation's score, and fits a proximity-weighted ridge regression of the score on the on/off pattern; each superpixel's coefficient is its local importance. Fully model-agnostic – it only ever calls the supplied prediction function.
    LinalgMatrixBinding counterpart of Mat/SpMat with shared, immutable expression operands. Transpose, multiplication and inverse actions defer native computation until eval(), values() or text(). Handles keep temporary operands alive across garbage collection. Sparse products use CSR; solves use the canonical dense LU/QR implementation. Concurrent const evaluation is safe; no evaluation cache is mutated.
    cad::Line3
    random::LinearCongruential64Full-period mixed unsigned64 affine generator with explicit raw transition evidence. Recurrence x_next=a*x+c modulo2^64, returning the updated state. Constructor requires a=1 modulo4 and odd c, exactly the mixed full-period conditions for this modulus. Any seed is valid, including0. The period theorem is not an empirical traversal of2^64 states, independence or cryptographic security. Low bits have short autonomous periods; all raw outputs are predictable from known state/parameters. Copies own raw state and inherited normal() spare cache. Raw next calls leave that cache unchanged, matching other engines. O(1) raw step/time/storage; separate instances share no mutable state, concurrent mutation requires synchronization. Default constants are not a quality proof.
    algorithms::LinearInterpolationEvaluationOwned actual selected interval endpoints, blend and branch/work evidence.
    algorithms::LinearInterpolationProbeOne actual interval-selection comparison from the shared producing search. The bool field reports the actual role-specific predicate: kind0 uses<=, kind1 uses>= and kind2 uses<. It is not always a strict less-than relation.
    algorithms::LinearInterpolationSineStudyOwned original sine sampling/grid experiment and actual interpolated/error observations.
    algorithms::LinearInterpolationTraceOwned original knots and actual interval-search probes plus producing blend result. Conservative complete admission uses2*n+2+bit_width(n) records before copying/evaluation; actual count can be smaller due to endpoint guards. Excludes fields/capacities/result/runtime copies and bytes/RAM, default million records;0 optional cap off. No interval or blend replay.
    algorithms::LinearInterpolatorOwn once-validated piecewise-linear knots for repeated finite interpolation/extrapolation queries. Require at least2 finite strictly increasing xs and equal-length finite ys; duplicates/descending knots rejected. Complete constructor validation O(n) precedes owned copies. Each subsequent interval search is O(log n), O(1) ordinary query storage; no complete validation repeated. Exterior queries extrapolate along the nearest end segment without clamping query or value. Numeric knot matches return the original ordinate exactly. Ordinary finite y0+t*(y1-y0) operation order retained; nonfinite intermediates trigger a widened same-line fallback with checked finite double output. No mutation during inference or shared state; concurrent const queries are independent.
    linalg::LinearRegressionResultFit and inference summary returned by linear_regression() and sparse_linear_regression().
    causal::LinearSEMRecursive linear Gaussian structural model with independent disturbances.
    algorithms::LinearSolutionOwned legacy direct-solve result: computed cutoff success and solution. For gaussian_elimination(), solved=false means an absolute pivot fell below 1e-12, not a mathematical singularity certificate. No unique-solution or forward-accuracy guarantee follows from solved=true. Empty valid input succeeds. Field order and aggregate layout are unchanged; no caller storage is borrowed.

    algorithms::LISAnalysisOwned actual deterministic strict-LIS values, source indices and producing work.
    algorithms::LISInsertionOwned real frontier indices before/after one original value and its actual predecessor link.
    algorithms::LISProbeOne actual lower-bound comparison against the real current frontier.
    nn::ListenAttendSpellResultLogits, attention and actual feedback tokens for a three-step decode.
    algorithms::LISTraceOwned original integers, final actual predecessor/frontier arrays and every producing search/update record. Input/predecessor2*n records admitted before copies; each actual probe and insertion record plus before/after frontier members admitted before append, final-tail records before ownership transfer. Complete result or exception. Default million actual records,0 optional cap off; excludes scalar fields, capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Frontier snapshots can take quadratic capture storage despite O(n log n) ordinary producing work.
    algorithms::LISWorkActual selected strict-LIS binary search, tail updates and witness reconstruction work. Excludes guards/copies/allocation/capture, elapsed time and CPU instructions.
    nn::LiteModelCompile a local TensorFlow Lite model once and reuse its CPU buffers.
    algorithms::LL1BuildWorkActual selected monotone fixed-point and predictive-table construction counts.
    algorithms::LL1ConflictOwned actual conflicting table-cell witness, with earliest retained and new production identities. Conflicted models remain inspectable but parsing refuses them. Duplicate indexed productions can also conflict; no silent arbitrary-choice recognizer.
    algorithms::LL1ParseAnalysisActual predictive-parser status and selected real action/input/stack counts.
    algorithms::LL1ParseEventOwned actual stack/input decision before and after one real parser action.
    algorithms::LL1ParserOwn a checked grammar, its actual FIRST/FOLLOW predictive table and explicit cell-conflict witnesses. A symbol is nonterminal exactly when used as a production lhs. Grammar start must be a defined nonterminal; lhs/rhs symbols cannot be empty or "$"; epsilon is an empty rhs vector, not a literal empty token. All production indices must fit int. FIRST/FOLLOW use finite monotone insertion fixed points; build work is grammar dependent, not a claimed constant-time preprocessing step. Retain earliest production per table cell and record actual conflicting later indices. is_ll1() means this indexed construction has no conflicts, including duplicate-rule IDs; conflicted models are inspectable but parsing throws. Parsing consumes complete finite string tokens, no lexing/backtracking/error recovery. Explicit action budget separates incomplete computation from a syntax rejection. Owned model has no borrowed grammar lifetime/shared state; independent const inference is safe when no caller mutates the object.
    algorithms::LL1ParseTraceOwned complete original tokens, native initial stack and every actual bounded parse action. Complete actual run until accept/reject/step budget, or capture exception; budget exhaustion is explicitly represented and not a silent rejection. Capture cap counts original token symbols,2 initial stack symbols and each event record plus actual before/after stack symbols. String characters, scalar fields/capacities/runtime/result copies and bytes/RAM are excluded.
    LLESWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::LLE — locally linear embedding: preserves each point's local reconstruction weights from its k nearest neighbors rather than global distances, letting it unfold nonlinear manifolds PCA/MDS cannot.
    stats::LLELocally Linear Embedding (Roweis and Saul 2000) of selected numeric columns of a DataFrame.
    stats::LLEOptionsOptions for LLE. regularization means the same as scikit-learn's LocallyLinearEmbedding(reg=...) and has its default.
    algorithms::LLLAnalysisOwned actual equivalent integer basis, exact row transform and floating reduction observations. Checked row subtraction/swap preserves the exact original integer lattice, including incomplete runs. Decisions use double Gram-Schmidt, so completed status and observed inequalities are not a rigorous exact-arithmetic LLL or shortest-vector certificate. Transform overflow can throw even if the basis row would fit; no arbitrary-precision fallback is implied.
    algorithms::LLLEventActual producing row reduction, Lovasz decision or adjacent swap linked to a real state.
    algorithms::LLLStateOwned actual basis/transform and computed Gram-Schmidt arrays at one real committed row state.
    algorithms::LLLTraceOwned complete original basis and every actual bounded row-operation/check/state record. Each actual state counts1+2*n*d+2*n*n+n logical entries; original input counts n*d and each actual event1. Records admitted before snapshot/event copy; unknown future operations are not fabricated. Default million cap, 0 optional cap off. Excludes scalar fields/row headers/capacities/result/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Complete bounded trace or exception.
    algorithms::LLLWorkActual selected floating Gram-Schmidt, integer row-operation and outer-loop work. Excludes complete guards, copies/allocation/capture, property-summary comparisons, elapsed time and CPU instruction counts.
    LMSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::LM — R-lm()-style linear models fit from a DataFrame.
    stats::LMAn R-lm()-style linear model fit by ordinary or weighted least squares from a DataFrame and a formula.
    LMMSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::LMM — a linear mixed model fit by (RE)ML, with a single grouping factor, e.g. "score ~ x1 + (1 + x1 | school)".
    stats::LMMA linear mixed model \(y=X\beta+Zb+\varepsilon\) with one grouping factor, fit by REML or ML from a DataFrame and an lme4-style formula.
    stats::LMMOptionsOptions for LMM: the criterion and the settings of the search over \(\theta\).
    stats::LmOptionsFitting options for LM, like the extra arguments of R's lm().

    geometry::LocateAnalysisOwned scalar query result and selected actual work, with no mesh references. Seed zero uses the legacy nonzero fallback stream. Containment includes edges and vertices; when several faces contain q, the actual walk selects one, not necessarily the least index. Triangle is -1 outside/empty/budget exhaustion; stop distinguishes these cases. All fields are values, no shared state.
    geometry::LocateMeshOwned finite mesh input for controlled location experiments. Points use row-major original identities; triangles are strict CCW and in cell-row,cell-column,two-face order. No locator or borrowed internal pointers.
    geometry::LocateOptionsQuery walk bound and optional actual trace-record ceiling. Zero max_steps selects 4*T+16 for T triangles, not an unbounded walk. A positive value overrides that bound. Reaching it is StepLimit, never proof of exterior location. max_events counts samples+step starts+edge tests, before each actual operation; zero disables that optional ceiling. No partial trace is returned on failure; capacities/bytes/peak RAM are outside these counts.
    geometry::LocateSampleOne actual sampled triangle and running centroid-score winner. Scores use coordinates divided by a common max(1,absolute mesh/query coordinate) scale before centroid/difference/square arithmetic. They are rounded dimensionless long-double values, not exact nearest-centroid certificates. Strict decrease keeps the first sampled winner on ties. Sampling is with replacement.
    geometry::LocateStepActual triangle entry and random cyclic edge start for a walk step. Edge order is first_edge,(first_edge+1)%3,(first_edge+2)%3, not a uniform permutation of all six orders. No geometric distance monotonicity is promised.
    geometry::LocateTestOne actual directed edge inspection in a walk step. Exact sign is for represented finite binary64 endpoints/query. A negative sign triggers exactly one adjacency lookup; neighbor is -1 on boundary, >=0 for a crossing, or -2 when no lookup was made. No tolerance or predicate replay.
    geometry::LocateTraceOwned original mesh and complete actual sample/start/test records from one query. Samples precede all starts/tests; test.step groups tests under each actual start. A negative test records the actual crossing/boundary decision. No repeated-prefix runs or full intermediate snapshots. Copies own all storage; trace remains valid after the borrowed locator/input are destroyed. Recording adds O(P+T+K) storage/copy work for P points,T triangles,K scalar records.
    geometry::LocateWorkSelected actual query work, excluding mesh construction, validation and copies. Random draws equal samples+steps. Edge tests count exact orientation calls, not their internal arithmetic. Crossings exclude the terminal boundary edge.

    random::MersenneTwister64MT19937-64: a 312-word simulation engine with period 2^19937-1. Scalar seeding and every raw output match std::mt19937_64. The recurrence updates in place in increasing index order, with an invertible output temper. Period refers to the nonzero effective recurrent state, not to a short test, all arbitrary restored arrays, or 19968 independent stored bits. A scalar seed chooses at most 2^64 streams. This is not a cryptographic generator. Instances own state; copying preserves both raw position and the inherited normal() cache. Separate instances share no state; concurrent mutation of one instance needs external synchronisation. Construction/refill cost O(312); next_u64() is O(1) amortised, with 312 stored 64-bit words plus metadata/cache.

Element i spans [nodes[i], nodes[i+1]] for i in [0, num_elements()) – no separate connectivity array is needed since consecutive nodes are always the two endpoints of one linear (P1) element. nodes is a public field for direct C++ construction, but (matching datamunge::ode::ODESolution's t/y fields – a swig-jse R-backend codegen bug hits plain vector<double> struct field getters) is not exposed to language bindings; node_at()/num_nodes() are the cross-language-safe accessors.
    fem::Mesh2DA 2D triangular finite-element mesh: shared vertex coordinates plus a triangle connectivity list. Reuses datamunge::geometry's Point2D and (Delaunay-oriented, always-counterclockwise) Triangle index type directly rather than duplicating them. nodes/triangles are public fields for direct C++ construction, but – same rationale as Mesh1D::nodes – are not exposed to language bindings; node_at()/ triangle_at()/num_nodes()/num_triangles() are the cross-language-safe accessors.

    stats::MLPClassifierA feed-forward neural network (multi-layer perceptron) classifier, trained by backpropagation with mini-batch stochastic gradient descent. Each layer computes an affine map followed by a nonlinearity, z = W a + b, a' = act(z); the final layer's outputs pass through a softmax to give class probabilities, and training minimizes the cross-entropy loss. With one or more hidden layers the network learns nonlinear decision boundaries no linear model can express (the classic XOR/two-moons problems); with an empty hidden-layer list it reduces exactly to multinomial logistic regression. Uses the same formula + DataFrame constructor style as the other classifiers. Rows with a null value in any model column are dropped before fitting.

Default width .125 and side 64 make a compact model. This is trained from scratch, without pretrained weights. The checkpoint includes architecture, every learned tensor and every BN moving moment. Single-writer, including inference; fitting is not resumable from optimizer state.
