    cad::ModifyOptions
    algorithms::ModPowStepOne actual low-bit fold, running-base square and exponent shift. Before the step, accumulator*running^remaining equals the original power modulo m. multiply is the low bit of remaining_before; squared_base is computed even for the final bit. No independent replay is used to obtain these values.
    algorithms::ModPowTraceOwned scalar inputs, actual exponent-bit states and final modular residue. No replay or shared state. All trace data, including exponent bits, is exposed. Modulus one has result/initial_base zero and no steps/products, regardless of exponent; exponent zero otherwise returns one with no steps/products.
    algorithms::ModPowWorkActual operation counts of right-to-left square-and-multiply. Each processed bit performs one square, including the final unused square. Set bits additionally multiply the accumulator. Counts exclude input reduction, division internals, copying and allocation; these are not timings.
    algorithms::ModSqrtOwn ModSqrt values for one independent native execution. Fields describe actual producing values or policy units. In-class initializers define defaults. Containers own their values; constructing a record alone performs no algorithm work and retains no caller storage or shared mutable state.
    algorithms::ModularInverseTraceCanonical modular inverse and the actual same-pass Euclid certificate history. value and positive modulus are the original inputs; inverse lies in [0,modulus). euclid captures the actual computation on (value,modulus), followed by reduction of its coefficient of value. No explanatory rerun occurs. Modulus one returns zero, retaining the original degenerate-residue convention. Nonunits or invalid moduli throw instead of returning this record. All fields own their values.
    nn::ModulatedConv2DOutputOwn per-example modulated convolution output and its live output-channel demodulators.
    nn::ModuleCallable functional neural-network module with an architecture plot method.
    nn::models::switch_lm::MoeOwn Moe source graph endpoints or configuration.
    optim::MOEADApproximate a multi-objective minimum using neighboring scalar subproblems. Weights use the largest Das-Dennis lattice fitting max(requested,m); exactly requested for two objectives. Neighbors use Euclidean weight distance; equal distances retain the standard sort's unspecified tie arrangement. Tchebycheff uses max(w,1e-6)*abs(f-ideal); weighted_sum uses sum(w*(f-ideal)). No global archive or convergence guarantee. Final non-dominated extraction is quadratic in population size, so the complete optimizer is not merely O(N*T). Fixed seed repeats on the same standard library; callbacks and shared variation operators remain observable. Const calls share no optimizer state, but the callback is mutable and responsible for its own concurrency behavior.
    optim::MOEADDiscreteChoiceActual discrete scalarization choice for a supplied weight.
    optim::MOEADOptionsOwned configuration for the native MOEA/D variant. Validation occurs on optimize()/trace(), before callbacks except objective dimension, which requires one actual discarded probe. Same legacy field order.
    optim::MOEADReplacementActual two scalar values and update decision for one neighboring slot. Both scores use the same ideal point after the child evaluation. Equality replaces, so duplicate individuals can propagate. Values are observed, not replayed.
    optim::MOEADStepActual offspring and all neighbor updates from one subproblem visit. Parents are drawn with replacement and can coincide. Only the first SBX child is mutated/evaluated. These are sequential in-place population updates.
    optim::MOEADTraceOwned actual setup, offspring, scalar decisions and final population/front. The probe determines objective count but is discarded from the population and ideal point. Capture units count bound scalars, each stored vector row plus its elements, each ParetoPoint record plus coordinates/objectives, ideal scalars, each offspring record plus child coordinates/objectives/ideal, and each replacement record. Options and other scalar metadata are not additional units.
    nn::models::MonocularDepthResultOwn coarse/refined positive depth and every model stage.
    algorithms::MonotoneCubicOwned prepared shape-preserving cubic Hermite model with endpoint clamping. Initial interior tangents average adjacent secants, endpoints use one-sided secants. In left-to-right order, zero secants zero both tangents; wrong-sign tangents are clamped before radial limiting to alpha^2+beta^2<=9. Later updates only decrease shared tangent magnitudes. This sufficient region gives interval monotonicity in exact arithmetic, including local extrema. C1, generally not C2. Floating-point evaluation has roundoff. No smoothing. Preparation O(n), owned storage O(n); each query O(log n). Independent const queries share no mutation. Finite geometry/secants and results are required.
    algorithms::MonotoneCubicDecisionActual mutations of one interval's shared endpoint tangents. Records precede subsequent intervals, which can further decrease a shared tangent. Final model tangents, rather than an earlier record, define evaluation.
    algorithms::MontgomeryContextPrecompute one odd modulus for carry-safe Montgomery arithmetic. R=2^64. Setup computes nprime=-n inverse modulo R using five Newton refinements from the odd seed n, plus R and R squared modulo n. Setup and arbitrary-input reduction use remainder operations; only the reduced-domain REDC kernel avoids division. All inputs/results use unsigned64-bit words, with full128-bit products and an explicit129th sum bit. No constant-time guarantee. Methods do not mutate the context and are independently callable.
    algorithms::MontgomeryPowerStepActual powering step in the Montgomery domain.
    algorithms::MontgomeryPowerTraceOwned actual exponentiation states with one shared modulus context. One conversion into the domain and one conversion out surround the binary loop. Counts are actual REDC calls, not CPU instructions or timings.
    algorithms::MontgomeryReductionActual carry-safe REDC state for a product of two reduced residues. The exact sum T+q*n can require129 bits. sum_carry retains that bit; quotient_low retains the low64 bits after division by2^64. A subtraction occurs if the carry is set or quotient_low>=n. These are owned observations.
    algorithms::MooreOptionsComplete projected-input and actual history policies for Moore refinement. States/transitions include unreachable states and any materialized rejecting sink. Zero disables each independent cap. Ordinary moore_minimize() disables policies, preserving its legacy uncapped entry point.
    algorithms::MooreRoundActual before/after labels and per-state signatures in one synchronous round. Each signature begins with its state's old block, then destination old-block IDs in symbol order. New IDs follow first state encounter, not map key order. Stable means block count unchanged; numeric labels can still be renamed.
    algorithms::MooreRunOwned completed graph, final partition and reachable minimal quotient. Completed graph/partition include unreachable states; result removes unreachable quotient blocks in ascending-symbol BFS order. Acceptance bytes retain the first state's original nonzero representation, rather than normalizing to one.
    algorithms::MooreTraceOwned actual initial labels, complete round histories and producing run. Initial capture units count one label per completed state. Each full round adds one record, before/after labels, signature row records and their integers: 1+3n+n*(k+1). Working maps and ordinary run output are excluded from this logical capture policy. Admission precedes complete history copies; no replay.
    algorithms::MooreWorkActual Moore rounds, state/signature work and ordered-map comparisons. Signature components count examined integer pairs, not individual less-than instructions. Map counts depend on the standard-library tree implementation. Completion, quotient construction, allocations and copying are excluded.
    algorithms::MorrisCounterA probabilistic (Morris) counter with a tunable base for accuracy/space trade-off.
    rl::environments::MountainCarMountainCar-v0-style clipped position/velocity dynamics and discrete throttle.
    rl::environments::MountainCarContinuousContinuous mountain-car throttle with clipped force and action-squared cost.
    nn::models::MovingDotDataOwn the detached original moving-dot next-frame fixture.
    nn::Mt19937Mutable std::mt19937 stream with independent float and double normal caches. Instances are unsynchronized; callers serialize access if shared across threads.
    nn::Mt19937_64Mutable std::mt19937_64 stream with float/double normal caches and a distinct 64-bit sequence. Instances are unsynchronized; the normal and shuffle algorithms follow the active standard library.
    algorithms::MTFAnalysisActual linear-search comparisons and shifted alphabet entries. Encode comparisons include the successful test; decoding indexes directly and has zero search comparisons. Alphabet initialization's256 stores are excluded.
    algorithms::MTFIndexSummaryNative observed rank distribution, including exact count-based median. Median averages the two central ranks for even count. Empty means/median/ entropy are explicit zero placeholders. Entropy is empirical marginal bits per rank, not compressed size or a claim that an entropy coder was run.
    algorithms::MTFStepActual selected byte/rank before moving it to the alphabet front. Previous front and the selected byte are observed from the same evolving 256-byte permutation as ordinary execution; no Unicode normalization occurs.
    algorithms::MTFTraceOwned original stream and actual per-byte transform history. Encode retains input_bytes and result.indices; decode retains input_indices and result.bytes. Other two stream fields stay empty. Capture units are one input element, one output element and one step record per byte, exactly3n.
    algorithms::MullerEvaluationOne actual finite callback observation, in invocation order.
    algorithms::MullerRunActual selected callbacks, residual inspections, updates and discriminant clamps. Initial three callbacks count even when x2 already passes or update cap is zero. Inspections include the final cap check, which reuses the last callback value.
    algorithms::MullerStepActual residual inspection and, when needed, its quadratic proposal. quadratic=false means complete coefficients/discriminant are unavailable; spacing fields can retain an attempted coincident-node check, while unused coefficient fields are zero placeholders and next=x2. updated=false means no callback at next was performed. A final cap check records at_limit=true without fabricating a new quadratic iteration.
    algorithms::MullerTraceOwned actual seed/controls, callback history and quadratic inspections. Capture units are five seed/control scalars, each actual callback record and each actual inspection record. Optional quota is online; earlier callback side effects remain if later admission fails. No partial trace is returned.
    rl::environments::MultiArmedBanditOwn the MultiArmedBandit simulation state or interface.
    nn::MultiGateRegressionDifferentiable output and routing diagnostics from a multitask forward pass.

    optim::MultiObjectiveFunctionA vector-valued objective for multi-objective optimization: evaluate() returns one value per objective, all of which are minimized simultaneously. Unlike the single-objective ArbitraryFunction, there is generally no single best point – the solution is a set of mutually non-dominated trade-offs (the Pareto front).

Exposed to bindings via parallel arrays (exponents()/coefficients()) rather than the internal map, matching this module's std::map-avoidance convention for SWIG-facing types.

    optim::NadamNadam on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Fixed-beta Nadam variant: direction beta1*m/(1-beta1^t)+(1-beta1)*g/(1-beta1^t), divided by sqrt(v/(1-beta2^t))+epsilon. Does not implement scheduled momentum products. Tests the gradient used after updating; O(p) reset state. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::NadamOptionsConfiguration for Nadam; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    algorithms::NagleAnalysisActual final packet stream and widened sender accounting. Conservation holds: written=sent+buffered and sent=unacked+acknowledged. Oversized ACK requests saturate at outstanding bytes; no implicit final ACK or flush is supplied. Zero-byte events remain events but emit no zero packet.
    algorithms::NagleEmissionActual packet emission and its immediate scheduling reason. Reason0=full segment,1=idle partial write,2=ACK-released partial,3=baseline.
    algorithms::NagleEventOne application write or acknowledgment in an ordinal sender simulation. Events have no timestamps, network window, retransmission or delayed-ACK model.
    algorithms::NagleStepActual buffer/outstanding states and packet span of one input event.
    algorithms::NagleTraceOwned original events, actual sender states/emissions and final accounting. Capture units count mss/enabled scalars, original events, step records, result packet sizes and emission records:2+2*events+2*packets.

For k=max(n-2,0) interior unknowns, system vectors have length k. lower[0] and upper[k-1] are structural zeros; pivots/reduced_rhs are the actual post-elimination arrays, and multipliers[0]=0. Moments include both zero natural endpoints; degenerate empty/singleton fits use zero/one zero moments. All arrays own storage, with no prefix reruns or shared mutable state.     algorithms::NearestNeighborInterpolantOwned prepared one-dimensional nearest-sample interpolant. Equal-size finite node arrays, with strictly increasing xs. Empty arrays are allowed and produce zero by legacy convention; this is not a data estimate. Finite out-of-range queries select the nearest endpoint; exact midpoint ties select the lower index. Ordinates may be nonmonotone. No smoothing or new ordinate values are introduced. O(n) validation/setup/storage, then O(log(n+1)) query work and constant query-driver storage. Const queries do not mutate.

    algorithms::NearestNeighborStudyOwned native smooth-function interpolation and finite-grid error study. The reference bound1.3*h/2 uses |cos(x)+.3|<=1.3 on the sampled domain. It bounds exact-arithmetic nearest-sample error on[0,6.4], not extrapolation or floating-point roundoff; the reported maximum is only over its query grid.
    algorithms::NearestNeighborTraceOwned nodes/query and actual binary-search/nearest-choice observations. Capture units are both node arrays, query/result scalar records and actual search-step records:2n+2+steps. Empty result index0 is a placeholder. Route0=empty,1=lower endpoint,2=upper endpoint,3=interior nearest choice. Distances are meaningful only for route3 and use widened arithmetic.
    algorithms::NearestTSPAnalysisActual greedy tour and selected scan/sum work counts. Candidate checks include visited IDs; distance comparisons occur only after the first eligible candidate has established a current best. Counts are not matrix-load or CPU-operation totals. Final tour sum includes the closing edge.
    algorithms::NearestTSPChoiceActual chosen next city and its eligible-trial span.
    algorithms::NearestTSPEdgeActual post-route sequential edge sum, including closure.
    algorithms::NearestTSPTraceOwned original matrix/start and actual greedy/summation history. Capture units count start, input rows/weights, result route IDs, eligible trial records, choice records and edge-sum records. Scalar fields within a record are not additional units. Empty input retains start but no route.
    algorithms::NearestTSPTrialActual eligible candidate and current-best update at one greedy visit. Candidates appear by ascending ID; first=true means no prior best, so no distance comparison occurred. Equal-distance later candidates never replace.
    nn::NeatEvolve feed-forward, single-output tanh networks with NEAT.
    algorithms::NeedlemanWunschCellActual candidates, selected score and first-max direction of an interior cell. Fill order is increasing first prefix then increasing second prefix. Ties choose diagonal, then up, then left. The ordinary producer makes this same first-maximum selection; no report-side score table is reconstructed.
    algorithms::NeedlemanWunschOptionsComplete score-table and actual capture policies, zero disabling either. max_cells includes both boundary row and column before table allocation. Ordinary needleman_wunsch() disables optional policies, retaining its entry point.
    algorithms::NeedlemanWunschRunActual global optimum, full native score table and selected work. Default scoring2,−1,−2 uses linear gaps. Positive gap scores are allowed and can prefer opposing inserted gaps. No affine-gap state or biological probability model is implied. Rows index first-input prefixes, columns second.
    algorithms::NeedlemanWunschTraceOwned original byte inputs, actual table fills and actual traceback. Capture units count3 scoring scalars, both input strings, row records, score values, interior-cell records, traceback records and both aligned outputs. For alignment length L:3+n+m+(n+1)+(n+1)*(m+1)+n*m+3L. Table and fill counts are pre-admitted; actual traceback/output units follow online. No replay, truncation or partial returned trace.
    algorithms::NeedlemanWunschTracebackActual reverse-order traceback emission and score-table coordinates. Records run from bottom-right to origin; final aligned rows reverse these emitted bytes. Literal input hyphens are rejected so inserted gaps are unambiguous.
    optim::NelderMeadNelderMead on the ArbitraryFunction callback interface. Local simplex reflection, expansion, contraction and shrink search. Starts with per-coordinate displacements initial_simplex_scale and stops when simplex diameter and value spread are small. Those conditions do not prove stationarity or a global minimum. O(p^2) simplex storage. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::NelderMeadOptionsConfiguration for NelderMead; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.

    optim::NSGA2Native NSGA-II with original random/selection/variation order and guarded objective contracts. Every objective is minimized. Actual initial population requires no discarded dimension probe; callbacks=N*(G+1). Rank-first/crowding-second tournaments sample with replacement, and exact ties choose the second draw. Both SBX children mutate/evaluate in original order. Survival processes complete fronts until the final partial front, truncating by descending crowding. Nondominated points CAN be lost when a front exceeds capacity; no global archive is kept. Sorting equal values preserves the standard library's unspecified tie order. Work O((G+1)*mN squared+G*N*nvars), including quadratic final filtering, plus callback/variation and crowding-sort costs. Driver dominated-set storage is O(N squared+N*(nvars+m)); actual detailed traces can cost O(G*N squared). Concurrent const calls own RNG/state, but callbacks own their thread safety.

Ties use std::sort without an added ID rule; no cross-standard-library tie ordering promise.

This reduces cancellation, but does not guarantee offset-independent accuracy, exact M2, or recovery of signal lost when original inputs were rounded. Empty/singleton sample variance and empty mean use historical0 conventions. O(1) work/state per add/merge, no references/callbacks/shared mutable state.     algorithms::PackratParserOwned byte PEG interpreter memoizing completed named-rule/position results. Complete grammar validation covers every node/operator/child arity/reference and start name before parsing. Direct/indirect left recursion at an active identical(rule,position) throws rather than recursing forever; right recursion remains subject to actual depth/work limits. Predicates do not consume input; ordered choice never revisits a successful child after a later sequence fails. Empty repetition stops on no progress, preserving original nullable behavior. Uses ordered std::map memo, not constant-time lookup. Only named rules are memoized: repeated greedy expression scans can still be quadratic. Therefore no general linear-time/linear-space packrat bound is promised by this API. Each parse owns its copied input, clears old memo/counters and uses no caller references/callbacks. A failed attempt clears incomplete memo and returns no trace, retaining explicit partial last-attempt counters/completed=false. Copies own grammar/input/cache; concurrent calls on one instance need caller synchronization. Zero disables optional policies, not the finite native stack.

    optim::ParallelTemperingParallel tempering (replica exchange Monte Carlo): the population-based generalization of SimulatedAnnealing. Runs num_replicas Metropolis chains simultaneously, each held at its own fixed temperature on a geometric ladder, and periodically proposes swapping adjacent-temperature replicas' states so hot chains help cold chains escape local minima. Derivative-free, unconstrained, suitable for non-differentiable/black-box objectives – like SimulatedAnnealing, requires nothing beyond evaluate().

    filter::ParticleFilterA bootstrap particle filter (Sequential Importance Resampling): the fully general, non-Gaussian generalization of the Kalman family – represents the state's entire posterior distribution as a weighted swarm of sample points rather than assuming any particular family of distribution (Gaussian, etc.), so it remains correct even for strongly non-Gaussian or multimodal posteriors where every other filter in this module (which all assume approximately-Gaussian beliefs) can fail. Costs scale with particle count and can need many particles in high dimensions ("the curse of dimensionality" for particle filters) – EnsembleKalmanFilter is usually preferred for high-dimensional problems where the Gaussian assumption is acceptable.

    PCASWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::PCA — principal component analysis fit from a DataFrame and a list of numeric feature columns via eigendecomposition of the correlation (default) or covariance matrix.
    stats::PCAPCA from a named numeric DataFrame schema, retaining a full p-axis basis. Like R prcomp in centred/scaled score semantics, but uses a covariance eigensolver, defaults scale=true, permits constant columns and always returns p components, including null directions when p>=n. Rank is separate from num_components(). Fitting drops rows with any null selected feature and rejects retained nonfinite values. Training means/scales and axes are frozen for new rows. With centring, eigenvalues are sample variances; without it they are second-moment energies. Signs are arbitrary, and repeated eigenvalues permit rotations of their eigenspace. Gram formation squares the data condition number; this is not a high-relative-accuracy SVD for near-null directions. Work O(np^2+p^3) for bounded Jacobi sweeps, storage O(np+p^2). Model owns all state; const operations have no shared mutable caches.
    stats::PCAOptionsPreprocessing for PCA; scaling defaults true, unlike R prcomp's false. With center=true, scale=true uses sample standard deviations (n-1 divisor). With center=false it uses sqrt(sum(x^2)/(n-1)), not centred standard deviation. Exactly zero scales become one. With centring, constant columns remain null directions.
    random::Pcg32PCG XSH-RR with 64-bit state and odd selectable increment. Two consecutive 32-bit outputs form each next_u64(), first in the high half. Stream selectors differing only in bit63 alias after doubling; different streams are not claimed statistically independent. Each odd-increment state transition has period 2^64. Deterministic simulation use, not cryptography. Instances own state; copies continue identically, including inherited caches. Concurrent mutation of one instance requires external synchronisation.

    algorithms::PiReferenceAccuracyComputed comparison with rounded double and long-double pi references. These are reference differences, not certified errors against mathematical pi. rounded_ulp_offset uses spacing at the double reference, not a bit-distance metric for distant candidates. Wider precision is platform-dependent. Log fields have zero placeholders when the corresponding difference is zero, with explicit has-log flags. -log10(error) is an accuracy measure, not a certified count of correct decimal digits. No shared state or allocation.

    algorithms::PlanningActionOne grounded positive-precondition operator on a 64-bit fact state. Applicable when all require bits hold. Transition is (state & ~remove) | add; overlapping add/remove bits end present. No negative preconditions, variables, theorem prover or external action is executed. All 64 bits are valid, including bit 63. Names may be empty, duplicated or arbitrary byte strings; identity is position in the operator vector. Legacy field order and types are preserved.
    algorithms::PlanningCertificateOwned finite certificate from independently executing operator indices. Validates the entire index vector before any transition. If a precondition fails, stops before that action: applicable=false, applied is its zero-based failing position, states retains the valid prefix including initial. A goal miss after a fully applicable sequence is reported by reaches_goals=false. Empty sequences are applicable; goals may already hold. O(p) transition work and O(p) owned states for p indices; no search, shortest-path or budget claim.
    algorithms::PlanningEventOne actual fixed-schema search event; state masks are constant-width values. state/depth identify the current frame. apply has the actual successor in next_state; other kinds use next_state=state. action_index is meaningful for test/apply/backtrack/finish, otherwise size_t maximum. applicable is meaningful only for test. repeat/reopen expose the previous expansion depth and set has_previous_depth; other events leave it false. No vector/path is replayed.
    algorithms::PlanningResultOwned legacy planning outcome with operator names in application order. Success contains an executable plan no longer than the requested budget, not necessarily shortest. Initially satisfied goals give an empty successful plan and final_state=initial. Failure has empty actions/final_state0/found=false; its final_state is a placeholder, not a reached failure witness. Names alone can be ambiguous; PlanningRun also retains operator indices. Stable layout.
    algorithms::PlanningRunOwned ordinary planning result, unambiguous operator indices and actual work. action_indices and result.actions describe the same successful sequence; both are empty on failure. No replay or history is performed by this result. Indices refer to the caller's original operator order; no shared state or caller mutation. DFS frame storage is on the heap, not the C++ call stack.
    algorithms::PlanningTraceOwned inputs, ordinary result and ordered actual search events from one execution. Every event is one fixed-schema record, not one numeric entry or byte. The online event quota excludes owned input operators/names, root and work metadata, final ordinary output, working stack/map and allocator storage; it is not a peak RAM limit. No partial or truncated trace is returned when a quota is exceeded. Inputs, labels and snapshots are independent owned copies.
    algorithms::PlanningWorkActual node, operator and pruning work from one ordered forward DFS. Visits include root, goal, depth-cutoff and repeated-state entries. Expanded states pass all three terminal/pruning checks and can be expanded again after a shallower arrival. Goal/depth checks precede the best-depth map. Counters exclude copies, allocation, hashing internals and trace capture; not timings.

    PlotArgsOwned plot-level text options for Plot().with(PlotArgs{...}), the named-argument spelling of R's plot(..., main =, sub =, xlab =, ylab =).
    PlotLabelAn owned heading or axis-label update for a plot pipe.

No pointer ownership or shared mutable state is involved.

Subsets are sorted/unique and indexed exactly like dfa states; numbering is discovery order, scanning symbols ascending. Only reachable subsets are created. complete records the requested policy, not whether a partial-policy result happens to have every move. The empty initial subset is omitted in partial mode, yielding zero states/start=-1, or retained in complete mode.
    algorithms::PrattEventOne actual binding decision or completed native evaluation event. Offsets count bytes in the original borrowed string. End is the immediate parser position. Binding records expose the actual context/operator powers; other inapplicable scalar fields are zero.
    algorithms::PrattOptionsDepth, selected parser-call/event and retained-record policies. Zero independently disables the corresponding policy; default depth bounds recursive call frames rather than expression length alone.

    algorithms::PreflowEventOne actual residual push or height relabel with immediately used state. For relabels, to=from, amount and residual fields are zero, and input is the size_t maximum sentinel. Height/excess fields refer to actual current vertices. Forward=false identifies an original-edge cancellation arc.
    algorithms::PreparedCubicSplineOwned validated local-power spline for repeated value/derivative evaluation. Comparable to a scalar SciPy PPoly with endpoint-piece extrapolation. Construction checks/copies a public record once; evaluations never re-scan all coefficients. No references to the input survive. Empty/singleton models use the same zero/constant conventions as cubic_spline_eval(). Const methods are safe for independent concurrent reads. Finite arithmetic is checked, without a numerical error bound or a shape-preservation guarantee.
    cad::PreparedSceneOwned immutable transformed geometry reusable across cameras and frames. Construction validates and prepares a snapshot. Copies share that immutable snapshot; later changes to the source Scene cannot affect it. Concurrent const renders are safe. An optional actor scene is prepared for just that call and participates in all primary, shadow and AO rays. Base lighting is retained. Actor rendering shares validated, transformed base triangles and rebuilds a combined hierarchy in flattened scene order, preserving equal-depth ties. The base-only hierarchy is initialized lazily under a thread-safe once guard.

    optim::ProximalFunctionComposite objective for proximal methods. gradient() is the gradient of the smooth component, and proximal() applies the non-smooth component's proximal operator.
    optim::ProximalGradientProximalGradient on the ProximalFunction callback interface. ISTA update prox(x-step_size*gradient(x),step_size), with gradient of the smooth part only. Stops on coordinate displacement norm. There is no Lipschitz estimation or backtracking; caller chooses a stable rate. The returned objective includes both smooth and nonsmooth parts. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::ProximalGradientOptionsConfiguration for ProximalGradient; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    nn::ProxyMetricResultOwn cosine scores and a differentiable proxy metric objective.

    algorithms::PruferEncodingOwned produced sequence, final survivors and optional actual leaf transitions. Ordinary output is the sequence; trace records expose producing decisions rather than a reconstructed deletion run.
    algorithms::PruferEnumerationActual exhaustive Prüfer enumeration counts and checked Cayley reference. Only the summary is returned; exact canonical edge sets are compared during enumeration without hash collisions.
    algorithms::PruferOptionsVertex and retained-entry policies for native tree coding. Zero independently disables a cap; default limits count vertices and logical records/leaf ids, not bytes.
    algorithms::PruferStepOne actual smallest-leaf removal or final decoding connection. Leaf sets are copied from the actual ordered set before and after its updates; records own all values.
    nn::PrunedConvChannelsCompacted filter pair and retained intermediate channel indices.
    optim::PSOPSO on the ArbitraryFunction callback interface. Box-constrained particle swarm with global or ring attraction and constant or linearly decayed inertia. Coordinates seed one clamped particle; returns the best visited feasible point. Stops after more than twenty small-best-improvement iterations or its budget. O(population_size*p) storage; no global-optimality certificate. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::PSOOptionsConfiguration for PSO; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

    fda::PSplineOptionsDifference-penalty settings for fit_pspline().

    random::RandomGeneratorCommon distribution samplers driven by a deterministic raw-word interface. Instances own a cached Box-Muller normal spare; copying an engine also copies that cache and duplicates the stream. Distribution calls may consume zero (cached normal), one, or multiple (rejection/retry) raw words. Mutating one instance concurrently requires external synchronization. Floating results use the host libm; raw deterministic sequences do not guarantee cross-libm bitwise transcendental results. No entropy, independence or security claim follows from sampling.
    optim::RandomizedBlockCoordinateDescentRandomizedBlockCoordinateDescent on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Randomly permutes coordinates each epoch and visits consecutive blocks once. Full-gradient block directions use Armijo backtracking and restore a failed block. This is random reshuffling, not independent coordinate draws. Stops on the full epoch-end gradient norm; O(p) local storage. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::RandomizedBlockCoordinateDescentOptionsConfiguration for RandomizedBlockCoordinateDescent; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

    bayes::RandomWalkMetropolisRandom-walk Metropolis-Hastings: the classic gradient-free MCMC baseline, proposing x' = x + step_size * N(0, I) and accepting with probability min(1, exp(log_posterior(x') - log_posterior(x))).     optim::RMSPropRMSProp on the DifferentiableFunction callback interface. Uses an exponential squared-gradient average with decay_rate, dividing by sqrt(average)+epsilon. Tests the pre-update gradient norm after updating. Fixed rates can oscillate. O(p) local state, reset on every call. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::RMSPropOptionsConfiguration for RMSProp; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

Coordinates are URDF metres/radians; CAD STEP files keep their own file units. Inertial/collision/dynamics/transmissions are not evaluated by this visual loader. Xacro must be expanded first. Geometry is owned; copies share immutable source meshes and have independent joint positions. Concurrent const scene generation is safe.

    algorithms::RTJobActual per-job release, execution, completion and deadline evidence. Job ids are indices in RTTrace::jobs, ordered by release time then input task. Deadlines use int64_t so release+period cannot overflow int. A zero-work job completes at release; an unfinished job has completion=-1 even if already late.
    algorithms::RTScheduleResultMerged task timeline and deadline verdict for a finite simulation. Timeline covers [0,H) exactly. deadline_missed includes all job deadlines through boundary H; unfinished jobs due after H are not yet misses. Copies own their timeline. A finite clean prefix is not an infinite schedulability proof.
    algorithms::RTSimulationFinite scheduling outcome and work, with no retained job/tick history. Independent calls leave input unchanged. Runtime retains unfinished jobs; completed jobs are removed. There is no optional capture quota.
    algorithms::RTSliceAn owned-label interval in a merged task execution timeline. Half-open [start,end); returned slices have nonnegative start and end>start. Adjacent units running the same task are merged, even across job boundaries.
    algorithms::RTTaskAn independent synchronous periodic task with implicit deadlines. Jobs release at 0,T,2T,... and need C integer processor units by the next release. One fully preemptive processor, zero overhead and no blocking are assumed. APIs require positive period, nonnegative wcet and unique ids other than SIZE_MAX (reserved for idle). C>T is a valid overloaded task.
    algorithms::RTTraceOwned actual release records and per-unit job selections, without replay. Capture has N task records, H tick selections and J released job records, so captured_entries=N+H+J. Scalars, result timeline, working heap/counters, vector capacity and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not a peak-RAM bound. Retained history uses O(N+H+J) entries; result/runtime memory is additional.
    algorithms::RTWorkChecked logical counters for the actual unit-granularity simulator. Counts are not elapsed time or scheduler overhead. Preemption means the next unit selects a different job while the previously selected job is unfinished; stopping at the horizon is not a preemption. Zero-work releases complete at once.

    algorithms::SafetyResultResult of the safety check: whether the state is safe and, if so, a safe sequence.
    optim::SAGASAGA on the DifferentiableSeparableFunction callback interface. Uses current_i-table_i+mean(table), then refreshes one stored component gradient and its running mean. The estimator targets mean component loss while evaluate() returns their sum. Stops on epoch-boundary objective change or the last estimator norm; the latter is not the full gradient norm. O(n*p) gradient table. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::SAGAOptionsConfiguration for SAGA; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

    algorithms::Salsa20OptionsComplete stream-byte and actual captured-block policies; zero disables a cap.

    SammonMappingSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::SammonMapping — iteratively minimizes a weighted distance-preservation "stress" (small high-dimensional distances weighted much more heavily than large ones) via Sammon's original pseudo-Newton update.
    stats::SammonMappingSammon mapping (Sammon, 1969): a classic nonlinear-MDS-family method that predates and directly influenced t-SNE. Unlike classical MDS's closed-form eigendecomposition, Sammon mapping iteratively minimizes a weighted sum-of-squared-distance-errors "stress" via a pseudo-Newton update, WEIGHTING errors by 1/Dstar_ij – so small (nearby) high- dimensional distances are preserved much more faithfully than large ones, unlike classical MDS which weights all pairs equally. Rows with a null value in any feature column are dropped before fitting.

Bindings without director support must instead use FEM1D::solve_builtin()'s fixed set of named source terms.

    algorithms::SCCEventOwned actual first-discovery, edge, finish or component-assignment operation. u is the actual vertex/source; v is the actual target only for edge events and -1 otherwise. component is meaningful on Assign/TransposeEdge and-1 otherwise.
    algorithms::SccSummaryOwned groups and the deduplicated quotient graph for supplied labels. Dense quotient indices follow ascending raw labels, distinct from those labels. Internal edges are omitted from adjacency; cross edges are sorted/deduplicated. For arbitrary labels the quotient may contain cycles: no SCC correctness certificate is computed. Gabow labels make reverse_topological true, which proves acyclicity by strict label decrease.

    random::Sfc64Small Fast Counter raw64-bit engine with inspectable actual transitions. Owns three uint64 words and a counter, plus the inherited normal spare. Updates use modulo2^64 addition, xor/right11, multiplication by9 and rotate-left24. Historical local seeding expands the supplied seed through three SplitMix64 steps, initializes counter1 and performs NO warmup; this seeding policy differs from some reference-library initialization recipes. All raw states, including zeros and counter wrap, are supported. Raw next calls do not clear the inherited normal spare; copying the engine preserves both raw state and distribution cache. State snapshots exclude that cache. O(1) step work/storage; no entropy/security or universal period claim. Concurrent mutation requires caller synchronization.

    optim::SGDSGD on the DifferentiableSeparableFunction callback interface. Uses the mean gradient of each mini-batch, reshuffling component indices each epoch when enabled. Full objective remains the sum of components. Stops on absolute full-objective change per epoch. Nonempty components and positive batch_size are required; seeds reproduce the same build, not a cross-library shuffle transcript. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.

    stats::ShapImageExplainerSHAP (Lundberg & Lee, 2017) via exact Shapley values from cooperative game theory: each superpixel's attribution is its average marginal contribution to the model's score over all coalitions of the other superpixels. Computed exactly by enumerating every one of the 2^P coalitions of the P = patch_rows*patch_cols superpixels (so P must stay small), which makes the result independent of any sampling and exactly satisfies the efficiency axiom: the attributions sum to f(full image) - f(empty image). Model-agnostic.

    optim::SimulatedAnnealingSimulatedAnnealing on the ArbitraryFunction callback interface. Gaussian random-walk proposals with geometrically decaying temperature and Metropolis acceptance of worse values. Returns the best visited point, not the last accepted state. A finite cooling schedule does not certify a global optimum; O(p) storage. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.

    optim::SmoothBenchmarkRosenbrock valley (1-x)^2+100*(y-x^2)^2, Rastrigin or a quadratic-plus-sinusoidal bumpy surface. Rastrigin is 20+sum(x_j^2-10*cos(2*pi*x_j)); their global minima are zero, at (1,1) for Rosenbrock and (0,0) for Rastrigin. Bumpy is (x-3)^2+(y+1)^2+5*sin(x)*cos(y), bounded below by -5; no exact global minimizer is asserted. Analytic derivatives are available even when a derivative-free optimizer is used. No mutable caches.

    algorithms::StabilityDiagnosticsStructural feasibility and all actual blocking pairs for a candidate. A malformed candidate gives feasible=false,complete=false,stable=false and no witnesses. Empty witnesses alone do not certify stability. Valid partial maps may be feasible but are unstable under complete equal-side preferences. Empty valid maps are complete and stable. Proposal metadata is ignored.
    algorithms::StableBlockingPairA genuine mutually preferred pair from a feasible candidate. All ranks are one-based, with smaller better. An unmatched incumbent has rank n+1. Candidate pair ranks are strictly less than incumbent ranks on both sides. This witness is meaningful only after feasibility validation.
    algorithms::StableMatchingEnumerationOwned stable perfect candidates from bounded exhaustive search. Candidates are tested in lexicographic proposer-map order. Their proposal metadata is0 because enumeration is not a proposal execution. For n0 there is one empty permutation and one empty stable matching. Shared blocking checks are not an independent correctness oracle.
    algorithms::StableMatchingProfileOwned complete strict preferences for two equal sides. Both matrices retain original agent and rank order. The fixture and generators produce independent owned rows without shared mutable state.
    algorithms::StableMatchingRanksOne-based assigned-partner ranks for a perfect candidate. Requires mutual perfect maps; does not itself certify stability. Means are descriptive averages of ordinal ranks, not utility or probabilities. Empty input has has_agents=false and zero mean placeholders, not observed mean satisfaction.
    algorithms::StableMatchingResultOwned mutual partner maps and proposal-count metadata. Legacy field order/layout retained. A structurally feasible partial matching uses kUnmatched symmetrically; complete strict equal-size inputs produce a perfect matching. Stability ignores proposals, allowing manually constructed candidates. Reversing orientation exchanges the maps and preserves the original execution count.

    optim::SVRGSVRG on the DifferentiableSeparableFunction callback interface. Uses mean component gradients: current_i-snapshot_i+full_snapshot_gradient/n. The division by n is essential for an unbiased mean-loss estimator and matches SGD/SAGA scale. Earlier code omitted it. Stops on absolute full-sum objective change per epoch. O(p) snapshot state, two component-gradient calls per inner update plus one full gradient per epoch. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::SVRGOptionsConfiguration for SVRG; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().

    TapeSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::autodiff::Tape – a reverse-mode ("backpropagation") computation tape. Create leaf Vars against a Tape, build an expression out of named Var operations, then call backward() on the output Var to get the derivative of that output with respect to every node on the tape (index a leaf's own index() into the result to read its gradient).
    autodiff::TapeA reverse-mode ("backpropagation") computation tape – an append-only Wengert list. Every Var operation records one node holding its value and the local derivative(s) with respect to its immediate parent node(s); a single backward() sweep then yields the derivative of the seeded output with respect to every node (including every leaf) in one reverse pass.

    geometry::TriangleThree original point indices in counterclockwise order for finite mesh faces. Original field layout/defaults are retained. A trace ghost uses c=points.size() as a symbolic infinity marker, with a,b the reversed finite hull edge; it is never returned by delaunay_triangulation(). No coordinate is constructed for it.
    geometry::TriangulationLocatorBorrow a conforming CCW triangulation and cache its edge-to-face adjacency. Both input vectors must outlive this object and remain unchanged, including through public pointer/map fields. Copies retain the same borrowed inputs and own copied adjacency. Concurrent const queries use independent RNG/work state. Construction checks all finite coordinates, face indices, strict exact CCW, at most two faces per edge and opposite shared-edge directions. It does NOT certify global nonoverlap, convex-domain coverage, absence of holes or Delaunay empty circles: those embedding properties remain caller preconditions for interpreting boundary as outside. Canonical delaunay_triangulation() supplies an appropriate mesh. General non-Delaunay walks may exhaust their bound. Packed legacy edge keys require each used point index<=UINT32_MAX; triangle count<=INT_MAX. Expected hash construction O(P+T) work/O(T) adjacency storage, excluding borrowed inputs and exact predicate constant factors. No cube-root query bound is promised for arbitrary meshes or query distributions.

    optim::TrustRegionNewtonTrustRegionNewton on the HessianFunction callback interface. Cauchy-point variant: clips a steepest-descent ray using gHg and the current radius. Accepts any strict objective decrease and doubles the radius, otherwise halves it. It does not compute a model-agreement ratio, dogleg step or exact trust-region subproblem. Stops on gradient norm or tiny radius; O(p^2) Hessian work. The caller supplies finite, dimensionally consistent callbacks. Inputs are borrowed; coordinates mutate in place and can retain a partial state if a callback throws. Calls use local optimizer state and propagate callback exceptions; sharing a mutable objective across threads requires external synchronisation. Normal return alone is not a uniform convergence certificate.
    optim::TrustRegionNewtonOptionsConfiguration for TrustRegionNewton; fields retain their documented native defaults. Supply finite values in the supported ranges. Controls are copied at construction; validation, stopping and loss scaling belong to optimize().
    TSNESWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::TSNE — t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding, a nonlinear method that preserves local neighborhood structure (via a perplexity-calibrated probability distribution) primarily for 2D/3D visualization.
    stats::TSNEt-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (van der Maaten & Hinton, 2008): converts pairwise distances into conditional probabilities (calibrated per-point via a perplexity-targeted binary search over a Gaussian bandwidth), symmetrizes them into a joint distribution P, and iteratively moves points in a low-dimensional space via momentum-based gradient descent so that a Student-t-distributed joint distribution Q over the embedded points matches P as closely as possible (minimizing their KL divergence). Unlike PCA/MDS, t-SNE preserves local neighborhood structure rather than global distances or variance, and is primarily useful for visualization (typically n_components 2 or 3). Rows with a null value in any feature column are dropped before fitting.
    stats::TSNEOptions
    stats::TukeyHSDTukey's honest significant differences for a one-way layout, like R's TukeyHSD(aov(value ~ group)).

    U

    UMAPSWIG-friendly facade for datamunge::stats::UMAP — builds a fuzzy simplicial set (a smoothly-calibrated, fuzzy-union-symmetrized k-nearest-neighbor graph) and optimizes a low-dimensional embedding via cross-entropy minimization (attractive + negative-sampled repulsive forces). A deliberately simplified but honest implementation – see the real class's own documentation for the two named simplifications.
    stats::UMAPUMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection): builds a fuzzy simplicial set (a weighted k-nearest-neighbor graph with per-point smooth calibration and probabilistic t-conorm symmetrization) from the high-dimensional data, then optimizes a low-dimensional embedding via cross-entropy minimization using attractive forces on graph edges and repulsive forces from negative sampling. McInnes, Healy & Melville (2018), arXiv:1802.03426. Differs from MDS (no eigendecomposition of a distance matrix – an iterative force-based layout) and from t-SNE elsewhere in this module (smooth k-NN calibration against a fixed log2(k) target rather than perplexity/entropy calibration, fuzzy-union symmetrization rather than plain averaging, and negative-sampled cross-entropy forces rather than a full KL-divergence gradient). This implementation is deliberately simplified in two named respects – see the comment in umap.cpp's fit(). Rows with a null value in any feature column are dropped before fitting.
    stats::UMAPOptions

    filter::UnscentedKalmanFilterThe Unscented Kalman Filter: propagates a small deterministic set of "sigma points" through the true nonlinear f/h (rather than linearizing f/h itself, as ExtendedKalmanFilter does), then reconstructs the predicted mean/covariance from the propagated points' weighted statistics. Captures nonlinearity to (at least) second order without ever needing a Jacobian – generally more accurate than EKF for strongly nonlinear models, at the cost of 2n+1 function evaluations per step instead of one. Exactly reproduces KalmanFilter's result when f and h are linear.
    algorithms::UnweightedSearchResultOwned path, producer-specific traversal sequence and success flag. Field order/types retain the historical search_batch.hpp interface. Interpret order using the producer's contract: BFS records dequeues, while the legacy bidirectional_search wrapper reports the path in that field. Other searchers may revisit vertices. No input graph storage is borrowed.
    algorithms::UPGMAMergeOne actual size-weighted cluster merge.
    algorithms::UPGMAResultActual UPGMA merge sequence and selected work.
    sim::UrdfModelImmutable native URDF dynamics/collision model, independent of rendering and MuJoCo. Supports rooted trees, fixed/revolute/continuous/prismatic joints, affine mimic gearing, full rotated COM tensors, and box/sphere/cylinder/STL collision geometry. Cylinders use 32-sided hulls; meshes use deterministic sampled convex hulls (concavities require multiple collision elements). Missing inertias are rejected unless explicitly given nominal import options. Copies share immutable geometry.
    sim::UrdfPhysicsOptionsExplicit physical import approximations for URDF collision meshes and missing inertias. Source units are metres/radians/kg. No external physics engine is used.
    stats::UStatisticAverage a symmetric degree-m kernel over all distinct-index subsets or random subset draws.
    stats::UStatisticAnalysisOwned U-statistic fit, per-observation diagnostics and separately identified uncertainties.
    stats::UStatisticLawExact finite-sample law of a complete U-statistic under a two-point i.i.d. population.
    stats::UStatisticOptionsEnumeration or random-subset settings for UStatistic.
    stats::UStatisticResultU estimate and legacy first-projection variance diagnostics, not total uncertainty.

    algorithms::VehicleRouteEvaluationOwned independent route-feasibility and widened distance measurements. Every nondepot occurrence contributes demand, including repeated customers or customer endpoints of malformed routes. repeated_visits counts extra visits, not the number of multiply visited customers. Missing customers count once. A malformed route has fewer than three vertices or wrong depot endpoints. Interior depot visits are reported separately. No capacity tolerance applies. This record certifies no optimality and validates no manually assigned fields.
    algorithms::VehicleRoutesOwned depot-closed vehicle routes and their measured total Euclidean length. Each nonempty generated route begins and ends at the chosen depot, with every customer served exactly once. Depot-only input returns no routes and zero distance. This plain record validates nothing and certifies no optimality. The original field order and types are retained. Values own their storage.

    cad::VideoWriterStream rendered frames directly into a silent H.264 MP4 without intermediate PNGs. Requires ffmpeg with libx264 on PATH. Uses a bounded OS stream with synchronous backpressure; there is no unbounded queue or shell command interpolation. Encoding uses baseline/yuv420p, CRF19, fast, no B frames and a two-second GOP. Input alpha is discarded by the encoder. One writer is single-threaded; independent writers may coexist. Call finish() to publish the completed file; destruction closes the child and discards unfinalized temporary output. Existing destinations are retained until successful finalization.

Work/storage per call is O(Y+R+W+E_y), for Y young objects, R root slots, W remembered old-to-young slots and E_y fields of retained young objects.

    Z

    algorithms::ZArrayStatsOwned Z-array and work counters from the same preprocessing loop.
    optim::ZDT1FrontSummaryObserved coverage and vertical gaps of an approximate ZDT1 front. Empty fronts are rejected by the producer. Gaps are objective2 minus 1-sqrt(objective1), not hypervolume, distance to a set or a convergence proof.
    optim::ZDT1ObjectiveNative original ZDT1 benchmark, minimizing two objectives on[0,1]^n. f1=x0, g=1+9*mean(x1..), f2=g*(1-sqrt(f1/g)). Optimum g=1 gives f2=1-sqrt(f1). No optimizer or sampling is hidden in the objective.
